A Senate Majority Leader has no statutory entitlement to waived DoD SAP notification by virtue of that office. david-grusch.label: The Wilson-Davis Notes (16 October 2002)

christopher-mellon.why: National Security Affairs Advisor / advisory board (2017-2020)
christopher-mellon.note: A former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and SSCI minority staff director lending his name to the vehicle.

christopher-mellon.label: Anna Paulina Luna
christopher-mellon.why: Luna read Mellon's demolition of AARO's historical report into her 2025 opening statement
christopher-mellon.note: Mellon called it 'the most error-ridden and unsatisfactory government report I can recall reading after decades of government service.'

christopher-mellon.label: House Oversight joint hearing, 13 November 2024 - 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth'
christopher-mellon.why: His hearing letter was submitted into the record by Rep. Mace
christopher-mellon.note: Index of Documents: 'Mellon Hearing Letter; submitted by Rep. Mace.'

christopher-mellon.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
christopher-mellon.note: Mellon's judgement six days after Release 01 became the framing for the entire research community's response.

christopher-mellon.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
christopher-mellon.note: Mellon's verdict on the first PURSUE drop of 8 May 2026 became the caucus's framing.

christopher-mellon.label: FLIR1, Gimbal and GoFast Navy gun-camera videos
christopher-mellon.why: Received the three files in the Pentagon parking lot and passed them to the NYT
christopher-mellon.note: Mellon's own on-record account in The Phenomenon: 'I received the videos, the now famous videos in the Pentagon parking lot from a Defense Department official.' The handing official has never been identified.

christopher-mellon.label: New York Times, 'Glowing Auras and Black Money: The Pentagon's Mysterious U.F.O. Program'
christopher-mellon.why: Supplied the videos published with the story
christopher-mellon.note: Mellon says he provided the files to the Times; the Times separately stated the Department of Defense was its on-the-record source for them.

christopher-mellon.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
christopher-mellon.why: 'The most error-ridden and unsatisfactory government report I can recall reading'
christopher-mellon.note: Mellon, a former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and SSCI staff director, attacked the AARO report's quality at the September 2025 Task Force hearing - an oversight professional's judgment on the rebuttal's workmanship rather than on the phenomenon.

christopher-mellon.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
christopher-mellon.why: 'Data alone is not disclosure' - the framing the House adopted
christopher-mellon.note: Mellon conceded the scale of the retained holdings is itself a revelation while rejecting the sufficiency of context-free files.

christopher-mellon.label: FY2026 NDAA UAP provisions
christopher-mellon.note: The FY2026 NDAA's three UAP provisions reflect recommendations from Mellon and the Disclosure Foundation.

christopher-mellon.label: FY2026 NDAA UAP provisions
christopher-mellon.why: Two of the three provisions mirror recommendations he championed
christopher-mellon.note: Per Disclosure Foundation executive director Jordan Flowers.

christopher-mellon.label: David Charles Grusch
christopher-mellon.why: Corroborates the existence of a class of well-placed sources; facilitated congressional briefings
christopher-mellon.note: Grusch referred roughly 40 witnesses to the ICIG; Mellon independently states well-placed officials shared detailed information with him and has facilitated classified congressional briefings. Reasoning: the two streams are described separately in the same article, and no document establishes overlap - but they converge on the same committees.

christopher-mellon.label: UAP Gerb - 'The Hidden Wing' (USAF structure)
christopher-mellon.why: Identifies candidates for Mellon's unnamed Air Force SES-2 gatekeeper
christopher-mellon.note: Gerb proposes that SAF/AAH (Sensitive Activities) and SAF/AZ and their directors Russell Wyler and William Maclure are the likely referents of the Air Force SES-2 gatekeeper Christopher Mellon has described publicly. This is Gerb's method in miniature: take a witness's unnamed role and resolve it against the published org chart.

christopher-mellon.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF)
christopher-mellon.why: Congressional advocacy channel from 2018 that fed the Task Force and AARO
christopher-mellon.note: Mellon's March 2018 Washington Post op-ed and his subsequent Hill work are the bridge between the TTSA period and the formal government structures. The causal link is reasoned from sequence and his documented access, not from a single primary record.

garry-reid.label: Garry Reid memoranda on AATIP and Elizondo, December 2017
garry-reid.note: Reid wrote the memorandum for record and the memorandum for the Secretary asserting Elizondo 'aggrandized his role'.

garry-reid.label: James N. Mattis
garry-reid.why: Secretary's office put six questions to Reid about Elizondo, Dec 2017
garry-reid.note: Rather than engaging Elizondo, the Secretary's office tasked the Director for Defense Intelligence to explain him. Reid's answer is the origin of the Department's counter-narrative.

garry-reid.label: Elizondo complaint to the DoD Inspector General, May 2021
garry-reid.why: Named respondent; Reid removed from post by April 2022
garry-reid.note: Separate DoD IG investigations substantiated ethics and information-handling findings against Reid. Defense officials told The Debrief he 'played a central role in obfuscating information' about UAP.

lincoln-lapaz.label: Albuquerque, New Mexico
lincoln-lapaz.why: LaPaz investigated the green fireballs from the University of New Mexico
lincoln-lapaz.note: Lincoln LaPaz, the UNM meteoriticist retained by the Air Force, conducted the green fireball investigation from Albuquerque and attended the 16 February 1949 Los Alamos conference.

lincoln-lapaz.label: Los Alamos Green Fireballs Conference
lincoln-lapaz.why: Brought in by Kirtland intelligence officers; his assessment drove the conference
lincoln-lapaz.note: LaPaz concluded the fireballs did not behave like meteors despite superficially resembling them.

david-abba.label: AARO Memorandum for Record: Invitations to Interview Mr. David Grusch (FOIA 24-F-0266)
david-abba.why: SAPCO director's March 2023 memorandum cited as AARO's access authority
david-abba.note: Maj. Gen. David W. Abba, Director of the DoD Special Access Program Central Office, signed the memorandum AARO invoked in its invitations. SAPCO is the one office that could resolve the read-on denial and has never publicly addressed it.

pat-ryder.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
pat-ryder.why: Released and framed the report as 'the widest possible aperture'
pat-ryder.note: Ryder is the named officer who put the Department's presentation on the record. The framing claim is unfalsifiable without publication of the underlying interview list, which AARO has not released.

nathan-twining.label: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio
nathan-twining.why: Twining wrote the 1947 AMC assessment from this command
nathan-twining.note: Lt. Gen. Nathan Twining signed 'AMC Opinion Concerning Flying Discs' on 23 September 1947 as commander of Air Materiel Command, headquartered at Wright Field.

nathan-twining.label: Twining Memorandum: AMC Opinion Concerning "Flying Discs"
nathan-twining.note: Lt. Gen. Twining signed 'AMC Opinion Concerning Flying Discs' on 23 September 1947 as commander of Air Materiel Command. The document survives in scanned form and is quoted in the Condon Report.

nathan-twining.label: Air Force Regulation 200-2
nathan-twining.why: The 1954 regulation was issued under Twining as Chief of Staff
nathan-twining.note: The officer who wrote in 1947 that the phenomenon was real was Air Force Chief of Staff when the regulation restricting public discussion of unexplained cases was promulgated.

nathan-twining.label: Project MOGUL
nathan-twining.why: The AMC commander's 1947 assessment predates and undercuts the MOGUL account
nathan-twining.note: Twining wrote in September 1947 that the phenomenon was real while noting the lack of recovered exhibits; the Air Force's 1994 position requires that his own command's exploitation centre never connected the wave to a programme it was cleared for.

kenneth-arnold.label: Roswell Incident
kenneth-arnold.why: Arnold's 24 June 1947 sighting opened the wave that Roswell fell inside
kenneth-arnold.note: The Cascades sighting on 24 June 1947 triggered the national wave; the Roswell recovery followed within two weeks and the Twining memo eleven weeks later.

kenneth-arnold.label: Project Blue Book
kenneth-arnold.why: Arnold's case entered the official file series from the outset
kenneth-arnold.note: Army Air Forces intelligence investigated the sighting and the case documentation survives in the Blue Book record series now held at the National Archives.

edward-condon.label: University of Colorado UFO Project (Condon Committee)
edward-condon.why: Condon directed the study and wrote its conclusions personally
edward-condon.note: Condon authored the summary, conclusions and recommendations placed at the front of the report — the only section most readers and reporters ever saw.

edward-condon.label: Robert J. Low
edward-condon.why: Condon fired the investigators who surfaced Low's memo
edward-condon.note: David Saunders and Norman Levine found the memo in project files and it reached Look magazine in May 1968; both were dismissed.

gerald-ford.label: House Armed Services Committee UFO Hearing
gerald-ford.why: Ford forced the first congressional hearing on the subject
gerald-ford.note: The House Minority Leader wrote to committee chairmen in late March 1966; the House Armed Services Committee held its one-day hearing on 5 April 1966, nineteen years into official investigation.

carroll-bolender.label: Bolender Memorandum
carroll-bolender.note: Brig. Gen. Bolender, USAF Deputy Director of Development, signed the 20 October 1969 memorandum recommending Blue Book's closure and explaining why closure cost the Air Force nothing operationally.

paul-bennewitz.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
paul-bennewitz.why: AARO's 2024 historical review makes no mention of Bennewitz, Doty, AFOSI or Kirtland
paul-bennewitz.note: The best-documented instance of US government disinformation about UFOs directed at an American citizen is entirely absent from the government's own historical review of the subject.

paul-bennewitz.label: AFOSI Kirtland AFB UFO File (1980-1983)
paul-bennewitz.why: Bennewitz's reporting generated the AFOSI Kirtland file
paul-bennewitz.note: The 10 November 1980 AFOSI record documents Kirtland security police observations of unexplained objects over Coyote Canyon and notes Bennewitz's photography and reporting.

paul-bennewitz.label: Kirtland Air Force Base and Albuquerque, New Mexico
paul-bennewitz.why: Bennewitz's 1979-1980 observations were of the Manzano area of Kirtland AFB
paul-bennewitz.note: Bennewitz dated his personally funded study to July 1979, filmed lights and recorded signals over the base, contacted Kirtland on 24 October 1980 and briefed base officials on 10 November 1980. Attested by his own correspondence and contemporary press.

paul-bennewitz.label: Richard C. Doty
paul-bennewitz.why: Ran fabricated material at Bennewitz out of the same AFOSI office
paul-bennewitz.note: Doty has acknowledged on the record passing fabricated documents to Bennewitz while an AFOSI agent; Bennewitz's psychiatric collapse is the documented outcome. This is the field's baseline case for government-authored disinformation.

paul-bennewitz.label: William L. Moore
paul-bennewitz.why: Moore admitted in 1989 to feeding Bennewitz false information
paul-bennewitz.note: On 1 July 1989 William Moore stated publicly that he had attempted to push Bennewitz into a mental breakdown by feeding him false information about aliens.

paul-bennewitz.label: Thunder Scientific Corporation
paul-bennewitz.why: Bennewitz founded and ran Thunder Scientific, a USAF instrumentation vendor
paul-bennewitz.note: The company's location gave sightlines to the Manzano Weapons Storage Area at Kirtland; Bennewitz had the technical capability to record and characterise emissions.

richard-doty.label: Kirtland AFB / Manzano Weapons Storage Area incident
richard-doty.why: Filed the AFOSI complaint form documenting the incident
richard-doty.note: Complaint form dated 9 September 1980, District File No. 8017D93-0/29, 'alleged sighting of unidentified aerial lights in restricted test range'.

richard-doty.label: Air Force Office of Special Investigations
richard-doty.why: Doty served as an AFOSI special agent at the Kirtland detachment
richard-doty.note: The AFOSI Kirtland file and Doty's later New Mexico State Police personnel file, released in 321 pages, document his AFOSI service during the Manzano intrusion period.

richard-doty.label: Richard Doty New Mexico State Police Personnel File [321 pages]
richard-doty.why: 321-page New Mexico State Police personnel file released 2021
richard-doty.note: Obtained under NMSA 14-2-1 et seq. after federal channels produced nothing; state public-records law delivered what FOIA did not.

richard-doty.label: Kirtland Air Force Base and Albuquerque, New Mexico
richard-doty.why: Doty's AFOSI detachment ran the Bennewitz deception from Kirtland
richard-doty.note: Richard C. Doty, an AFOSI special agent at Kirtland, has said publicly he was tasked in the 1980s with hoaxing documents and feeding false information to UFO researchers including Bennewitz. A 1992 article held in the CIA library names Doty and William Moore.

richard-doty.label: Linda Moulton Howe
richard-doty.why: Doty showed Howe a purported classified briefing paper at Kirtland, April 1983
richard-doty.note: Howe's contemporaneous notes record being permitted to read but not copy a document describing retrieved craft and biological entities, with a promise of film footage that was never delivered.

richard-doty.label: Paul Frederick Bennewitz
richard-doty.why: Ran fabricated material at Bennewitz out of the same AFOSI office
richard-doty.note: Doty has acknowledged on the record passing fabricated documents to Bennewitz while an AFOSI agent; Bennewitz's psychiatric collapse is the documented outcome. This is the field's baseline case for government-authored disinformation.

richard-doty.label: William L. Moore
richard-doty.why: Moore admitted cooperating with AFOSI and passing disinformation to Bennewitz
richard-doty.note: Moore told the 1989 MUFON symposium that he had worked with Air Force counterintelligence in exchange for access, and had knowingly fed Bennewitz false material.

richard-doty.label: AFOSI Kirtland AFB UFO File (1980-1983)
richard-doty.why: Doty was the AFOSI special agent associated with the Kirtland UFO file
richard-doty.note: Doty served in AFOSI at Kirtland from 1979 and is the agent identified with the Kirtland UFO documents and with the subsequent contact with Bennewitz and Howe.

richard-doty.label: YANKEE BLUE (alleged AFOSI indoctrination program)
richard-doty.why: The Bennewitz method and the alleged YANKEE BLUE practice are the same technique at different scale
richard-doty.note: Doty's documented AFOSI activity - feeding fabricated alien-technology material to a target to protect classified programmes - is the same technique Yankee Blue applied internally to cleared personnel. The inference is about method, not about Doty's involvement in Yankee Blue.

thomas-wilson.label: The Wilson-Davis Notes (16 October 2002)
thomas-wilson.why: Wilson denies the meeting and the substance attributed to him
thomas-wilson.note: Wilson's denial is recorded as a primary artefact. It is irreconcilable with Davis's confirmation of authorship, and no agency has attempted to resolve it.

thomas-wilson.label: The Disclosure Project
thomas-wilson.why: The Wilson notes place Wilson's 1997 inquiry immediately after exposure to Greer's Washington briefings
thomas-wilson.note: The Disclosure Project briefed members of Congress and officials in Washington in April 1997; the notes record Wilson beginning his search for the programme in the same period.

robert-wood.label: McDonnell Douglas Corporation
robert-wood.why: Wood ran a company-funded study of unidentified craft at McDonnell Douglas Astronautics
robert-wood.note: Wood spent his career at the Huntington Beach astronautics organisation and has repeatedly described initiating an internal study on the reasoning that a prime could not afford to be last to know if the propulsion were real.

pete-hegseth.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
pete-hegseth.why: Releasing authority; signed transparency statement on the portal
pete-hegseth.note: Hegseth is the addressee of the presidential direction and the signatory of the statement published on the PURSUE portal.

pete-hegseth.label: Anna Paulina Luna
pete-hegseth.why: 1 April 2026 letter demanding AARO's UAP video holdings
pete-hegseth.note: Luna wrote to the Secretary of War for video files held by AARO after September 2025 witnesses told the Task Force AARO held additional records; the PURSUE releases followed within five weeks.

pete-hegseth.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
pete-hegseth.note: Hegseth, Louisville, 23 February 2026: 'We're going to be in full compliance with that executive order... there'll be more coming on that.' He set no timeline.

pete-hegseth.label: Anna Paulina Luna
pete-hegseth.why: 1 April 2026 letter demanding AARO's video holdings
pete-hegseth.note: Luna wrote to the Secretary of War seeking AARO's UAP video after the September 2025 testimony; the first PURSUE tranche with 29 sensor videos followed five weeks later.

pete-hegseth.label: Trump Truth Social post directing release of UAP files (20 February 2026)
pete-hegseth.note: Trump named Secretary of War Hegseth and 'other departments' as the recipients of the direction; Hegseth accepted it publicly three days later.

pete-hegseth.label: Presidential direction to identify and release UAP files (19-20 February 2026)
pete-hegseth.why: Named implementer; called it 'that executive order'
pete-hegseth.note: Hegseth told reporters on 25 February 2026 the department would be in full compliance with 'that executive order' and would coordinate with ODNI, while declining to give a schedule.

donald-trump.label: Executive Office of the President
donald-trump.why: Signed EO 14347 and issued the 2026 UAP release directives
donald-trump.note: EO 14347 is signed; the February 2026 UAP directives are attested by contemporary reporting and by the Department's subsequent PURSUE releases.

donald-trump.label: Presidential direction to identify and release UAP files (19-20 February 2026)
donald-trump.why: Issued the direction that created PURSUE
donald-trump.note: Trump's 19-20 February 2026 Truth Social post directing Hegseth and relevant agencies to begin identifying and releasing UAP files is the sole originating instrument for the release programme.

donald-trump.label: Presidential directive waiving UAP-related nondisclosure agreements
donald-trump.why: Directed the NDA waiver in July 2026
donald-trump.note: The administration directed DoW and the IC to waive UAP-related NDAs for former employees and contractors speaking with authorised investigators; officials stressed it is not a declassification directive.

tulsi-gabbard.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
tulsi-gabbard.why: ODNI coordinating authority for the release programme
tulsi-gabbard.note: Gabbard described the first release as an ongoing joint effort between intelligence and defence agencies; ODNI-numbered documents appear inside the war.gov series.

tim-phillips.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
tim-phillips.why: Deputy Director from Oct 2023; Acting Director Dec 2023 - Aug 2024
tim-phillips.note: Phillips came to AARO on assignment from ODNI and ran the office between Kirkpatrick and Kosloski.

tim-phillips.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
tim-phillips.why: fronted the Volume I rollout and media engagement
tim-phillips.note: Phillips conducted a private press briefing on 6 March 2024 and an on-record media engagement published by DoD on 8 March 2024.

kathleen-hicks.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
kathleen-hicks.why: took direct oversight; AARO director reports to her from summer 2023
kathleen-hicks.note: Weeks after Grusch testified, Hicks pulled AARO out of the USD(I&S) chain and made its director report directly to the Deputy Secretary of Defense.

kathleen-hicks.label: Memorandum: Establishment of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (15 July 2022)
kathleen-hicks.why: signatory of the AARO establishment memorandum
kathleen-hicks.note: Hicks signed the memorandum on 15 July 2022; DoD announced it on 20 July.

kathleen-hicks.label: Airborne Object Identification and Management Synchronization Group (AOIMSG)
kathleen-hicks.note: Hicks stood up AOIMSG as the Department's answer to the FY2022 NDAA Section 1683 requirement for a permanent office.

david-norquist.label: DoD Agency-Wide Financial Statement Audit (FY2018-present)
david-norquist.why: Signed the FY2018 report announcing the first full-scope audit and its disclaimer
david-norquist.note: Norquist, as USD(Comptroller)/CFO, wrote that 'In FY 2018, the Department underwent its first full-scope financial statement audit' and that the OIG 'issued a Disclaimer of Opinion'. Attested by his own signed message in the FY2018 Agency Financial Report.

david-norquist.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF)
david-norquist.why: approved establishment of the UAP Task Force
david-norquist.note: Norquist, as Deputy Secretary of Defense, formally approved the UAPTF on 4 August 2020; the Navy announced it on 14 August.

avril-haines.label: ODNI Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (25 June 2021)
avril-haines.why: DNI who transmitted the assessment to Congress
avril-haines.note: Haines was Director of National Intelligence when ODNI delivered the Preliminary Assessment on 25 June 2021.

avril-haines.label: YANKEE BLUE (alleged AFOSI indoctrination program)
avril-haines.why: DNI briefed that the practice affected 'hundreds and hundreds' of personnel over decades
avril-haines.note: Officials escalated the finding to the Director of National Intelligence, establishing that the deception was known at the top of the IC before any public account existed.

steve-feinberg.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
steve-feinberg.note: The Senate voted 59-40 on 14 March 2025 to confirm Stephen A. Feinberg as Deputy Secretary of Defense, the department's number-two official and the office that has historically signed the memoranda standing up DoD UAP bodies. No sourced UAP, AARO or PURSUE role for Feinberg personally was found.

william-b-adkins.label: Central Intelligence Agency
william-b-adkins.why: CIA officer detailed to NRO advanced systems
william-b-adkins.note: Per his NRO bio: 'From 1997 to 2000, Mr. Adkins worked for the Central Intelligence Agency and was assigned to the NRO in the Advanced Systems and Technology Directorate, where he managed several technology development projects.'

william-b-adkins.label: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
william-b-adkins.why: Staff Director, House Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee
william-b-adkins.note: From 2000 to 2006 Adkins served on the House Science Committee and was appointed Staff Director for the House Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee, leading legislative and oversight activity over NASA and other civilian space agencies.

william-b-adkins.label: National Reconnaissance Office
william-b-adkins.why: Principal Deputy Director, then Acting Director, NRO
william-b-adkins.note: NRO's official leadership page lists Adkins as 'Acting Director, NRO' and states he 'was appointed Principal Deputy Director, National Reconnaissance Office (PDDNRO), on 12 January 2026,' with 'overall day-to-day management of the NRO.'

william-b-adkins.label: United States House of Representatives
william-b-adkins.why: House Appropriations Defense subcommittee staff overseeing NRO/NSA/NGA
william-b-adkins.note: Before becoming PDDNRO he 'served on the professional staff of the House Appropriations Committee, Subcommittee on Defense, where he led the subcommittee's oversight and legislative responsibility for the NRO, U.S. Space Force, U.S. Space Command, National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, National Security Agency, and U.S. Cyber Command' - the panel that writes the classified defense appropriations annex.

brett-mansfield.label: DoD Agency-Wide Financial Statement Audit (FY2018-present)
brett-mansfield.why: Testified to the current figures on the congressional record
brett-mansfield.note: Deputy Inspector General Mansfield told the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform on 13 May 2026 that unsupported adjustments exceeded $859 billion in the last two quarters of FY2025. Attested by his published oral statement.

brett-mansfield.label: House Oversight hearing: 'DoW Financial Management: Examining Progress and New Audit Approaches' (13 May 2026)
brett-mansfield.note: Mansfield was the Office of Inspector General witness at 'DoW Financial Management: Examining Progress and New Audit Approaches'. Attested by the OIG's publication of his statement.

platte-moring.label: Office of Inspector General, Department of Defense / Department of War
platte-moring.note: The OIG leadership page identifies Platte B. Moring III as Inspector General of the Department of War. Attested by the office's own site.

michael-powers-comptroller.label: The Classified Annex (NDAA and Defense Appropriations)
michael-powers-comptroller.note: The Under Secretary (Comptroller)/CFO is the official responsible for execution of appropriated funds including those directed by the classified annex tables under section 8006(a). Reasoned inference from the office's statutory functions; no document names the incumbent in connection with the annex.

chuck-schumer.label: Jared Evan Moskowitz
chuck-schumer.why: Moskowitz read Schumer's disclosure language into the House record
chuck-schumer.note: 'The American public has a right to learn about technologies of unknown origins, nonhuman intelligence, and unexplainable phenomena.'

chuck-schumer.label: S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226 (Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act amendment)
chuck-schumer.note: Congress.gov lists Schumer as the sole sponsor of S.Amdt. 797, submitted 13 July 2023, with the text printed at 169 Cong. Rec. S2953.

chuck-schumer.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226; Division G of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA)
chuck-schumer.note: congress.gov lists Sen. Schumer as sponsor of S.Amdt.797, submitted 07/13/2023; the Congressional Record entry names him as the submitting senator.

chuck-schumer.label: Harry M. Reid
chuck-schumer.why: Schumer names Reid as the legacy he is continuing
chuck-schumer.note: Schumer publicly framed the UAPDA as inheriting from Reid, who had funded AAWSAP through leadership discretion rather than committee process.

chuck-schumer.label: P.L. 118-31 Subtitle C — Secs. 1841-1843 (what survived)
chuck-schumer.why: Publicly called the removal of the Review Board an outrage
chuck-schumer.note: Schumer said it was 'really an outrage the House didn't work with us on adopting our proposal for a review board' after the conference product removed it.

mike-rounds.label: S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226 (Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act amendment)
mike-rounds.note: Rounds is listed as an original cosponsor with sponsorship date 13 July 2023.

mike-rounds.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2024 (S.Amdt. 2610 to S. 4638)
mike-rounds.note: S.Amdt. 2610 was submitted 11 July 2024 by 'Mr. ROUNDS (for himself and Mr. Schumer)' with the full text and the eminent domain clause intact.

mike-rounds.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226; Division G of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA)
mike-rounds.note: First-listed cosponsor in the Congressional Record entry for SA 797.

mike-rounds.label: 2026 Disclosure Symposium
mike-rounds.why: Announces a fourth filing at an outside conference
mike-rounds.note: Nine days after SASC reported a bill with no UAP content, Rounds announced the next UAPDA attempt at the 2026 Disclosure Symposium rather than in committee.

marco-rubio.label: Senate Select Committee on Intelligence
marco-rubio.note: Rubio's Gang of Eight access is what makes his cosponsorship of the eminent domain text evidentially significant.

marco-rubio.label: S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226 (Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act amendment)
marco-rubio.why: Original cosponsor while serving as SSCI Vice Chairman
marco-rubio.note: Rubio cosponsored the eminent domain text while holding one of the eight most senior intelligence-access positions in Congress.

marco-rubio.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226; Division G of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA)
marco-rubio.note: Named in the Congressional Record entry for SA 797.

marco-rubio.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2024 (S.Amdt. 2610 to S. 4638)
marco-rubio.why: Absent from the 2024 refiling; left the Senate January 2025
marco-rubio.note: The 2024 amendment carries only Rounds and Schumer; Rubio, Gillibrand, Young and Heinrich are not on it, and Rubio left the Senate the following January.

marco-rubio.label: Comer-Luna letters to Rubio, Hegseth and Ratcliffe on UAP records, February 2025
marco-rubio.why: Addressed to the Secretary of State, who had publicly described UAP whistleblowers approaching Senate Intelligence
marco-rubio.note: Rubio was one of five Senate cosponsors of the UAP Disclosure Act before joining the executive branch.

jasmine-crockett.label: Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets

lauren-boebert.label: Immaculate Constellation 12-page report entered into the Congressional Record

clay-higgins.label: Immaculate Constellation 12-page report entered into the Congressional Record

andy-biggs.label: David Charles Grusch

andy-biggs.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF)

I think it is fair. I did actually help author that with the Director.' Biggs replied, 'Uh-oh. You got a bias then.'

andy-biggs.label: House Oversight hearing, 26 July 2023 - 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency'

maxwell-frost.label: National Aeronautics and Space Administration

maxwell-frost.label: Ryan Graves
maxwell-frost.why: questioned Graves on scientific advisory board and NASA reporting

maxwell-frost.label: House Oversight hearing, 26 July 2023 - 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency'
maxwell-frost.why: questioned witnesses at the 26 July 2023 UAP hearing
maxwell-frost.note: Frost used his round to question Ryan Graves and David Fravor on NASA's independent study team, stigma reduction and how Congress can 'facilitate partnerships between the scientific community and the UAP focus groups within government.'

jamie-raskin.label: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

thomas-monheim.label: Inspector General of the Intelligence Community

mike-turner.label: Daniel P. Sheehan

roger-wicker.label: FY2026 NDAA, Public Law 119-60 - secs. 1671-1673, NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept briefings and UAP classification-guide accounting

roger-wicker.note: P.L. 119-60 originated as S. 1071 and was enacted 18 December 2025 with a three-section housekeeping subtitle and no disclosure regime.

roger-wicker.label: Waived SAP Notification Group
roger-wicker.why: seat 1 of 12 - Chairman, Senate Armed Services
roger-wicker.note: Also held a 119(e)(2) seat as Ranking Member during the 118th Congress.

daniel-sheehan.label: Luis D. Elizondo

mitch-mcconnell.why: Named as supporting the effort against the Act

tom-delonge.label: To The Stars Academy of Arts & Science Inc. (later To The Stars Inc.)

jim-semivan.label: The Sol Foundation
jim-semivan.why: Continuity from TTSA into the successor policy institution

jim-semivan.label: To The Stars Academy of Arts & Science Inc. (later To The Stars Inc.)
jim-semivan.note: A retired CIA Senior Intelligence Service officer accepting a named directorship in an SEC-registered UFO company is a deliberate reputational commitment.

steve-justice.label: To The Stars Academy of Arts & Science Inc. (later To The Stars Inc.)
steve-justice.note: 31 years at Lockheed's Skunk Works, latterly Program Director for Advanced Systems, per the company's own filing.

steve-justice.label: ADAM Research Project (Acquisition and Data Analysis of Materials)
steve-justice.why: Justice, ex-Lockheed Skunk Works Advanced Systems director, fronted the acquisition

steve-justice.label: ADAM Research Project (Acquisition and Data Analysis of Materials)
steve-justice.why: Public technical voice: material 'not from any known existing military or commercial application'

christopher-sherwood.label: Luis D. Elizondo

christopher-sherwood.label: Susan Gough
christopher-sherwood.why: Repudiated Sherwood's acknowledgement as 'not entirely fact-based'
christopher-sherwood.note: The Department conceded Sherwood was accurately reported and then disowned what he said — while keeping his denial of Elizondo's role intact. One spokesman, two statements, one retained.

christopher-sherwood.label: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)
christopher-sherwood.why: 22 May 2019: AATIP 'did pursue research and investigation into unidentified aerial phenomena'

christopher-sherwood.label: 'Unidentified: Inside America's UFO Investigation' (History Channel)
christopher-sherwood.why: The series premiere prompted the 1 June 2019 Pentagon denial
christopher-sherwood.note: The Intercept tested the Department's position because the series presented Elizondo as having led AATIP for eight years. Media pressure produced the operative denial.

neill-tipton.label: Luis D. Elizondo
neill-tipton.why: 7 May 2019 internal email: 'no assigned responsibilities for this program'

neill-tipton.label: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence
neill-tipton.why: Director for Defense Intelligence (Collection & Special Programs); Elizondo's superior c.2010-2012

neill-tipton.label: Elizondo complaint to the DoD Inspector General, May 2021

neill-tipton.label: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)
neill-tipton.why: Sept 2017: Elizondo drafts a memo helping Tipton 'assume the new responsibilities for AATIP'
neill-tipton.note: Five years after the Department says the program ended, and by the account of the man who says Elizondo had nothing to do with it. This is the sharpest internal contradiction in the record.

thomas-crosson.label: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)
thomas-crosson.why: Confirmed the program existed and was shut down in 2012
thomas-crosson.note: The Department's original December 2017 position was acknowledgement with a budgetary rationale — 'other, higher priority issues that merit' the funding — not denial.

joseph-gradisher.label: DD Form 1910 for GoFast, Gimbal and FLIR video files
joseph-gradisher.why: 'Neither the cognizant Navy offices nor DOPSR have record' of a 2017 unrestricted-release request

joseph-gradisher.label: FLIR1, Gimbal and GoFast Navy gun-camera videos
joseph-gradisher.why: Navy designates the objects as unidentified aerial phenomena, 10 Sep 2019
joseph-gradisher.note: The single most consequential official concession of the period, made by a named service spokesman.

james-mattis.label: Garry P. Reid
james-mattis.why: Secretary's office put six questions to Reid about Elizondo, Dec 2017
james-mattis.note: Rather than engaging Elizondo, the Secretary's office tasked the Director for Defense Intelligence to explain him. Reid's answer is the origin of the Department's counter-narrative.

james-mattis.why: Memorandum saluted 'Mr. Secretary'; NYT reported it as addressed to Mattis

john-garrity.label: Elizondo Resignation Letter #1, 3 October 2017

kari-delonge.label: To The Stars Academy of Arts & Science Inc. (later To The Stars Inc.)

joseph-cannon.label: U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command, Ground Vehicle Systems Center

joseph-cannon.label: CRADA between U.S. Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center and To The Stars Academy
joseph-cannon.note: Named in the agreement alongside Bean Soave and quoted in the announcement calling TTSA 'an exciting, non-traditional source for novel materials'.

jeffery-langhout.label: Detroit Arsenal, Warren, Michigan
jeffery-langhout.note: The signature block is the documentary anchor: an executed federal instrument, not a press release.

jeffery-langhout.label: CRADA between U.S. Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center and To The Stars Academy
jeffery-langhout.why: Signed for the United States Army, 10 October 2019

john-greenewald.label: DoW OIG FOIA case DODIG-2021-000806 - the withheld UAP evaluation methodology
john-greenewald.note: The fourth interim release of five pages, with approximately 245 pages still pending, shows the Department withholding its own UAP evaluation methodology.

john-greenewald.label: OSD/JS FOIA Case 18-F-0324

matthew-szydagis.label: UAPx

matthew-szydagis.note: A liquid-xenon dark-matter physicist applying direct-detection discipline - background rates, instrumental artefacts, false positives - to open-air field observation.

matthew-szydagis.label: University at Albany (SUNY), Department of Physics
matthew-szydagis.why: Employs Szydagis; Associate Professor of Physics, with UAP listed as a departmental research interest
matthew-szydagis.note: The department's own faculty page for Szydagis lists his research interests as 'Experimental astroparticle physics, in particular direct detection of dark matter WIMPs (Weakly Interacting Massive Particles) and general detector development for rare event searches, neutron activation, and Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena'. That the phrase appears on a university department page, not a personal site, is the load-bearing fact: UAP is here a declared institutional research interest rather than a private hobby. Szydagis created the Noble Element Simulation Technique (NEST) in 2011 and works on LZ at the Sanford Underground Research Facility.

matthew-szydagis.label: Knuth et al. (2025), 'The New Science of Unidentified Aerospace-Undersea Phenomena (UAP)', Progress in Aerospace Sciences
matthew-szydagis.note: Named by the University as co-writer alongside Knuth and more than thirty other researchers.

matthew-szydagis.label: Cecilia Levy
matthew-szydagis.why: Snowball Chamber co-developers; the dark-matter group whose instrumentation was carried into the UAP field work
matthew-szydagis.note: Levy's faculty page lists 'Szydagis, Knight, Levy, The Snowball chamber: neutron induced nucleation in supercooled water' (arXiv:1807.09253, 2018) and describes the Snowball Chamber as 'a research topic completely unique to the UAlbany dark matter group'. The UAlbany release makes the methodological carry-over explicit: the C-TAP frame-differencing software is 'similar to an approach used by physicists like him and Levy to look for direct evidence of dark matter'. This is the mechanism by which rare-event detection practice reached UAP field work at this institution.

matthew-szydagis.label: UAP Science Advisory Council

matthew-szydagis.note: The government's outside science body took its detector expertise from a self-funded civil expedition group, UAPx, rather than from a national laboratory.

kevin-knuth.label: University at Albany (SUNY), Department of Physics
kevin-knuth.why: Employs Knuth; Professor of Physics since 2023, on the faculty since 2005
kevin-knuth.note: The UAlbany Department of Physics faculty page lists Knuth's appointments as Assistant Professor 2005-2009, Associate Professor 2009-2023, Professor 2023-present, immediately following four years as a GS-14 Research Scientist in the Intelligent Systems Division at NASA Ames (2001-2005). The same page records him as Editor-in-Chief of Entropy (MDPI) since 2012, which is the journal that published the 2019 Nimitz kinematics paper. This is the primary reason the institution is on the board: it is the salaried academic post from which the peer-reviewed UAP kinematics and field-instrumentation literature was produced.

kevin-knuth.label: Knuth et al. (2025), 'The New Science of Unidentified Aerospace-Undersea Phenomena (UAP)', Progress in Aerospace Sciences

kevin-knuth.label: Knuth, Powell & Reali (2019), Entropy 21(10):939

kevin-knuth.note: Entropy 21(10):939 estimated accelerations, velocities and required power from documented cases including the 2004 Nimitz encounter.

IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT: this pass found no evidence that Knuth holds an SCU board seat, officer post or executive role. robert-powell.label: Knuth, Powell & Reali (2019), Entropy 21(10):939

stephen-bruehl.label: Beatriz Villarroel

uyrange-hollanda.label: Operação Prato (Operation Saucer)

Flag for the audit: this pass found no support for any claim that the 2009 BAASS teams met Hollanda, and his 1997 death makes it impossible — Basterfield's account names only Ademar Gevaerd and Helio Loyola as the BAASS teams' Brazilian contacts.

Pratt was later able to secure brief summaries of 281 incidents in Colares and surrounding areas, plus maps, and twenty photographs.' Hollanda told him his team 'took about three hundred photos and we photographed eight different types of UFOs.' Tier 2: the interview and the 281 summaries are reported by a named researcher quoting Pratt's 1996 book, and the Pratt file at The Black Vault is the surviving public artefact of that chain.

pessoa-cavalcanti.label: Noite Oficial dos OVNIs - the Brazilian 'Night of the UFOs', 19 May 1986

george-miley.note: Entry 1 on both the KLAS list of July 2018 and the DIA letter of 9 January 2018: 'Inertial Electrostatics Confinement Fusion, Dr George Miley, Univ. of Illinois.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(5). Miley is co-author of the Springer monograph on IEC fusion, making him a documented subject-matter authority rather than a fringe recruit.

ulf-leonhardt.label: Invisibility Cloaking: Theory and Experiments
ulf-leonhardt.why: authored by Ulf Leonhardt, University of St Andrews
ulf-leonhardt.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Invisibility Cloaking, Dr Ulf Leonhardt, Univ of St Andrews.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Leonhardt had been publishing on transformation optics and cloaking since 2006 and was, by the ICOD of 1 December 2009, one of the small number of internationally recognised authorities in the field. George Knapp released a copy of the DIRD in February 2019.

bruce-towe.label: Biosensors and BioMEMS: A Survey of the Present Field
bruce-towe.note: Attribution rests on the DIA list of 38 AATIP products transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee on 9 January 2018, entry 6: 'Biosensors and BioMEMS, Dr Bruce Towe, Univ of Arizona.' The released PDF's own author block is redacted under FOIA exemption (b)(5), so the DIA list is the sole authority for authorship. Towe also wrote the 'Biomaterials' DIRD (entry 17).

robert-baker.label: High-Frequency Gravitational Wave Communications
robert-baker.why: authored by Robert M. L. Baker Jr., GravWave LLC
robert-baker.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records entry 9 as 'High Frequency Gravitational Wave Communications, Dr Robert Baker, GravWave' - the earlier KLAS transcription rendered the title as 'Gravity Wave Communication'. The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Baker confirmed to researcher Keith Basterfield that he published three related HFGW papers in 2010.

marc-millis.label: Cockpits in the Era of Breakthrough Flight
marc-millis.why: authored by Marc G. Millis, Tau Zero Foundation
marc-millis.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Cockpits in the Era of breakthrough Flight, Dr G Millis, Tau Zero'. The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Identification with Marc G. Millis, founder of the Tau Zero Foundation and former head of NASA's Breakthrough Propulsion Physics project, is supported by the Tau Zero affiliation on the DIA list, by the open-source counterpart published as 'M G Millis' in JBIS in 2013, and by The War Zone's identification of Marc Millis among the AATIP authors.

richard-genik.label: Wayne State University
richard-genik.why: director, Emergent Technology Research Division; assistant professor of psychiatry and behavioral neurosciences
richard-genik.note: Wayne State University School of Medicine identifies Genik as director of its Emergent Technology Research Division and an assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neurosciences. Wayne State is the affiliation DIA recorded for him on the congressional list. The dateStart is the date of the university announcement establishing the role, not necessarily the start of his tenure.

richard-genik.label: Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft
richard-genik.why: authored by Richard J. Genik II
richard-genik.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft, Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Genik wrote three of the 38 DIRDs, the largest single-author block after Eric Davis's five.

richard-genik.label: Quantum Computing and Utilizing Organic Molecules in Automation Technology
richard-genik.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Quantum Computing and Utilizing Organic Molecules in Automation Technology' to 'Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ'. Genik is credited elsewhere on the same list with the brain-machine interface deliverable on controlling external devices without limb-operated interfaces, making him a multi-product AAWSAP contributor.

richard-genik.label: Technological Approaches to Controlling External Devices in the Absence of Limb-Operated Interfaces
richard-genik.why: author of record on the DIA list
richard-genik.note: DIA list item 20: "Technological Applications to Controlling External Devices in the Absence of Limb-Operated Interfaces, Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ." The KLAS-TV list of July 2018 gives the same document the plainer title "Brain-Machine Interfaces."

richard-genik.label: Christopher C. 'Kit' Green
richard-genik.why: co-affiliated AAWSAP authors at Wayne State University
richard-genik.note: The DIA congressional list records Wayne State University as the affiliation for both Genik's deliverables and for Kit Green's human biological tissue field-effects deliverable. This establishes a documented shared institutional affiliation on the same contract, not a documented working relationship — no primary source describing collaboration between them has been located, and the edge should not be read as one.

george-hathaway.label: Maverick Inventor Versus Corporate Inventor: Where Will the Next Major Innovations Arise?
george-hathaway.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Maverick Inventor Versus Corporate Inventor: Where Will the Next Major Innovations Arise?' to 'Dr George Hathaway, Hathaway Consulting'. Hathaway is also credited on the same list with 'Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research'. The author line on the released PDF is redacted under (b)(6).

george-hathaway.label: The Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research
george-hathaway.why: author of record on the DIA list
george-hathaway.note: DIA list item 10: "Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research, Dr George Hathaway, Hathaway Consulting." This is the attribution most likely to be got wrong from the title alone: the paper reviews the Podkletnov and Ning Li gravity-modification claims but was not written by either of them or by any academic advocate of the effect. It was written by the Toronto engineer who had run the Podkletnov replication and reported null results.

sergey-macheret.label: MHD Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications
sergey-macheret.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications' to 'Dr S Macheret, Lockheed Martin'. Macheret is a plasma physicist (Ph.D., Kurchatov Institute) with a substantial peer-reviewed record in MHD flow control, and this DIRD is among the most conventionally grounded on the list.

sergey-macheret.label: Lockheed Martin Corporation
sergey-macheret.why: senior staff engineer, Lockheed Martin Aeronautics (Skunk Works)
sergey-macheret.note: Macheret held a senior staff engineer post at Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Company, Skunk Works, from 2006 to 2014, working on advanced aerospace plasma applications, before joining Purdue University as professor of aeronautics and astronautics in 2014. Lockheed Martin is the affiliation DIA recorded for him on the congressional list.

gerald-smith.label: Positron Aerospace Propulsion
gerald-smith.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Positron Aerospace Propulsion' to 'Dr Gerald Smith, Positronics Research'. Smith is a Yale physics Ph.D., former Penn State physics department head, and developer of the Mark I portable antiproton trap for NASA JPL and the High Performance Antimatter Trap for NASA Marshall; the DIRD subject matter tracks his own NASA Institute for Advanced Concepts study on positron-propelled vehicles.

james-wells.label: Pulsed High-Power Microwave Source Technology
james-wells.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Pulsed High-Power Microwave Technology' to 'Dr James Wells, J W Enterprises'. The earlier Knapp/KLAS-TV roster gives the same author with the affiliation Northrop Grumman; the DIA list governs. No verified biography for this author has been located beyond the list entry.

paul-czysz.label: Space Access: Where We've Been and Where We Could Go
paul-czysz.why: author of record on the DIA list
paul-czysz.note: The DIA letter of 9 January 2018 to the Senate Armed Services Committee lists item 4 as "Space Access, Dr P Czysz, HyperTech." The released document's own author line is redacted under FOIA exemption (b)(6), so the attribution rests entirely on the government list, not on the document.

john-cramer.label: The Space-Communication Implications of Quantum Entanglement and Nonlocality
john-cramer.why: author of record on the DIA list
john-cramer.note: DIA list item 25: "Space_Communication Implications of Quantum Entanglement and Nonlocality, Dr J Cramer, Univ of Washington." A mainstream university physicist, not a programme insider.

richard-obousy.label: Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions
richard-obousy.why: author of record on the DIA list; lead author
richard-obousy.note: CORRECTION EDGE. The DIA letter of 9 January 2018, item 19, names "Dr R Obousy, Obousy Consultants" as the author of the warp-drive DIRD. Press coverage almost universally attributes this paper to Eric Davis. EarthTech's own citation gives it as Obousy, R. K. and Davis, E. W. (2010), with Obousy first named, so the two records reconcile as a co-authored paper on which DIA recorded the lead author.

john-albertine.label: State of the Art and Evolution of High-Energy Laser Weapons
john-albertine.why: author of record on the DIA list, both versions
john-albertine.note: The DIA letter lists this paper twice, items 37 and 38, both credited to J Albertine of Directed Technologies: one formerly classified SECRET//NOFORN, one unclassified. The board node is labelled with the initial because no source consulted confirms the given name; the probable identification with John R. Albertine of the Navy High Energy Laser Program Office is carried as a tier-3 claim on the person node.

j-golightly.label: Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices for Commercial and Military Applications
j-golightly.why: author of record on the DIA list
j-golightly.note: DIA list item 35: "Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices, Dr J Golightly, Lockheed Martin." The given name behind the initial was not established by any source consulted, and the node is labelled accordingly rather than guessed.

aatip.label: Harry M. Reid

aatip.label: Harold E. Puthoff

aatip.label: Thomas Crosson

aatip.label: Luis D. Elizondo
aatip.why: Ran the program from c.2010 to 2017 (asserted); role denied by DoD

aatip.label: Neill Tipton

baass.label: Operação Prato (Operation Saucer)
baass.why: BAASS sent teams to Brazil in 2009 and reported on Colares to its DIA sponsor
baass.note: Basterfield and Cecotti's reporting has BAASS sending team members to Brazil in May 2009 and again in October 2009. The AAWSAP product list in 'Skinwalkers at the Pentagon' includes the BAASS March 2009 monthly report 'The UFO Assault on Brazil with its Epicenter at Colares (1977-2003) by John Schuessler', the August 2009 monthly report 'Relations with South American organizations', and a July 2009 report 'Project Colares/Brazil, Outreach to South America'. Brazilian researcher A.J. Gevaerd, who met the team in Curitiba, said 'They wanted artifacts from UFOs, such as metamaterials'; Fortaleza researcher Helio Loyola said 'Here in Brazil they didn't do any research. They took and photographed what the ufologists saw and documented.' Tier 2: book and named-researcher sourcing, no BAASS document obtained. Note the collection direction — the US contractor collected from Brazilian civilians, not from the FAB or the Arquivo Nacional.

baass.label: William Culbreth
baass.why: UNLV academic in the prime contractor's home city

AAWSAP was executed by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies out of Las Vegas under DIA contract HHM402-08-C-0072, and BAASS subcontracted subject-matter experts to write the DIRDs. Culbreth was the University of Nevada, Las Vegas nuclear engineering faculty member who received two deliverables. No document in the public record states that BAASS specifically recruited him, and this edge should not be read as one.
