dird-aneutronic-fusion-propulsion-2.note: TIER 2 AND DELIBERATELY SO. Cover author field is redacted under (b)(6) and reads "Authors" plural, so there may have been co-authors. Assigned to Teofilo because endnote 17 cites "G. Miley, H. Momota, L. Wu, M. Reilley, V. Teofilo, R. Dell, and R. Hargus, Space Probe Application of IEC Thrusters, Fusion Science and Technology 56 1, 533-539, July 2009" - the only occurrence of either candidate author's surname in either aneutronic document - immediately adjacent to a citation of AeroJet/Lockheed Martin Space Systems Hall thruster hardware that also appears in the body text. Paired with the Culbreth edge; if reversed, swap both.

dird-anomalous-acute-and-subacute-field-.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-anomalous-acute-and-subacute-field-.why: published and holds; document number not recoverable
dird-anomalous-acute-and-subacute-field-.note: Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Acquisition Threat Support series, 11 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009. No DIA document number is legible in the released scan; left unrecorded rather than inferred.

dird-anomalous-acute-and-subacute-field-.label: Wayne State University
dird-anomalous-acute-and-subacute-field-.note: The DIA list gives Green's affiliation of record for this deliverable as Wayne State University. Wayne State is second only to EarthTech on the DIRD author list, supplying Green plus R. Genik's three human-interface papers.

dird-anomalous-acute-and-subacute-field-.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-anomalous-acute-and-subacute-field-.note: Inside cover names the DIA Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program, FY 2009 series, Acquisition Threat Support.

dird-anomalous-acute-and-subacute-field-.label: Christopher C. 'Kit' Green
dird-anomalous-acute-and-subacute-field-.note: DIA list item 12 names "Dr Kit Green, Wayne State Univ", under the shorter title "Field Effects on Biological Tissues". The released document's printed title is longer and more specific.

dird-antigravity-for-aerospace-applicati.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-antigravity-for-aerospace-applicati.note: Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Acquisition Threat Support series, DIA-08-1003-018, ICOD 1 December 2009, originating with the Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3) of the Defense Warning Office, Directorate for Analysis.

dird-antigravity-for-aerospace-applicati.label: EarthTech International / Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
dird-antigravity-for-aerospace-applicati.note: EarthTech International supplied six of the 38 DIRDs through Eric Davis plus one through Hal Puthoff, making it the single most represented institution on the author list.

dird-antigravity-for-aerospace-applicati.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-antigravity-for-aerospace-applicati.note: Inside cover names the DIA Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program, FY 2009 series.

dird-antigravity-for-aerospace-applicati.label: Eric W. Davis
dird-antigravity-for-aerospace-applicati.note: DIA list item 11 names "Dr Eric Davis, EarthTech International". Independently confirmed by EarthTech International's own publication list, which cites the document as Davis, E. W. (2010) with document number DIA-08-1003-018 and originating office Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3), Defense Warning Office.

dird-biosensors-and-biomems-a-survey-of.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-biosensors-and-biomems-a-survey-of.note: The document's own administrative note states it 'is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency ... Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program', with comments directed to the AAWSA Program Manager, DIA, Bldg 6000, Washington DC 20340-5100. Hal Puthoff, subcontracting to BAASS through EarthTech International, has stated he let the 38 contracts himself, acting as a surrogate so DIA would not have to expose its interest.

dird-biosensors-and-biomems-a-survey-of.label: Bruce C. Towe
dird-biosensors-and-biomems-a-survey-of.note: Attribution rests on the DIA list of 38 AATIP products transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee on 9 January 2018, entry 6: 'Biosensors and BioMEMS, Dr Bruce Towe, Univ of Arizona.' The released PDF's own author block is redacted under FOIA exemption (b)(5), so the DIA list is the sole authority for authorship. Towe also wrote the 'Biomaterials' DIRD (entry 17).

dird-biosensors-and-biomems-a-survey-of.label: Biology & Non-Human Biologics
dird-biosensors-and-biomems-a-survey-of.why: subject domain: implantable biosensors and neuro-interface
dird-biosensors-and-biomems-a-survey-of.note: The contents cover brain-implanted BioMEMS micromachine neuroelectrodes, implantable sensors, microelectrode array fabrication, brain-machine interfaces, polymer BioMEMS electrodes, retinal devices and microscale therapeutic neurostimulation. This is the human-effects and human-interface leg of the AAWSAP survey, alongside Kit Green's field-effects paper and Richard Genik's three neuro deliverables.

dird-cockpits-in-the-era-of-breakthrough.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-cockpits-in-the-era-of-breakthrough.why: commissioned under AAWSAP, published in the 'Defense Futures' series
dird-cockpits-in-the-era-of-breakthrough.note: The cover carries DIA-08-1011-002, 1 November 2010, ICOD 8 July 2010, under the 'Defense Futures' banner. The administrative note confirms the product is one of a series produced in FY 2009 under the DIA Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program. The shift from 'Acquisition Threat Support' to 'Defense Futures' across the later 2010 deliverables marks a change in the DIA office of record, from the Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3) to the Technology Warning Division (DWO-4) of the Defense Warning Office.

dird-cockpits-in-the-era-of-breakthrough.label: Aerospace Engineering & Advanced Projects
dird-cockpits-in-the-era-of-breakthrough.why: subject domain: crew-station design for breakthrough flight regimes
dird-cockpits-in-the-era-of-breakthrough.note: The paper asks what a cockpit must look like once a vehicle has inertial control, a hover-to-superluminal speed range and no separation between near-ground, orbital and interstellar operating regimes, including the loss of the pilot's own inertia and visual motion cues. It is the only DIRD that reasons from observed flight behaviour back to onboard design constraints rather than to physics.

dird-cockpits-in-the-era-of-breakthrough.label: Marc G. Millis
dird-cockpits-in-the-era-of-breakthrough.why: authored by Marc G. Millis, Tau Zero Foundation
dird-cockpits-in-the-era-of-breakthrough.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Cockpits in the Era of breakthrough Flight, Dr G Millis, Tau Zero'. The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Identification with Marc G. Millis, founder of the Tau Zero Foundation and former head of NASA's Breakthrough Propulsion Physics project, is supported by the Tau Zero affiliation on the DIA list, by the open-source counterpart published as 'M G Millis' in JBIS in 2013, and by The War Zone's identification of Marc Millis among the AATIP authors.

dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.label: Wayne State University
dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.why: author's institution at time of writing
dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.note: Genik was director of the Emergent Technology Research Division and assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neurosciences at the Wayne State University School of Medicine. Wayne State supplied four of the 38 DIRDs across two authors - Genik's three plus Kit Green's 'Field Effects on Biological Tissues' - the second-largest institutional concentration after EarthTech International's six.

dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.why: commissioned under AAWSAP; latest document number in the released set
dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.note: DIA-08-1101-001, published 15 December 2010 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 8 September 2010, in the 'Defense Futures' series. The 1101 block places it at the end of the AAWSAP deliverable sequence, consistent with Puthoff's account of letting the 38 contracts over a two-year period from 2008.

dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.label: Biology & Non-Human Biologics
dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.why: subject domain: cognitive load limits on multi-vehicle control
dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.note: The commissioned question is how many unmanned vehicles a single human operator can control simultaneously - the human-factors constraint that would bound any swarming or multi-object control architecture. It forms a set with Genik's other two deliverables on limb-free control of external devices and on organic-molecule automation.

dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.label: Richard J. Genik II
dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.why: authored by Richard J. Genik II
dird-cognitive-limits-on-simultaneous-co.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft, Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Genik wrote three of the 38 DIRDs, the largest single-author block after Eric Davis's five.

dird-concepts-for-extracting-energy-from.label: EarthTech International / Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
dird-concepts-for-extracting-energy-from.note: EarthTech, run by Hal Puthoff, was the largest single source of DIRDs, producing six of the 38. Puthoff has stated that BAASS 'connected me at EarthTech International to collaborate as a subcontractor' and that he then let the 38 contracts himself. The arrangement means EarthTech occupied both sides of the transaction on this document: commissioning agent and author's employer.

dird-concepts-for-extracting-energy-from.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-concepts-for-extracting-energy-from.why: commissioned under AAWSAP; Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3), Defense Warning Office
dird-concepts-for-extracting-energy-from.note: EarthTech's citation gives the full DIA provenance: 'Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Acquisition Threat Support, DIA-08-1004-007, Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3), Defense Warning Office, Directorate for Analysis, Defense Intelligence Agency, Washington, DC.' This is the clearest public statement of which DIA office of record owned the AAWSAP deliverable series.

dird-concepts-for-extracting-energy-from.label: Exotic Technology & Physics
dird-concepts-for-extracting-energy-from.note: Davis and Puthoff had published the same argument in the open literature the year before as Chapter 18, 'On Extracting Energy from the Quantum Vacuum', in 'Frontiers of Propulsion Science' (AIAA, 2009), the volume Davis co-edited with Marc G. Millis - who wrote the 'Cockpits' DIRD. The AAWSAP author network is largely a pre-existing publishing network.

dird-concepts-for-extracting-energy-from.label: Eric W. Davis
dird-concepts-for-extracting-energy-from.note: Doubly sourced. The DIA list of 9 January 2018 gives entry 14 as 'Concepts for Extracting Energy from the Quantum Vacuum, Dr Eric Davis, EarthTech International'. EarthTech's own bibliography for Davis cites the same document with the matching DIA number DIA-08-1004-007, confirming the attribution against the redacted cover page independently of the DIA list.

dird-detection-and-high-resolution-track.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-detection-and-high-resolution-track.note: DIA-08-1012-001, published 20 November 2010 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 30 August 2010. Puthoff described the DIA Broad Area Announcement as naming twelve threat areas including 'lift, propulsion, signature reduction, human effects and so on'; this deliverable answers the detection-and-tracking side of that brief.

dird-detection-and-high-resolution-track.label: Signals & Sensor Intelligence
dird-detection-and-high-resolution-track.why: subject domain: sensing and tracking at hypersonic velocity
dird-detection-and-high-resolution-track.note: The sensor-side counterpart to Leonhardt's cloaking DIRD: one asks how an object could be made undetectable, the other how an object moving at hypersonic velocity could nevertheless be tracked at high resolution. Together they bracket the observability problem that any UAP sensor programme has to solve.

dird-detection-and-high-resolution-track.label: William Culbreth
dird-detection-and-high-resolution-track.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Detection and High Resolution Tracking of Vehicles at Hypersonic Velocities, Dr W Culbreth, Univ of Nevada-Las Vegas.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Culbreth also wrote 'Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion II'. He is among the few DIRD authors to have discussed the work publicly, in a 2019 interview with George Knapp.

dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.label: JASON
dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.why: JASON found the underlying physics wrong two years before DIA published the DIRD
dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.note: In 2008 JASON reviewed separate HFGW work Baker had done for the Office of the Director of National Intelligence and rejected it at the root: 'The proposed applications of the science of HFGW are fundamentally wrong,' and 'No foreign threat in HFGW is credible.' DIA published Baker's HFGW paper as an official Defense Intelligence Reference Document on 6 April 2010 regardless. This is the sharpest available evidence of AAWSAP's quality-control failure: the programme placed on a JWICS-hosted DIA reference series a topic the government's own senior scientific review body had already assessed as wrong and whose threat premise it had declared not credible. It is also the only case in the 38 where an external government review directly contradicts a published deliverable.

dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.why: DIA money spent on HFGW after JASON's rejection
dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.note: DIA-08-1004-005, published 6 April 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 'Acquisition Threat Support' series. DIA spent approximately $22 million on the programme between 2008 and 2012 across 38 reports. The HFGW commission is the clearest instance where that spending went to a line of work already adjudicated against by JASON, and it bears on how much weight any of the other 37 deliverables should carry.

dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.label: Signals & Sensor Intelligence
dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.why: subject domain: gravitational-wave communications and surveillance
dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.note: Baker's open-source 2010 counterpart claims theoretical aerospace, military and civilian applications in 'communications, surveillance, remote initiation of nuclear events and propulsion, including moving space objects and missiles in flight and frustrating anti-missile and anti-satellite systems.' The breadth of that claim is precisely what JASON's 'no foreign threat in HFGW is credible' was rejecting.

dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.label: Robert M. L. Baker, Jr.
dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.why: authored by Robert M. L. Baker Jr., GravWave LLC
dird-high-frequency-gravitational-wave-c.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records entry 9 as 'High Frequency Gravitational Wave Communications, Dr Robert Baker, GravWave' - the earlier KLAS transcription rendered the title as 'Gravity Wave Communication'. The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Baker confirmed to researcher Keith Basterfield that he published three related HFGW papers in 2010.

dird-inertial-electrostatic-confinement-.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-inertial-electrostatic-confinement-.why: commissioned under AAWSAP as a compact energy source study
dird-inertial-electrostatic-confinement-.note: DIA-08-1003-006, published 10 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 'Acquisition Threat Support' series; 72 pages, the longest document in DIA's 1,473-page release. Puthoff named 'IEC fusion as a compact energy source' among the studies he commissioned when describing the 38 contracts at the Society for Scientific Exploration in June 2018.

dird-inertial-electrostatic-confinement-.label: Plasma Physics & Atmospheric Electricity
dird-inertial-electrostatic-confinement-.why: subject domain: compact non-tokamak fusion power
dird-inertial-electrostatic-confinement-.note: IEC is one of the few AAWSAP topics with a plausible conventional aerospace reading: a compact fusion device is what a small craft would need if it were producing the observed energy budget. The DIRD set contains four fusion-adjacent deliverables in total - Miley's IEC paper, Winterberg's advanced nuclear propulsion, Teofilo's aneutronic fusion propulsion for Lockheed Martin, and Culbreth's aneutronic fusion propulsion II.

dird-inertial-electrostatic-confinement-.label: George H. Miley
dird-inertial-electrostatic-confinement-.why: authored by George H. Miley, University of Illinois
dird-inertial-electrostatic-confinement-.note: Entry 1 on both the KLAS list of July 2018 and the DIA letter of 9 January 2018: 'Inertial Electrostatics Confinement Fusion, Dr George Miley, Univ. of Illinois.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(5). Miley is co-author of the Springer monograph on IEC fusion, making him a documented subject-matter authority rather than a fringe recruit.

dird-invisibility-cloaking-theory-and-ex.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-invisibility-cloaking-theory-and-ex.why: commissioned under AAWSAP; lowest DIA document number in the released set
dird-invisibility-cloaking-theory-and-ex.note: DIA-08-1003-001, published 2 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009 - the first document out of the FY2009 'Acquisition Threat Support' pipeline. Puthoff explicitly named 'invisibility cloaking' among the papers he commissioned in his June 2018 account of letting the 38 contracts.

dird-invisibility-cloaking-theory-and-ex.label: Materials and custody analysis
dird-invisibility-cloaking-theory-and-ex.why: subject domain: transformation optics, metamaterials and signature reduction
dird-invisibility-cloaking-theory-and-ex.note: Contents run Camouflage, Transparency, Cloaking. The paper is the signature-reduction leg of the survey, sitting alongside Shvets's 'Metamaterials for Aerospace Applications' and against Culbreth's hypersonic detection paper. Puthoff listed signature reduction among the twelve threat areas DIA specified in the Broad Area Announcement.

dird-invisibility-cloaking-theory-and-ex.label: Ulf Leonhardt
dird-invisibility-cloaking-theory-and-ex.why: authored by Ulf Leonhardt, University of St Andrews
dird-invisibility-cloaking-theory-and-ex.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Invisibility Cloaking, Dr Ulf Leonhardt, Univ of St Andrews.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Leonhardt had been publishing on transformation optics and cloaking since 2006 and was, by the ICOD of 1 December 2009, one of the small number of internationally recognised authorities in the field. George Knapp released a copy of the DIRD in February 2019.

dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.why: published, numbered and released by DIA as DIA-08-1011-001
dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.note: DIA assigned document number DIA-08-1011-001, published it 1 November 2010 in the 'Defense Futures' series with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 30 August 2010, marked it UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY, and later released it in redacted form under FOIA.

dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.label: EarthTech International / Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.why: author's institutional affiliation at time of writing
dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.note: EarthTech International of Austin, Texas is the affiliation recorded against this title on the DIA congressional list. EarthTech is the single largest institutional source on the list; Puthoff and Davis between them are primary authors on six of the 38 products.

dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.why: produced under the AAWSA/AAWSAP contract, FY 2010
dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.note: The document's own administrative note states it is 'one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2010 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program', and directs comments to the AAWSA Program Manager at DIA, Bldg 6000, Washington DC 20340-5100.

dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.label: Eric W. Davis
dird-laser-lightcraft-nanosatellites.note: The DIA list of all 38 AATIP/AAWSAP products, transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee in January 2018 and released under FOIA in January 2019, credits 'Laser Lightcraft Nanosatellites' to 'Dr E Davis, EarthTech'. The author line on the released PDF cover page is redacted, so this attribution rests on the congressional list rather than the document.

dird-maverick-inventor-versus-corporate-.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-maverick-inventor-versus-corporate-.why: produced under the AAWSA/AAWSAP contract, FY 2009
dird-maverick-inventor-versus-corporate-.note: The document's administrative note states it is 'one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program'. Issued as DIA-08-1003-017 on 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009. It is not a physics paper: it is a research-culture argument about whether breakthrough invention originates with lone inventors or corporate laboratories, which is the clearest single illustration of how loosely the DIRD mandate was drawn in practice.

dird-maverick-inventor-versus-corporate-.label: George D. Hathaway
dird-maverick-inventor-versus-corporate-.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Maverick Inventor Versus Corporate Inventor: Where Will the Next Major Innovations Arise?' to 'Dr George Hathaway, Hathaway Consulting'. Hathaway is also credited on the same list with 'Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research'. The author line on the released PDF is redacted under (b)(6).

dird-maverick-inventor-versus-corporate-.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
dird-maverick-inventor-versus-corporate-.why: commissioned via the BAASS prime contract
dird-maverick-inventor-versus-corporate-.note: Hathaway Consulting was a one-man Toronto engineering consultancy with no independent DIA relationship; its deliverable reached DIA through the AAWSAP prime contract held by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies. Tier 2 because the contractor name is redacted on the cover page under (b)(3):10 USC 424 and the subcontract has not been released. Reporting has separately characterised Hathaway as having ties to Bigelow's fringe and paranormal research interests, but no primary document establishing an employment or advisory relationship has been located.

dird-mhd-air-breathing-propulsion-and-po.label: Lockheed Martin Corporation
dird-mhd-air-breathing-propulsion-and-po.why: author's employer at time of writing (Skunk Works)
dird-mhd-air-breathing-propulsion-and-po.note: Lockheed Martin is the affiliation recorded on the DIA congressional list. Macheret was a senior staff engineer at Lockheed Martin Aeronautics, Skunk Works, from 2006 to 2014, bracketing the document's ICOD and publication date. Lockheed Martin is credited with three of the 38 products on the DIA list.

dird-mhd-air-breathing-propulsion-and-po.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-mhd-air-breathing-propulsion-and-po.note: Issued as DIA-08-1011-006 on 21 November 2010, ICOD 20 July 2010, in the DIRD 'Defense Futures' series. Its subject — MHD control of ionised flow around a hypersonic air-breathing vehicle, referencing Soviet Ajax/Ayaks work — sits directly within the stated AAWSAP purpose of assessing foreign advanced aerospace weapon threats out to forty years.

dird-mhd-air-breathing-propulsion-and-po.label: Sergey O. Macheret
dird-mhd-air-breathing-propulsion-and-po.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications' to 'Dr S Macheret, Lockheed Martin'. Macheret is a plasma physicist (Ph.D., Kurchatov Institute) with a substantial peer-reviewed record in MHD flow control, and this DIRD is among the most conventionally grounded on the list.

dird-negative-mass-propulsion.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-negative-mass-propulsion.why: published, numbered and released by DIA as DIA-08-1101-023
dird-negative-mass-propulsion.note: DIA numbered, published and marked the document UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY, and subsequently released it in redacted form to its FOIA Electronic Reading Room, where it is held as FileId 170039.

dird-negative-mass-propulsion.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-negative-mass-propulsion.why: produced under the AAWSA/AAWSAP contract, FY 2010
dird-negative-mass-propulsion.note: The document's administrative note states it is 'one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2010 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program'. Issued as DIA-08-1101-023 on 3 January 2011, ICOD 30 August 2010.

dird-negative-mass-propulsion.label: Friedwardt Winterberg
dird-negative-mass-propulsion.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Negative Mass Propulsion' to 'Dr F Winterberg, Univ of Nevada-Reno'. Winterberg is also credited on the same list with 'Advanced Nuclear Propulsion for Manned Deep Space Missions', and published related negative-mass propulsion work in the Journal of the British Interplanetary Society in 2011.

dird-negative-mass-propulsion.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
dird-negative-mass-propulsion.why: commissioned via the BAASS prime contract
dird-negative-mass-propulsion.note: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies held the DIA contract under which the DIRDs were produced and subcontracted the individual authors; the DIA cover letter to SASC describes the list as 'all products produced under the AATIP contract'. Tier 2 rather than tier 1 because the contractor name is redacted under (b)(3):10 USC 424 on the DIRD cover page itself, so the subcontracting chain for this specific paper is inferred from the programme structure rather than read off the document.

dird-positron-aerospace-propulsion.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-positron-aerospace-propulsion.note: Issued as DIA-08-1003-002 on 2 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, in the DIRD 'Acquisition Threat Support' series — the earlier of the two series labels used across the AAWSAP deliverable set, the later being 'Defense Futures'.

dird-positron-aerospace-propulsion.label: Gerald A. Smith
dird-positron-aerospace-propulsion.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Positron Aerospace Propulsion' to 'Dr Gerald Smith, Positronics Research'. Smith is a Yale physics Ph.D., former Penn State physics department head, and developer of the Mark I portable antiproton trap for NASA JPL and the High Performance Antimatter Trap for NASA Marshall; the DIRD subject matter tracks his own NASA Institute for Advanced Concepts study on positron-propelled vehicles.

dird-positron-aerospace-propulsion.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
dird-positron-aerospace-propulsion.why: commissioned via the BAASS prime contract
dird-positron-aerospace-propulsion.note: Positronics Research LLC was an outside small business with no standing DIA relationship; its deliverable reached DIA through the AAWSAP prime contract held by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies. Tier 2 because the contractor name is redacted on the cover page under (b)(3):10 USC 424 and the subcontract itself has not been released.

dird-pulsed-high-power-microwave-source-.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-pulsed-high-power-microwave-source-.why: published, numbered and released by DIA as DIA-08-0912-005
dird-pulsed-high-power-microwave-source-.note: DIA numbered and published the 37-page document marked UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY and released it in redacted form under FOIA. All 38 DIRDs were marked FOUO except a single Directed Technologies laser deliverable that was classified Secret/NOFORN.

dird-pulsed-high-power-microwave-source-.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-pulsed-high-power-microwave-source-.note: Issued as DIA-08-0912-005 on 28 January 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, in the DIRD 'Acquisition Threat Support' series. The 0912 number block places its assignment in December 2009, the earliest of the eight documents in this batch, and its directed-energy subject matter is among the most conventionally military on the DIA list.

dird-pulsed-high-power-microwave-source-.label: James Wells
dird-pulsed-high-power-microwave-source-.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Pulsed High-Power Microwave Technology' to 'Dr James Wells, J W Enterprises'. The earlier Knapp/KLAS-TV roster gives the same author with the affiliation Northrop Grumman; the DIA list governs. No verified biography for this author has been located beyond the list entry.

dird-quantum-computing-and-utilizing-org.label: Wayne State University
dird-quantum-computing-and-utilizing-org.why: author's institutional affiliation at time of writing
dird-quantum-computing-and-utilizing-org.note: Wayne State University is the affiliation recorded against this title on the DIA congressional list. Wayne State appears more than once on the list: it is also the affiliation given for Kit Green's human-tissue field-effects deliverable, so both the human-effects and human-interface strands of the AAWSAP deliverable set run through the same medical school.

dird-quantum-computing-and-utilizing-org.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-quantum-computing-and-utilizing-org.note: Issued as DIA-08-1102-005 on 10 December 2010 in the DIRD 'Defense Futures' series. Unusually for the series, the Intelligence Cut-Off Date is identical to the publication date, indicating no lag between research cutoff and issue.

dird-quantum-computing-and-utilizing-org.label: Richard J. Genik II
dird-quantum-computing-and-utilizing-org.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Quantum Computing and Utilizing Organic Molecules in Automation Technology' to 'Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ'. Genik is credited elsewhere on the same list with the brain-machine interface deliverable on controlling external devices without limb-operated interfaces, making him a multi-product AAWSAP contributor.

dird-quantum-tomography-of-negative-ener.label: EarthTech International / Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
dird-quantum-tomography-of-negative-ener.why: author's institutional affiliation at time of writing
dird-quantum-tomography-of-negative-ener.note: EarthTech International, Austin, Texas — the affiliation recorded against this title on the DIA congressional list.

dird-quantum-tomography-of-negative-ener.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-quantum-tomography-of-negative-ener.note: Issued as DIA-08-1102-007 on 11 January 2011 in the DIRD 'Defense Futures' series, the vehicle DIA used exclusively for AAWSAP contract deliverables. The DIA cover letter to SASC describes the enclosed list as 'all products produced under the AATIP contract for DIA to publish'.

dird-quantum-tomography-of-negative-ener.label: Eric W. Davis
dird-quantum-tomography-of-negative-ener.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Quantum Tomography of Negative Energy States in the Vacuum' to 'Dr Eric Davis, EarthTech'. This is one of a coherent negative-energy sub-series by the same author within the DIRD set, alongside 'Traversable Wormholes, Stargates and Negative Energy' and the quantum-vacuum energy extraction paper.

dird-space-access-where-we-ve-been.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-space-access-where-we-ve-been.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1001-006, Acquisition Threat Support series
dird-space-access-where-we-ve-been.note: Cover page: "March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1001-006," prepared by the Defense Intelligence Agency. Released under FOIA and held in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

dird-space-access-where-we-ve-been.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-space-access-where-we-ve-been.note: Inside cover: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program." Comments were to be addressed to the AAWSA Program Manager, DIA, Bldg 6000, Washington DC 20340-5100.

dird-space-access-where-we-ve-been.label: Paul A. Czysz
dird-space-access-where-we-ve-been.why: author of record on the DIA list
dird-space-access-where-we-ve-been.note: The DIA letter of 9 January 2018 to the Senate Armed Services Committee lists item 4 as "Space Access, Dr P Czysz, HyperTech." The released document's own author line is redacted under FOIA exemption (b)(6), so the attribution rests entirely on the government list, not on the document.

dird-state-of-the-art-and-evolution.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-state-of-the-art-and-evolution.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1003-019, Acquisition Threat Support series
dird-state-of-the-art-and-evolution.note: Cover page: "31 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-019." Released under FOIA in the March 2022 bulk release of 37 DIRDs.

dird-state-of-the-art-and-evolution.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-state-of-the-art-and-evolution.why: AAWSAP deliverable; the only one with a classified version
dird-state-of-the-art-and-evolution.note: The existence of a SECRET//NOFORN twin of this paper is the answer to the long-standing question of what the redacted 38th DIRD was. It is also the counterexample to DIA's October 2009 assessment that the AAWSAP deliverables were basic research not warranting Special Access Program protection: one deliverable was in fact classified, and it was the conventional directed-energy weapons survey rather than any of the exotic-physics papers.

dird-state-of-the-art-and-evolution.label: J. Albertine
dird-state-of-the-art-and-evolution.why: author of record on the DIA list, both versions
dird-state-of-the-art-and-evolution.note: The DIA letter lists this paper twice, items 37 and 38, both credited to J Albertine of Directed Technologies: one formerly classified SECRET//NOFORN, one unclassified. The board node is labelled with the initial because no source consulted confirms the given name; the probable identification with John R. Albertine of the Navy High Energy Laser Program Office is carried as a tier-3 claim on the person node.

dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1003-013, Acquisition Threat Support series
dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.note: Cover page as printed: "23 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2010 / DIA-08-1003-013." The Intelligence Cut-Off Date printed on this document postdates its publication date, which is anomalous against every other March 2010 DIRD examined. Recorded as printed and flagged in unresolved[].

dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.note: Inside cover: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program."

dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.label: Materials and custody analysis
dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.why: subject domain: superconducting materials and claimed gravitational coupling
dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.note: The paper's subject is a materials question posed as a physics question: whether a rotating high-temperature superconductor can produce a measurable gravitational anomaly. It sits with the materials strand of the DIRD set rather than with the metric-engineering strand.

dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.label: George D. Hathaway
dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.why: author of record on the DIA list
dird-the-role-of-superconductors-in-grav.note: DIA list item 10: "Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research, Dr George Hathaway, Hathaway Consulting." This is the attribution most likely to be got wrong from the title alone: the paper reviews the Podkletnov and Ning Li gravity-modification claims but was not written by either of them or by any academic advocate of the effect. It was written by the Toronto engineer who had run the Podkletnov replication and reported null results.

dird-the-space-communication-implication.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-the-space-communication-implication.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1003-016, Acquisition Threat Support series
dird-the-space-communication-implication.note: Cover page: "30 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-016."

dird-the-space-communication-implication.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-the-space-communication-implication.note: Standard AAWSA FY2009 administrative note on the inside cover. The tasking, per the KLAS-TV rendering of the title, was quantum entanglement communication.

dird-the-space-communication-implication.label: John G. Cramer
dird-the-space-communication-implication.why: author of record on the DIA list
dird-the-space-communication-implication.note: DIA list item 25: "Space_Communication Implications of Quantum Entanglement and Nonlocality, Dr J Cramer, Univ of Washington." A mainstream university physicist, not a programme insider.

dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1004-004, Acquisition Threat Support series
dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.note: Cover page: "6 April 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1004-004." Issued through the Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3), Defense Warning Office, Directorate for Analysis.

dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.label: EarthTech International / Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.why: author's affiliation of record; DIRD carried on EarthTech's own publications list
dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.note: EarthTech International lists six DIRDs by Eric Davis on its publications page, with DIA document numbers and the issuing division named as the Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3) or Technology Warning Division (DWO-4) of the Defense Warning Office. A contractor publishing its DIA reference-document numbers on an open website is itself part of how the DIRD series became documentable.

dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.note: Produced under the DIA AAWSA Program contract executed by BAASS. Eric Davis has described his role as a BAASS subcontractor tasked with setting up the expert studies and extrapolating terrestrial technology to roughly 2050.

dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.label: Eric W. Davis
dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.why: author of record on the DIA list and on EarthTech's own citation list
dird-traversable-wormholes-stargates-and.note: DIA list item 8: "Traversable Wormholes, Stargates and Negative Energy, Dr Eric Davis, EarthTech International." Unlike the warp-drive paper, the popular attribution to Davis is confirmed by the government list here. EarthTech's own bibliography carries the same citation with the document number DIA-08-1004-004.

dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.label: Lockheed Martin Corporation
dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.why: author's affiliation of record; one of three Lockheed Martin DIRDs
dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.note: Lockheed Martin appears three times on the DIA list: this paper, Dr V Teofilo's "Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion," and Dr S Macheret's MHD air-breathing propulsion paper. Eric Davis said in a June 2018 interview that the advanced nuclear fusion for aerospace propulsion work was done by colleagues at Lockheed Martin, which matches the list. This is a direct, documented thread from the DIRD series into the prime-contractor cluster.

dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.note: Dated 1 November 2010 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 20 July 2010 and a DIA-08-1011 series number, placing it in the November 2010 batch rather than the FY2009 tranche delivered in March and April 2010. The DIRD series was produced in at least two waves.

dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.label: Materials and custody analysis
dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.why: subject domain: energy-storage materials for commercial and military applications
dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.note: Electrode and electrolyte materials science applied to high-power energy storage. One of the DIRDs with immediate conventional military application and no anomalous content.

dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.label: J. Golightly
dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.why: author of record on the DIA list
dird-ultracapacitors-as-energy-and-power.note: DIA list item 35: "Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices, Dr J Golightly, Lockheed Martin." The given name behind the initial was not established by any source consulted, and the node is labelled accordingly rather than guessed.

dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1004-001, Acquisition Threat Support series
dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.note: Cover page: "2 April 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1004-001." Issued through the Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3), Defense Warning Office, Directorate for Analysis, per EarthTech's citation of the same document.

dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.note: Produced under the DIA AAWSA Program contract executed by BAASS. Along with the traversable-wormholes DIRD, this is one of the two papers that reached the public internet in December 2017, more than four years before the bulk FOIA release, and is the single most reproduced document of the thirty-eight.

dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.label: Eric W. Davis
dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.why: co-author per EarthTech International's own citation
dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.note: EarthTech International's publications page cites the paper as "Obousy, R. K. and Davis, E. W. (2010)." Davis is a co-author, not the sole author, and is not the name DIA recorded on its list to Congress. Both facts are true and the board should carry both edges rather than collapse them.

dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.label: Richard K. Obousy
dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.why: author of record on the DIA list; lead author
dird-warp-drive-dark-energy-and-the.note: CORRECTION EDGE. The DIA letter of 9 January 2018, item 19, names "Dr R Obousy, Obousy Consultants" as the author of the warp-drive DIRD. Press coverage almost universally attributes this paper to Eric Davis. EarthTech's own citation gives it as Obousy, R. K. and Davis, E. W. (2010), with Obousy first named, so the two records reconcile as a co-authored paper on which DIA recorded the lead author.

dird-technological-approaches-to-control.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
dird-technological-approaches-to-control.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1003-012, Acquisition Threat Support series
dird-technological-approaches-to-control.note: Cover page: "23 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-012."

dird-technological-approaches-to-control.label: Wayne State University
dird-technological-approaches-to-control.note: Wayne State is the DIA-listed affiliation for four DIRDs: Genik's three human-factors papers and Kit Green's "Field Effects on Biological Tissues." That makes it the single most productive institution in the DIRD set after EarthTech International, and the locus of the programme's human-effects line of inquiry.

dird-technological-approaches-to-control.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dird-technological-approaches-to-control.note: Inside cover carries the standard AAWSA FY2009 administrative note and directs comments to the AAWSA Program Manager at DIA.

dird-technological-approaches-to-control.label: Richard J. Genik II
dird-technological-approaches-to-control.why: author of record on the DIA list
dird-technological-approaches-to-control.note: DIA list item 20: "Technological Applications to Controlling External Devices in the Absence of Limb-Operated Interfaces, Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ." The KLAS-TV list of July 2018 gives the same document the plainer title "Brain-Machine Interfaces."

hearing-2024-11-13.why: Entered into the Congressional Record from the dais

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Luis D. Elizondo
hearing-2024-11-13.why: Elizondo's testimony converted the contractor transfer story into a congressional record

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Christopher K. Mellon

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Nancy Ruth Mace

hearing-2024-11-13.note: Joint hearing of the Cybersecurity/IT/Government Innovation and National Security/Border/Foreign Affairs subcommittees, with Rep. Glenn Grothman co-chairing.

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Timothy Floyd Burchett
hearing-2024-11-13.why: Elicited Elizondo's corroboration of Grusch under oath

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Luis D. Elizondo
hearing-2024-11-13.why: sworn witness

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Michael Gold
hearing-2024-11-13.why: sworn witness
hearing-2024-11-13.note: Listed in the printed hearing record as a witness.

hearing-2024-11-13.why: sworn witness; delivered the Immaculate Constellation document
hearing-2024-11-13.note: Chairwoman Mace on the record: the 12-page Pentagon document 'that Michael Shellenberger brought today'.

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Nancy Ruth Mace
hearing-2024-11-13.why: presiding chair; entered Immaculate Constellation into the record
hearing-2024-11-13.note: INDEX OF DOCUMENTS: 'Report, Pentagon, "Immaculate Constellation"; submitted by Rep. Mace.'

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Timothy Gallaudet
hearing-2024-11-13.why: sworn witness
hearing-2024-11-13.note: Listed in the printed hearing record as a witness.

hearing-2024-11-13.label: AARO FY2024 Consolidated Annual Report on UAP
hearing-2024-11-13.why: AARO released its annual report the day after the hearing
hearing-2024-11-13.note: The hearing was 13 November 2024; the FY2024 report and Kosloski's media roundtable were 14 November 2024, and his Senate testimony 19 November.

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Karl E. Nell
hearing-2024-11-13.why: Mace read his 'nonhuman intelligence exists' statement into the hearing record

hearing-2024-11-13.why: Sworn witness; testified to a SCIF-signed document barring him from discussing crash retrieval

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Michael Gold
hearing-2024-11-13.why: Testified before the House Oversight joint subcommittees

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Public
hearing-2024-11-13.why: Founder Shellenberger testified as a hearing witness

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Timothy Gallaudet
hearing-2024-11-13.why: Testified before the House Oversight joint subcommittees
hearing-2024-11-13.note: Gallaudet's statement urged members to 'wield their subpoena power against hostile witnesses and prevent additional government funding to those UAP efforts that remain hidden from congressional oversight.'

hearing-2024-11-13.label: Michael Shellenberger
hearing-2024-11-13.why: Testified and submitted the report at the 13 November 2024 hearing
hearing-2024-11-13.note: The hearing is the fixed, dateable event at which the Immaculate Constellation document entered the record.

hearing-2024-11-13.label: House Oversight hearing, 26 July 2023 - 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency'
hearing-2024-11-13.why: The crash-retrieval allegation moved from second-hand to affirmative between the two hearings
hearing-2024-11-13.note: Grusch testified in 2023 to being informed of a retrieval programme; in 2024 Elizondo answered Mace's direct question with 'Yes'.

hearing-2024-11-13.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
hearing-2024-11-13.why: Volume I's 'no NDAs' finding against Elizondo's sworn SCIF testimony
hearing-2024-11-13.note: Volume I states AARO found no NDAs containing UAP-related information; eight months later Elizondo testified under oath to signing a SCIF instrument barring discussion of crash retrieval.

ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.label: Lockheed Martin Corporation
ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.why: The IR&D restriction applies directly to covered prime contractors
ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.note: DoDI 3204.01 covers major contractors allocating over $11 million in IR&D and bid-and-proposal costs; the primes on this board are all covered contractors, and none has publicly reported a disclosure under Sec. 1687(b).

ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.label: DoD Instruction 3204.01 - Oversight of Independent Research and Development
ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.why: Congress legislated directly against the IR&D mechanism, citing the instruction by number and change date
ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.note: Sec. 1687(b) makes UAP-related IR&D unallowable as an indirect expense unless disclosed to the defense and intelligence committees and congressional leadership. A statute does not cite an accounting instruction that precisely unless someone has explained how it is being used.

ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.label: S. 2103 Sec. 1104 - SSCI contractor disclosure and immunity provision (stripped)
ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.why: Only the funding limitation and the IR&D restriction survived into law
ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.note: Sec. 1687 and Sec. 7343 of Public Law 118-31 carry forward the funding cutoff and the IR&D clause from the Senate provision; the contractor disclosure, inventory and immunity subsections were removed.

ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.label: 10 U.S.C. 119 — Special Access Programs: Congressional Oversight
ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.why: Sec. 1687 is Congress overriding the Sec. 119 waiver for one subject matter
ndaa-fy2024-sec1687.note: Where Sec. 119(e) permits reporting to only the chairman and ranking member of each defense committee, Sec. 1687 conditions the money itself on disclosure to both intelligence committees and all four congressional leaders for UAP activity specifically.

carve-out.label: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1 — DoD SAP Security Manual: General Procedures
carve-out.why: Defined verbatim in the SAP Security Manual glossary
carve-out.note: 'carve-out. A provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense that relieves DSS of its NISP obligation to perform industrial security oversight functions for a DoD SAP.'

carve-out.label: 32 CFR Part 117 — NISPOM Rule
carve-out.why: The carve-out is codified in the NISPOM rule itself
carve-out.note: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) is the operative regulatory text relieving the Director, DCSA of NISP oversight for a carved-out DoD SAP.

carve-out.label: Program structure and organisational mapping
carve-out.why: the provision that removes a contractor facility from the government's own industrial security oversight
carve-out.note: Defined in DoD Directive 5205.07 and DoD Manual 5205.07 Volume 1 as a provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense relieving the defence security agency of its National Industrial Security Program oversight responsibilities at a contractor facility. It is the structural seam at which a programme held at a company stops being visible to any government security official outside the programme.

carve-out.label: DCSA as DoD Cognizant Security Office under the NISP
carve-out.why: Switches off the only external inspector of a contractor SAP facility
carve-out.note: DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 2 para 2.c enumerates what DSS/DCSA does 'Unless a carve-out provision is approved' - inspections, IS authorisation and CI cross-sharing.

carve-out.label: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)
carve-out.why: DoD SAPCO holds the list of carved-out facilities
carve-out.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 2 para 2.k requires DoD SAPCO to provide 'DSS confirmation of SAP facilities where the DSS has been carved out of security oversight functions'. [Re-pointed from a collapsed duplicate, 14 Aug 2026.]

carve-out.label: 50 U.S.C. 3091a — Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
carve-out.why: Congress prohibited moving a capability out of a CAP into a SAP without notice
carve-out.note: 50 U.S.C. 3091a(b)(2)(A), added by section 6603 of Public Law 118-159, bars transfer of a capability from a CAP to a special access program until notice is submitted to the appropriate committees and leadership.

carve-out.label: DoDI 5205.11 — Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD SAPs (12 Sep 2024)
carve-out.note: DoDI 5205.11 Appendix 2 to Enclosure 6 item 11.d requires a 'Contract strategy (carve-out justification if applicable)'; Enclosure 7 requires the signed carve-out approval and the list of carved-out facilities in the program record file.

carve-out.label: DoDD 5205.07, DoD Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (12 Sep 2024)
carve-out.why: Still cited by regulation, no longer defined by the directive it cites
carve-out.note: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) conditions the carve-out on approval 'in accordance with DoDD 5205.07', but the 12 September 2024 reissue of that directive contains no definition of carve-out.

carve-out.label: 32 CFR Part 117 — NISPOM Rule
carve-out.why: 32 CFR 117.6(b) writes the carve-out into regulation

carve-out.label: DCSA as DoD Cognizant Security Office under the NISP
carve-out.why: relieves DCSA of NISP industrial security oversight for a DoD SAP

carve-out.label: David Charles Grusch
carve-out.why: Contractor custody without government inspection is the carve-out configuration
carve-out.note: Grusch has alleged material held at defence contractors; the carve-out is the documented mechanism by which a contractor SAP facility ceases to receive DCSA inspection, IS accreditation and CI cross-sharing.

dodd-5205-07-2024.label: Acknowledged, unacknowledged and waived — the three states of a DoD SAP
dodd-5205-07-2024.why: The 2024 reissue deletes acknowledged, unacknowledged, waived and carve-out from the definitions
dodd-5205-07-2024.note: The glossary of the 12 September 2024 directive substitutes 'Joint Force Integration SAP' and 'Strategic Enabler SAP' and contains none of the four prior terms.

dodd-5205-07-2024.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
dodd-5205-07-2024.why: Current charter of the DoD SAP enterprise
dodd-5205-07-2024.note: Effective 12 September 2024, incorporating the 11 July 2023 SAP Enterprise Reform implementation guidance.

dodd-5205-07-2024.label: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
dodd-5205-07-2024.why: Cancelled and replaced the 2010 directive on 12 September 2024
dodd-5205-07-2024.note: The 2024 reissue cancels DoDD 5205.07 of 1 July 2010 as amended and incorporates the 11 July 2023 Deputy Secretary memorandum on SAP Enterprise Reform.

dodd-5205-07-2024.label: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)
dodd-5205-07-2024.why: Still cited by regulation, no longer defined by the directive it cites
dodd-5205-07-2024.note: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) conditions the carve-out on approval 'in accordance with DoDD 5205.07', but the 12 September 2024 reissue of that directive contains no definition of carve-out.

dodd-5205-07-2024.label: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
dodd-5205-07-2024.why: 12 Sep 2024 reissuance cancels the 1 Jul 2010 directive

dodi-5205-11.label: Program structure and organisational mapping
dodi-5205-11.why: the issuance that documents the approval and oversight chain this domain is trying to map
dodi-5205-11.note: DoDI 5205.11 (effective 12 September 2024) sets out the prospective SAP approval sequence in days from establishment, the review bodies (SSWG, Senior Review Group, SAPOC) and the oversight roles. It is the only public document that walks the whole chain end to end, which makes it the domain's primary methodological source rather than merely one of its members.

dodi-5205-11.label: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1 — DoD SAP Security Manual: General Procedures
dodi-5205-11.why: The manual implements the instruction's policy
dodi-5205-11.note: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1 para 1.a(1) states that it 'implements policy established in DoD Instruction (DoDI) 5205.11'.

dodi-5205-11.label: Special Access Program Oversight Committee (SAPOC)
dodi-5205-11.why: Sets SAPOC membership and its annual validation of the congressional report
dodi-5205-11.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3 para 2 lists the eighteen SAPOC positions and assigns it 'an annual review and validation of SAP reports sent to the Congressional defense and intelligence committees'.

dodi-5205-11.label: Senior Review Group (DoD SAP governance)
dodi-5205-11.why: Makes the SRG the working-level body that reviews every waived program annually
dodi-5205-11.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3 para 3.b(4)-(5): the SRG 'Reviews all waived DoD SAPs annually' and 'Ensures the accuracy of the SAP list submitted to Congress'.

dodi-5205-11.label: SAP Senior Working Group (SSWG)
dodi-5205-11.why: Chairs the deconfliction forum at the DoD SAPCO director level
dodi-5205-11.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3 para 4.a makes the Director, DoD SAPCO the SSWG Chair, with SAPCO directors from USD(I), USD(P), USD(AT&L), the services, the Joint Staff, DARPA and MDA.

dodi-5205-11.label: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)
dodi-5205-11.note: DoDI 5205.11 Appendix 2 to Enclosure 6 item 11.d requires a 'Contract strategy (carve-out justification if applicable)'; Enclosure 7 requires the signed carve-out approval and the list of carved-out facilities in the program record file.

dodi-5205-11.label: Waived Unacknowledged SAP (waived USAP) — the mechanism
dodi-5205-11.why: para 1.2.f designates select unacknowledged SAPs as waived

dodm-5205-07-series.label: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1 — DoD SAP Security Manual: General Procedures
dodm-5205-07-series.why: Volume 1 is the general procedures volume of the four-volume manual
dodm-5205-07-series.note: DoDM 5205.07 is issued in volumes; Volume 1 carries the responsibilities, general procedures, HVSACO rules and the glossary containing the carve-out definition.

dodm-5205-07-series.label: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
dodm-5205-07-series.why: manual implements policy established in DoDD 5205.07

sap-taxonomy.label: DoDD 5205.07, DoD Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (12 Sep 2024)
sap-taxonomy.why: The 2024 reissue deletes acknowledged, unacknowledged, waived and carve-out from the definitions
sap-taxonomy.note: The glossary of the 12 September 2024 directive substitutes 'Joint Force Integration SAP' and 'Strategic Enabler SAP' and contains none of the four prior terms.

sap-taxonomy.label: 32 CFR Part 117 — NISPOM Rule
sap-taxonomy.why: Supplies the regulatory definition of a special access program binding on contractors
sap-taxonomy.note: 32 CFR 117.3(b) defines SAP as a program controlling access and distribution 'beyond that normally required for TOP SECRET, SECRET, or CONFIDENTIAL information'.

sap-taxonomy.label: CAP Registry / CAPCO Register of control systems, compartments and sub-compartments
sap-taxonomy.why: Gives special access programs their own marking category in the banner line
sap-taxonomy.note: CAPCO Register v5.1 moved the Special Access Required marking into a new Special Access Program Markings category following the SCI control markings, with the indicator 'SPECIAL ACCESS REQUIRED-' or 'SAR-'.

sap-taxonomy.label: Executive Order 13526 — Classified National Security Information
sap-taxonomy.why: All SAP categories descend from a single executive order provision
sap-taxonomy.note: Section 4.3(a) names the six officials who may create a SAP; the DoD taxonomy of acknowledged, unacknowledged and waived operates entirely below that grant.

sap-taxonomy.label: Waived Unacknowledged SAP (waived USAP) — the mechanism
sap-taxonomy.why: Waived is the terminal state of the taxonomy
sap-taxonomy.note: DoDI 5205.11 defines a waived SAP as 'An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs.'

sap-taxonomy.label: Pub. L. 118-159 secs. 6602 & 6603 — CAP funding cutoff and the CAP-to-SAP transfer bar
sap-taxonomy.why: 6603 bars CAP-to-SAP capability transfer without notice

sap-cover-mechanisms.label: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1 — DoD SAP Security Manual: General Procedures
sap-cover-mechanisms.why: HVSACO, nicknames and unacknowledged locations are all defined in the manual
sap-cover-mechanisms.note: DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 5 applies HVSACO 'When using a SAP nickname for an unacknowledged SAP' and states 'HVSACO is not a classification'; Enclosure 10 bars federal ID cards for identification at unacknowledged locations.

sap-cover-mechanisms.label: The annual DoD special access program report to Congress
sap-cover-mechanisms.note: DoDI 5205.11 para 5.d: 'Unclassified nicknames will be used in the annual SAP report to Congress.'

sap-cover-mechanisms.label: Luis D. Elizondo
sap-cover-mechanisms.why: HVSACO and nickname practice describe the paperwork environment Elizondo has described
sap-cover-mechanisms.note: Elizondo's account of AATIP-era handling turns on material moving in special access channels; DoDM 5205.07-V1 documents HVSACO as the caveat used for unacknowledged SAP nicknames and expressly not a classification.

dcsa-nisp.label: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)
dcsa-nisp.why: Switches off the only external inspector of a contractor SAP facility
dcsa-nisp.note: DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 2 para 2.c enumerates what DSS/DCSA does 'Unless a carve-out provision is approved' - inspections, IS authorisation and CI cross-sharing.

dcsa-nisp.label: 32 CFR Part 117 — NISPOM Rule
dcsa-nisp.why: Designated the DoD Cognizant Security Office by regulation
dcsa-nisp.note: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(1): the Director, DCSA 'Oversees and manages DCSA, which serves as the DoD CSO.'

dcsa-nisp.label: GAO-04-332 — Industrial Security: DOD Cannot Provide Adequate Assurances That Its Oversight Ensures the Protection of Classified Information
dcsa-nisp.why: GAO found DoD could not assure adequate industrial security oversight - and excluded SAPs
dcsa-nisp.note: GAO-04-332 title states the finding; its footnote 2 records that the review 'did not include DSS's oversight of special access programs at contractor facilities'.

dcsa-nisp.label: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)
dcsa-nisp.why: relieves DCSA of NISP industrial security oversight for a DoD SAP

sapoc.label: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
sapoc.note: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.b: 'The Special Access Program Oversight Committee (SAPOC), hereby established, shall advise and assist the Secretary of Defense and the Deputy Secretary of Defense'.

sapoc.label: DoDI 5205.11 — Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD SAPs (12 Sep 2024)
sapoc.why: Sets SAPOC membership and its annual validation of the congressional report
sapoc.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3 para 2 lists the eighteen SAPOC positions and assigns it 'an annual review and validation of SAP reports sent to the Congressional defense and intelligence committees'.

sapoc.label: Senior Review Group (DoD SAP governance)
sapoc.why: Unanimous SRG recommendations bypass the SAPOC entirely
sapoc.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3 para 3: 'Unanimous recommendations of the SRG may be forwarded directly to the DepSecDef for decision.'

srg-dod.label: DoDI 5205.11 — Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD SAPs (12 Sep 2024)
srg-dod.why: Makes the SRG the working-level body that reviews every waived program annually
srg-dod.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3 para 3.b(4)-(5): the SRG 'Reviews all waived DoD SAPs annually' and 'Ensures the accuracy of the SAP list submitted to Congress'.

srg-dod.label: Special Access Program Oversight Committee (SAPOC)
srg-dod.why: Unanimous SRG recommendations bypass the SAPOC entirely
srg-dod.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3 para 3: 'Unanimous recommendations of the SRG may be forwarded directly to the DepSecDef for decision.'

srg-dod.label: Waived Unacknowledged SAP (waived USAP) — the mechanism
srg-dod.why: Every waived program is reviewed once a year by a named standing body
srg-dod.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3 para 3.b(4) assigns the SRG the annual review of all waived DoD SAPs and recommendations on continued waived status.

sswg.label: DoDI 5205.11 — Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD SAPs (12 Sep 2024)
sswg.why: Chairs the deconfliction forum at the DoD SAPCO director level
sswg.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3 para 4.a makes the Director, DoD SAPCO the SSWG Chair, with SAPCO directors from USD(I), USD(P), USD(AT&L), the services, the Joint Staff, DARPA and MDA.

dia.label: James T. Lacatski
dia.why: redacted the PM's name it had already published
dia.note: Lacatski is named in the public solicitation and redacted under 10 USC 424 in every post-award release — a records posture aimed at breaking the link between office and person.

dia.label: Advanced Nuclear Propulsion for Manned Deep Space Missions
dia.why: published and holds; DIA-08-1003-007
dia.note: Published by DIA as a Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Acquisition Threat Support series, DIA-08-1003-007, ICOD 1 December 2009. Later released by DIA under FOIA.

dia.label: Advanced Space Propulsion Based on Vacuum (Spacetime Metric) Engineering
dia.why: published and holds; DIA-08-1003-015
dia.note: Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Acquisition Threat Support series, DIA-08-1003-015, ICOD 1 December 2009.

dia.label: Aerospace Applications of Programmable Matter
dia.why: published and holds; DIA-08-0911-016
dia.note: Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Acquisition Threat Support series, DIA-08-0911-016, ICOD 1 December 2009. Released in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room, FileId 170022.

dia.label: An Introduction to the Statistical Drake Equation
dia.why: published and holds; document number not recoverable
dia.note: Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Acquisition Threat Support series, 11 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009. No DIA document number is legible in the released scan; deliberately left unrecorded rather than inferred.

dia.label: Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion
dia.why: published and holds; DIA-08-1011-003
dia.note: Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Defense Futures series, DIA-08-1011-003, ICOD 20 July 2010. 50 pages, 28 endnotes, singular "Author" byline.

dia.label: Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion
dia.why: published and holds; DIA-08-1011-004
dia.note: Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Defense Futures series, DIA-08-1011-004, ICOD 20 July 2010. 37 pages, 20 endnotes, plural "Authors" byline. Sequential to DIA-08-1011-003 and issued the same day.

dia.label: Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues
dia.why: published and holds; document number not recoverable
dia.note: Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Acquisition Threat Support series, 11 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009. No DIA document number is legible in the released scan; left unrecorded rather than inferred.

dia.label: Antigravity for Aerospace Applications
dia.why: published and holds; DIA-08-1003-018
dia.note: Defense Intelligence Reference Document, Acquisition Threat Support series, DIA-08-1003-018, ICOD 1 December 2009, originating with the Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3) of the Defense Warning Office, Directorate for Analysis.

dia.label: Laser Lightcraft Nanosatellites
dia.why: published, numbered and released by DIA as DIA-08-1011-001
dia.note: DIA assigned document number DIA-08-1011-001, published it 1 November 2010 in the 'Defense Futures' series with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 30 August 2010, marked it UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY, and later released it in redacted form under FOIA.

dia.label: Negative Mass Propulsion
dia.why: published, numbered and released by DIA as DIA-08-1101-023
dia.note: DIA numbered, published and marked the document UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY, and subsequently released it in redacted form to its FOIA Electronic Reading Room, where it is held as FileId 170039.

dia.label: Pulsed High-Power Microwave Source Technology
dia.why: published, numbered and released by DIA as DIA-08-0912-005
dia.note: DIA numbered and published the 37-page document marked UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY and released it in redacted form under FOIA. All 38 DIRDs were marked FOUO except a single Directed Technologies laser deliverable that was classified Secret/NOFORN.

dia.label: DIA Contract HHM402-08-C-0072 (BAASS)
dia.why: withheld the contract for eleven years
dia.note: DIA withheld the BAASS award entirely in a 2011 FOIA response and released it only in October 2022 — a contract that had been competed on a public bid board.

dia.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection (Record Group 615)
dia.why: Produced no records for the first statutory UAP transfer
dia.note: NARA's 24 April 2025 release named only ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. DIA, which holds documented UAP equity, transferred nothing.

dia.label: Skinwalkers at the Pentagon (Lacatski, Kelleher, Knapp, 2021)
dia.why: no records located for the documents the book describes
dia.note: DIA could locate neither the 19 June 2007 Lacatski letter nor the 'Utah Ranch Investigation: August 2009-February 2010' report, in a program contractually required to file monthly status reports.

dia.label: Defense Appropriations Acts FY2008 and FY2010 — the $22M AAWSAP appropriation
dia.why: $22M appropriated to DIA
dia.note: The appropriation named DIA as the recipient agency to assess long-term and over-the-horizon foreign advanced aerospace threats.

dia.label: Reid–DIA meetings on AAWSAP (Nov 2008, May 2009, Nov 2009)
dia.why: $22M congressionally directed to DIA for advanced aerospace threat work
dia.note: Per AARO HRR Vol. 1: 'In coordination with the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, DIA established AAWSAP in 2009... The contract for this DIA-managed program was awarded to a private sector organization.' The report also notes DIA 'did not seek, nor specifically authorize' some of the resulting work.

dia.label: SUN STREAK
dia.why: DIA sponsored the remote-viewing effort 1986-1995
dia.note: DIA's prior experience running an unacknowledged programme in a ridiculed domain is the institutional precedent for its 2008 AAWSAP contract.

dia.label: Space Access: Where We've Been and Where We Could Go
dia.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1001-006, Acquisition Threat Support series
dia.note: Cover page: "March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1001-006," prepared by the Defense Intelligence Agency. Released under FOIA and held in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

dia.label: State of the Art and Evolution of High-Energy Laser Weapons
dia.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1003-019, Acquisition Threat Support series
dia.note: Cover page: "31 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-019." Released under FOIA in the March 2022 bulk release of 37 DIRDs.

dia.label: Technological Approaches to Controlling External Devices in the Absence of Limb-Operated Interfaces
dia.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1003-012, Acquisition Threat Support series
dia.note: Cover page: "23 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-012."

dia.label: The Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research
dia.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1003-013, Acquisition Threat Support series
dia.note: Cover page as printed: "23 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2010 / DIA-08-1003-013." The Intelligence Cut-Off Date printed on this document postdates its publication date, which is anomalous against every other March 2010 DIRD examined. Recorded as printed and flagged in unresolved[].

dia.label: The Space-Communication Implications of Quantum Entanglement and Nonlocality
dia.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1003-016, Acquisition Threat Support series
dia.note: Cover page: "30 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-016."

dia.label: Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, and Negative Energy
dia.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1004-004, Acquisition Threat Support series
dia.note: Cover page: "6 April 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1004-004." Issued through the Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3), Defense Warning Office, Directorate for Analysis.

dia.label: Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions
dia.why: published by DIA as DIA-08-1004-001, Acquisition Threat Support series
dia.note: Cover page: "2 April 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1004-001." Issued through the Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3), Defense Warning Office, Directorate for Analysis, per EarthTech's citation of the same document.

dia.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
dia.why: Named contributor to the 2021 ODNI Preliminary Assessment on UAP
dia.note: ODNI's 25 June 2021 assessment names DIA among the contributing elements, establishing that this agency produced or held UAP-relevant reporting.

dia.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995
dia.why: DIA held the programme from 1985 as SUN STREAK and STAR GATE
dia.note: The effort moved to DIA's Scientific and Technical Intelligence Directorate as SUN STREAK in late 1985 and was consolidated as STAR GATE in 1991.

dia.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
dia.why: executive agent for AAWSAP
dia.note: DIA's Defense Warning Office housed the program office and its Virginia Contracting Activity issued the solicitation and award.

dia.label: DIA Info Memo to USD(AT&L) on AATIP (U-10-2552CE-IM-ATL)
dia.why: proposes transitioning AATIP out of DIA
dia.note: DIA tells USD(AT&L) the reports were of limited value to DIA but could merit other organisations and the project could move to a better-suited component.

dia.label: David Charles Grusch
dia.why: Accuses DIA of obstructing congressional oversight by withholding documents
dia.note: Made at the 9 June 2026 Capitol press conference. DIA is the agency that housed AAWSAP and the historical thread most directly implicated in the legacy record; the allegation is specific to document production, not to phenomenon.

dia.label: ODNI Memorandum ES 2026-00818 - Preliminary Guidance for Implementation of NDA Waiver
dia.why: directed to release; absent from the statutory archive
dia.note: The Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency is an addressee of ES 2026-00818; DIA has no RG 615 series as of 12 August 2026.

dia.label: Radiance Technologies, Inc.
dia.why: Radiance is a mid-tier technical prime in the space where compartmented analytical tasks are placed
dia.note: Reasoning: roughly $2.6 billion in prime obligations since FY2008 across intelligence, sensors and advanced concepts. Radiance recurs in UAP-adjacent reporting as an employer of personnel who moved between government UAP work and industry, but no primary personnel record has been located and none is asserted.

dia-deliverables-review-2009.label: Sandia National Laboratories
dia-deliverables-review-2009.why: three Sandia staff among the five outside reviewers
dia-deliverables-review-2009.note: A DOE weapons laboratory peer-reviewed the AAWSAP physics portfolio and DIA recorded the reviews as positive, some exceptionally so.

dia-deliverables-review-2009.label: The 38 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents (DIRDs)
dia-deliverables-review-2009.why: formal DIA quality assessment of the 26 FY09 reports
dia-deliverables-review-2009.note: Thirteen reviews: eight by other report authors, five external. Conclusion: the quality hoped for was achieved. [Re-pointed from dird-collection, 14 Aug 2026: dird-collection and dird-series described the same object and were collapsed.]

dia-deliverables-review-2009.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
dia-deliverables-review-2009.why: 2024 'lack of merit' contradicts DIA's 2009 quality finding
dia-deliverables-review-2009.note: DIA in 2009: reviews 'positive, some exceptionally so'. AARO in 2024: terminated due to concerns about the project. Same department, opposite assessments, fifteen years apart.

l-skinwalker.label: Robert T. Bigelow
l-skinwalker.why: purchased the ranch in 1996 and owned it throughout the DIA contract
l-skinwalker.note: The Deseret News reported the sale in June 1996 and Bigelow confirmed in August 1998 that the Shermans had agreed as a condition of purchase to keep quiet about what they had witnessed.

l-skinwalker.label: Uintah Basin, Utah
l-skinwalker.why: The ranch sits inside the Uintah Basin reporting region
l-skinwalker.note: The property is in Uintah County southeast of Ballard, bordering the Uintah and Ouray Indian Reservation, inside a region with a folk reporting record dating to the 1970s.

l-skinwalker.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
l-skinwalker.why: funded field investigation of the Utah site
l-skinwalker.note: AARO confirms the investigation; DIA says it cannot locate the resulting 'Utah Ranch Investigation: August 2009-February 2010' report.

l-skinwalker.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
l-skinwalker.why: The AAWSAP appropriation followed the Lacatski visit to the ranch
l-skinwalker.note: Reid and Sen. Ted Stevens secured roughly $22 million in Defense appropriations after Bigelow relayed Lacatski's ranch experience. BAASS, headquartered in Las Vegas, won the contract.

l-skinwalker.label: National Institute for Discovery Science (NIDS)
l-skinwalker.why: NIDS operated a permanently instrumented field station at the ranch
l-skinwalker.note: Bigelow moved in a research team, surveillance equipment and full-time caretakers immediately after the purchase.

l-skinwalker.label: National Institute for Discovery Science (NIDS)
