thunder-scientific.note: The company's location gave sightlines to the Manzano Weapons Storage Area at Kirtland; Bennewitz had the technical capability to record and characterise emissions.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: The Sol Foundation
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Advisory seat conditioned on unclassified-only access
uap-science-advisory-council.note: The council's announced terms guarantee its members will never see classified material. Recorded as a denial-type edge: the access granted is precisely the access that cannot resolve the question the members were appointed for.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: Abraham 'Avi' Loeb
uap-science-advisory-council.note: Loeb says he was 'tasked by' the White House, AARO, ODNI, the FBI and all Intelligence Community members to create the research team.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Established by ODNI with FBI support
uap-science-advisory-council.note: ODNI announced the council following the PURSUE records releases; the FBI is named as supporting.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: The Sol Foundation
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Sol leadership named to the ODNI/FBI council, 22 June 2026
uap-science-advisory-council.note: Nolan, Skafish, senior adviser Tim Gallaudet, advisory board member Jacob Haqq-Misra and production lead Ross Howard were all named; the foundation called it 'a fulfillment of its founding mission'.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Council established following the PURSUE releases
uap-science-advisory-council.note: Loeb's Medium account references a government disclosure release date of 12 June 2026 immediately before describing his tasking; the council's formation follows the release programme rather than preceding it.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: Chain of custody
uap-science-advisory-council.why: No budget, no classified access - constitutionally unable to reach the material
uap-science-advisory-council.note: The Associated Press reported the council has no budget and no access to classified material, and the Sol Foundation confirmed all shared data is unclassified. An advisory body denied money and clearances cannot audit a special access programme.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Council announced 17 June 2026, between Releases 03 and 04
uap-science-advisory-council.note: The council was announced as formed at the request of the White House and in coordination with AARO, ODNI, the FBI and other agencies, reporting to a higher-level UAP Governance Board.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: Garry Nolan
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Named as the council's molecular biologist
uap-science-advisory-council.note: The scientist who published the first peer-reviewed UAP materials analysis is seated on a body with no access to the government's own materials.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: Jacob Haqq-Misra
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Astrobiology seat, via the Sol Foundation advisory board
uap-science-advisory-council.note: One of five Sol-affiliated appointments announced by the foundation in June 2026.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: Matthew Szydagis
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Named for instrumentation and data collection
uap-science-advisory-council.note: The government's outside science body took its detector expertise from a self-funded civil expedition group, UAPx, rather than from a national laboratory.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: Peter Skafish
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Named as the council's cultural anthropologist
uap-science-advisory-council.note: Skafish's appointment completes the Sol Foundation's placement of its executive leadership on the federal advisory body.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: Richard Cloete
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Named for data analysis and AI tools
uap-science-advisory-council.note: Cloete brings the Galileo Project detection-and-tracking pipeline published in the Journal of Astronomical Instrumentation in 2023.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: Timothy Gallaudet
uap-science-advisory-council.why: Gallaudet named to the council as its oceanographer
uap-science-advisory-council.note: A retired rear admiral and former acting NOAA administrator, and a Sol Foundation senior adviser, seated on the government's outside science body.

uap-science-advisory-council.label: Robertson Panel
uap-science-advisory-council.why: third iteration of the external-scientific-panel pattern after Robertson (1953) and Condon (1966-68)
uap-science-advisory-council.note: Each prior panel supplied an authoritative dismissal on terms set by the sponsoring agency. Whether this one differs depends on its access to the Governance Board's classified holdings, which has not been publicly described.

mcdonnell-douglas.label: The Boeing Company
mcdonnell-douglas.why: Boeing absorbed McDonnell Douglas in 1997, inheriting the Huntington Beach organisation and its records
mcdonnell-douglas.note: Any corporate record of the Wood study, and of anything else the astronautics organisation held, passed to Boeing. No committee has requested it.

mcdonnell-douglas.label: Robert M. Wood
mcdonnell-douglas.why: Wood ran a company-funded study of unidentified craft at McDonnell Douglas Astronautics
mcdonnell-douglas.note: Wood spent his career at the Huntington Beach astronautics organisation and has repeatedly described initiating an internal study on the reasoning that a prime could not afford to be last to know if the propulsion were real.

mcdonnell-douglas.label: DoD Instruction 3204.01 - Oversight of Independent Research and Development
mcdonnell-douglas.why: Corporate self-funded UAP research is the historical precedent for the IR&D channel
mcdonnell-douglas.note: Robert Wood's late-1960s company-funded study at Huntington Beach is the earliest described instance of a prime studying the phenomenon on internal money with no reporting obligation - the pattern later formalised in IR&D policy. No company record of the study has been released.

dodi-3204-01.label: FY2024 NDAA sec. 1687 — Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs
dodi-3204-01.why: Targets contractor independent research and development as a concealment route
dodi-3204-01.note: Sec. 1687(b) makes UAP-related IR&D unallowable as indirect expense under DoDI 3204.01 unless the material is made available to the committees and leadership.

dodi-3204-01.label: NDAA FY2024 Sec. 1687 - Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs
dodi-3204-01.why: Congress legislated directly against the IR&D mechanism, citing the instruction by number and change date
dodi-3204-01.note: Sec. 1687(b) makes UAP-related IR&D unallowable as an indirect expense unless disclosed to the defense and intelligence committees and congressional leadership. A statute does not cite an accounting instruction that precisely unless someone has explained how it is being used.

dodi-3204-01.label: David Charles Grusch
dodi-3204-01.why: Grusch named contractor IR&D under oath as the funding channel for concealed UAP work
dodi-3204-01.note: Asked whether corporations overcharge government with the excess flowing to programs, Grusch answered 'Correct, through something called IR&D,' adding that 'IR&D is literally internal to the contractors... they do whatever they want.'

dodi-3204-01.label: McDonnell Douglas Corporation
dodi-3204-01.why: Corporate self-funded UAP research is the historical precedent for the IR&D channel
dodi-3204-01.note: Robert Wood's late-1960s company-funded study at Huntington Beach is the earliest described instance of a prime studying the phenomenon on internal money with no reporting obligation - the pattern later formalised in IR&D policy. No company record of the study has been released.

pursue-release-01.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
pursue-release-01.note: 160 files - 117 PDFs, 29 sensor videos, 14 photographs - spanning 1944 to 2026, at least 100 carrying redactions.

pursue-release-01.label: FBI Records: The Vault - UFO collection
pursue-release-01.why: Published FBI 62-HQ-83894, well beyond the Vault's 1947-1954 scope
pursue-release-01.note: The Bureau's master flying disc file covering 1947 to 1968 was released as a single 101MB PDF through war.gov rather than through the FBI's own reading room.

pursue-release-01.label: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
pursue-release-01.why: Released Apollo 12 and Apollo 17 mission records
pursue-release-01.note: Apollo mission records including cockpit transcript describing 'very bright particles or fragments' appear in the first tranche.

pursue-release-02.label: ODNI-UAP-D001 - serving senior intelligence officer's UAP encounter narrative
pursue-release-02.why: Published the serving officer's encounter narrative
pursue-release-02.note: A serving senior intelligence officer's first-person narrative of a one-hour, multi-witness encounter, published under an ODNI document number five months after the event.

pursue-release-02.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
pursue-release-02.note: 64 files including 51 sensor videos in a DOW-UAP-PR050 to PR099 series; the 5.6GB video bundle is the largest of the five.

pursue-release-02.label: AARO FY2024 Consolidated Annual Report on UAP
pursue-release-02.why: 'Lack of timely and actionable sensor data' against 51 released sensor videos
pursue-release-02.note: The FY2024 report attributes AARO's analytic constraint to sensor-data scarcity nineteen months before the same department published 51 sensor videos in a single tranche, all of incidents predating the report.

pursue-release-02.label: Anna Paulina Luna
pursue-release-02.why: letter said to be answered by the tranche
pursue-release-02.note: Release 02 is the only tranche with an identified congressional trigger - Luna's April 2026 letter - and the letter itself has not been published.

pursue-release-03.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
pursue-release-03.note: 72 files with the FBI the largest contributor at 29 files, including a less-redacted CIA Robertson Panel record.

pursue-release-03.label: CIA FOIA Reading Room - UFO collection
pursue-release-03.why: Released a less-redacted 1953 Robertson Panel record
pursue-release-03.note: A version of the Agency's own foundational UAP document less redacted than the one in its public reading room appeared seventy-three years later, by executive direction.

pursue-release-03.label: FBI Records: The Vault - UFO collection
pursue-release-03.why: 29 FBI files including a 2021-2025 orb corpus and an agents' own FD-1057
pursue-release-03.note: The tranche established the FBI as an active modern UAP collector, a posture invisible in its own Vault collection last modified in 2013.

pursue-release-03.label: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
pursue-release-03.note: Gemini crew debriefings and 1962 Cronkite-Cooper interview audio were published in the third tranche.

pursue-release-04.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
pursue-release-04.note: 227MB of documents and 1.4GB of video spanning the 1940s to 2026, published without any stated file count.

pursue-release-04.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
pursue-release-04.why: Assessment language reappears despite the no-comment posture
pursue-release-04.note: Release 04 material was characterised as consistent with balloons or sensor artefacts and as not clear evidence of unknown aircraft, reverting to the AARO idiom the release programme had disclaimed.

pursue-release-04.label: war.gov/UFO release portal
pursue-release-04.why: By the fourth tranche the programme stopped stating what it released
pursue-release-04.note: Releases 01, 02, 03 and 05 have published file counts; Release 04 has none on the portal or in independent inventories.

pursue-release-05.label: PURSUE Release 05 file identifiers (7 August 2026)
pursue-release-05.note: 41 files - 16 videos, 22 documents, 3 images - with identifiers spanning DOW, FBI, DOS and EOP originators.

pursue-release-05.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
pursue-release-05.note: 41 files - 16 videos, 22 documents, 3 images - spanning 1953 to 2026 per the portal, with content reaching back to a 1950 case.

pursue-release-05.label: CIA FOIA Reading Room - UFO collection
pursue-release-05.note: A CIA report of an alleged November 1963 recovery of a metal sphere with a deceased occupant, deemed unsubstantiated by the American Consulate, appears in Release 05 and not in the Agency's curated collection.

pursue-release-05.label: Gulf of Oman AC-130J UAP engagement, 8 September 2021
pursue-release-05.why: Released the AC-130J gunship videos and DOW-UAP-D101
pursue-release-05.note: Six videos and an intelligence report documenting approximately 25 UAP instances over the Gulf of Oman on 8 September 2021, with objects reportedly reacting to cannon fire.

pursue-release-05.label: 1953 Navy Photographic Interpretation Center analysis of the Great Falls and Tremonton films
pursue-release-05.note: The Navy Photographic Interpretation Center's assessment that the Tremonton objects were self-luminous and intelligently controlled surfaced publicly for the first time in this tranche.

war-gov-ufo-portal.label: AARO in 2025-2026 - Kosloski's office as PURSUE's silent partner
war-gov-ufo-portal.why: signposts users to a channel it does not run
war-gov-ufo-portal.note: AARO's homepage carries a PURSUE banner linking to war.gov/UFO and a NARA banner linking to archives.gov, directing the public away from its own EFOIA reading room.

war-gov-ufo-portal.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
war-gov-ufo-portal.note: All five tranches are published on the Secretary of War's web estate at war.gov/UFO, with video served from a CloudFront distribution and no FOIA case numbers or exemption citations.

war-gov-ufo-portal.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
war-gov-ufo-portal.why: Published through the Secretary's web estate, not AARO's
war-gov-ufo-portal.note: All five tranches are posted at war.gov/UFO as paired document and video bundles, with video served from a CloudFront distribution; AARO links out to it rather than hosting it.

war-gov-ufo-portal.label: Executive Office of the President
war-gov-ufo-portal.why: Presidential direction produced the PURSUE release portal
war-gov-ufo-portal.note: Following the February 2026 presidential directive to identify and release UAP files, the Department of War established the PURSUE portal at war.gov/UFO and published its first tranche on 8 May 2026.

war-gov-ufo-portal.label: PURSUE Release 04
war-gov-ufo-portal.why: By the fourth tranche the programme stopped stating what it released
war-gov-ufo-portal.note: Releases 01, 02, 03 and 05 have published file counts; Release 04 has none on the portal or in independent inventories.

trump-uap-release-directive-2026.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
trump-uap-release-directive-2026.why: The directive is the stated basis of the release programme
trump-uap-release-directive-2026.note: The war.gov/UFO portal attributes PURSUE to the President's direction to the Secretary of War, and AARO's own homepage links to it under the PURSUE name.

trump-uap-release-directive-2026.label: Sean Parnell
trump-uap-release-directive-2026.why: First departmental acknowledgement of the directive
trump-uap-release-directive-2026.note: Parnell said the department 'looks forward to working with the interagency to fulfill the president's directive', framing PURSUE as interagency implementation rather than an AARO or congressional product.

trump-uap-release-directive-2026.label: Donald J. Trump
trump-uap-release-directive-2026.why: Issued the direction that created PURSUE
trump-uap-release-directive-2026.note: Trump's 19-20 February 2026 Truth Social post directing Hegseth and relevant agencies to begin identifying and releasing UAP files is the sole originating instrument for the release programme.

trump-uap-release-directive-2026.label: Pete Hegseth
trump-uap-release-directive-2026.why: Named implementer; called it 'that executive order'
trump-uap-release-directive-2026.note: Hegseth told reporters on 25 February 2026 the department would be in full compliance with 'that executive order' and would coordinate with ODNI, while declining to give a schedule.

aaro-official-uap-imagery.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
aaro-official-uap-imagery.why: AARO's own small video release channel, Dec 2025 - Jan 2026
aaro-official-uap-imagery.note: Seven numbered PR items released across five weeks, all short European clips, one resolved as birds - the office's entire video output before PURSUE.

aaro-official-uap-imagery.label: House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets hearing, 9 September 2025 - 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection'
aaro-official-uap-imagery.why: Video releases began five weeks after testimony that AARO was withholding video
aaro-official-uap-imagery.note: The timing and the scale together read as minimum compliance: seven short clips in response to sworn testimony that the office holds an unreleased video archive.

aaro-official-uap-imagery.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
aaro-official-uap-imagery.why: AARO's channel stops; the Secretary's channel starts
aaro-official-uap-imagery.note: AARO's last imagery release is 6 January 2026; the Department's first tranche is 8 May 2026 with 29 videos, and AARO published nothing further.

aaro-declassification-info-paper-2025.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
aaro-declassification-info-paper-2025.why: The office's own account of why it cannot declassify
aaro-declassification-info-paper-2025.note: AARO states it cannot declassify independently, must request review from originating offices, and is bound by DOPSR - a description falsified within eight months by its own department.

d-materials.label: Reverse Engineering

d-materials.label: Aerospace Applications of Programmable Matter
d-materials.why: subject domain: exotic and reconfigurable materials

d-materials.label: Invisibility Cloaking: Theory and Experiments
d-materials.why: subject domain: transformation optics, metamaterials and signature reduction
d-materials.note: Contents run Camouflage, Transparency, Cloaking. The paper is the signature-reduction leg of the survey, sitting alongside Shvets's 'Metamaterials for Aerospace Applications' and against Culbreth's hypersonic detection paper. Puthoff listed signature reduction among the twelve threat areas DIA specified in the Broad Area Announcement.

d-materials.label: The Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research
d-materials.why: subject domain: superconducting materials and claimed gravitational coupling
d-materials.note: The paper's subject is a materials question posed as a physics question: whether a rotating high-temperature superconductor can produce a measurable gravitational anomaly. It sits with the materials strand of the DIRD set rather than with the metric-engineering strand.

d-materials.label: Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices for Commercial and Military Applications
d-materials.why: subject domain: energy-storage materials for commercial and military applications
d-materials.note: Electrode and electrolyte materials science applied to high-power energy storage. One of the DIRDs with immediate conventional military application and no anomalous content.

d-materials.label: ADAM Research Project (Acquisition and Data Analysis of Materials)
d-materials.why: Custody chain: anonymous source to Art Bell, to Linda Moulton Howe, to Carnegie DTM (1996), to Puthoff, to TTSA (2019), to the US Army
d-materials.note: Howe says the samples were tested by Carnegie Science's Department of Terrestrial Magnetism in 1996 and by Puthoff on several later occasions before TTSA bought them for $35,000 in 2019.

d-materials.label: Prime Contractor Custody
d-materials.note: Material alleged to be held by primes cannot be independently analysed, which is why the custody question and the materials question cannot be separated.

d-materials.label: Galileo Project Pacific Ocean expedition to the CNEOS 2014-01-08 (IM1) site, June-July 2023
d-materials.why: The control case: what a public physical-recovery attempt looks like, failures included
d-materials.note: Claim, rebuttal and re-analysis all appeared in the peer-reviewed literature within eighteen months. That is the benchmark against which seventy years of unpublished government custody should be judged.

d-materials.label: Nolan, Vallee, Jiang & Lemke (2022), Progress in Aerospace Sciences 128:100788

dod.label: SETKA-AN / SETKA-MO (later Galaktika, then Gorizont) - Soviet state anomalous phenomena programme
dod.why: opposite reporting posture: mandated versus stigmatised
dod.note: A January 1980 Directive of the Soviet General Staff obliged every serviceman to report any inexplicable phenomenon in writing and routed the results to a single analysis centre, putting the army 'into the on-duty regime of observation' for thirteen years. The contrast with the US chain of command over the same period, where reporting carried career risk and no service-wide collection mandate existed, is the comparison this node exists to make. The Soviet side of the comparison is documented by the programme's own coordinators; no institutional contact between the two is claimed. [Re-pointed from the collapsed duplicate `setka`, 14 Aug 2026.]

Feinberg as Deputy Secretary of Defense, the department's number-two official and the office that has historically signed the memoranda standing up DoD UAP bodies. dod.note: Robert Spencer Carr's 1974 public claim that bodies recovered near Aztec were held at 'Hangar 18' at Wright-Patterson AFB drew official Air Force denials. The FBI separately disowned the Guy Hottel memo, the one federal document ever cited as corroboration, in a published 2013 statement.

dod.label: David Charles Grusch
dod.why: Clearance removal, denial of promotion and loss of medical retirement following his disclosure
dod.note: Enumerated by Rep. Crane on the hearing record and in his letter to the Secretary of Defense.

dod.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
dod.why: Release volume without release quality

dod.label: USS Ronald Reagan Encounter and Logbook Tampering (2003-2004)

dod.label: Michigan State University, East Lansing, Michigan
dod.why: site of the DoD unsupported-adjustment study
dod.note: Economist Mark Skidmore conducted the aggregation of unsupported journal voucher adjustments in DoD and HUD financial statements for 1998-2015 at Michigan State University. The aggregate figure is an accounting-adjustment total, not spending, and the distinction is why this is tier 2 rather than tier 1.

dod.label: Vanderbilt University
dod.why: Vanderbilt UAP statistician invited to a Pentagon-sponsored expert meeting
dod.note: Vanderbilt University Medical Center reports that Stephen Bruehl, PhD, professor of Anesthesiology, 'was invited to attend a Pentagon-sponsored meeting for discussions with UAP experts from the government and academia' in August 2025, as his cluster analysis of 216 well-documented UAP cases (1947-2016) neared publication in World Futures. The sponsoring office is not named in the source.

dod.label: David Charles Grusch
dod.why: First protected disclosure to the DoD Inspector General, July 2021
dod.note: The Debrief records that Grusch provided classified information to the DoD IG in July 2021 regarding the concealment of UAP-related material from Congress, ten months before the ICIG filing. The reprisal complaint alleges his identity and those communications were later disclosed outside the IG channel.

dod-sapco.label: David Charles Grusch
dod-sapco.why: The office that must approve any contractor's provision of SAP material to Congress
dod-sapco.note: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.e requires DoD SAPCO approval before any contractor provides SAP material to a member of Congress - the structural barrier a contractor witness would face. [Re-pointed from a collapsed duplicate, 14 Aug 2026.]

dod-sapco.label: Congressional oversight of special access programs
dod-sapco.why: Contractor disclosure to Congress requires the approval of the office being disclosed about
dod-sapco.note: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.e bars any contractor entity, employee, representative or consultant from providing SAP material to members of Congress or staff 'without Director, DoD SAPCO, approval'. [Re-pointed from a collapsed duplicate, 14 Aug 2026.]

dod-sapco.label: The Classified Annex (NDAA and Defense Appropriations)
dod-sapco.why: DoDI 5205.11 para. 7.2.h - waived-programme justification materials go only to committee staff directors
dod-sapco.note: DoDI 5205.11 para. 7.2.h, 'Congressional Budget Justification Materials': 'The DoD will conform to all congressional reporting requirements. The DoD will submit to the congressional defense and intelligence committees such additional materials as are requested by the committees and are within the jurisdiction of each committee. Justification materials for waived programs will be presented only to the committee staff directors.' This is the best available primary evidence that DoD continued to route waived-programme justification material to the defense committees after the 31 December 2021 termination of 10 U.S.C. 119(a) and (b) - but note that it routes that material to staff directors rather than through the 119(e)(2) chair-and-ranking channel, and it rests on committee request rather than on a standing statutory reporting duty.

dod-sapco.label: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)
dod-sapco.why: DoD SAPCO holds the list of carved-out facilities
dod-sapco.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 2 para 2.k requires DoD SAPCO to provide 'DSS confirmation of SAP facilities where the DSS has been carved out of security oversight functions'. [Re-pointed from a collapsed duplicate, 14 Aug 2026.]

dod-sapco.label: Program structure and organisational mapping
dod-sapco.why: the office that holds the Department's SAP portfolio and is its single point of contact to Congress
dod-sapco.note: Established by DoD Directive 5205.07 (reissued 12 September 2024) 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense', with a Director who must be a general or flag officer or SES equivalent, and designated the primary DoD liaison with the Executive Branch and Congress on all DoD SAP issues. Any structural map of where a legacy programme could sit starts at this node.

dod-sapco.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
dod-sapco.why: Central SAP management office under the Deputy Secretary of Defense
dod-sapco.note: DoDD 5205.07 (12 Sep 2024) places DoD SAPCO 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense', with a general officer, flag officer or SES Director reporting directly to DEPSECDEF. Attested by the directive itself.

dod-sapco.label: DoDD 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 of 4 Feb 2020)
dod-sapco.why: Established DoD SAPCO under the Deputy Secretary of Defense
dod-sapco.note: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.c establishes DoD SAPCO 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense' with a flag officer or SES Director. [Re-pointed from a collapsed duplicate, 14 Aug 2026.]

dod-sapco.label: United States House of Representatives
dod-sapco.why: Single point of congressional liaison for every DoD special access program
dod-sapco.note: DoDD 5205.07 requires personnel to notify the Director, DoD SAPCO and OA SAPCO directors when briefing Congress or congressional staff with SAP material, and bars contractors from providing such material without specific approval. The office being overseen is notified before the overseer is briefed.

dod-sapco.label: Waived SAP Notification Group
dod-sapco.why: DoDI 5205.11 para. 7.2.a(3) - waived-SAP access limited to chair, ranking member, staff directors and one security manager
dod-sapco.note: DoD Instruction 5205.11, 'Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD Special Access Programs,' effective 12 September 2024, para. 7.2.a(3): 'Only the chair, the ranking member, the staff directors, and one designated security manager of the defense and intelligence committees will be authorized access to waived DoD SAPs within their committee's respective oversight jurisdiction. Requests to access additional members of Congress or professional staff must be approved by the Secretary of Defense or Deputy Secretary of Defense.' This is materially wider than 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) on two axes: it admits committee staff directors and a security manager, and it extends to the intelligence committees, which have no entitlement under section 119. Any board text asserting that the twelve have no staff who can read the material should be corrected against this paragraph. Para. 7.2.b confirms that ordinary members of the defense and intelligence committees are authorised access to all DoD SAPs in their jurisdiction 'except for waived programs.'

dod-sapco.label: Waived unacknowledged special access program (waived USAP)
dod-sapco.why: DoDI 5205.11 retains the acknowledged / unacknowledged / waived taxonomy the 2024 directive omitted
dod-sapco.note: DoDI 5205.11 para. 1.2.f, effective the same day as the reissued DoDD 5205.07: 'The Secretary of Defense may designate select unacknowledged SAPs as "waived" when it is determined that using standard procedures for reporting to Congress would adversely affect national security, pursuant to Section 119 of Title 10, United States Code. Waived SAPs remain subject to congressional oversight.' The glossary retains definitions of acknowledged SAP, unacknowledged SAP, SAP type and waived SAP, the last defined as 'A SAP for which the Secretary of Defense has waived applicable ... An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs.' The taxonomy was therefore not retired in September 2024; it was moved down one level from the directive into the instruction. Para. 3 further requires the SAP Oversight Committee's annual review to assess 'All waived DoD SAPs to determine the need for continued waived status' - an internal executive-branch review with no congressional trigger and no analogue in section 119.

dod-sapco.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
dod-sapco.why: AARO's SAP review ran through the DoD SAP control office
dod-sapco.note: AARO states it 'established a partnership with the Special Access Program Control Offices for the DoD, IC, and DHS to review programs identified in interviews by name or description' and that 'AARO investigators have been granted full access to all pertinent sensitive USG programs'.

dod-sapco.label: Section 8009 - 30-day advance notice before initiating or materially modifying a special access program
dod-sapco.why: The appropriations tripwire on initiating or modifying a special access programme
dod-sapco.note: Section 8009 of the FY2026 Defense Appropriations Act bars use of that Act's funds to initiate or materially modify the scope of a SAP without 30 days advance notice to the congressional defense committees; DoD SAPCO is the office that administers the SAP enterprise under the Deputy Secretary. Attested by the statute.

dod-sapco.label: Waived unacknowledged special access program (waived USAP)
dod-sapco.why: contractor disclosure to Congress requires SAPCO approval
dod-sapco.note: DoDD 5205.07 para. 3.1.g bars any DoD contractor entity, contractor employee, contractor representative or consultant from providing SAP material to any member of Congress or their staff without Director, DoD SAPCO approval, and requires all accessed personnel to notify SAPCO when briefing Congress.

dod-sapco.label: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence
dod-sapco.why: OSD principal for intelligence and security policy in the SAP enterprise
dod-sapco.note: DoDD 5205.07 assigns SAP policy responsibilities across OSD principals including the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, while vesting central management in DoD SAPCO under DEPSECDEF.

dod-sapco.label: The HASC/HAC-D special access program read-in gate
dod-sapco.why: SAPCO administers the read-in architecture Luna described
dod-sapco.note: Chairwoman Luna testified on 9 September 2025 that a non-committee member must be approved by the chairman and ranking member of both HASC and HAC-D to view specific material; the underlying access records and accreditation are held by the SAPCO enterprise.

dod-sapco.label: David Charles Grusch
dod-sapco.why: Grusch alleges programs were withheld from the reporting mechanism SAPCO administers
dod-sapco.note: Grusch's sworn testimony to House Oversight on 26 July 2023 alleges a multi-decade materials acquisition and exploitation activity concealed from Congress. In statutory terms the allegation is that programs were not reported under 10 U.S.C. 119 or were reported only under the waiver.

dod-sapco.label: Sean M. Kirkpatrick
dod-sapco.why: AARO Director's programmatic access ran through the SAPCO enterprise
dod-sapco.note: Kirkpatrick directed AARO throughout the period covered by the Historical Record Report, so the 'full access to all pertinent sensitive USG programs' assurance is his. Reasoning: the report is AARO's product under his directorship, and no independent verification of the SAP list handed to AARO has been produced.

dod-sapco.why: all component submissions route through DoD SAPCO

nga.label: David Charles Grusch

nga.note: From November 2021 to April 2023 Grusch was a GS-15 at NGA and, in his sworn words, 'my agency's co-lead in unidentified anomalous phenomena and trans medium object analysis as well as reporting to the UAP Task Force and eventually, once it was established, the All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office.' He also testified that reviewing overhead collection of such events was one of his primary NGA tasks.

nga.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
nga.why: Named contributor to the 2021 ODNI Preliminary Assessment on UAP
nga.note: ODNI's 25 June 2021 assessment names NGA among the contributing elements, establishing that this agency produced or held UAP-relevant reporting.

oni.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
oni.why: Named contributor to the 2021 ODNI Preliminary Assessment on UAP
oni.note: ODNI's 25 June 2021 assessment names Navy/ONI among the contributing elements, establishing that this agency produced or held UAP-relevant reporting.

oni.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF)
oni.why: sited in the Department of the Navy with ONI involvement
oni.note: The Deputy Secretary of Defense established the UAPTF under USD(I&S) cognisance with the Department of the Navy leading, placing it in ONI's institutional orbit.

oni.label: UAP Gerb - The MITRE Corporation investigation
oni.why: Alleges MITRE support to two Navy-spearheaded legacy programs
oni.note: The two alleged programs: reverse engineering and maturation of technologies from late-1940s recoveries, and tracking of a large USO with semi-permanent Atlantic station, with all-source data processed by MITRE. Gerb notes the oddity that MITRE was founded by and modelled on USAF structures yet is intimately involved in Navy secret programs.

doe.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection (Record Group 615)
doe.why: DOE produced nothing for the first statutory UAP records transfer
doe.note: NARA's 24 April 2025 release named ODNI, OSD, FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. DOE - which holds the weapons complex and performed AARO's materials analysis - was not among them.

doe.label: JASON
doe.why: NNSA rescued and now sponsors JASON after DoD declined renewal
doe.note: On 25-26 April 2019 NNSA issued a notice of intent to award a short-term sole source contract to MITRE for JASON management and logistics support, two weeks after OUSD(R&E) confirmed it was ending the contract.

doe.label: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory
doe.why: DOE weapons laboratory operating under Atomic Energy Act classification authority
doe.note: Restricted Data classification is statutory rather than executive-order-derived, and is therefore untouched by presidential declassification directives of the kind driving the 2026 PURSUE releases.

doe.label: Nevada Test Site / Nevada National Security Site
doe.why: DOE operating authority over the Nevada National Security Site
doe.note: The Nevada test complex is DOE/NNSA property operated by contract, with its own protective force and clearance regime, and is named repeatedly in retrieval testimony.

doe.label: Los Alamos National Laboratory
doe.why: DOE/NNSA management and operating contract; Los Alamos
doe.note: Los Alamos is an NNSA laboratory operated under contract; its National Security Research Center holds and processes FOIA on the laboratory's classified historical record, including 1949 green fireball material.

doe.label: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory
doe.why: DOE/NNSA management and operating contract; Lawrence Livermore
doe.note: Livermore is an NNSA weapons laboratory operating under DOE classification authority rather than DoD SAP authority.

doe.label: National Nuclear Security Administration
doe.why: Semi-autonomous agency within DOE established by Congress in 2000
doe.note: NNSA describes itself as 'a semi-autonomous agency within the U.S. Department of Energy responsible for enhancing national security through the military application of nuclear science'.

doe.label: Sandia National Laboratories
doe.why: DOE/NNSA management and operating contract; Sandia
doe.note: Sandia is an NNSA laboratory adjacent to Kirtland AFB and the Manzano Weapons Storage Area, the site of the 1980 intrusions investigated by AFOSI.

doe.label: AARO FY2025 Consolidated Annual Report on UAP
doe.why: 50 UAS notifications near nuclear infrastructure, nearly triple the prior period
doe.note: AARO's own FY2025 figures show unmanned system activity over nuclear infrastructure rising from 18 to 50 notifications, unresolved in the report.

doe.label: 50 U.S.C. 2426 — Congressional Oversight of DOE/NNSA Special Access Programs
doe.why: Governs special access programs of the nuclear weapons complex
doe.note: 50 U.S.C. 2426 imposes SAP reporting on the Administrator of the National Nuclear Security Administration, a semi-autonomous DOE agency.

doe.label: Los Alamos Green Fireballs Conference
doe.why: AEC laboratories convened the February 1949 green fireball conference
doe.note: The green fireball events centred on the Los Alamos and Sandia complexes and produced a conference and the subsequent Project TWINKLE instrumented observation effort. Attested by the FBI and Air Force file material released through the 2026 PURSUE tranches.

doe.label: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (UT-Battelle, LLC)
doe.why: DOE laboratory performed AARO's metallic specimen analysis
doe.note: AARO's published materials analysis synopsis was produced with Oak Ridge National Laboratory, a DOE laboratory - meaning DOE analytical capability was the government's chosen instrument for testing alleged recovered material.

doe.label: 'Manhattan Project 2.0' (alleged secrecy architecture)
doe.why: Alleges custody of recovered disks vested in AEC national laboratories
doe.note: Gerb argues Truman and Eisenhower placed recovered material inside Atomic Energy Commission laboratories - the institutional ancestors of today's DOE national labs - to obtain the Atomic Energy Act's statutory protections.

doe.label: 'The Pentagon's UFO Program Is Real [Here's How It Works!]'
doe.note: The episode places the Department of Energy's Nuclear Emergency Support Team inside the crash-retrieval architecture, consistent with the AEC-custody thesis.

doe.label: ODNI Memorandum ES 2026-00818 - Preliminary Guidance for Implementation of NDA Waiver
doe.why: directed to release; absent from the statutory archive
doe.note: The Director of the Office of Intelligence and Counterintelligence, Department of Energy, is an addressee of ES 2026-00818; DOE has no RG 615 series.

doe.label: Executive Office of the President
doe.why: Restricted Data authority sits outside presidential EO declassification power
doe.note: Restricted Data under the Atomic Energy Act is classified by statute, not by executive order. A UAP declassification directive operating on EO 13526 information cannot reach it. Reasoning: the two classification systems have separate legal foundations.

doe.label: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
doe.why: Both hold analytical capability that could resolve material claims and neither has been tasked publicly
doe.note: NASA's report identifies the classification of military and intelligence data as the binding constraint; DOE laboratories hold the analytical instruments actually used by AARO. Reasoning: the capability exists and the tasking does not.

dhs.label: AARO/DHS release: History and Origin of KONA BLUE
dhs.why: DHS co-authored the 2024 declassified KONA BLUE history
dhs.note: The paper 'History and Origin of KONA BLUE' is published on AARO's UAP Records page as a joint AARO/DHS product.

dhs.label: KONA BLUE
dhs.why: DHS Deputy Secretary disapproved and terminated KONA BLUE approximately six months later
dhs.note: The AARO/DHS paper states the Deputy Secretary disapproved and terminated the PSAP roughly six months after it was established, and that KONA BLUE was 'never approved or formally established'. Neither official is named in the released text.

dhs.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection (Record Group 615)
dhs.why: Produced no records for the first statutory UAP transfer
dhs.note: NARA's 24 April 2025 release named only ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. DHS, which holds documented UAP equity, transferred nothing.

dhs.label: DHS Science and Technology Directorate
dhs.why: Science and Technology Directorate is the DHS R&D component
dhs.note: The Under Secretary for Science and Technology is a DHS component head; the KONA BLUE paper identifies that office as the one that established the prospective program.

dhs.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
dhs.why: AARO's SAP review extended to the DHS control office enterprise
dhs.note: AARO names DHS as the third SAP control office enterprise with which it partnered - the only public confirmation that DHS operates a SAP control office at all.

dhs.label: KONA BLUE
dhs.why: DHS prospective special access program, terminated 10 February 2012
dhs.note: DHS Acting Deputy Secretary Kristie Canegallo transmitted the declassified Kona Blue records to the Deputy Secretary of Defense on 5 February 2024.

afosi.label: AFOSI Kirtland AFB UFO File (1980-1983)
afosi.why: AFOSI is the originating agency of the released Kirtland UFO file
afosi.note: The file covering the Manzano Weapons Storage Area intrusions was released under FOIA and is archived in full by NICAP.

afosi.label: YANKEE BLUE (alleged AFOSI indoctrination program)
afosi.why: AFOSI states it holds no records of any YANKEE BLUE investigation
afosi.note: The Wall Street Journal reported an alleged Air Force practice of showing fabricated recovered-craft material to personnel as a loyalty test; the Department first denied any such memo existed, then in December 2025 reopened the search.

afosi.label: Richard C. Doty
afosi.why: Doty served as an AFOSI special agent at the Kirtland detachment
afosi.note: The AFOSI Kirtland file and Doty's later New Mexico State Police personnel file, released in 321 pages, document his AFOSI service during the Manzano intrusion period.

afosi.label: United States Air Force
afosi.why: Air Force felony investigative and counterintelligence field agency
afosi.note: AFOSI is the Air Force's independent investigative agency with units 'located at most Air Force bases worldwide', covering espionage, terrorism and counterintelligence.

afosi.label: Garry Reid memoranda on AATIP and Elizondo, December 2017
afosi.why: Records an AFOSI inquiry into possible mishandling of classified material
afosi.note: AFOSI examined the video handling and concluded the material was unclassified, closing the matter. Elizondo later alleged the inquiry was orchestrated against him.

afosi.label: Kirtland AFB / Manzano Weapons Storage Area incident
afosi.why: AFOSI investigated the 1980 intrusions at the nuclear weapons storage area
afosi.note: The intrusions occurred at the Manzano Weapons Storage Area adjacent to Sandia National Laboratories; AFOSI ran the investigation and simultaneously ran the Bennewitz operation.

afosi.label: UAP Gerb - 'The Hidden Wing' (USAF structure)
afosi.why: Names AFOSI/PJ, the Office of Special Projects, as an operative node
afosi.note: Gerb identifies AFOSI/PJ and its former director Terry Phillips - now Northrop Grumman VP for Security - as a bridge between Air Force counterintelligence and contractor security.

afrl.label: National Air and Space Intelligence Center
afrl.why: Co-located at Wright-Patterson with the successor to the Foreign Technology Division
afrl.note: NASIC is the lineal successor to ATIC and FTD, the organisations that ran SIGN, GRUDGE and BLUE BOOK and exploited foreign aerospace materiel. AFRL and NASIC share the installation.

afrl.label: United States Air Force
afrl.why: Single Air Force science and technology laboratory, Wright-Patterson AFB
afrl.note: AFRL consolidated the Wright, Phillips, Rome and Armstrong laboratories and AFOSR at Wright-Patterson - the installation named in every retrieval account since 1947.

darpa.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
darpa.why: Named contributor to the 2021 ODNI Preliminary Assessment on UAP
darpa.note: ODNI's 25 June 2021 assessment names DARPA among the contributing elements, establishing that this agency produced or held UAP-relevant reporting.

darpa.label: Waived unacknowledged special access program (waived USAP)
darpa.why: The open counterfactual to a concealed breakthrough-technology effort
darpa.note: DARPA runs breakthrough research with named program managers, published solicitations and a public budget of $4.322 billion enacted for FY2026. Reasoning: a concealed eighty-year exploitation effort producing no transitions is either failing or structured specifically to avoid DARPA-style visibility.

oversight-congress.label: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)
oversight-congress.why: Contractor disclosure to Congress requires the approval of the office being disclosed about
oversight-congress.note: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.e bars any contractor entity, employee, representative or consultant from providing SAP material to members of Congress or staff 'without Director, DoD SAPCO, approval'. [Re-pointed from a collapsed duplicate, 14 Aug 2026.]

oversight-congress.label: Howard P. "Buck" McKeon
oversight-congress.note: Occupied one of the two House authorising seats in the section 119 channel across a change of party control, moving from ranking member to chairman without leaving the group.

oversight-congress.label: Program structure and organisational mapping
oversight-congress.why: the statutory oversight scheme, and the exception written into it
oversight-congress.note: Under 10 U.S.C. 119 the Secretary must report annually by 1 March to the four defense committees on every special access program, with a brief description, major milestones and costs - and under 119(e) may waive any of that on a case-by-case basis. The scheme and its exception are the same statute, which is why oversight belongs on the structural map rather than outside it.

oversight-congress.label: Thad Cochran
oversight-congress.why: Senate appropriations leadership in 2009, the year of the Reid SAP request
oversight-congress.note: The Senate half of the 119(e)(2) group in 2009 comprised only four people filling six seats: Levin and McCain on armed services, Inouye and Cochran holding both appropriations pairs. Harry Reid, who made the 2009 SAP request, held none of them.

oversight-congress.label: Waived SAP Notification Group
oversight-congress.why: the narrow aperture through which Congress sees waived DoD SAPs
oversight-congress.note: Section 119 contains no analogue to 50 U.S.C. 3093(g), which requires that the rest of the committee be told a limited notification occurred. Members of the defense committees outside the twelve are not informed that a waiver has been exercised.

oversight-congress.label: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)
oversight-congress.why: The audit Congress has, and cannot read
oversight-congress.note: The only formal evaluation of DoD's UAP conduct is classified in full, so the oversight value available to members outside the cleared channels is an unclassified summary.

oversight-congress.label: Anna Paulina Luna
oversight-congress.why: Chairwoman stated the HASC/HAC-D read-in gate on the record
oversight-congress.note: 'For a non-committee member to be allowed to view these documents and videos, individual members must be approved by the Chairman and Ranking Member of both HASC and HAC-D.'

oversight-congress.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
oversight-congress.why: 10 U.S.C. 119 annual SAP report to the four defense committees
oversight-congress.note: The Secretary of Defense must report annually by 1 March on every special access program, notify newly designated SAPs by 1 February, and give 30 days notice before initiating a new SAP.

oversight-congress.label: House Armed Services Committee
oversight-congress.note: Under 10 U.S.C. 119(e) the chairman and ranking minority member of each defense committee receive the waived program information and the waiver justification.

oversight-congress.label: Senate Armed Services Committee
oversight-congress.note: Same statutory provision; four committees, eight members.

oversight-congress.label: Waived unacknowledged special access program (waived USAP)
oversight-congress.why: The 10 U.S.C. 119(e) waiver reduces notification to eight members
oversight-congress.note: Where the Secretary waives reporting, the statute directs that the information and the justification go 'jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each of the defense committees'. This is the lawful mechanism by which a program can be hidden from the rest of Congress.

eop.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
eop.why: EO 14347 renamed the department by presidential signature
eop.note: Executive Order 14347 authorised 'Department of War' as a secondary designation and directed a recommendation within 60 days on permanent statutory renaming.

eop.label: Donald J. Trump
eop.why: Signed EO 14347 and issued the 2026 UAP release directives
eop.note: EO 14347 is signed; the February 2026 UAP directives are attested by contemporary reporting and by the Department's subsequent PURSUE releases.

eop.label: war.gov/UFO release portal
eop.why: Presidential direction produced the PURSUE release portal
eop.note: Following the February 2026 presidential directive to identify and release UAP files, the Department of War established the PURSUE portal at war.gov/UFO and published its first tranche on 8 May 2026.

eop.label: United States Department of Energy
eop.why: Restricted Data authority sits outside presidential EO declassification power
eop.note: Restricted Data under the Atomic Energy Act is classified by statute, not by executive order. A UAP declassification directive operating on EO 13526 information cannot reach it. Reasoning: the two classification systems have separate legal foundations.

nara-uap-collection.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
nara-uap-collection.why: ODNI transferred UAP records into the statutory collection
nara-uap-collection.note: NARA's press release nr25-07 names ODNI as one of four transferring agencies, alongside OSD, the FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

nara-uap-collection.label: United States Air Force
nara-uap-collection.why: Project BLUE BOOK records are held at the National Archives
nara-uap-collection.note: 94 rolls of 35mm microfilm, T-1206, permanently transferred to NARA - the Air Force is the one agency whose UFO records were fully accessioned, and they stop in 1969.

nara-uap-collection.label: Central Intelligence Agency
nara-uap-collection.why: Produced no records for the first statutory UAP transfer
nara-uap-collection.note: NARA's 24 April 2025 release named only ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. CIA, which holds documented UAP equity, transferred nothing.

nara-uap-collection.label: United States Department of Homeland Security
nara-uap-collection.why: Produced no records for the first statutory UAP transfer
nara-uap-collection.note: NARA's 24 April 2025 release named only ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. DHS, which holds documented UAP equity, transferred nothing.

nara-uap-collection.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
nara-uap-collection.why: Produced no records for the first statutory UAP transfer
nara-uap-collection.note: NARA's 24 April 2025 release named only ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. DIA, which holds documented UAP equity, transferred nothing.

nara-uap-collection.label: United States Department of Energy
nara-uap-collection.why: DOE produced nothing for the first statutory UAP records transfer
nara-uap-collection.note: NARA's 24 April 2025 release named ODNI, OSD, FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. DOE - which holds the weapons complex and performed AARO's materials analysis - was not among them.

nara-uap-collection.label: National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency
nara-uap-collection.why: Named 2021 UAP contributor that produced nothing for the statutory collection
nara-uap-collection.note: ODNI named NGA as a contributor of UAP reporting in June 2021; NARA's April 2025 transfer list does not include NGA, CIA, NSA, NRO, DIA, DOE or DHS.

nara-uap-collection.label: National Reconnaissance Office
nara-uap-collection.why: Produced no records for the first statutory UAP transfer
nara-uap-collection.note: NARA's 24 April 2025 release named only ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. NRO, which holds documented UAP equity, transferred nothing.

nara-uap-collection.label: National Security Agency
nara-uap-collection.why: Produced no records for the first statutory UAP transfer
nara-uap-collection.note: NARA's 24 April 2025 release named only ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. NSA, which holds documented UAP equity, transferred nothing.

nara-uap-collection.label: Information Security Oversight Office
nara-uap-collection.why: Both are components of the National Archives
nara-uap-collection.note: NARA hosts both the statutory UAP collection and the Information Security Oversight Office, the body responsible to the President for the classification system.

nara-uap-collection.label: FY2024 NDAA, Public Law 118-31 - Div. A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C (secs. 1841-1843), UAP Records Collection; Div. G (IAA FY2024) secs. 7341, 7343
nara-uap-collection.why: Collection created by sections 1841-1843 of the FY2024 NDAA
nara-uap-collection.note: The surviving remnant of the Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act. The 24 April 2025 release drew records from ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the NRC, with rolling additions - the statutory machinery any executive declassification directive must eventually run through.

nara-uap-collection.label: United States Senate
nara-uap-collection.why: Created by sections 1841-1843 of Public Law 118-31
nara-uap-collection.note: The collection is the surviving remnant of the Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act after the review board and eminent domain provisions were removed in conference.

nara-uap-collection.label: The annual DoD special access program report to Congress
nara-uap-collection.why: The statutory UAP records collection reaches records the SAP report describes
nara-uap-collection.note: Sections 1841-1843 of Public Law 118-31 require transmission of UAP records regardless of classification; the annual SAP report and waived-program list are agency records that would fall within the definition if UAP-related.

dhs-st.label: United States Department of Homeland Security
dhs-st.why: Science and Technology Directorate is the DHS R&D component
dhs-st.note: The Under Secretary for Science and Technology is a DHS component head; the KONA BLUE paper identifies that office as the one that established the prospective program.

dhs-st.label: KONA BLUE
dhs-st.why: DHS Under Secretary for S&T established KONA BLUE as a Prospective SAP in 2011
dhs-st.note: 'In 2011 the DHS Under Secretary for Science and Technology (S&T) established KONA BLUE as a PSAP' - the government's own words in the joint AARO/DHS paper.

nnsa.label: United States Department of Energy
nnsa.why: Semi-autonomous agency within DOE established by Congress in 2000
nnsa.note: NNSA describes itself as 'a semi-autonomous agency within the U.S. Department of Energy responsible for enhancing national security through the military application of nuclear science'.

nnsa.label: 50 U.S.C. 2426 — Congressional Oversight of DOE/NNSA Special Access Programs
nnsa.why: The Administrator may waive both the reports and the 30-day clock
nnsa.note: 50 U.S.C. 2426(e)(1) permits waiver of subsections (a), (b) and (c) and, uniquely, of the report-and-wait requirement in subsection (f).

dod-oig.label: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1 — DoD SAP Security Manual: General Procedures
dod-oig.why: SAP fraud and abuse complaints must not use collateral reporting channels
dod-oig.note: DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 4 para 3.a: SAP FWAC reporting 'will be accomplished through SAP channels. Collateral FWAC reporting channels must not be used for SAP information.'

dod-oig.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
dod-oig.why: Statutory internal oversight body within the Department
dod-oig.note: The DoD OIG is the Department's independent inspector general and the author of DODIG-2023-109, the only formal evaluation of the Department's UAP conduct.

dod-oig.label: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)
dod-oig.why: DoD OIG issued the only formal audit of the Department's UAP conduct
dod-oig.note: The evaluation examined 'how the DoD, military services, defense agencies, and military department counterintelligence organizations took intelligence, counterintelligence, and force protection actions to detect, report, collect, analyze, and identify UAP'. The full report is classified.

dod-oig.label: Luis D. Elizondo
dod-oig.why: Elizondo complaint to the DoD Inspector General, May 2021
dod-oig.note: Elizondo submitted a complaint to the DoD OIG alleging reprisal and improper handling; the OIG is the same body whose UAP evaluation remains classified.

ic-sapco.label: Program structure and organisational mapping
ic-sapco.why: the parallel control-office enterprise on the intelligence-community side of the same architecture
ic-sapco.note: The IC maintains its own special access and controlled access program control architecture under DNI authority, separate from the DoD SAP enterprise administered by DoD SAPCO. AARO's Historical Record Report Volume I confirms its existence in the government's own UAP record. The two-sided structure matters because a programme can be lodged on either side, and the oversight statutes differ.

ic-sapco.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
ic-sapco.why: AARO's SAP review extended to the IC control office enterprise
ic-sapco.note: Same AARO sentence, p. 34 of the Historical Record Report Volume I. The scope of what counted as 'pertinent' was set by the offices being reviewed.

ic-sapco.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
ic-sapco.why: IC-side SAP control office enterprise under DNI authority
ic-sapco.note: AARO names three distinct SAP control office enterprises - DoD, IC and DHS. The IC enterprise operates under the DNI's compartmentation authority and is not reported under 10 U.S.C. 119 to the defense committees.

waived-usap.label: James R. Clapper Jr.
waived-usap.why: USD(I) recommendation against SAP status for the AAWSAP effort, November 2009
waived-usap.note: Clapper as Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence recommended against establishing a special access program in response to Senator Reid's June 2009 request. The refusal is the documented instance of the SAP decision being made against, not for, concealment.

waived-usap.label: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)
waived-usap.why: DoDI 5205.11 retains the acknowledged / unacknowledged / waived taxonomy the 2024 directive omitted
waived-usap.note: DoDI 5205.11 para. 1.2.f, effective the same day as the reissued DoDD 5205.07: 'The Secretary of Defense may designate select unacknowledged SAPs as "waived" when it is determined that using standard procedures for reporting to Congress would adversely affect national security, pursuant to Section 119 of Title 10, United States Code. Waived SAPs remain subject to congressional oversight.' The glossary retains definitions of acknowledged SAP, unacknowledged SAP, SAP type and waived SAP, the last defined as 'A SAP for which the Secretary of Defense has waived applicable ... An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs.' The taxonomy was therefore not retired in September 2024; it was moved down one level from the directive into the instruction. Para. 3 further requires the SAP Oversight Committee's annual review to assess 'All waived DoD SAPs to determine the need for continued waived status' - an internal executive-branch review with no congressional trigger and no analogue in section 119.

waived-usap.label: Nancy Ruth Mace
waived-usap.why: Stated the compartmentation trap in a public hearing
waived-usap.note: 'only certain people know the name of the program, and if you do not know it, you cannot get the information.' This is the operational definition of an unacknowledged program from the oversight side.

waived-usap.label: Congressional oversight of special access programs
waived-usap.why: The 10 U.S.C. 119(e) waiver reduces notification to eight members
waived-usap.note: Where the Secretary waives reporting, the statute directs that the information and the justification go 'jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each of the defense committees'. This is the lawful mechanism by which a program can be hidden from the rest of Congress.

waived-usap.label: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)
waived-usap.why: contractor disclosure to Congress requires SAPCO approval
waived-usap.note: DoDD 5205.07 para. 3.1.g bars any DoD contractor entity, contractor employee, contractor representative or consultant from providing SAP material to any member of Congress or their staff without Director, DoD SAPCO approval, and requires all accessed personnel to notify SAPCO when briefing Congress.

waived-usap.label: Waived SAP Notification Group
waived-usap.why: the twelve members with statutory sight of a waived programme
waived-usap.note: Entitlement is bounded by characterisation: section 119 reaches only activity the Department treats as a DoD special access program. Activity held outside that characterisation is outside the group's statutory sight line entirely.

waived-usap.label: Information Security Oversight Office
waived-usap.why: NISP oversight is the only government-wide window on contractor-held classified work
waived-usap.note: ISOO is 'responsible to the President for policy and oversight of the Government-wide security classification system and the National Industrial Security Program'. A contractor-held program with no government sponsor of record would be visible, if anywhere, through NISP - and ISOO has never been directed at the UAP question.

waived-usap.label: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
waived-usap.why: The open counterfactual to a concealed breakthrough-technology effort
waived-usap.note: DARPA runs breakthrough research with named program managers, published solicitations and a public budget of $4.322 billion enacted for FY2026. Reasoning: a concealed eighty-year exploitation effort producing no transitions is either failing or structured specifically to avoid DARPA-style visibility.

dod-agencywide-audit.label: David L. Norquist
dod-agencywide-audit.why: Signed the FY2018 report announcing the first full-scope audit and its disclaimer
dod-agencywide-audit.note: Norquist, as USD(Comptroller)/CFO, wrote that 'In FY 2018, the Department underwent its first full-scope financial statement audit' and that the OIG 'issued a Disclaimer of Opinion'. Attested by his own signed message in the FY2018 Agency Financial Report.

dod-agencywide-audit.label: Office of Inspector General, Department of Defense / Department of War
dod-agencywide-audit.why: The OIG is the independent auditor issuing the annual opinion
dod-agencywide-audit.note: The DoD/DoW Office of Inspector General has issued the opinion on the agency-wide financial statements every year since FY2018, each time a disclaimer. Attested by the FY2018 AFR and by DOWIG-2026-081.

dod-agencywide-audit.label: DOWIG-2026-081 - The FY 2025 DoW Financial Statement Audit Explained
dod-agencywide-audit.why: The current authoritative statement of the audit result
dod-agencywide-audit.note: DOWIG-2026-081 records the eighth consecutive disclaimer, 26 material weaknesses, and more than $859 billion of unsupported adjustments in two quarters of FY2025. Attested by the report.

dod-agencywide-audit.label: GAO High-Risk List: DOD Financial Management
dod-agencywide-audit.why: Thirty years of Comptroller General certification that the books cannot produce reliable information
dod-agencywide-audit.note: DOD Financial Management remains on GAO's 2025 High-Risk List with status maintained, alongside four other DoD entries. Attested by GAO's own list.

dod-agencywide-audit.label: SFFAS 56 - Classified Activities (FASAB, 4 October 2018)
dod-agencywide-audit.why: Authorises modification of the same public financial reports the audit examines
dod-agencywide-audit.note: SFFAS 56 became effective for periods beginning after 30 September 2018 - the first period after the Department's first full-scope audit - and permits amounts to be presented in a different line item without narrative explanation. Attested by the Statement and by the FY2018 Agency Financial Report.

dod-agencywide-audit.label: Brett A. Mansfield
dod-agencywide-audit.why: Testified to the current figures on the congressional record
dod-agencywide-audit.note: Deputy Inspector General Mansfield told the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform on 13 May 2026 that unsupported adjustments exceeded $859 billion in the last two quarters of FY2025. Attested by his published oral statement.

dod-agencywide-audit.label: Reprogramming of DoD Appropriated Funds (DoD FMR Volume 3, Chapter 6; DD Form 1415 series)
dod-agencywide-audit.why: Below-threshold and internal reprogramming are where the unsupported adjustments live
dod-agencywide-audit.note: The FMR permits internal reprogramming on DD 1415-3 with no congressional action and below-threshold realignment with none at all; the FY2025 audit found more than $859 billion of adjustments in two quarters that could not be supported. The inference is that the undocumented volume is concentrated in the layer that generates no external record.

dod-agencywide-audit.label: The misappropriation allegation: Grusch's ICIG complaint and sworn testimony
dod-agencywide-audit.why: An unauditable ledger cannot disprove the allegation
dod-agencywide-audit.note: The Department's standing 'Universe of Transactions' material weakness means the complete population of its transactions is not established; no search of that population can therefore establish that funds did not flow to an undisclosed activity. Reasoned inference from the auditor's own definition of the weakness.

dowig-2026-081.label: DoD Agency-Wide Financial Statement Audit (FY2018-present)
dowig-2026-081.why: The current authoritative statement of the audit result
dowig-2026-081.note: DOWIG-2026-081 records the eighth consecutive disclaimer, 26 material weaknesses, and more than $859 billion of unsupported adjustments in two quarters of FY2025. Attested by the report.

dodig-2016-113.label: Office of Inspector General, Department of Defense / Department of War
dodig-2016-113.note: The report is the OIG's own audit of Army General Fund compilation adjustments for FY2015. Attested by the report.

dodig-2016-113.label: Summary Report on 'Unsupported Journal Voucher Adjustments' (Skidmore and Fitts, 2017)
dodig-2016-113.why: The single largest figure in the $21 trillion compilation comes from this report
dodig-2016-113.note: The Skidmore-Fitts compilation draws on published OIG reports including DODIG-2016-113, whose $6.5 trillion year-end unsupported adjustment figure is the largest single component. Attested by the authors' own supporting documentation index.

reprogramming-dd1415.label: Section 8005 Transfer Authority (annual DoD Appropriations Act)
reprogramming-dd1415.why: The administrative layer beneath the statutory transfer authority
reprogramming-dd1415.note: DoD FMR Volume 3 Chapter 6 implements reprogramming and transfer actions, including Below-Threshold Reprogramming which requires no approval or notification. Attested by the regulation.

The inference is that the undocumented volume is concentrated in the layer that generates no external record.

dodig.label: DoD Agency-Wide Financial Statement Audit (FY2018-present)
dodig.why: The OIG is the independent auditor issuing the annual opinion
dodig.note: The DoD/DoW Office of Inspector General has issued the opinion on the agency-wide financial statements every year since FY2018, each time a disclaimer. Attested by the FY2018 AFR and by DOWIG-2026-081.

dodig.label: Platte B. Moring III
dodig.note: The OIG leadership page identifies Platte B. Moring III as Inspector General of the Department of War. Attested by the office's own site.
