hearing-2025-09-09.label: Dylan Borland
hearing-2025-09-09.why: Testified before the House Oversight Task Force
hearing-2025-09-09.note: Borland alleges blacklisting and clearance-record manipulation and states he filed complaints with AARO in March 2023 and the ICIG in August 2023.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: George Knapp
hearing-2025-09-09.why: Journalist witness at the September 2025 hearing
hearing-2025-09-09.note: Knapp told the task force that documents paint a much different picture than the public, press and Congress have been told, and alleged UAP materials had been moved to private contractors.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: Jeffrey Nuccetelli
hearing-2025-09-09.why: Testified before the House Oversight Task Force
hearing-2025-09-09.note: Nuccetelli described 2003-2005 incursions at Vandenberg AFB during NRO launches and asserted each was documented and reported up the chain.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: Joe Spielberger
hearing-2025-09-09.why: Minority witness on whistleblower protection architecture
hearing-2025-09-09.note: Called by Ranking Member Crockett, who devoted her entire round to him.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: KLAS-TV (Las Vegas)
hearing-2025-09-09.why: Knapp testified as KLAS-TV chief investigative reporter
hearing-2025-09-09.note: George Knapp, identifying himself in his statement for the record as 'Chief Investigative Reporter for KLAS-TV in Las Vegas', testified under oath before the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability UAP Task Force hearing of 9 September 2025 chaired by Rep. Luna.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: Vandenberg Space Force Base, California
hearing-2025-09-09.why: The Vandenberg incidents entered the congressional record in September 2025
hearing-2025-09-09.note: Nuccetelli named AARO and the FBI as custodians of the official Air Force records for specific dated incidents at a named installation - a checkable custody claim Congress has not pursued to production.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
hearing-2025-09-09.why: Witnesses testified AARO holds unreleased UAP video
hearing-2025-09-09.note: The testimony that AARO possesses additional video records is the specific factual basis for Luna's April 2026 letter and, through it, for the video composition of the PURSUE tranches.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: Eric Burlison
hearing-2025-09-09.why: presented unreleased footage of a drone Hellfire engagement with an orb off Yemen, October 2024
hearing-2025-09-09.note: A sitting member introducing military engagement footage that AARO had not published is a direct measure of the office's disclosure posture.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: H.R. 5060 - UAP Whistleblower Protection Act (119th Congress)
hearing-2025-09-09.why: hearing findings underwrite the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act
hearing-2025-09-09.note: The Task Force found witnesses face career damage and retaliation requiring congressional safeguards; the bill was on the agenda in the run-up to the hearing.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: Eric Burlison
hearing-2025-09-09.why: Unveiled the alleged Hellfire-versus-orb footage
hearing-2025-09-09.note: Burlison presented previously unreleased footage said to show a US military drone firing a Hellfire missile at a high-speed orb off Yemen in October 2024.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: AARO Official UAP Imagery releases (PR series)
hearing-2025-09-09.why: Video releases began five weeks after testimony that AARO was withholding video
hearing-2025-09-09.note: The timing and the scale together read as minimum compliance: seven short clips in response to sworn testimony that the office holds an unreleased video archive.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: PURSUE Task Force
hearing-2025-09-09.why: the executive channel that competes with the congressional one
hearing-2025-09-09.note: Burlison warned that it is uncertain whether the NDA abrogation applies to testimony given to Congress before referral to the executive branch - a witness routed to PURSUE may be routed away from a hearing room.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: Burlison production demand to MITRE (22 May 2026)
hearing-2025-09-09.why: acts on the hearing's fourth finding
hearing-2025-09-09.note: The September 2025 Oversight wrap-up recorded that UAP materials had been moved to private contractors, complicating oversight and FOIA access; the MITRE demand is the first instrument aimed at that finding.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act (Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA)
hearing-2025-09-09.why: The FOIA-reach finding is the antecedent of the 2026 contractor-disclosure amendment
hearing-2025-09-09.note: The Task Force found UAP spending flows to entities outside FOIA reach; the amendment adopted 23 July 2026 extends disclosure obligations to government contractors. Reasoning: direct correspondence between the finding and the remedy.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: House Oversight Task Force hearing: 'Mind Control and Accountability: Uncovering the Truth of the CIA's MKULTRA Project', 30 June 2026
hearing-2025-09-09.why: No UAP hearing was held in the eleven months between them
hearing-2025-09-09.note: The period covers the February 2026 release directive, five PURSUE tranches, the late FY2025 annual report, the NDA waiver and the Burlison amendment - all executive or floor action without contemporaneous testimony. Reasoning: House Oversight published hearing index.

hearing-2025-09-09.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
hearing-2025-09-09.why: Hearing, then letter, then release - the causal spine of 2026
hearing-2025-09-09.note: The sequence runs from sworn testimony that video was being withheld, through a subcommittee chair's letter to the Secretary, to a release channel that bypassed the office entirely.

hearing-2023-04-19.label: Sean M. Kirkpatrick
hearing-2023-04-19.why: sole DoD witness; testified AARO held 650+ cases
hearing-2023-04-19.note: The only open Senate hearing on AARO under its first director, published as S.Hrg. 118-648.

hearing-2023-04-19.label: Kirsten E. Gillibrand
hearing-2023-04-19.note: Gillibrand chaired the Senate Armed Services Emerging Threats and Capabilities Subcommittee for both AARO oversight hearings.

hearing-2023-04-19.label: Sean M. Kirkpatrick
hearing-2023-04-19.note: S. Hrg. 118-648 lists Kirkpatrick as the only witness.

ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.label: Enacted Statute
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.why: the statutory root of the modern apparatus, codified at 50 U.S.C. 3373
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.note: Sec. 1683 of P.L. 117-81, signed 27 December 2021, directed establishment within 180 days of an office to carry out the duties of the UAP Task Force, with enumerated duties reaching beyond analysis into governance. Everything later in the enacted corpus amends or builds on what this section created.

ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.label: IAA FY2025 Title LXVIII — Secs. 6801-6802 (P.L. 118-159)
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.why: GAO review of AARO's implementation of Sec. 1683
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.note: Sec. 6801 of P.L. 118-159 commissions a Comptroller General review with a report due on a mutually agreed timeframe rather than a date.

ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.label: Kirsten E. Gillibrand
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.why: Author of the founding AARO authority
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.note: Sec. 1683 of P.L. 117-81, codified at 50 U.S.C. 3373, is the statute every later UAP provision cross-references.

ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.label: FY2022 NDAA, Public Law 117-81, Sec. 1683 (50 U.S.C. 3373) - statutory UAP office
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.why: Sec. 1683 is the UAP-office provision of P.L. 117-81
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.note: Section 1683 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117-81, 27 December 2021) is titled 'Establishment of office, organizational structure, and authorities to address unidentified aerial phenomena.'

ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.label: FY2023 NDAA, Public Law 117-263 - Sec. 1673 (50 U.S.C. 3373b) UAP reporting/whistleblower protection; Div. F secs. 6802-6803 establishing AARO
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.note: IAA FY2023 sec. 6802(a) rewrites sec. 1683 in full.

ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.label: FY2023 NDAA Sec. 1673 (P.L. 117-263; 50 U.S.C. 3373b)
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.why: Sec. 1673 builds the reporting channel on the Sec. 1683 office
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.note: Sec. 1673 of P.L. 117-263 defines 'Office' by reference to Sec. 1683(a) and creates the authorized reporting mechanism administered by it.

ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.label: FY2024 NDAA, Public Law 118-31 - Div. A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C (secs. 1841-1843), UAP Records Collection; Div. G (IAA FY2024) secs. 7341, 7343
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.why: Sec. 1841 defines UAP by cross-reference to 50 U.S.C. 3373
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.note: The enacted collection statute borrows its definition from Gillibrand's section, but miscites it as 'section 1673(n)(8) of the NDAA for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117-81)' — conflating two different Acts.

ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.label: FY2026 NDAA, Public Law 119-60 - secs. 1671-1673, NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept briefings and UAP classification-guide accounting
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.why: FY2026 amends Sec. 1683(l) to add intercept briefings
ndaa-fy2022-sec-1683.note: Sec. 1671 of P.L. 119-60 adds a new paragraph (5) requiring NORAD and NORTHCOM intercept detail in AARO briefings, reaching back to 1 January 2004.

ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.label: FY2022 NDAA Sec. 1683 (P.L. 117-81; 50 U.S.C. 3373)
ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.why: Sec. 1673 builds the reporting channel on the Sec. 1683 office
ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.note: Sec. 1673 of P.L. 117-263 defines 'Office' by reference to Sec. 1683(a) and creates the authorized reporting mechanism administered by it.

ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226; Division G of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA)
ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.why: Statutory NDA-voiding precedent behind the Act's whistleblower posture
ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.note: Sec. 1673(b)(1)(A) had already established that an authorized disclosure 'shall not be subject to a nondisclosure agreement'; the UAPDA extends that logic to records and material.

ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.label: David Charles Grusch
ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.why: The statute legislates the exact programme category he alleges
ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.note: Sec. 1673(a)(1)(B) creates a reporting channel for programmes involving 'material retrieval, material analysis, reverse engineering' — Congress legislating for a category of activity it does not officially acknowledge.

ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.label: IAA FY2024 Sec. 1102 — contractor turn-in of 'non-earth origin or exotic' UAP material
ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.why: Gag-order census feeds the contractor turn-in
ndaa-fy2023-sec-1673.note: Sec. 1673(b)(3) requires agencies and contractors to deliver copies of all UAP nondisclosure orders to AARO; Sec. 1102(d) would have required the same parties to deliver the material itself.

ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Review Board
ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.why: Postponement authority returned to the original classifier
ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.note: Sec. 1843(a) vests the clear-and-convincing determination in 'the original classification authority' — the very offices the Review Board was created to review.

ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection (NARA Record Group 615)
ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.why: Secs. 1841-1843 created RG 615 at the National Archives
ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.note: The collection is the only concrete institution produced by the entire UAPDA fight.

ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.label: National Archives Record Group 615 - UAP Records Collection
ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.note: Record Group 615 exists under sections 1841-1843 of the FY2024 NDAA, which require NARA to establish the collection and each agency to review, identify and organise its UAP records.

ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226; Division G of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA)
ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.why: Fifteen sections reduced to three in conference
ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.note: Secs. 9001-9015 as passed by the Senate became Secs. 1841-1843 as enacted; the Review Board, Board personnel, record review, eminent domain, court-sealed materials and the $20,000,000 authorization have no enacted counterpart.

ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.label: Charles E. Schumer
ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.why: Publicly called the removal of the Review Board an outrage
ndaa-fy2024-subtitle-c.note: Schumer said it was 'really an outrage the House didn't work with us on adopting our proposal for a review board' after the conference product removed it.

uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.label: FY2024 NDAA, Public Law 118-31 - Div. A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C (secs. 1841-1843), UAP Records Collection; Div. G (IAA FY2024) secs. 7341, 7343
uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.why: No enacted statute contains the eminent domain language
uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.note: P.L. 118-31, P.L. 118-159 and P.L. 119-60 contain zero instances of 'eminent domain' in any UAP provision.

uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.label: IAA FY2024 Sec. 1102 — contractor turn-in of 'non-earth origin or exotic' UAP material
uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.why: Two independent Senate routes at the same private holdings
uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.note: Sec. 9010 takes the material by condemnation; Sec. 1102 compels its surrender by cutting off contract funding and granting immunity. Both passed the Senate on 27 July 2023; both were removed.

uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226; Division G of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA)
uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.note: Section 9010(a) of Division G is the eminent domain command; it is the only provision in the Act that reaches physical material rather than records.

uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.label: Michael R. Turner
uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.why: Named as demanding removal of the eminent domain provision
uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain.note: Daniel Sheehan, who lobbied the conference, states Turner attacked the eminent domain clause and the subpoena power first and demanded both be struck; the enacted text lacks exactly those two things.

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.label: Senate Select Committee on Intelligence
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.why: SSCI produced the contractor turn-in language
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.note: Sec. 1102 rode in the Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2024, Division M of the engrossed Senate bill.

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.label: Mark R. Warner
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.why: Author of the IAA FY2024 contractor turn-in
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.note: Warner submitted S.Amdt. 666 on 13 July 2023, which became Division M of the engrossed bill containing Sec. 1102.

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.label: P.L. 118-31 Sec. 7343 — the truncated funding limitation
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.why: Reduced in conference to a bare funding limitation
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.note: Subsections (b), (d), (e) and (g) of Sec. 1102 — the sense of Congress, the contractor turn-in, the immunity grant and the notice to Congress — have no enacted counterpart in Sec. 7343.

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.label: Section 9010(a) — Exercise of Eminent Domain
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.why: Two independent Senate routes at the same private holdings
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.note: Sec. 9010 takes the material by condemnation; Sec. 1102 compels its surrender by cutting off contract funding and granting immunity. Both passed the Senate on 27 July 2023; both were removed.

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.label: P.L. 118-31 Sec. 7343 — the truncated funding limitation
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.why: Dangling cross-reference dates the excision to conference
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.note: Enacted Sec. 7343(c) refers to 'contracts covered by such instruction' with no antecedent; the DoDI 3204.01 citation it depended on was deleted with Sec. 1102(f)(1).

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.label: Funding Channels
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.why: the Senate committee text that would have closed the channel at the contractor end
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.note: As reported by the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, the IAA FY2024 UAP provision would have required any person currently or formerly under federal contract holding UAP material or information derived from the Government to notify the AARO Director within 60 days and to make it available within 180 days, alongside the funding and IR&D limitations. Tier 2 rather than Tier 1 because the enacted counterpart differed substantially from the Senate-approved text, and because the section number carried on this node does not match the reported bill (see unresolved).

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.label: Legislative Process (proposed and pending)
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.why: a committee-reported provision that did not survive conference in the form reported
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.note: The Senate Select Committee on Intelligence's UAP provision in the reported IAA FY2024 would have compelled contractor turn-in of UAP material within 180 days. The enacted counterpart in Division G of P.L. 118-31 differed substantially from the text approved by Senate committees and by the full Senate. Its home is the process domain because what is interesting about it is the gap between what was reported and what was enacted.

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.label: Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2024 (Div. G of PL 118-31) - secs. 7341, 7343
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.why: section node of this act (section number needs verification)
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.note: The board's section node is filed under this act. Caution: the contractor turn-in language (persons holding UAP material or 'non-earth origin or exotic' material to notify AARO and make it available within 180 days) is Sec. 1104 of S.2103 as reported by SSCI on 22 June 2023; the enacted Division G UAP sections are numbered 7341 and 7343. The '1102' designation in the node id is not confirmed against either text.

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.label: FY2023 NDAA Sec. 1673 (P.L. 117-263; 50 U.S.C. 3373b)
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.why: Gag-order census feeds the contractor turn-in
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.note: Sec. 1673(b)(3) requires agencies and contractors to deliver copies of all UAP nondisclosure orders to AARO; Sec. 1102(d) would have required the same parties to deliver the material itself.

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.label: David Charles Grusch
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.why: Warner's contractor turn-in targets the same private holders
iaa-fy2024-sec-1102.note: Sec. 1102 orders contractors to surrender a list of 'non-earth origin or exotic' material, the category Grusch alleged had been moved to industry.

pl118-31-sec-7343.label: P.L. 118-31 Sec. 1687 — limitation on funds for unreported programs
pl118-31-sec-7343.why: Twin limitations on the intelligence and defence sides
pl118-31-sec-7343.note: Sec. 7343 applies the same bar to intelligence funds through the DNI that Sec. 1687 applies to DoD funds through the Secretary of Defense.

pl118-31-sec-7343.label: IAA FY2024 Sec. 1102 — contractor turn-in of 'non-earth origin or exotic' UAP material
pl118-31-sec-7343.why: Reduced in conference to a bare funding limitation
pl118-31-sec-7343.note: Subsections (b), (d), (e) and (g) of Sec. 1102 — the sense of Congress, the contractor turn-in, the immunity grant and the notice to Congress — have no enacted counterpart in Sec. 7343.

pl118-31-sec-7343.label: IAA FY2024 Sec. 1102 — contractor turn-in of 'non-earth origin or exotic' UAP material
pl118-31-sec-7343.why: Dangling cross-reference dates the excision to conference
pl118-31-sec-7343.note: Enacted Sec. 7343(c) refers to 'contracts covered by such instruction' with no antecedent; the DoDI 3204.01 citation it depended on was deleted with Sec. 1102(f)(1).

iaa24-sec7343.label: NDAA FY2024 Section 1687 - Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs
iaa24-sec7343.why: The same bar enacted twice, once for SECDEF and once for the DNI
iaa24-sec7343.note: Sections 1687 and 7343 of P.L. 118-31 impose parallel funding limitations, the first running through the Secretary of Defense, the second through the Director of National Intelligence. Attested by the enacted text of both.

iaa24-sec7343.label: National Intelligence Program (NIP)
iaa24-sec7343.why: Binds funds authorised by the intelligence division
iaa24-sec7343.note: Section 7343(b) bars use of funds authorised by Division F for UAP activity under special or restricted access limitation absent DNI disclosure to six committees and congressional leadership. Attested by the statute.

iaa-fy2024-7343.label: FY2024 NDAA sec. 1687 — Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs
iaa-fy2024-7343.why: Twin provisions covering the defense and intelligence sides of the same gap
iaa-fy2024-7343.note: Both were enacted in Public Law 118-31 on 22 December 2023 and both reference activities described in an AARO report released in fiscal year 2024.

iaa-fy2024-7343.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
iaa-fy2024-7343.why: Imposes the same funding condition on the Director of National Intelligence
iaa-fy2024-7343.note: FY2024 IAA sec. 7343(b) bars obligation of division funds for UAP activity under special or restricted access limitation absent DNI disclosure to six committees and four leaders.

pl118-31-sec-1687.label: FY2024 NDAA, Public Law 118-31 - Div. A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C (secs. 1841-1843), UAP Records Collection; Div. G (IAA FY2024) secs. 7341, 7343
pl118-31-sec-1687.why: Sec. 1687 is the enacted funding bar on undisclosed UAP SAPs
pl118-31-sec-1687.note: The only enacted provision that conditions money on disclosure of special access UAP activity, including the independent research and development indirect-cost bar.

pl118-31-sec-1687.label: FY2026 NDAA, Public Law 119-60 - secs. 1671-1673, NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept briefings and UAP classification-guide accounting
pl118-31-sec-1687.why: Not renewed; the funding bar has lapsed since FY2024
pl118-31-sec-1687.note: Sec. 1687 restricts only funds authorised by the FY2024 Act; neither P.L. 118-159 nor P.L. 119-60 contains the phrase 'special access or restricted access'.

pl118-31-sec-1687.label: House Armed Services Committee
pl118-31-sec-1687.why: Retained remedy routes back to the committees
pl118-31-sec-1687.note: Sec. 1687 does not open anything to the public; it compels description to the defence and intelligence committees and congressional leadership.

pl118-31-sec-1687.label: P.L. 118-31 Sec. 7343 — the truncated funding limitation
pl118-31-sec-1687.why: Twin limitations on the intelligence and defence sides
pl118-31-sec-1687.note: Sec. 7343 applies the same bar to intelligence funds through the DNI that Sec. 1687 applies to DoD funds through the Secretary of Defense.

ndaa24-sec1687.label: IAA FY2024 Section 7343 - Funding Limitations Relating to Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena
ndaa24-sec1687.why: The same bar enacted twice, once for SECDEF and once for the DNI
ndaa24-sec1687.note: Sections 1687 and 7343 of P.L. 118-31 impose parallel funding limitations, the first running through the Secretary of Defense, the second through the Director of National Intelligence. Attested by the enacted text of both.

ndaa24-sec1687.label: Independent Research and Development (IR&D) as a funding channel
ndaa24-sec1687.why: Statutory bar on UAP-related IR&D as an allowable indirect cost
ndaa24-sec1687.note: Section 1687(b) provides that IR&D funding relating to UAP shall not be allowable as an indirect expense for contracts covered by DoD Instruction 3204.01 unless disclosed to the appropriate committees and leadership. Attested by the enacted statute.

ndaa24-sec1687.label: NDAA FY2026 UAP provisions (Secs. 1671-1673)
ndaa24-sec1687.why: The funding bar was not renewed; only the IR&D provision survives
ndaa24-sec1687.note: Section 1687(a) applied only to funds authorised by the FY2024 Act; a full-text search of the FY2025 and FY2026 NDAAs returns no equivalent provision. Section 1687(b), codified as a 50 U.S.C. 3373 note, has no fiscal-year limit. Attested by the enacted texts of all three Acts.

ndaa-fy2024-1687.label: DoD Instruction 3204.01 - Oversight of Independent Research and Development
ndaa-fy2024-1687.why: Targets contractor independent research and development as a concealment route
ndaa-fy2024-1687.note: Sec. 1687(b) makes UAP-related IR&D unallowable as indirect expense under DoDI 3204.01 unless the material is made available to the committees and leadership.

ndaa-fy2024-1687.label: FY2024 Intelligence Authorization Act sec. 7343 — Funding Limitations Relating to UAP
ndaa-fy2024-1687.why: Twin provisions covering the defense and intelligence sides of the same gap
ndaa-fy2024-1687.note: Both were enacted in Public Law 118-31 on 22 December 2023 and both reference activities described in an AARO report released in fiscal year 2024.

ndaa-fy2024-1687.label: Waived Unacknowledged SAP (waived USAP) — the mechanism
ndaa-fy2024-1687.why: Cuts off funding for UAP activity held under special or restricted access unless disclosed
ndaa-fy2024-1687.note: FY2024 NDAA sec. 1687(a) conditions obligation of funds on the Secretary of Defense providing details to the defense and intelligence committees and congressional leadership.

ndaa-fy2024-1687.label: Waived Unacknowledged SAP (waived USAP) — the mechanism
ndaa-fy2024-1687.why: sec. 1687(a) bars FY2024 funds for UAP activity under special or restricted access absent disclosure

iaa-fy2025-title-lxviii.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2024 (S.Amdt. 2610 to S. 4638)
iaa-fy2025-title-lxviii.why: Never called up; FY2025 enacted with no disclosure regime
iaa-fy2025-title-lxviii.note: The amendment was 'ordered to lie on the table' and received no vote; P.L. 118-159's only UAP content is a GAO review and a sunset on audit briefings.

iaa-fy2025-title-lxviii.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
iaa-fy2025-title-lxviii.why: Sunsets GAO audit briefings on the Historical Record Report
iaa-fy2025-title-lxviii.note: Sec. 6802 terminates quarterly audit information-sharing 90 days after the final volume and semiannual congressional briefings 180 days after.

iaa-fy2025-title-lxviii.label: FY2022 NDAA Sec. 1683 (P.L. 117-81; 50 U.S.C. 3373)
iaa-fy2025-title-lxviii.why: GAO review of AARO's implementation of Sec. 1683
iaa-fy2025-title-lxviii.note: Sec. 6801 of P.L. 118-159 commissions a Comptroller General review with a report due on a mutually agreed timeframe rather than a date.

ndaa-fy2026-uap-provisions.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
ndaa-fy2026-uap-provisions.why: statutorily compels the intercept record and an accounting of classification guides
ndaa-fy2026-uap-provisions.note: Congress required AARO to brief on NORAD/USNORTHCOM UAP intercepts since 2004 and to account for the security classification guides it uses - a legislative finding that the office has been withholding and overclassifying.

ndaa-fy2026-uap-provisions.label: DoD OIG - Evaluation of the DoD's Actions Regarding Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (DODIG-2023-109)
ndaa-fy2026-uap-provisions.why: the data-sharing streamlining provision answers the IG's 2023 reporting-requirement finding
ndaa-fy2026-uap-provisions.note: The IG found components were not required to report to AARO; two years later Congress legislated to streamline agency data sharing into AARO investigations.

ndaa26-uap-provisions.label: NDAA FY2024 Section 1687 - Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs
ndaa26-uap-provisions.why: The funding bar was not renewed; only the IR&D provision survives
ndaa26-uap-provisions.note: Section 1687(a) applied only to funds authorised by the FY2024 Act; a full-text search of the FY2025 and FY2026 NDAAs returns no equivalent provision. Section 1687(b), codified as a 50 U.S.C. 3373 note, has no fiscal-year limit. Attested by the enacted texts of all three Acts.

fy2026-ndaa-uap-provisions.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
fy2026-ndaa-uap-provisions.why: Directs AARO to brief on NORAD/NORTHCOM UAP intercepts back to 2004 and account for its classification guides
fy2026-ndaa-uap-provisions.note: The first legislative attempt to reach the classification guides themselves, which govern what may be said about a sighting before any declassification question arises.

fy2026-ndaa-uap-provisions.label: Christopher K. Mellon
fy2026-ndaa-uap-provisions.note: The FY2026 NDAA's three UAP provisions reflect recommendations from Mellon and the Disclosure Foundation.

fy2026-ndaa-uap-provisions.label: NORAD and US Northern Command
fy2026-ndaa-uap-provisions.note: AARO must brief Congress on the number, location and nature of UAP intercepts by NORAD and US Northern Command since 2004 and the data collected during them.

fy2026-ndaa-uap-provisions.label: Christopher K. Mellon
fy2026-ndaa-uap-provisions.why: Two of the three provisions mirror recommendations he championed
fy2026-ndaa-uap-provisions.note: Per Disclosure Foundation executive director Jordan Flowers.

usc-10-119.label: KONA BLUE
usc-10-119.why: A program can be designed and formally requested without ever crossing the congressional reporting threshold
usc-10-119.note: AARO: 'KONA BLUE was not reported to Congress at that time because it was never established as a SAP and, therefore, did not meet the threshold for congressional reporting.' The government states the gap in its own defence.

usc-10-119.label: Enacted Statute
usc-10-119.why: codified permanent law - the only statute governing what Congress is told about special access programs
usc-10-119.note: Added by sec. 1132(a)(1) of the NDAA for FY1988-89, P.L. 100-180, signed 4 December 1987, and amended five times since. It is positive law in title 10 rather than a standalone provision, which places it at the centre of the enacted corpus this domain isolates.

usc-10-119.label: The defense committees (10 U.S.C. 119(g))
usc-10-119.why: Reports run to six named congressional bodies and no others
usc-10-119.note: 119(g) enumerates SASC, Senate Appropriations and its Defense Subcommittee, HASC, House Appropriations and its Subcommittee on Defense.

usc-10-119.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
usc-10-119.why: Imposes the entire SAP reporting duty on the Secretary of Defense
usc-10-119.note: Section 119 runs to 'the Secretary of Defense' alone; no subordinate official, program manager or contractor is an obligor under it.

usc-10-119.label: Executive Order 13526 — Classified National Security Information
usc-10-119.why: Creates the programs the statute then reports on
usc-10-119.note: E.O. 13526 sec. 4.3 is the source of authority to create a SAP; 10 U.S.C. 119 only prescribes what must be told to Congress afterwards.

usc-10-119.label: The four SAP reporting regimes and the seams between them
usc-10-119.why: DoD regime: weakest waiver of the four
usc-10-119.note: 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) narrows waived reporting to the chairman and ranking minority member of each defense committee.

usc-10-119.label: NDAA FY2024 Sec. 1687 - Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs
usc-10-119.why: Sec. 1687 is Congress overriding the Sec. 119 waiver for one subject matter
usc-10-119.note: Where Sec. 119(e) permits reporting to only the chairman and ranking member of each defense committee, Sec. 1687 conditions the money itself on disclosure to both intelligence committees and all four congressional leaders for UAP activity specifically.

usc-10-119.label: Public Law 100-180 sec. 1132 — creation of SAP congressional oversight (4 Dec 1987)
usc-10-119.note: Source credit to 10 U.S.C. 119: added by Pub. L. 100-180, div. A, title XI, sec. 1132(a)(1), 101 Stat. 1151.

usc-10-119.label: 10 U.S.C. 119(e) — Waiver of SAP Reporting (the 'waived SAP' authority)
usc-10-119.why: Subsection (e) is the escape hatch inside the reporting statute
usc-10-119.note: 119(e)(1) permits waiver of any requirement under (a), (b) or (c) on the Secretary's own national-security determination, case by case.

usc-10-119.label: 50 U.S.C. 3348 — Reports Relating to Certain SAPs and Similar Programs
usc-10-119.why: Supplies the statutory definition of 'special access program' that title 10 lacks
usc-10-119.note: 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(3) defines the term; 10 U.S.C. 119 uses it throughout without defining it. Section 3091a(b)(2)(A) cross-references 3348(g) for the definition.

usc-10-119.label: Waived SAP Notification Group
usc-10-119.why: created by 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) and defined by 119(g)
usc-10-119.note: Section 119 was added by Pub. L. 100-180 div. A title XI sec. 1132(a)(1), 4 December 1987. Subsection (e)(2) directs waived-SAP information and the waiver justification jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each defense committee; subsection (g) supplies the six-body definition of 'defense committees' used by the section.

usc-10-119.label: David Charles Grusch
usc-10-119.why: Grusch identified the Sec. 119 waiver as the statutory route by which programs escape committee reporting
usc-10-119.note: Grusch described the Secretary's ability to waive congressional reporting and the Gang of Eight backstop for a waived unacknowledged SAP; subsection (e) of the statute contains exactly the waiver he described.

usc-10-119.label: Bechtel Nevada Corporation
usc-10-119.why: DOE contractor custody sits outside the DoD special access program reporting regime entirely
usc-10-119.note: Atomic Energy Act Restricted Data authorities are a separate statutory classification scheme; material held under them by a DOE management and operating contractor is not reachable by the Sec. 119 reporting obligations Congress relies on. No document places UAP material under DOE authority.

usc-10-119.label: Alternative Compensatory Control Measures (ACCM)
usc-10-119.why: ACCM sits below the definitional trigger of every SAP reporting statute
usc-10-119.note: 32 CFR 117.3(b) defines ACCM as the case 'where SAP controls are not required'; the reporting statutes are triggered only by the term 'special access program'.

usc-10-119.label: Booz Allen Hamilton
usc-10-119.why: Security-support primes administer the compartmentation the statute is supposed to make visible
usc-10-119.note: Reasoning: Sec. 119 places the reporting duty on the Secretary of Defense, but the underlying program-protection and access records are held by contractors with no independent reporting obligation to Congress.

usc-10-119.label: Executive Order 13526 — Classified National Security Information
usc-10-119.why: Sec. 4.3(c): nothing in the order supersedes any requirement made by or under 10 U.S.C. 119

usc-10-119.label: 50 U.S.C. 3348 — Reports Relating to Certain SAPs and Similar Programs
usc-10-119.why: 3348(g)(2)(B)(i) writes DoD out of the government-wide SAP statute and points to 10 U.S.C. 119

usc-10-119e.label: The defense committees (10 U.S.C. 119(g))
usc-10-119e.why: Waiver narrows the audience to chairman and ranking minority member of each defense committee
usc-10-119e.note: 119(e)(2) directs the waived information and its justification 'jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each of the defense committees'.

usc-10-119e.label: The Gang of Eight and the limited-notification convention
usc-10-119e.why: The waived-SAP notification convention mirrors, but is weaker than, the covert action rule
usc-10-119e.note: 119(e)(2) reaches chairs and ranking members of the defense committees with no 180-day widening requirement; 50 U.S.C. 3093(c)(5)(B) requires reconsideration of limited access within 180 days.

usc-10-119e.label: 10 U.S.C. 119 — Special Access Programs: Congressional Oversight
usc-10-119e.why: Subsection (e) is the escape hatch inside the reporting statute
usc-10-119e.note: 119(e)(1) permits waiver of any requirement under (a), (b) or (c) on the Secretary's own national-security determination, case by case.

usc-10-119e.label: Waived Unacknowledged SAP (waived USAP) — the mechanism
usc-10-119e.why: The waived category exists only because subsection (e) exists
usc-10-119e.note: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Enclosure 2 para 5 permits the Secretary to 'designate select unacknowledged SAPs as waived in accordance with Reference (c)' - Reference (c) being 10 U.S.C. 119.

usc-10-119e.label: Waived Unacknowledged SAP (waived USAP) — the mechanism
usc-10-119e.why: 119(e) is the waiver that defines a waived SAP

waived-usap-mechanism.label: The annual DoD special access program report to Congress
waived-usap-mechanism.why: A waived program is precisely a program removed from the annual report
waived-usap-mechanism.note: 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(1) permits waiver of the requirement that certain information be included in the report; DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.h keeps the substitute material in DoD custody.

waived-usap-mechanism.label: The HASC/HAC-D special access program read-in gate
waived-usap-mechanism.why: The read-in gate members describe is the policy text of paragraph 4.f
waived-usap-mechanism.note: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.f is the written rule that members of the defense and intelligence committees are authorised access to DoD SAPs 'except for waived programs'.

waived-usap-mechanism.label: Senior Review Group (DoD SAP governance)
waived-usap-mechanism.why: Every waived program is reviewed once a year by a named standing body
waived-usap-mechanism.note: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 3 para 3.b(4) assigns the SRG the annual review of all waived DoD SAPs and recommendations on continued waived status.

waived-usap-mechanism.label: Waived SAP Notification Group
waived-usap-mechanism.why: sole statutory recipient of waived-SAP notification
waived-usap-mechanism.note: The waiver mechanism at 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(1) does not eliminate reporting; it redirects it. Whatever the Secretary withholds from the report goes instead to these twelve members under 119(e)(2), together with the justification for withholding.

waived-usap-mechanism.label: Information Security Oversight Office
waived-usap-mechanism.why: The only external body with a claim of access, and the claim is conditional
waived-usap-mechanism.note: E.O. 13526 sec. 4.3(b) affords the ISOO Director access to SAPs 'consistent with the policies and procedures directed by the President'.

waived-usap-mechanism.label: FY2024 NDAA sec. 1687 — Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs
waived-usap-mechanism.why: Cuts off funding for UAP activity held under special or restricted access unless disclosed
waived-usap-mechanism.note: FY2024 NDAA sec. 1687(a) conditions obligation of funds on the Secretary of Defense providing details to the defense and intelligence committees and congressional leadership.

waived-usap-mechanism.label: 10 U.S.C. 119(e) — Waiver of SAP Reporting (the 'waived SAP' authority)
waived-usap-mechanism.why: The waived category exists only because subsection (e) exists
waived-usap-mechanism.note: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Enclosure 2 para 5 permits the Secretary to 'designate select unacknowledged SAPs as waived in accordance with Reference (c)' - Reference (c) being 10 U.S.C. 119.

waived-usap-mechanism.label: Acknowledged, unacknowledged and waived — the three states of a DoD SAP
waived-usap-mechanism.why: Waived is the terminal state of the taxonomy
waived-usap-mechanism.note: DoDI 5205.11 defines a waived SAP as 'An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs.'

waived-usap-mechanism.label: David Charles Grusch
waived-usap-mechanism.why: Grusch's allegation is an allegation about this specific legal category
waived-usap-mechanism.note: Grusch's sworn testimony of 26 July 2023 concerned a multi-decade recovery and reverse-engineering effort concealed from Congress; the waived unacknowledged SAP is the only lawful configuration in which DoD reporting is removed from the committees by design.

waived-usap-mechanism.label: DoDI 5205.11 — Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD SAPs (12 Sep 2024)
waived-usap-mechanism.why: para 1.2.f designates select unacknowledged SAPs as waived

waived-usap-mechanism.label: FY2024 NDAA sec. 1687 — Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs
waived-usap-mechanism.why: sec. 1687(a) bars FY2024 funds for UAP activity under special or restricted access absent disclosure

waived-usap-mechanism.label: 10 U.S.C. 119(e) — Waiver of SAP Reporting (the 'waived SAP' authority)
waived-usap-mechanism.why: 119(e) is the waiver that defines a waived SAP

usc-50-3348.label: The four SAP reporting regimes and the seams between them
usc-50-3348.why: All other agencies: reporting runs to House Oversight and Senate Homeland Security
usc-50-3348.note: 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(1) names the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs among the congressional oversight committees.

usc-50-3348.label: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
usc-50-3348.why: Gives House Oversight a statutory entitlement to SAP reports from every covered agency
usc-50-3348.note: 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(1)(C) names the committee; 3348(g)(2)(B) excludes only DoD, NNSA and IC agencies from the reporting obligation.

usc-50-3348.label: 10 U.S.C. 119 — Special Access Programs: Congressional Oversight
usc-50-3348.why: Supplies the statutory definition of 'special access program' that title 10 lacks
usc-50-3348.note: 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(3) defines the term; 10 U.S.C. 119 uses it throughout without defining it. Section 3091a(b)(2)(A) cross-references 3348(g) for the definition.

usc-50-3348.label: 10 U.S.C. 119 — Special Access Programs: Congressional Oversight
usc-50-3348.why: 3348(g)(2)(B)(i) writes DoD out of the government-wide SAP statute and points to 10 U.S.C. 119

usc-50-3348.label: 50 U.S.C. 2426 — Congressional Oversight of DOE/NNSA Special Access Programs
usc-50-3348.why: 3348(g)(2)(B)(ii) writes NNSA out and points to 50 U.S.C. 2426

eo-13526.label: Information Security Oversight Office
eo-13526.why: ISOO access to SAPs is granted and simultaneously conditioned
eo-13526.note: Section 4.3(b) affords the ISOO Director access to special access programs 'consistent with the policies and procedures directed by the President' - a defeasible right.

eo-13526.label: ICD 906 — Controlled Access Programs (ODNI)
eo-13526.why: ICD 906 is the DNI's exercise of the section 4.3 SAP authority
eo-13526.note: ICD 906 section B.1 establishes oversight of IC special access programs 'pursuant to EO 13526, Section 4.3', which assigns intelligence SAPs to the DNI.

eo-13526.label: FY2024 IAA sec. 7606(c) — Agency Review of Special Access Programs
eo-13526.why: Requires a personnel census from each of the six SAP-creating officials
eo-13526.note: FY2024 IAA sec. 7606(c) addresses 'each head of an agency who is authorized to establish a special access program by Executive Order 13526', due within one year.

gang-of-eight.why: The waived-SAP notification convention mirrors, but is weaker than, the covert action rule
gang-of-eight.note: 119(e)(2) reaches chairs and ranking members of the defense committees with no 180-day widening requirement; 50 U.S.C. 3093(c)(5)(B) requires reconsideration of limited access within 180 days.

gang-of-eight.note: 50 U.S.C. 3093(c)(2) names the four committee leaders and four chamber leaders to whom a finding may be limited; no SAP statute uses that group.

ndaa-fy2024-7606.note: Sec. 7606(c)(2) names the Committee on Oversight and Accountability of the House of Representatives among the recipients.

usc-50-3091a-2024amend.label: 50 U.S.C. 3091a — Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs

pogo.label: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
pogo.why: Outside watchdog seated as witness before Oversight's declassification task force
pogo.note: POGO appeared before the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, and used the appearance to recommend statutory changes (overturning Navy v. Egan, independent adjudication for IC and military whistleblowers) that bear directly on the committee's UAP inquiry.

pogo.label: House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets hearing, 9 September 2025 - 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection'
pogo.why: POGO counsel testified at the UAP transparency hearing
pogo.note: Joe Spielberger, senior policy counsel at the Project On Government Oversight, was a witness at the 9 September 2025 hearing 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection.' His written testimony argued that national security whistleblowers -- the category David Grusch and the military witnesses fall into -- lack an independent enforcement mechanism and are uniquely exposed to clearance-based retaliation.

pogo.label: Anna Paulina Luna
pogo.why: POGO recommendations delivered to Luna's task force
pogo.note: Spielberger's testimony is addressed to 'Chairwoman Luna, Ranking Member Crockett, and task force members' and lays out a legislative agenda for protecting UAP whistleblowers. Luna convened and chaired the hearing; the connection is a witness-to-chair relationship at a single hearing, not an ongoing partnership.

the-intercept.label: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)
the-intercept.why: Pentagon confirmation of AATIP's existence obtained by The Intercept
the-intercept.note: In the same piece the Pentagon confirmed to The Intercept that AATIP existed and 'did pursue research and investigation into unidentified aerial phenomena,' while declining to confirm the earlier Dana White statement that Elizondo ran it. The article is a primary source for the contradiction between DoD's public position and the TTSA account of AATIP's chain of command.

the-intercept.label: Independent media as the disclosure substrate
the-intercept.why: the adversarial counterweight inside the same substrate
the-intercept.note: The Intercept's contribution to this record is subtractive rather than additive: its June 2019 investigation found no discernible evidence that Luis Elizondo led AATIP and obtained a Pentagon statement in tension with the earlier one given to Politico, and in August 2023 it published FOIA'd records on David Grusch weeks after his testimony. A domain about the disclosure substrate that contains only friendly outlets is not a domain, it is a reading list.

the-intercept.label: David Charles Grusch
the-intercept.why: FOIA'd police records on Grusch published weeks after his testimony
the-intercept.note: Ken Klippenstein obtained Loudoun County Sheriff's Office incident reports under the Virginia FOIA showing Grusch was placed under an emergency custody order in October 2018 and retained his clearance afterward. Grusch's advocates publicly claimed the records were leaked medical files; The Intercept published its FOIA correspondence to rebut that.

the-intercept.label: Luis D. Elizondo
the-intercept.why: First major press challenge to Elizondo's AATIP leadership claim
the-intercept.note: Keith Kloor reported for The Intercept that 'there is no discernible evidence that he ever worked for a government UFO program, much less led one,' and obtained a Pentagon statement from spokesperson Christopher Sherwood that Elizondo 'had no responsibilities with regard to the AATIP program while he worked in OUSDI ... up until the time he resigned effective 10/4/2017.'

the-intercept.label: To The Stars Academy of Arts & Science Inc. (later To The Stars Inc.)
the-intercept.why: Scrutiny of To The Stars Academy's media apparatus and financing
the-intercept.note: The Intercept documented TTSA's SEC filing identifying it as a 'Motion Picture & Video Tape Production' concern, the undisclosed employment relationship between TTSA staff and the History Channel series 'Unidentified,' and reporter George Knapp's purchase of 400 shares of TTSA stock, which Knapp confirmed to The Intercept.

us-navy.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
us-navy.why: Nimitz encounter was a Navy carrier strike group event; Navy released the FLIR video
us-navy.note: The November 2004 encounters involved aircrew and sensors of the USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group. DoD authorized release of the unclassified Navy video 'taken in November 2004' through the Naval Air Systems Command FOIA reading room on 27 April 2020, stating the aerial phenomena in the videos 'remain characterized as unidentified.' The DoD statement itself dates the video but does not name the strike group.

us-navy.label: USS Theodore Roosevelt Encounters (2014-2015)
us-navy.why: East Coast UAP encounters reported by Roosevelt-deployed Navy aircrew
us-navy.note: The 2014-2015 Atlantic training-range encounters were reported by U.S. Navy F/A-18F aircrew from squadrons working up with and deployed aboard the USS Theodore Roosevelt, as described in Ryan Graves' congressional testimony. DoD separately authorized release of two unclassified Navy videos 'taken in January 2015' via the NAVAIR FOIA reading room on 27 April 2020, stating the phenomena 'remain characterized as unidentified.'

us-navy.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF)
us-navy.why: Navy designated lead service for the UAP Task Force
us-navy.note: Deputy Secretary of Defense David L. Norquist approved establishment of the UAP Task Force on 4 August 2020, with the Department of the Navy leading it under the cognizance of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security. The Navy therefore owned the institutional predecessor to AOIMSG and AARO.

us-navy.label: Ryan Graves
us-navy.why: Navy F/A-18F pilot turned first active-duty-era witness before Congress
us-navy.note: Graves is a former U.S. Navy F/A-18F pilot whose squadron logged repeated UAP encounters on the Atlantic training ranges; he carried that service experience into congressional testimony and into founding Americans for Safe Aerospace as a reporting channel for military and commercial aircrew.

enigma-labs.label: John Greenewald Jr.
enigma-labs.why: Black Vault FOIA surfaced the AARO-Enigma correspondence
enigma-labs.note: Greenewald filed the January 2023 FOIA request that eventually produced the AARO-Enigma Labs email set in July 2025, making The Black Vault the origin point for public knowledge of contact between the Pentagon's UAP office and a private UAP data company.

enigma-labs.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
enigma-labs.why: Enigma cross-referencing PURSUE files against its civilian sighting database
enigma-labs.note: After the first PURSUE tranche (roughly 160 files) posted to war.gov/ufo on 8 May 2026, Enigma Labs consultant Alejandro Rojas said the team was adding PURSUE elements to Enigma's maps and app so official cases could be cross-referenced 'against our database of over 200,000 public sightings.' He also criticised the drop for lacking coordinates, sensor parameters and altitude data.

enigma-labs.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
enigma-labs.why: Documented AARO contact with Enigma Labs, released heavily redacted
enigma-labs.note: DoD released 50 pages of emails and internal correspondence between AARO and Enigma Labs under FOIA case 23-F-0711, finalized 3 July 2025, with most content withheld under exemptions (b)(5) and (b)(6). Enigma Labs states on its own FAQ that it has 'no signed partnerships or collaborations to date' with any government. The edge records documented contact, not a contractual relationship.

blue-marble-space-institute.label: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
blue-marble-space-institute.why: BMSIS research investigator seated on NASA's UAP independent study team
blue-marble-space-institute.note: NASA's announced 16-member independent study team on UAP included Anamaria Berea, described by NASA as 'a research investigator with Blue Marble Space Institute of Science in Seattle.' That team produced the September 2023 public report and the recommendation that NASA build a UAP data pipeline.

ocsa-canada.label: Canada Department of Transport
ocsa-canada.why: Sky Canada Project audited and issued recommendations to Transport Canada
ocsa-canada.note: The Office of the Chief Science Advisor's report 'Management of Public Reporting of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena in Canada' maps Transport Canada's CADORS as the federal channel where pilot and public UAP sightings are logged (via NAV CANADA Aviation Occurrence Reports), and its Recommendation 3 directs Transport Canada to encourage aircrew and controllers to report UAP 'without fear of stigmatization.'

ocsa-canada.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
ocsa-canada.why: AARO reviewed as a foreign model and named as a proposed partner
ocsa-canada.note: The Sky Canada report summarizes AARO's June 2024 report on 757 UAP cases and AARO's Historical Record Report Volume I, and its Recommendation 13 directs the future Canadian lead organization to establish partnerships with 'AARO and NASA (U.S.A.), GEIPAN (France), and SEFAA (Chile).' The report also notes the RCAF attended a May 2023 Five Eyes UAP briefing hosted by AARO at the Pentagon, which OCSA could not access.

ocsa-canada.label: DGAC Chile — Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil
ocsa-canada.why: Chile's civil-aviation UAP unit used as a model and proposed partner
ocsa-canada.note: The Sky Canada report singles out Chile alongside the U.S. and France as a coordinated, transparent model, describing SEFAA as the official Chilean body for collecting and scientifically studying UAP that 'operates within the General Directorate of Civil Aeronautics (DGAC).' Recommendation 13 tells the proposed Canadian lead organization to establish partnerships with SEFAA (Chile) among others.

ocsa-canada.label: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
ocsa-canada.why: NASA's UAP study cited as precedent and named as a proposed partner
ocsa-canada.note: The Sky Canada report cites NASA's September 2023 UAP Independent Study Report in its bibliography and lists NASA among the international entities the recommended Canadian lead organization should partner with to share data and methodologies.

canada-dot.label: Office of the Chief Science Advisor of Canada
canada-dot.why: Sky Canada Project audited and issued recommendations to Transport Canada
canada-dot.note: The Office of the Chief Science Advisor's report 'Management of Public Reporting of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena in Canada' maps Transport Canada's CADORS as the federal channel where pilot and public UAP sightings are logged (via NAV CANADA Aviation Occurrence Reports), and its Recommendation 3 directs Transport Canada to encourage aircrew and controllers to report UAP 'without fear of stigmatization.'

dgac-chile.label: CEFAA / SEFAA - Chilean anomalous aerial phenomena office, Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil
dgac-chile.why: created and housed by the DGAC
dgac-chile.note: Created by DGAC Resolución Exenta N° 01599 of 3 October 1997, signed by Director General Gonzalo Miranda Aguirre; reorganised under the Secretaría General from 1 January 2010 by Resolución N° 02/0/01937; renamed SEFAA and moved under the Subdepartamento Comunicacional on 18 October 2021 by Resolución Exenta N° 04/3/0113/1385.

dgac-chile.label: Office of the Chief Science Advisor of Canada
dgac-chile.why: Chile's civil-aviation UAP unit used as a model and proposed partner
dgac-chile.note: The Sky Canada report singles out Chile alongside the U.S. and France as a coordinated, transparent model, describing SEFAA as the official Chilean body for collecting and scientifically studying UAP that 'operates within the General Directorate of Civil Aeronautics (DGAC).' Recommendation 13 tells the proposed Canadian lead organization to establish partnerships with SEFAA (Chile) among others.

509th-bomb-group.label: Roswell Incident
509th-bomb-group.why: 509th intelligence office took possession of the Roswell debris
509th-bomb-group.note: The 8 July 1947 RAAF press release stated that 'the intelligence office of the 509th Bomb Group of the Eighth Air Force, Roswell Army Air Field, was fortunate enough to gain possession of a disc.' GAO later confirmed 'Army Air Forces personnel from the RAAF's 509th Bomb Group were credited with the recovery,' and located the July 1947 combined 509th/RAAF history report noting recovery of a 'flying disc' subsequently called a radar-tracking balloon.

509th-bomb-group.label: United States House of Representatives
509th-bomb-group.why: Congressionally requested GAO search of 509th and RAAF records
509th-bomb-group.note: At the request of Rep. Steven H. Schiff, GAO searched for records of the units assigned to RAAF in 1947, including the 509th Bomb Group. It found that RAAF administrative records (Mar 1945-Dec 1949) and RAAF outgoing messages (Oct 1946-Dec 1949) had been destroyed, with the disposition form failing to record who destroyed them, when, or under what authority.

saf-aaz.label: United States House of Representatives
saf-aaz.why: Air Force SAP directive bars congressional briefings without SAPCO approval
saf-aaz.note: Air Force Policy Directive 16-7, 'Special Access Programs,' 29 December 2010, states: 'It is strictly forbidden for any employee of the Air Force or any appropriately accessed organization or company to brief or provide SAP material to any Congressional Member or staff without DoD SAPCO approval. Additionally, the Director, SAF/AAZ will be kept informed of any interaction with Congress.' This is the documented mechanism behind the recurring complaint that SAP-compartmented material cannot reach non-HASC/HAC-D members.

saf-aaz.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
saf-aaz.why: Air Force SAP Central Office subordinate to DoD SAPCO approval authority
saf-aaz.note: SAF/AAZ is the Air Force Special Access Program Central Office. Under AFPD 16-7 it administers Air Force SAPs on behalf of the Secretary of the Air Force while release of SAP material outside the department requires DoD SAPCO approval, placing SAF/AAZ inside the OSD-level special access architecture.

wayne-state-university.label: Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues
wayne-state-university.note: The DIA list gives Green's affiliation of record for this deliverable as Wayne State University. Wayne State is second only to EarthTech on the DIRD author list, supplying Green plus R. Genik's three human-interface papers.

wayne-state-university.label: Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft
wayne-state-university.why: author's institution at time of writing
wayne-state-university.note: Genik was director of the Emergent Technology Research Division and assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neurosciences at the Wayne State University School of Medicine. Wayne State supplied four of the 38 DIRDs across two authors - Genik's three plus Kit Green's 'Field Effects on Biological Tissues' - the second-largest institutional concentration after EarthTech International's six.

wayne-state-university.label: Quantum Computing and Utilizing Organic Molecules in Automation Technology
wayne-state-university.why: author's institutional affiliation at time of writing
wayne-state-university.note: Wayne State University is the affiliation recorded against this title on the DIA congressional list. Wayne State appears more than once on the list: it is also the affiliation given for Kit Green's human-tissue field-effects deliverable, so both the human-effects and human-interface strands of the AAWSAP deliverable set run through the same medical school.

wayne-state-university.label: Technological Approaches to Controlling External Devices in the Absence of Limb-Operated Interfaces
wayne-state-university.note: Wayne State is the DIA-listed affiliation for four DIRDs: Genik's three human-factors papers and Kit Green's "Field Effects on Biological Tissues." That makes it the single most productive institution in the DIRD set after EarthTech International, and the locus of the programme's human-effects line of inquiry.

wayne-state-university.label: Christopher C. 'Kit' Green
wayne-state-university.why: Green's academic base for UAP-injury neuroimaging work
wayne-state-university.note: Christopher 'Kit' Green, MD, PhD, former CIA life sciences analyst, is professor in the Departments of Diagnostic Radiology and of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neurosciences at Wayne State University School of Medicine, where he ran the Emergent Technology Research Division. Wayne State is the institutional address for the clinical neuroimaging he applied to patients reporting injury after anomalous encounters.

wayne-state-university.label: Richard J. Genik II
wayne-state-university.why: director, Emergent Technology Research Division; assistant professor of psychiatry and behavioral neurosciences
wayne-state-university.note: Wayne State University School of Medicine identifies Genik as director of its Emergent Technology Research Division and an assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neurosciences. Wayne State is the affiliation DIA recorded for him on the congressional list. The dateStart is the date of the university announcement establishing the role, not necessarily the start of his tenure.

wayne-state-university.label: The 38 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents (DIRDs)
wayne-state-university.why: Wayne State clinician authored the AAWSAP human-effects reference document
wayne-state-university.note: Green, while a Wayne State professor, wrote the Defense Intelligence Reference Document 'Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human and Biological Tissues' for the DIA-funded AAWSAP contract; DIA released it with the other DIRDs in 2022. Tier 2 because the work was Green's, commissioned through BAASS, not a Wayne State institutional contract.

vanderbilt-university.label: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)
vanderbilt-university.why: AATIP's 2017 disclosure pulled a Vanderbilt lab into UAP research
vanderbilt-university.note: Bruehl told VUMC that the December 2017 New York Times report revealing AATIP is what restarted his interest and led him to conclude 'nobody's really studying this scientifically'; his Anesthesiology chair then authorized him to publish UAP work under the Vanderbilt name. His 2025 papers with Beatriz Villarroel in PASP and Scientific Reports followed.

vanderbilt-university.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
vanderbilt-university.why: Vanderbilt UAP statistician invited to a Pentagon-sponsored expert meeting
vanderbilt-university.note: Vanderbilt University Medical Center reports that Stephen Bruehl, PhD, professor of Anesthesiology, 'was invited to attend a Pentagon-sponsored meeting for discussions with UAP experts from the government and academia' in August 2025, as his cluster analysis of 216 well-documented UAP cases (1947-2016) neared publication in World Futures. The sponsoring office is not named in the source.

sheffield-hallam.label: Rendlesham Forest Incident, RAF Woodbridge/Bentwaters
sheffield-hallam.why: Sheffield Hallam academic curated the MoD file release containing Rendlesham
sheffield-hallam.note: Dr David Clarke, associate professor at Sheffield Hallam University, first obtained MoD documents on the 1980 Rendlesham Forest incident in May 2001 under the Code of Practice for Access to Government Information, then served 2008-2013 as consultant and curator for the MoD/National Archives UFO files project that transferred and opened more than 60,000 pages, including the Rendlesham file at TNA reference DEFE 24/1948.

izmiran.label: SETKA-AN / SETKA-MO (later Galaktika, then Gorizont) - Soviet state anomalous phenomena programme
izmiran.why: head institute of the Academy of Sciences branch
izmiran.note: Academician V. Migulin, director of IZMIRAN and a radio physicist specialising in oscillation theory, radio wave propagation and radiolocation, was made scientific head of the academic branch, and IZMIRAN was designated head institute. The four-to-five person working group there was headed by Yu. Platov, co-author of the programme's published account. [Re-pointed from the collapsed duplicate `setka`, 14 Aug 2026.]

senado-brasil.label: Brasilia, Federal District, Brazil
senado-brasil.why: The Senado Federal sits in Brasília
senado-brasil.note: RQS 193/2022 also records the 2005 visit by ufologists to CINDACTA and COMDABRA 'em Brasília' to inspect the documents — the capital is where both the archive and the legislature that pressed on it are located. [CORRECTED 14 Aug 2026: RQS 193/2022 is a request for a COMMEMORATIVE SPECIAL SESSION under Art. 199 RISF, approved 16 Mar 2022, held 24 Jun 2022 - not a records-seeking or compelling instrument. senado-brasil.note: RQS 193/2022 names the event: 'em 1986, quando ocorreu a hoje conhecida como "Noite Oficial dos UFOs no Brasil", quando 21 OVNIs esféricos de 100 metros de diâmetro cada foram perseguidos durante horas por nossos caças a jato.' senado-brasil.why: The Senate instrument treats the Aeronáutica's record as the national record
senado-brasil.note: RQS 193/2022 credits Brazil as the first state to admit officially that the objects exist — the 1954 Escola Superior de Guerra meeting at which then-Captain João Adil de Oliveira spoke — lists SIOANI (1969, IV COMAR), Operação Prato (1977) and the 1986 night as official Aeronáutica programmes, and notes that the Aeronáutica 'sempre foi discreta quanto a estes e a outros fatos, mas nunca os negou quando inquirida'.
