senado-brasil.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
senado-brasil.why: 2022 Senate special session justified by the 2021 US UAP report
senado-brasil.note: Requerimento RQS 193/2022 (Sen. Eduardo Girao and seven co-signers) requested the Brazilian Senate special session on ufology, and its justification expressly cites the 2021 'Pentagon' UAP report covering 144 sightings of which only one was explained, plus FY2022 NDAA UAP research funding. The report described is the June 2021 Preliminary Assessment authored by the UAP Task Force and released by ODNI. The session was held in the Senate plenary on 24 June 2022 and ended with ufologists handing Girao the 'Carta de Brasilia' urging a permanent joint civil-military commission.

senado-brasil.label: Hospital Regional de Varginha
senado-brasil.why: Girao backed Varginha hospital witnesses in Washington
senado-brasil.note: Sen. Eduardo Girao, who presided over the 2022 Brazilian Senate UAP session, travelled to Washington for the 20 January 2026 National Press Club event and praised the Varginha witnesses, and discussed a joint Brazil-US evidence effort with Rep. Eric Burlison. The Debrief is explicit that Girao acted as a private citizen and was not officially representing the Brazilian Senate, so this is a personal rather than institutional linkage.

hospital-regional-varginha.label: Senado Federal do Brasil
hospital-regional-varginha.why: Girao backed Varginha hospital witnesses in Washington
hospital-regional-varginha.note: Sen. Eduardo Girao, who presided over the 2022 Brazilian Senate UAP session, travelled to Washington for the 20 January 2026 National Press Club event and praised the Varginha witnesses, and discussed a joint Brazil-US evidence effort with Rep. Eric Burlison. The Debrief is explicit that Girao acted as a private citizen and was not officially representing the Brazilian Senate, so this is a personal rather than institutional linkage.

hospital-regional-varginha.label: Anna Paulina Luna
hospital-regional-varginha.why: Hospital duty neurosurgeon described the being to Luna on the Hill
hospital-regional-varginha.note: At a closed-door 15 January 2026 meeting in Rep. Tim Burchett's Longworth office, Dr Italo Venturelli, who says he was on duty at the Hospital Regional de Varginha in January 1996, described examining a non-human being at the hospital. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, chair of the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, questioned him directly and afterwards said Congress should seek Air Force flight records and landing authorisations to test the claimed US removal of the body. No medical record of the treatment exists, per Venturelli.

hospital-regional-varginha.label: Eric Burlison
hospital-regional-varginha.why: Burlison took the Varginha hospital testimony and pressed for more witnesses
hospital-regional-varginha.note: Rep. Eric Burlison attended the 15 January 2026 closed meeting with the Varginha witnesses, asked whether other hospital staff could corroborate Venturelli's account and urged that they be brought forward, and spoke at the 20 January National Press Club event calling for international transparency.

hospital-regional-varginha.label: Varginha incident, Minas Gerais, January 1996
hospital-regional-varginha.why: The hospital is a named custody point in the Varginha sequence
hospital-regional-varginha.note: The facility registered in CNES as the Hospital Regional do Sul de Minas is the hospital named in the Varginha literature as a place to which an injured being was reportedly taken. Tier 2: the facility and its registry entry are verified fact, the custody sequence rests on witness testimony and journalism and on no hospital record obtained in this pass. The hospital node carried edges to the US congressional side of the story but, oddly, not to the 1996 event itself.

hospital-regional-varginha.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
hospital-regional-varginha.why: Varginha discussed in a 2024 meeting with AARO staff
hospital-regional-varginha.note: Filmmaker James Fox says that in 2024 he met AARO personnel to discuss video his team had obtained and that the Varginha incident was among the cases debated, with AARO director Dr Jon Kosloski entering the room. This rests solely on Fox's account as reported by The Debrief; AARO's own 2024 report states no investigation has concluded that any UAP report indicates extraterrestrial origin, and the Pentagon did not respond to requests for comment.

aawsap-solicitation.label: DIA Contract HHM402-08-C-0072 (BAASS)
aawsap-solicitation.why: solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 led to award HHM402-08-C-0072
aawsap-solicitation.note: Posted 18 August 2008, awarded 22 September 2008 — a five-week competition on an eleven-topic statement of work reaching to 2050.

aawsap-solicitation.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
aawsap-solicitation.why: requirement written to a capability only BAASS held
aawsap-solicitation.note: An eleven-topic statement of work including spatial/temporal translation, human interface and human effects, competed for five weeks, awarded to the one firm with a decade of exactly that field practice.

aawsap-contract.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
aawsap-contract.why: withheld the contract for eleven years
aawsap-contract.note: DIA withheld the BAASS award entirely in a 2011 FOIA response and released it only in October 2022 — a contract that had been competed on a public bid board.

aawsap-contract.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
aawsap-contract.note: Awarded 22 September 2008 to Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies LLC, DUNS 827037768, CAGE 54JU7, base year plus four options.

aawsap-contract.label: George Knapp
aawsap-contract.note: Knapp's KLAS I-Team established publicly that the DIA-funded study was executed in Nevada, ahead of DIA's own release of the contract in 2022.

aawsap-contract.label: DIA Solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211
aawsap-contract.why: solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 led to award HHM402-08-C-0072
aawsap-contract.note: Posted 18 August 2008, awarded 22 September 2008 — a five-week competition on an eleven-topic statement of work reaching to 2050.

reid-sap-letter-2009.label: DIA Memorandum: Review of Special Access Program Request (U-09-2660CE-IM)
reid-sap-letter-2009.why: DIA finds insufficient grounds to classify
reid-sap-letter-2009.note: DIA's 13 November 2009 answer evaluates only the written deliverables and never addresses the field investigation, database or human-effects work the same contract funded.

reid-sap-letter-2009.label: Susan Gough
reid-sap-letter-2009.why: authenticated the letter, denied its significance
reid-sap-letter-2009.note: 'It makes no change to previous statements.' DoD confirmed the document's authenticity in the same breath as dismissing it.

reid-sap-letter-2009.label: Harry M. Reid
reid-sap-letter-2009.note: The Senate Majority Leader asked DoD to compartment a program whose deliverables DoD would three months later describe as unclassifiable basic research.

reid-sap-letter-2009.label: William J. Lynn III
reid-sap-letter-2009.why: addressed to the Deputy Secretary of Defense
reid-sap-letter-2009.note: Lynn was the decision authority; he received the request in June and delivered the refusal in person in November.

reid-sap-letter-2009.label: KONA BLUE
reid-sap-letter-2009.why: second attempt at the protection Reid was refused
reid-sap-letter-2009.note: Reid asked DoD for a restricted SAP over engineering of advanced technologies in 2009 and was refused; two years later the same circle proposed a recovery-and-exploitation SAP at DHS instead.

dia-sap-denial-memo-2009.label: Reid Letter to DEPSECDEF Requesting Restricted SAP Status
dia-sap-denial-memo-2009.why: DIA finds insufficient grounds to classify
dia-sap-denial-memo-2009.note: DIA's 13 November 2009 answer evaluates only the written deliverables and never addresses the field investigation, database or human-effects work the same contract funded.

depsecdef-sap-packet-2009.label: James R. Clapper Jr.
depsecdef-sap-packet-2009.why: USD(I) recommends against establishing a SAP
depsecdef-sap-packet-2009.note: Clapper's recommendation is the decision that severed the Reid appropriation from any compartmented protection; he became DNI nine months later.

depsecdef-sap-packet-2009.label: William J. Lynn III
depsecdef-sap-packet-2009.note: Eighteen pages assembled to support refusing the Majority Leader; two days later Lynn briefed Reid in SVC-217.

depsecdef-sap-packet-2009.label: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program (AATIP / AAITP)
depsecdef-sap-packet-2009.why: records three concurrent names for one program
depsecdef-sap-packet-2009.note: AAWSAP as the contract title, AAITP as Reid's usage, AATIP as the unclassified nickname — the naming divergence originates in a single DoD document.

ousdi-atl-memo-2010.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
ousdi-atl-memo-2010.why: proposes transitioning AATIP out of DIA
ousdi-atl-memo-2010.note: DIA tells USD(AT&L) the reports were of limited value to DIA but could merit other organisations and the project could move to a better-suited component.

ousdi-atl-memo-2010.label: Luis D. Elizondo
ousdi-atl-memo-2010.note: DIA proposed a transition in December 2010; Elizondo says he picked up the residual effort in OUSD(I) at that time. No charter has ever been released either way.

baass-ten-month-report.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
baass-ten-month-report.note: The deliverable that shows the program's actual shape: physics, field teams, case database, ranch operations, human effects. Never released by DIA.

dia-aatip-letter-2018.label: Brian L. Jenkins
dia-aatip-letter-2018.why: signed the transmittal to the Senate Armed Services Committee
dia-aatip-letter-2018.note: A records officer's signature is the only formal notification the authorizing committee ever received about a ten-year program.

dia-aatip-letter-2018.label: The 38 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents (DIRDs)
dia-aatip-letter-2018.why: transmitted the complete list of 38 products
dia-aatip-letter-2018.note: Every subsequent FOIA request for individual DIRDs was built from this list; 37 of 38 have since been released. [Re-pointed from dird-collection, 14 Aug 2026: dird-collection and dird-series described the same object and were collapsed.]

dia-aatip-letter-2018.label: Defense Appropriations Acts FY2008 and FY2010 — the $22M AAWSAP appropriation
dia-aatip-letter-2018.note: That DIA had to introduce the program to SASC by letter in 2018 establishes the committee had no visibility during its life — the direct consequence of funding it through the classified appropriation.

nids.label: Robert T. Bigelow
nids.note: NIDS described itself as a privately funded science institute studying aerial phenomena and animal mutilations; Bigelow shut it down in 2004.

nids.label: Las Vegas, Nevada (alias of l-las-vegas)
nids.note: The National Institute for Discovery Science was a privately financed research organisation based in Las Vegas, Nevada, founded by Robert Bigelow in 1995 and disbanded in October 2004. It is the direct institutional predecessor of the BAASS staffing that later executed AAWSAP.

nids.label: George Knapp
nids.why: Worked with Bigelow's NIDS alongside Colm Kelleher
nids.note: Knapp's NIDS work with Kelleher produced the Skinwalker Ranch material that later carried into AAWSAP.

nids.label: Harold E. Puthoff
nids.why: Puthoff was among the consultants Bigelow hired at NIDS in 1995
nids.note: The New Yorker records that among the consultants Bigelow hired was Hal Puthoff, 'whose work in paranormal studies dated back decades, to Project Stargate.'

nids.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
nids.why: The private field programme was re-federalised as a DIA contract without changing personnel
nids.note: This is the structural pivot of the era: capability was privatised in 1995 and re-acquired by contract in 2008, meaning the government never had to stand up an acknowledged office.

nids.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
nids.why: personnel, methodology and site inherited wholesale
nids.note: Kelleher, Davis, Green and the Utah ranch operation all pass from Bigelow's private institute into the DIA-funded contractor.

nids.label: Colm A. Kelleher
nids.why: Kelleher was NIDS deputy administrator and ran field operations
nids.note: Kelleher managed the ranch instrumentation, the necropsy response programme and the hotline casework for the institute's whole life.

nids.label: Eric W. Davis
nids.why: NIDS scientist before the federal contract
nids.note: Davis carried the NIDS methodology forward into BAASS work under the DIA-funded AAWSAP contract after 2008.

nids.label: Jacques F. Vallee
nids.why: Vallee served on the NIDS advisory board
nids.note: Vallee had been at SRI in the 1970s and had documented deliberate human disinformation in UFO cases from 1979 - the phenomenon later confirmed in the Bennewitz affair.

nids.label: John B. Alexander
nids.why: Alexander sat on the NIDS board from its founding
nids.note: Alexander brought Los Alamos and Army INSCOM programme experience and had previously convened a cleared interagency canvass for a compartmented UFO effort.

nids.label: Christopher C. 'Kit' Green
nids.why: NIDS science advisory board before the DIRD
nids.note: Green's human-effects interest predates the federal contract by more than a decade, through Bigelow's private institute.

nids.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
nids.why: NIDS personnel and methods carried directly into the DIA-funded BAASS contract
nids.note: NIDS closed in 2004; in 2007 a senior DIA official wrote to Bigelow about Skinwalker Ranch, and BAASS won the AAWSAP contract the following year with substantially the same people.

nids.label: Skinwalker Ranch, Uintah Basin, Utah
nids.why: NIDS operated a permanently instrumented field station at the ranch
nids.note: Bigelow moved in a research team, surveillance equipment and full-time caretakers immediately after the purchase.

nids.label: Skinwalker Ranch, Uintah Basin, Utah
nids.why: NIDS ran the field investigation at the ranch under Bigelow
nids.note: NIDS investigators including retired Army Col. John B. Alexander examined close to 100 incidents while conceding they could not obtain publishable evidence.

earthtech-international.label: The 38 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents (DIRDs)
earthtech-international.why: largest single DIRD producer — six of 38
earthtech-international.note: A small Austin firm produced more of the deliverable set than any university or defence prime, indicating a directed rather than competed distribution. [Re-pointed from dird-collection, 14 Aug 2026: dird-collection and dird-series described the same object and were collapsed.]

earthtech-international.label: Federal Contracting Mechanics
earthtech-international.why: the subcontract path - how work reached the government without a prime relationship
earthtech-international.note: The reference documents that reached DIA were commissioned by the prime and written substantially by EarthTech and other subcontractors, then delivered as Defense Intelligence Reference Documents. The DIA transmittal list to SASC and the published list of funded studies establish the subcontract layer, which is the layer at which visibility normally stops.

earthtech-international.label: Advanced Space Propulsion Based on Vacuum (Spacetime Metric) Engineering
earthtech-international.note: The DIA list gives Puthoff's affiliation of record for this deliverable as EarthTech International, the Austin institute he founded and directs.

earthtech-international.label: Antigravity for Aerospace Applications
earthtech-international.note: EarthTech International supplied six of the 38 DIRDs through Eric Davis plus one through Hal Puthoff, making it the single most represented institution on the author list.

earthtech-international.label: Concepts for Extracting Energy From the Quantum Vacuum
earthtech-international.note: EarthTech, run by Hal Puthoff, was the largest single source of DIRDs, producing six of the 38. Puthoff has stated that BAASS 'connected me at EarthTech International to collaborate as a subcontractor' and that he then let the 38 contracts himself. The arrangement means EarthTech occupied both sides of the transaction on this document: commissioning agent and author's employer.

earthtech-international.label: Laser Lightcraft Nanosatellites
earthtech-international.why: author's institutional affiliation at time of writing
earthtech-international.note: EarthTech International of Austin, Texas is the affiliation recorded against this title on the DIA congressional list. EarthTech is the single largest institutional source on the list; Puthoff and Davis between them are primary authors on six of the 38 products.

earthtech-international.label: Quantum Tomography of Negative Energy States in the Vacuum
earthtech-international.why: author's institutional affiliation at time of writing
earthtech-international.note: EarthTech International, Austin, Texas — the affiliation recorded against this title on the DIA congressional list.

earthtech-international.label: DIA-08-1004-004: 'Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, and Negative Energy'
earthtech-international.why: Contractor of record: EarthTech International Inc., 11855 Research Blvd, Austin TX
earthtech-international.note: The author block on the released DIRD gives EarthTech's full street address, which makes the corporate performer identifiable and locatable rather than a generic 'contractor'.

earthtech-international.label: Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, and Negative Energy
earthtech-international.why: author's affiliation of record; DIRD carried on EarthTech's own publications list
earthtech-international.note: EarthTech International lists six DIRDs by Eric Davis on its publications page, with DIA document numbers and the issuing division named as the Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3) or Technology Warning Division (DWO-4) of the Defense Warning Office. A contractor publishing its DIA reference-document numbers on an open website is itself part of how the DIRD series became documentable.

earthtech-international.label: Eric W. Davis
earthtech-international.note: Davis wrote all five of his DIRDs under the EarthTech banner.

earthtech-international.label: Harold E. Puthoff
earthtech-international.note: EarthTech is the vehicle through which Puthoff's four-decade federally funded research line continued into AAWSAP.

earthtech-international.label: Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
earthtech-international.note: EarthTech's own About page states the corporate relationship; the two names are used interchangeably across the DIRD covers and the TTSA reporting.

earthtech-international.label: Austin, Texas - 11855 Research Blvd
earthtech-international.why: 11855 Research Blvd - the address printed on a DIA reference document
earthtech-international.note: The single street address connecting the DIA Defense Warning Office to the AAWSAP propulsion and medical documents and thence to the To The Stars metamaterials work.

earthtech-international.label: ADAM Research Project (Acquisition and Data Analysis of Materials)
earthtech-international.note: Puthoff's Austin laboratory is where the specimens were characterised. No results have been published.

sandia.label: Kirtland Air Force Base and Albuquerque, New Mexico
sandia.why: Sandia National Laboratories is adjacent to Kirtland AFB
sandia.note: Sandia, descended from the Manhattan Project's Z Division, sits adjacent to Kirtland; Bennewitz licensed his humidity sensor technology from Sandia in 1966.

sandia.label: DIA Memorandum: Review of Advanced Aerospace Contract Deliverables (U-429-09-DWO-IM)
sandia.why: three Sandia staff among the five outside reviewers
sandia.note: A DOE weapons laboratory peer-reviewed the AAWSAP physics portfolio and DIA recorded the reviews as positive, some exceptionally so.

sandia.label: United States Department of Energy
sandia.why: DOE/NNSA management and operating contract; Sandia
sandia.note: Sandia is an NNSA laboratory adjacent to Kirtland AFB and the Manzano Weapons Storage Area, the site of the 1980 intrusions investigated by AFOSI.

sandia.label: Kirtland AFB / Manzano Weapons Storage Area incident
sandia.why: A Sandia security guard is a named reporting party in the AFOSI file
sandia.note: A Sandia guard reported a round disc-shaped object near an alarmed structure at approximately 00:20 on 9 August 1980, with radio malfunction.

sandia.label: 'Manhattan Project 2.0' (alleged secrecy architecture)
sandia.why: Sandia named as an AEC-lineage custodial laboratory
sandia.note: Gerb's Sandia investigation of 1 November 2025 supplies the named-institution case for the AEC-custody thesis, citing Edgar Fouche and former New Mexico State Representative J. Andrew Kissner.

ousdi.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
ousdi.note: The establishment memorandum directed USD(I&S) to establish the office and placed AARO in that chain until summer 2023.

ousdi.label: Program structure and organisational mapping
ousdi.why: the OSD element with policy authority over intelligence, counterintelligence, security and sensitive activities
ousdi.note: OUSD(I), since 2020 OUSD(I&S), is where the sensitive-activities policy authority sits and where the whole Elizondo/AATIP dispute takes place. It is also the office under which the Military Intelligence Program is managed, which makes it the point where this domain's organisational and funding threads meet.

ousdi.label: Luis D. Elizondo
ousdi.note: His own resignation letter, released in FOIA 18-F-0324, states the title and the 4 October 2017 effective date. The Department has never disputed either.

ousdi.label: Neill Tipton
ousdi.why: Director for Defense Intelligence (Collection & Special Programs); Elizondo's superior c.2010-2012
ousdi.note: His own account places Elizondo under him during precisely the years Elizondo claims to have run AATIP.

ousdi.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
ousdi.why: Named contributor to the 2021 ODNI Preliminary Assessment
ousdi.note: ODNI's assessment names USD(I&S) first among contributing elements, confirming the office's cognisance of the UAP reporting stream.

ousdi.label: 'Manhattan Project 2.0' (alleged secrecy architecture)
ousdi.why: Non-Covert Action Programs alleged to carry waived reporting requirements
ousdi.note: The operative concealment mechanism on Gerb's account: full SAP security protocols combined with completely waived reporting and budgetary requirements, which would make congressional ignorance lawful rather than the product of active deception.

ousdi.label: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)
ousdi.why: OSD principal for intelligence and security policy in the SAP enterprise
ousdi.note: DoDD 5205.07 assigns SAP policy responsibilities across OSD principals including the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, while vesting central management in DoD SAPCO under DEPSECDEF.

mufon-sip.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
mufon-sip.why: funded MUFON's Star Team Impact Project
mufon-sip.note: A DIA-contracted firm bought rapid-response access to the largest civilian UFO reporting network in the United States; the arrangement collapsed in 2010.

skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.why: no records located for the documents the book describes
skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.note: DIA could locate neither the 19 June 2007 Lacatski letter nor the 'Utah Ranch Investigation: August 2009-February 2010' report, in a program contractually required to file monthly status reports.

skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.label: Colm A. Kelleher
skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.why: co-author, contractor side of the account
skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.note: Kelleher supplies the field-operations and human-effects record from the BAASS side.

skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.label: George Knapp
skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.why: co-author with the program manager and the contractor's deputy
skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.note: Knapp moves from reporter to co-author of the DOPSR-cleared insider account — and his earlier book is the proximate cause of the contract.

skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.label: James T. Lacatski
skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.why: co-author; states he entered a craft of unknown origin
skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon.note: A former DIA program manager made this claim in a manuscript DoD cleared for publication.

lacatski-book-series.label: James T. Lacatski
lacatski-book-series.why: releasing AAWSAP material through trade publication
lacatski-book-series.note: Three volumes 2023-2026, each DOPSR-cleared; Lacatski says he doubts the underlying files will ever be released and treats the books as the substitute.

lacatski-book-series.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
lacatski-book-series.why: claims a data warehouse of 100+ reports beyond the 38 DIRDs
lacatski-book-series.note: If accurate, the released deliverable set is a small fraction of what the appropriation produced, and the rest has no public custody trail.

uss-princeton.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
uss-princeton.why: Generated the primary sensor record of the encounter; no such data has ever been released
uss-princeton.note: Fravor testified Princeton tracked the objects on Aegis for two weeks. No Princeton radar or CEC data for 14 Nov 2004 has appeared in any release, and the range fouler report says reporting 'terminated at 3rd Fleet.'

uss-princeton.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
uss-princeton.why: Princeton's SPY-1B held the tracks and vectored the intercept
uss-princeton.note: Princeton had been observing the objects on Aegis for approximately two weeks, descending from above 80,000 ft to 20,000 ft, before vectoring the VFA-41 section.

uss-princeton.label: Gary Voorhis
uss-princeton.why: CEC/Aegis systems technician aboard USS Princeton, Nov 2004
uss-princeton.note: Voorhis's technical billet placed him at the node where the encounter's recorded machine data physically lived.

uss-princeton.label: Kevin Day
uss-princeton.why: Senior Chief Operations Specialist aboard USS Princeton, Nov 2004
uss-princeton.note: Day's billet is the reason his account of the radar record and its removal carries weight; he is the man who owned the air picture.

uss-princeton.label: Gary Voorhis
uss-princeton.why: Says recording media were surrendered or wiped after 14 Nov 2004
uss-princeton.note: The confiscation account rests on Voorhis and Day, in different billets, describing the same 48-hour window. No document, log entry or chain-of-custody form corroborating it has been located.

uss-princeton.label: Jason Turner
uss-princeton.note: Turner is one of several Princeton enlisted crew who have publicly described the post-encounter arrival of outside personnel; his rate and division are not established from primary records.

vfa-41.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
vfa-41.why: Squadron that flew the intercept and produced the FLIR1 footage
vfa-41.note: VFA-41 put two sections into the event: the Fravor/Dietrich visual intercept and a follow-on aircraft whose ATFLIR produced FLIR1.

vfa-11.label: USS Theodore Roosevelt Encounters (2014-2015)
vfa-11.why: Squadron at the centre of the Atlantic encounter series
vfa-11.note: Graves names VFA-11 and Warning Area W-72 in sworn testimony as the locus of the encounters and the near-midair.

americans-for-safe-aerospace.label: ODNI Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (25 June 2021)
americans-for-safe-aerospace.why: Official confirmation of the stigma ASA exists to route around
americans-for-safe-aerospace.note: The assessment concedes 'disparagement associated with observing UAP, reporting it, or attempting to discuss it with colleagues' - the condition that made a civilian aircrew nonprofit necessary.

americans-for-safe-aerospace.label: USS Theodore Roosevelt Encounters (2014-2015)
americans-for-safe-aerospace.why: Created in direct response to the reporting failure the encounters exposed
americans-for-safe-aerospace.note: Graves's testimony ties the founding to the fact that after his squadron's safety report 'there was no official acknowledgement of the incident and no further mechanism to report the sightings.'

americans-for-safe-aerospace.label: AARO FY2025 Consolidated Annual Report on UAP
americans-for-safe-aerospace.why: 'AARO did not receive reports indicating flight safety concerns during this reporting period'
americans-for-safe-aerospace.note: The same report records two cases of electronic or avionic interference attributed to UAP in proximity to an operational aircraft. The no-safety-concerns finding is a statement about AARO's intake, not about the sky.

americans-for-safe-aerospace.label: Ryan Graves
americans-for-safe-aerospace.note: Graves founded the organisation in 2022 to build the aircrew reporting channel the Navy did not provide, and appeared before Congress in that capacity in July 2023.

americans-for-safe-aerospace.label: NASA UAP Independent Study Team
americans-for-safe-aerospace.why: Shared reporting-reform agenda: ASRS and FAA pilot reporting
americans-for-safe-aerospace.note: The NASA study team recommended enhancing the Aviation Safety Reporting System for commercial pilot UAP reporting; ASA performs the equivalent intake function for aircrew outside the chain of command.

americans-for-safe-aerospace.label: Timothy Gallaudet
americans-for-safe-aerospace.why: Flag-officer corroboration of the safety-reporting failure ASA was built around
americans-for-safe-aerospace.note: Gallaudet's recalled-email account and Graves's unacknowledged squadron safety report describe the same broken machinery from opposite ends of the chain of command.

navy-range-fouler-reports.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF)
navy-range-fouler-reports.why: Reporting volume tracks the existence of a channel, not the phenomenon
navy-range-fouler-reports.note: The set contains no reports from 2005-2007, 2009-2012, 2017 or 2020, and nearly 40 percent from 2021 alone - the year after the Task Force was stood up.

navy-range-fouler-reports.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
navy-range-fouler-reports.why: The 2004 incident is formally documented in the Navy's own range fouler reporting
navy-range-fouler-reports.note: The January 2023 FOIA release proves the encounter was reported inside the Navy through intelligence personnel and then died at Third Fleet with no dissemination process.

navy-range-fouler-reports.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
navy-range-fouler-reports.why: Two decades of aviator records released only under external pressure
navy-range-fouler-reports.note: The 2023 range fouler release came via FOIA; the 2026 PURSUE releases came via presidential directive. Neither came from the reporting system that was supposed to surface them.

navy-range-fouler-reports.label: Fleet Forces Command 'URGENT SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE' Email (Jan 2015, recalled)
navy-range-fouler-reports.why: Two independent traces of the same suppression at fleet level
navy-range-fouler-reports.note: The range fouler set records reporting terminating at Third Fleet with no dissemination process; Gallaudet records a Fleet Forces Command safety message deleted within a day.

roosevelt-2014-2015.label: Americans for Safe Aerospace
roosevelt-2014-2015.why: Created in direct response to the reporting failure the encounters exposed
roosevelt-2014-2015.note: Graves's testimony ties the founding to the fact that after his squadron's safety report 'there was no official acknowledgement of the incident and no further mechanism to report the sightings.'

roosevelt-2014-2015.label: GIMBAL (Navy ATFLIR video, January 2015)
roosevelt-2014-2015.why: January 2015 ATFLIR artefact from the same operating environment
roosevelt-2014-2015.note: DoD released GIMBAL on 27 April 2020 as authentic and unidentified; AARO's published case slides contain no GIMBAL assessment.

roosevelt-2014-2015.label: GO FAST (Navy ATFLIR video, January 2015)
roosevelt-2014-2015.why: January 2015 ATFLIR artefact from the same operating environment
roosevelt-2014-2015.note: GO FAST is the video Gallaudet says was attached to the recalled Fleet Forces Command safety message, and the one AARO later reanalysed on parallax grounds.

roosevelt-2014-2015.label: Warning Area W-72, off Virginia Beach
roosevelt-2014-2015.why: Site of the near-midair that anchors the safety case
roosevelt-2014-2015.note: Restricted training airspace ten miles east of Virginia Beach where two F/A-18Fs 100 feet apart took evasive action around a stationary cube-in-sphere object.

roosevelt-2014-2015.label: United States Navy
roosevelt-2014-2015.why: East Coast UAP encounters reported by Roosevelt-deployed Navy aircrew
roosevelt-2014-2015.note: The 2014-2015 Atlantic training-range encounters were reported by U.S. Navy F/A-18F aircrew from squadrons working up with and deployed aboard the USS Theodore Roosevelt, as described in Ryan Graves' congressional testimony. DoD separately authorized release of two unclassified Navy videos 'taken in January 2015' via the NAVAIR FOIA reading room on 27 April 2020, stating the phenomena 'remain characterized as unidentified.'

roosevelt-2014-2015.label: Strike Fighter Squadron 11 (VFA-11 Red Rippers)
roosevelt-2014-2015.why: Squadron at the centre of the Atlantic encounter series
roosevelt-2014-2015.note: Graves names VFA-11 and Warning Area W-72 in sworn testimony as the locus of the encounters and the near-midair.

roosevelt-2014-2015.label: Ryan Graves
roosevelt-2014-2015.why: VFA-11 aircrew during the 2014-2015 encounter series
roosevelt-2014-2015.note: Graves testified in writing that his squadron 'began witnessing advanced UAP demonstrating complex maneuvers on a regular basis' after the AESA radar upgrade.

roosevelt-2014-2015.label: Fleet Forces Command 'URGENT SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE' Email (Jan 2015, recalled)
roosevelt-2014-2015.why: Command-level reaction to the encounter series
roosevelt-2014-2015.note: The message describes exactly the problem Graves's squadron reported - repeated near-midairs with unidentified objects in working airspace - and was withdrawn within 24 hours.

kidd-russell-2019.label: Southern California Operating Areas (W-291 and Baja approaches)
kidd-russell-2019.why: Multi-night unattributed swarms against destroyers in the SoCal operating areas
kidd-russell-2019.note: Deck logs from USS Kidd, Rafael Peralta, Russell and John Finn, obtained under FOIA and cross-checked against AIS tracking, document the July 2019 events.

kidd-russell-2019.label: ODNI Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (25 June 2021)
kidd-russell-2019.why: Within the November 2004 to March 2021 window the assessment covers
kidd-russell-2019.note: The ODNI preliminary assessment covers 144 reports from USG sources spanning November 2004 to March 2021, the window containing both the Nimitz and the 2019 swarm events.

kidd-russell-2019.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
kidd-russell-2019.why: Same operating areas, fifteen years apart, same failure to attribute
kidd-russell-2019.note: Both events occurred in the instrumented Southern California naval training space, both were documented in Navy records, and neither produced an attribution.

kidd-russell-2019.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF)
kidd-russell-2019.why: Fed the reporting stream that became the UAPTF caseload
kidd-russell-2019.note: The July 2019 events were investigated by the Navy, Coast Guard and FBI and reached the Chief of Naval Operations in the period immediately preceding the Task Force's establishment; the linkage is reasoned from timing and subject matter, not from a released tasking document.

langley-2023-incursions.label: Langley Air Force Base / Joint Base Langley-Eustis, Virginia
langley-2023-incursions.note: Joint Base Langley-Eustis first observed unidentified uncrewed aerial systems over the installation on the evening of 6 December 2023, with multiple further incursions through the month. The episode is the location's whole reason for being on this board.

langley-2023-incursions.label: Joint Base Langley-Eustis, Virginia
langley-2023-incursions.note: The Air Force confirmed activity beginning the evening of 6 December 2023 and continuing through the month, prompting F-16 CAPs, NASA WB-57F orbits and FBI coordination.

langley-2023-incursions.label: New Jersey and East Coast Drone Wave (Nov-Dec 2024)
langley-2023-incursions.why: Twelve months apart; the second wave was publicly resolved, the first never was
langley-2023-incursions.note: Langley produced no attribution and no public explanation; New Jersey produced a four-agency statement attributing 5,000 reports to hobbyists and misidentifications on the basis of about 100 leads.

langley-2023-incursions.label: NORAD and US Northern Command
langley-2023-incursions.note: Guillot testified the Langley incidents dominated his assessment on taking command in February 2024 and were 'the centerpiece' of his review.

langley-2023-incursions.label: Gregory M. Guillot
langley-2023-incursions.why: Public non-attribution finding by the homeland air defence commander
langley-2023-incursions.note: 'I have not seen [and] I do not know of any organized or unorganized foreign nexus' - a four-star conceding that seventeen nights of intrusions over an F-22 base cannot be attributed.

langley-2023-incursions.label: Jon T. Kosloski
langley-2023-incursions.why: AARO's case work does not address the domestic incursion wave
langley-2023-incursions.note: Neither the published case slides nor the FY2025 report present an assessment of the Langley, New Jersey or Barksdale incursions, which are handled as a counter-UAS force-protection matter by NORTHCOM and JIATF-401 instead. Reasoning: absence across all published AARO products, not a stated jurisdictional ruling.

nj-drone-incursions-2024.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
nj-drone-incursions-2024.note: DoD, DHS, FBI and FAA: 'We have not identified anything anomalous, and do not assess the activity to date to present a national security or public safety risk.' The same statement conceded limited sightings over restricted military airspace, contradicting earlier White House denials.

nj-drone-incursions-2024.label: Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401)
nj-drone-incursions-2024.why: Task force stood up in August 2025 after two years of unattributed incursions
nj-drone-incursions-2024.note: A standing joint interagency task force under a general officer is the institutional refutation of the hobbyist explanation issued eight months earlier.

nj-drone-incursions-2024.label: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio
nj-drone-incursions-2024.why: Wright-Patterson closed its airspace for nearly four hours during the wave
nj-drone-incursions-2024.note: The 14-15 December 2024 airspace closure over unauthorized drone activity occurred days before the federal statement that nothing anomalous had been identified.

nj-drone-incursions-2024.label: Langley AFB Drone Incursions (December 2023)
nj-drone-incursions-2024.why: Twelve months apart; the second wave was publicly resolved, the first never was
nj-drone-incursions-2024.note: Langley produced no attribution and no public explanation; New Jersey produced a four-agency statement attributing 5,000 reports to hobbyists and misidentifications on the basis of about 100 leads.

barksdale-2026-incursions.label: Barksdale Air Force Base, Louisiana
barksdale-2026-incursions.why: Site of the March 2026 incursion waves and FPCON Charlie alert
barksdale-2026-incursions.note: Barksdale raised force protection and issued a shelter-in-place order on 9 March 2026; base public affairs confirmed the UAS report and FAA involvement.

barksdale-2026-incursions.label: Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401)
barksdale-2026-incursions.why: The 2026 bomber-base incursions are the task force's live problem
barksdale-2026-incursions.note: Waves of 12-15 jam-resistant drones over a B-52 base during an active bombing campaign, with a single counter-drone fly-away kit fielded, define the capability gap DODIG-2026-045 described.

barksdale-2026-incursions.label: Gregory M. Guillot
barksdale-2026-incursions.why: Confirmed year-on-year increase in detections over installations
barksdale-2026-incursions.note: 'We've seen an increase from last year in the number of detections over military installations,' with roughly a quarter now defeated versus almost none previously.

shootdowns-feb-2023.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
shootdowns-feb-2023.why: Lake Huron engagement video withheld until the May 2026 PURSUE release
shootdowns-feb-2023.note: Infrared footage of the 12 February 2023 shootdown was released on 22 May 2026 via PURSUE, with the entry noting an unusual lack of substantiated chain of custody.

shootdowns-feb-2023.label: NORAD and US Northern Command
shootdowns-feb-2023.why: NORAD-controlled fighters destroyed three unidentified objects in four days
shootdowns-feb-2023.note: Two F-16CMs of the Minnesota Air National Guard's 148th Fighter Wing destroyed the Lake Huron object with an AIM-9X at roughly 20,000 feet on 12 February 2023.

shootdowns-feb-2023.label: Charette Privy Council Memorandum (Secret, 14 Feb 2023)
shootdowns-feb-2023.why: Allied government's contemporaneous Secret record of the engagements
shootdowns-feb-2023.note: The 14 February 2023 Privy Council memo to Prime Minister Trudeau documents that exploitation of the Alaska object was incomplete and the Yukon object unverified as to function and propulsion.

shootdowns-feb-2023.label: Sean M. Kirkpatrick
shootdowns-feb-2023.why: Retrospective 'they were balloons' characterisation contradicts the contemporaneous allied record
shootdowns-feb-2023.note: Kirkpatrick: 'We scrambled jets and shot down a bunch of things. Do you know what we shot down? Balloons.' The Canadian Clerk of the Privy Council's Secret memo of 14 Feb 2023 records the Yukon object's function and propulsion as unverified.

uss-jackson-2023.label: Southern California Operating Areas (W-291 and Baja approaches)
uss-jackson-2023.why: W-291 encounter occurred in the same operating-area complex
uss-jackson-2023.note: Wiggins's statement places the event in Warning Area W-291 off Southern California.

uss-jackson-2023.label: USS Jackson (LCS-6)
uss-jackson-2023.why: The ship whose EO/IR system produced the recording
uss-jackson-2023.note: The footage carries 'timestamps, lat/long, and platform readouts consistent with USS Jackson's location' - precisely the metadata the NASA study team said government UAP holdings lack.

uss-jackson-2023.label: Jeremy Kenyon Lockyer Corbell
uss-jackson-2023.why: Footage reached the public through journalists, not through the Navy or AARO
uss-jackson-2023.note: Wiggins's statement records that the stabilized footage and screenshots were published by journalists Jeremy Corbell and George Knapp.

uss-jackson-2023.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
uss-jackson-2023.why: Same warning-area complex, same object morphology, nineteen years later
uss-jackson-2023.note: A transmedium tic-tac-shaped object in W-291 in February 2023 repeats the November 2004 description in the same Southern California naval training space, with no published government assessment of either sensor record.

uss-jackson-2023.label: Alexandro Wiggins
uss-jackson-2023.why: Supervised the watch and the recording of the 15 Feb 2023 encounter
uss-jackson-2023.note: Wiggins testified as an active-duty Senior Chief Operations Specialist that CIC recorded four objects on Star SAFIRE with intact position and time metadata.

uss-reagan-2004.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
uss-reagan-2004.why: Federal records destroyed at the point of creation
uss-reagan-2004.note: A Boatswain's Mate of the Watch says he was ordered to 'rip it out' of the logbook; another witness says he watched an officer order subordinates to remove pages. No Navy accounting of this has ever been made.

uss-reagan-2004.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
uss-reagan-2004.why: Same year, opposite ocean, same record-destruction behaviour
uss-reagan-2004.note: Reagan watchstanders describe deck log pages being torn out on a senior officer's order; Princeton crew describe recording media removed. Deck logs are federal records.

vandenberg-2003.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
vandenberg-2003.why: Nuccetelli says the Air Force records are now held by AARO and the FBI
vandenberg-2003.note: 'Official Air Force records documenting it are now held by AARO and the FBI.' A specific, FOIA-targetable custody claim that neither agency has confirmed or denied.

vandenberg-2003.label: Jeffrey Nuccetelli
vandenberg-2003.why: Military police witness and report recipient at Vandenberg, 2003-2005
vandenberg-2003.note: Nuccetelli testified to reports of a glowing red square over two missile defense sites on 14 October 2003 and a triangular craft over the main base in 2005.

nasa-uap-ist.label: David N. Spergel
nasa-uap-ist.why: Chaired the NASA UAP Independent Study Team
nasa-uap-ist.note: Spergel chaired the sixteen-member panel whose final report was released 14 September 2023.

nasa-uap-ist.label: Michael Gold
nasa-uap-ist.note: Gold is listed among the team's members and later testified to Congress on its findings.

nasa-uap-ist.label: Nicola J. Fox
nasa-uap-ist.why: NASA science chief at the report release briefing
nasa-uap-ist.note: Fox appeared at the 14 September 2023 briefing where NASA announced a Director of UAP Research without naming the appointee.

nasa-uap-ist.label: ODNI Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (25 June 2021)
nasa-uap-ist.why: Both diagnose the same evidentiary deficit
nasa-uap-ist.note: ODNI: military sensors 'are not generally suited for identifying UAP.' NASA: analysis is 'hampered by poor sensor calibration, the lack of multiple measurements, the lack of sensor metadata.'

nasa-uap-ist.label: Americans for Safe Aerospace
nasa-uap-ist.why: Shared reporting-reform agenda: ASRS and FAA pilot reporting
nasa-uap-ist.note: The NASA study team recommended enhancing the Aviation Safety Reporting System for commercial pilot UAP reporting; ASA performs the equivalent intake function for aircrew outside the chain of command.

nasa-uap-ist.label: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
nasa-uap-ist.why: NASA chartered and published the Independent Study Team report
nasa-uap-ist.note: The 16-member panel reported on 14 September 2023 with findings on data curation, satellite assets and the classification obstacle.

nasa-uap-ist.label: David N. Spergel
nasa-uap-ist.why: Panel worked under sustained public harassment
nasa-uap-ist.note: Gold testified that designated federal officer Daniel Evans 'did an amazing job under difficult conditions' - the euphemism recording the abuse the panel absorbed.

nasa-uap-ist.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
nasa-uap-ist.why: Metadata stripping defeats the study team's core recommendation
nasa-uap-ist.note: NASA's panel identified missing sensor metadata as the principal obstacle to analysis; the 2026 releases removed exactly that metadata before publication.

jiatf-401.label: Matt Ross
jiatf-401.why: Director of JIATF-401 from its establishment
jiatf-401.note: Brig. Gen. Matt Ross directs the counter-drone joint interagency task force established in August 2025.

jiatf-401.label: New Jersey and East Coast Drone Wave (Nov-Dec 2024)
jiatf-401.why: Task force stood up in August 2025 after two years of unattributed incursions
jiatf-401.note: A standing joint interagency task force under a general officer is the institutional refutation of the hobbyist explanation issued eight months earlier.

jiatf-401.label: Barksdale AFB and Strategic Base Incursions (Feb-Mar 2026)
jiatf-401.why: The 2026 bomber-base incursions are the task force's live problem
jiatf-401.note: Waves of 12-15 jam-resistant drones over a B-52 base during an active bombing campaign, with a single counter-drone fly-away kit fielded, define the capability gap DODIG-2026-045 described.

charette-memo-2023.label: February 2023 Alaska, Yukon and Lake Huron Shootdowns
charette-memo-2023.why: Allied government's contemporaneous Secret record of the engagements
charette-memo-2023.note: The 14 February 2023 Privy Council memo to Prime Minister Trudeau documents that exploitation of the Alaska object was incomplete and the Yukon object unverified as to function and propulsion.

gallaudet-2015-email.label: Navy Range Fouler Reports (72 reports, 2004-2021)
gallaudet-2015-email.why: Two independent traces of the same suppression at fleet level
gallaudet-2015-email.note: The range fouler set records reporting terminating at Third Fleet with no dissemination process; Gallaudet records a Fleet Forces Command safety message deleted within a day.

gallaudet-2015-email.label: GO FAST (Navy ATFLIR video, January 2015)
gallaudet-2015-email.why: The recalled fleet safety message carried the GO FAST video
gallaudet-2015-email.note: Gallaudet's written testimony states the January 2015 'URGENT SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE' email attached the GO FAST video and cited 'multiple near-midair collisions.'

gallaudet-2015-email.label: USS Theodore Roosevelt Encounters (2014-2015)
gallaudet-2015-email.why: Command-level reaction to the encounter series
gallaudet-2015-email.note: The message describes exactly the problem Graves's squadron reported - repeated near-midairs with unidentified objects in working airspace - and was withdrawn within 24 hours.

gallaudet-2015-email.label: Immaculate Constellation disclosure, October-November 2024
gallaudet-2015-email.why: Gallaudet's inference points at an unacknowledged SAP; Shellenberger named one
gallaudet-2015-email.note: Gallaudet concluded the recalled information 'must have been classified within a special access program managed by an intelligence agency'; at the same hearing Shellenberger described an alleged parent USAP consolidating UAP imagery collection.

gallaudet-2015-email.label: Timothy Gallaudet
gallaudet-2015-email.why: Recipient of the message and the witness to its deletion
gallaudet-2015-email.note: Gallaudet, then Commander of Naval Meteorology and Oceanography Command, testified the email vanished from his and other recipients' accounts the next day.

l-socal-oparea.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
l-socal-oparea.why: The encounters occurred in the Southern California operating areas
l-socal-oparea.note: The Nimitz Carrier Strike Group was working up in the W-291 warning area and Baja approaches when Princeton began holding the tracks.

l-socal-oparea.label: July 2019 Drone Swarms, USS Kidd / USS Russell and CSG ships off California
l-socal-oparea.why: Multi-night unattributed swarms against destroyers in the SoCal operating areas
l-socal-oparea.note: Deck logs from USS Kidd, Rafael Peralta, Russell and John Finn, obtained under FOIA and cross-checked against AIS tracking, document the July 2019 events.

l-socal-oparea.label: USS Jackson (LCS-6) Encounter, 15 February 2023
l-socal-oparea.why: W-291 encounter occurred in the same operating-area complex
l-socal-oparea.note: Wiggins's statement places the event in Warning Area W-291 off Southern California.

l-w72.label: USS Theodore Roosevelt Encounters (2014-2015)
l-w72.why: Site of the near-midair that anchors the safety case
l-w72.note: Restricted training airspace ten miles east of Virginia Beach where two F/A-18Fs 100 feet apart took evasive action around a stationary cube-in-sphere object.

l-langley.label: Langley AFB Drone Incursions (December 2023)
l-langley.note: The Air Force confirmed activity beginning the evening of 6 December 2023 and continuing through the month, prompting F-16 CAPs, NASA WB-57F orbits and FBI coordination.

l-barksdale.label: Barksdale AFB and Strategic Base Incursions (Feb-Mar 2026)
l-barksdale.why: Site of the March 2026 incursion waves and FPCON Charlie alert
l-barksdale.note: Barksdale raised force protection and issued a shelter-in-place order on 9 March 2026; base public affairs confirmed the UAS report and FAA involvement.

uss-jackson.label: USS Jackson (LCS-6) Encounter, 15 February 2023
uss-jackson.why: The ship whose EO/IR system produced the recording
uss-jackson.note: The footage carries 'timestamps, lat/long, and platform readouts consistent with USS Jackson's location' - precisely the metadata the NASA study team said government UAP holdings lack.

house-oversight-committee.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
house-oversight-committee.why: Told committee staff that only HASC and HAC-D members could be read in on UAP special access programs
house-oversight-committee.note: Luna's 9 Sept 2025 opening statement is the primary record of the read-in gate.

house-oversight-committee.label: Legislative Process (proposed and pending)
house-oversight-committee.why: the venue where the record is made under oath, and the only House committee with unilateral subpoena power in the chair's hands
house-oversight-committee.note: Oversight held the 26 July 2023 hearing, the 13 November 2024 hearing and, through its declassification task force, the 9 September 2025 hearing. Sworn testimony taken in this committee is the mechanism by which allegations enter the legislative process at all, which is a different function from enacting text.

house-oversight-committee.label: House Oversight hearing: 'DoW Financial Management: Examining Progress and New Audit Approaches' (13 May 2026)
house-oversight-committee.note: The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform held the DoW financial management hearing at which Deputy IG Mansfield testified. Attested by the OIG's publication of his statement.

house-oversight-committee.label: Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation

house-oversight-committee.label: Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs
house-oversight-committee.why: Parent committee of the subcommittee that held the founding UAP hearing
house-oversight-committee.note: The Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs is a standing subcommittee of the Committee on Oversight and Accountability; the printed hearing record carries both rosters.

house-oversight-committee.label: Jamin Ben Raskin
house-oversight-committee.why: Ranking Member of the full committee at the time of the founding hearing
house-oversight-committee.note: Raskin took two full rounds of questioning at the 26 July 2023 subcommittee hearing.

house-oversight-committee.label: Project On Government Oversight
house-oversight-committee.why: Outside watchdog seated as witness before Oversight's declassification task force
house-oversight-committee.note: POGO appeared before the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, and used the appearance to recommend statutory changes (overturning Navy v. Egan, independent adjudication for IC and military whistleblowers) that bear directly on the committee's UAP inquiry.

house-oversight-committee.label: The HASC/HAC-D special access program read-in gate
house-oversight-committee.why: The jurisdictional routing that keeps the subpoena committee uncleared
house-oversight-committee.note: Documented by Luna on 9 September 2025; corroborated by Burlison's 2024 AARO briefing block and his 2025 non-germane amendment ruling.

house-oversight-committee.label: United States House of Representatives
house-oversight-committee.why: Committee that took the 2023 and 2024 public UAP testimony
house-oversight-committee.note: House Oversight held the 26 July 2023 hearing and the 13 November 2024 hearing, and its Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets held the 9 September 2025 hearing.

house-oversight-committee.label: Waived SAP Notification Group
house-oversight-committee.why: not a defense committee; receives nothing under 10 U.S.C. 119
house-oversight-committee.note: The July 2023 Grusch testimony was taken by a House Oversight subcommittee. That committee has no entitlement under section 119(e)(2) and no statutory route to compel waived-SAP material, which is a structural reason why the hearing could establish allegation but not access.

house-oversight-committee.label: FY2024 IAA sec. 7606(c) — Agency Review of Special Access Programs
house-oversight-committee.why: Reports on SAP access populations are addressed to House Oversight among others
house-oversight-committee.note: Sec. 7606(c)(2) names the Committee on Oversight and Accountability of the House of Representatives among the recipients.

house-oversight-committee.label: 50 U.S.C. 3348 — Reports Relating to Certain SAPs and Similar Programs
house-oversight-committee.why: Gives House Oversight a statutory entitlement to SAP reports from every covered agency
house-oversight-committee.note: 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(1)(C) names the committee; 3348(g)(2)(B) excludes only DoD, NNSA and IC agencies from the reporting obligation.

house-oversight-committee.label: The misappropriation allegation: Grusch's ICIG complaint and sworn testimony
house-oversight-committee.why: Sworn testimony before the committee, 26 July 2023
house-oversight-committee.note: Grusch testified with Ryan Graves and David Fravor at 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency'. Attested by the committee's own hearing page.

house-oversight-committee.label: The MITRE Corporation
house-oversight-committee.why: Conditions any production on coordination with the sponsoring federal agencies
house-oversight-committee.note: MITRE: 'If any relevant material is found, we will coordinate with the federal agencies responsible for the work to determine how to best provide any assets' - a compliance posture with an executive-branch veto inside it.

house-oversight-committee.label: House Oversight probe into deaths and disappearances of scientists, April 2026
house-oversight-committee.why: Run by the same committee and the same member as the UAP inquiry
house-oversight-committee.note: The convergence of the two inquiries in one subcommittee chair is the structural link between this board and The Vanishing.

house-oversight-committee.label: Robert Garcia
house-oversight-committee.why: Ranking Member of the full committee from 2025
house-oversight-committee.note: Garcia moved from subcommittee ranking member to full-committee ranking member in the 119th Congress; printed in the CHRG-119hhrg61718 roster.

house-oversight-committee.label: Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets
house-oversight-committee.why: Chairman Comer created the Task Force and gave it the UAP declassification remit
house-oversight-committee.note: Comer announced the Task Force on 11 February 2025 and named Luna chairwoman; its roster is printed in the 9 Sept 2025 hearing record.

house-oversight-committee.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
house-oversight-committee.why: Executive-controlled release running in parallel to, and in tension with, the committee's compelled-production track

hoc-subcommittee-national-security.label: Glenn S. Grothman

U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

hoc-subcommittee-national-security.label: Robert Garcia
hoc-subcommittee-national-security.note: Garcia delivered the Ranking Member opening statement on 26 July 2023.

hoc-subcommittee-cybersecurity-it.label: House Oversight joint hearing, 13 November 2024 - 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth'

hoc-subcommittee-cybersecurity-it.label: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

task-force-declassification-federal-secr.note: Printed as Chairwoman in the roster of CHRG-119hhrg61718 and on the committee's membership page.

House Oversight Task Force hearing: 'Mind Control and Accountability: Uncovering the Truth of the CIA's MKULTRA Project', 30 June 2026

congressional-uap-caucus.label: Legislative Process (proposed and pending)

congressional-uap-caucus.note: Launched by Rep. Tim Burchett on 22 August 2023 alongside a caucus letter to the Intelligence Community Inspector General, with documented members including Burchett, Luna, Burlison, Moskowitz and Ogles. Its confirmed operational achievement is the 12 January 2024 closed briefing; Ogles is a member without an Oversight seat, which is how the caucus extends reach beyond the committee.

congressional-uap-caucus.label: Waived SAP Notification Group
congressional-uap-caucus.why: caucus membership confers no statutory access
congressional-uap-caucus.note: A congressional caucus is not a committee and appears nowhere in 10 U.S.C. 119(g). Caucus members acquire no entitlement to waived-SAP notification, which is why UAP advocacy in Congress has consistently sought to legislate new access rather than to invoke existing access.

congressional-uap-caucus.label: Andrew Ogles
congressional-uap-caucus.why: Caucus member without an Oversight Committee seat
congressional-uap-caucus.note: Described by The Hill as 'part of the UAP Caucus but not the Oversight Committee.'

congressional-uap-caucus.label: Anna Paulina Luna
congressional-uap-caucus.why: Caucus member; later chairs the Task Force

congressional-uap-caucus.label: Eric Burlison
congressional-uap-caucus.note: Described as a member of the caucus in March 2024 and again in June 2026.

sap-readin-gate.why: The jurisdictional routing that keeps the subpoena committee uncleared

sap-readin-gate.label: United States House of Representatives

sap-readin-gate.note: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) para 4.f is the written rule that members of the defense and intelligence committees are authorised access to DoD SAPs 'except for waived programs'.

sap-readin-gate.label: Andrew Ogles
sap-readin-gate.why: Named the Holman Rule as the enforcement instrument against officials who deny Congress access
sap-readin-gate.note: The only statutory enforcement mechanism any member has named on the record; never used on this subject.

sap-readin-gate.label: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)
sap-readin-gate.why: SAPCO administers the read-in architecture Luna described
sap-readin-gate.note: Chairwoman Luna testified on 9 September 2025 that a non-committee member must be approved by the chairman and ranking member of both HASC and HAC-D to view specific material; the underlying access records and accreditation are held by the SAPCO enterprise.

sap-readin-gate.label: Glenn S. Grothman
sap-readin-gate.why: Grothman's 'inside and outside of the SCIF' claim cannot be reconciled with the read-in gate Luna documented
sap-readin-gate.note: Reasoning: Grothman said in Nov 2024 that members questioned agencies inside and outside the SCIF without substantiating Grusch; Luna said in Sept 2025 that Oversight members were not eligible for the relevant read-ins at all. Both are on the same committee's record.

sap-readin-gate.label: Michael John Gallagher
sap-readin-gate.why: Held simultaneously the HASC and HPSCI seats that constitute the read-in tier Oversight was excluded from
sap-readin-gate.note: Reasoning: Luna's 2025 statement identifies HASC and HAC-D membership as the read-in gate; Gallagher held HASC and HPSCI through the 118th Congress and chaired a select committee. Whether he was ever read in on UAP SAPs is unresolved and is a live research question.

sap-readin-gate.label: Proposed House Select Committee on UAP
sap-readin-gate.why: A select committee is the instrument that would route around the read-in gate
sap-readin-gate.note: Reasoning: a select committee carries its own clearance posture and subpoena authority and is not subject to another committee's read-in approval. Burlison's stated rationale was that DoD 'weren't transparent to us in a SCIF setting.'

immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.label: Timothy Floyd Burchett
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.why: Distributed the document to every member on the dais and moved to enter it
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.note: Mace announced that Burchett held the document and would enter it into the record.

immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.label: Immaculate Constellation disclosure, October-November 2024
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.why: The congressional-record instantiation of the alleged parent USAP
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.note: Shellenberger described the program in the document as 'a central or parent USAP that consolidates observations of UAPs by both tasked and untasked collection platforms.'

immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.label: Luis D. Elizondo
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.why: Refused to confirm or deny by name or trigraph
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.note: Asked directly whether he had been read in, Elizondo said he would not be authorised to confirm nor deny the existence of any special access program by name or trigraph.

immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.label: Michael Shellenberger
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.why: Delivered the document to Congress on the morning of the hearing and testified to its contents
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.note: Shellenberger supplied the 12-page report that Chairwoman Mace moved into the Congressional Record, and testified to its contents under oath.

immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.why: Pentagon says it has no record of the program described in the document entered into the Congressional Record
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.note: Pentagon spokesperson Sue Gough stated DoD has 'no record' of such a program; Kirkpatrick also denied it. The document remains in the Record.

immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.label: Sean M. Kirkpatrick
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.why: Former AARO director denied the programme's existence
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.note: Kirkpatrick, who authored Volume I's methodology, publicly denied that Immaculate Constellation exists.

immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.label: Sue Gough
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.why: Department says it has no record of the programme
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.note: Gough's 'no record' statement is the Department's entire published response to a document in the Congressional Record; no documentary rebuttal has been produced.

immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.label: AARO FY2025 Consolidated Annual Report on UAP
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.why: No AARO product has ever addressed the name in the Record
immaculate-constellation-12-page-report.note: Neither the FY2024 nor the FY2025 annual report, nor any statement for the record, addresses a purported USAP name entered into the Congressional Record in November 2024.

hr-10111-uap-whistleblower-protection-ac.label: Timothy Floyd Burchett
hr-10111-uap-whistleblower-protection-ac.note: Introduced 12 November 2024, the day before the Oversight hearing.

hr-5060-uap-whistleblower-protection-act.label: Elijah Crane
hr-5060-uap-whistleblower-protection-act.note: Congress.gov cosponsor record; Crane also entered the Grusch reprisal letter into the record of the hearing that followed.

hr-5060-uap-whistleblower-protection-act.label: Timothy Floyd Burchett
hr-5060-uap-whistleblower-protection-act.note: Introduced 29 August 2025, eleven days before the Task Force hearing.

hr-5060-uap-whistleblower-protection-act.label: Dylan Borland
hr-5060-uap-whistleblower-protection-act.why: The reprisal case the bill is designed to cover
hr-5060-uap-whistleblower-protection-act.note: Reasoning: Borland testified to a decade of sustained reprisal at the hearing convened to advance whistleblower protections, and Luna closed the hearing urging members to sign a protection letter on his behalf.

hr-1187-uap-transparency-act.label: Timothy Floyd Burchett
hr-1187-uap-transparency-act.note: Introduced 11 February 2025, the day the Task Force was announced.

hr-8424-uap-transparency-act.label: Timothy Floyd Burchett
hr-8424-uap-transparency-act.note: Died in referral; refiled as H.R. 1187.

hr-6967-safe-airspace-for-americans-act.label: Robert Garcia
hr-6967-safe-airspace-for-americans-act.note: Introduced 11 January 2024, the day before the ICIG briefing.

hr-6967-safe-airspace-for-americans-act.label: Glenn S. Grothman
hr-6967-safe-airspace-for-americans-act.note: The Hill records Garcia introducing the bill 'along with Rep. Glenn Grothman.'

hr-6967-safe-airspace-for-americans-act.label: Ryan Graves
hr-6967-safe-airspace-for-americans-act.why: His hearing testimony on the reporting gap is the bill's origin
hr-6967-safe-airspace-for-americans-act.note: Reasoning: Garcia's 26 July 2023 questioning of Graves concentrated entirely on the absence of a civilian reporting channel and pilot stigma, and the bill creates exactly that channel six months later.

uap-select-committee-proposal.label: James Comer Jr.
uap-select-committee-proposal.why: Reported to support the proposed select committee; never created one
uap-select-committee-proposal.note: Burlison named Comer's support publicly on 12 March 2024.

uap-select-committee-proposal.label: Eric Burlison
uap-select-committee-proposal.why: Led the March 2024 call for a select committee focused on expenditures
uap-select-committee-proposal.note: Burlison said he had the support of Comer, Burchett and Moskowitz but had not raised it with Speaker Johnson.

uap-select-committee-proposal.label: Timothy Floyd Burchett
uap-select-committee-proposal.why: Led the earlier select committee effort under Speaker McCarthy
uap-select-committee-proposal.note: The effort was lost when McCarthy lost the speakership.

uap-select-committee-proposal.label: The HASC/HAC-D special access program read-in gate
uap-select-committee-proposal.why: A select committee is the instrument that would route around the read-in gate
uap-select-committee-proposal.note: Reasoning: a select committee carries its own clearance posture and subpoena authority and is not subject to another committee's read-in approval. Burlison's stated rationale was that DoD 'weren't transparent to us in a SCIF setting.'

burlison-mitre-letter-2026.label: The MITRE Corporation
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.why: MITRE routes the answer back through its sponsoring agencies
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.note: A MITRE spokesperson said that if any relevant material is found, 'we will coordinate with the federal agencies responsible for the work' - restating the FAR structure under which disclosure runs to the sponsor, not to Congress.

burlison-mitre-letter-2026.label: Eric Burlison
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.why: Author of the 22 May 2026 records demand
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.note: Ten pages, 40+ production requests, records back to 1930, 45-day deadline, native format with metadata.

burlison-mitre-letter-2026.label: The MITRE Corporation
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.why: Demands production of all MITRE UAP and reverse-engineering records back to 1930
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.note: More than 40 production requests with a 5/10/14/30/45-day compliance schedule; MITRE confirmed it was reviewing its archives.

burlison-mitre-letter-2026.label: Eric Burlison
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.why: Author of the 22 May 2026 production request to MITRE
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.note: Burlison, a member of the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, issued the first congressional records demand ever addressed to an FFRDC operator on UAP.

burlison-mitre-letter-2026.label: FAR 35.017 - Federally Funded Research and Development Centers
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.why: The letter's legal theory rests on the FFRDC access provisions
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.note: Burlison argues FFRDCs 'often receive special access to government facilities, data, sponsor requirements, and sensitive technical information that ordinary private contractors may not receive' and therefore cannot be private vaults for federal records.

burlison-mitre-letter-2026.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.why: Framed as enforcement of the records identified for public release under the 2026 disclosure push
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.note: Burlison ties the demand to records 'Congress has directed to be identified, preserved, reviewed, and transferred for public release', naming NARA and Record Group 615.

burlison-mitre-letter-2026.label: 'The MITRE Corporation - UFO Reverse Engineering, USO Tracking, & Legacy Programs'
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.why: Published as declared support for the congressional inquiry opened 11 weeks earlier
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.note: Burlison's letter is dated 22 May 2026; the investigation was published 7 August 2026 and states it seeks to directly aid that inquiry.

burlison-mitre-letter-2026.label: David Charles Grusch
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.why: The letter reflects concerns raised by whistleblowers alleging contractor-held programmes
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.note: DefenseScoop reports the correspondence reflects whistleblower concerns; Grusch's central allegation is that programmes were compartmented inside private entities beyond congressional oversight.

burlison-mitre-letter-2026.label: David Charles Grusch
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.why: Grusch's contractor-custody thesis is the stated basis of Burlison's FFRDC campaign
burlison-mitre-letter-2026.note: Reasoning: Burlison paraphrases Grusch's testimony directly - 'If you really want to hide something from Congress, you don't put it in a government file cabinet. You hand it to a private contractor' - and then names the FFRDCs he is writing to.

burlison-mit-lincoln-letter-2026.label: Eric Burlison
burlison-mit-lincoln-letter-2026.why: Author of the May 2026 demand for the 1952 'flying saucer talk' recording
burlison-mit-lincoln-letter-2026.note: Announced 15 May 2026; Lincoln Laboratory's attorneys agreed to comply within 30 days.

burlison-mit-lincoln-letter-2026.label: MIT Lincoln Laboratory
burlison-mit-lincoln-letter-2026.why: Extracted an acknowledgment of existence and an agreement to produce from an FFRDC
burlison-mit-lincoln-letter-2026.note: By 25 June 2026 Lincoln Laboratory had agreed to make the material available - the first documented FFRDC production commitment in response to a UAP congressional demand.

luna-hegseth-video-letter-2026.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
luna-hegseth-video-letter-2026.why: Targets video records the Task Force was told AARO holds
luna-hegseth-video-letter-2026.note: The Department did not produce by the deadline.

luna-hegseth-video-letter-2026.label: Anna Paulina Luna
luna-hegseth-video-letter-2026.why: Author of the 1 April 2026 demand for AARO's unreleased UAP video files
luna-hegseth-video-letter-2026.note: Predicated on whistleblower information given to the Task Force that AARO holds additional video records.

crane-secdef-grusch-reprisal-letter-2025.label: Elijah Crane
crane-secdef-grusch-reprisal-letter-2025.why: Author; entered it into the hearing record while still awaiting a reply
crane-secdef-grusch-reprisal-letter-2025.note: Three enumerated adverse actions against the credible-and-urgent whistleblower.

crane-secdef-grusch-reprisal-letter-2025.label: David Charles Grusch
crane-secdef-grusch-reprisal-letter-2025.why: The only congressional document enumerating the reprisal actions taken against Grusch
crane-secdef-grusch-reprisal-letter-2025.note: Clearance removal, denial of promotion, loss of medical retirement.

comer-luna-agency-letters-2025.label: Anna Paulina Luna
comer-luna-agency-letters-2025.note: Requesting a briefing on all UAP-related records in the recipients' possession.

comer-luna-agency-letters-2025.label: Central Intelligence Agency
comer-luna-agency-letters-2025.note: Ratcliffe had said as DNI that UAP exhibit technologies the United States does not have.

comer-luna-agency-letters-2025.label: James Comer Jr.
comer-luna-agency-letters-2025.why: Co-author of the Task Force's opening records demand to State, Defense and CIA
comer-luna-agency-letters-2025.note: Sent on establishment of the Task Force in February 2025.

comer-luna-agency-letters-2025.label: Marco Rubio
comer-luna-agency-letters-2025.why: Addressed to the Secretary of State, who had publicly described UAP whistleblowers approaching Senate Intelligence
comer-luna-agency-letters-2025.note: Rubio was one of five Senate cosponsors of the UAP Disclosure Act before joining the executive branch.

mit-lincoln-laboratory.label: The MITRE Corporation
mit-lincoln-laboratory.why: MITRE was spun out of Lincoln Laboratory Division 6 in 1958
mit-lincoln-laboratory.note: 485 Lincoln Laboratory employees moved to the new corporation on incorporation, 21 July 1958, to continue SAGE systems engineering under Air Force sponsorship.

mit-lincoln-laboratory.label: Eric Burlison
mit-lincoln-laboratory.why: 8 May 2026 letter demanding the 1952 Ruppelt recording by file designation
mit-lincoln-laboratory.note: Burlison asked Lincoln Laboratory to determine the status of 'AF-ATIC-FILM, 03/52' and coordinate with NARA on preservation and archival review.

mit-lincoln-laboratory.label: AF-ATIC-FILM, 03/52 ('flying saucer talk')
mit-lincoln-laboratory.why: Holds the March 1952 Ruppelt 'flying saucer talk' recording
mit-lincoln-laboratory.note: By 25 June 2026 Burlison announced the laboratory had agreed to disclose it - the first FFRDC-held UAP record obtained by Congress by naming the file.

mit-lincoln-laboratory.label: Project Beacon Hill
mit-lincoln-laboratory.why: Beacon Hill was convened in the MIT/Lincoln Laboratory complex for the Air Force
mit-lincoln-laboratory.note: The study shaped US overhead reconnaissance and its records sit in institutional rather than federal custody.

mit-lincoln-laboratory.label: Rep. Burlison letter to MIT Lincoln Laboratory, May 2026
mit-lincoln-laboratory.why: Extracted an acknowledgment of existence and an agreement to produce from an FFRDC
mit-lincoln-laboratory.note: By 25 June 2026 Lincoln Laboratory had agreed to make the material available - the first documented FFRDC production commitment in response to a UAP congressional demand.

missing-scientists-probe-2026.label: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
missing-scientists-probe-2026.why: Run by the same committee and the same member as the UAP inquiry
missing-scientists-probe-2026.note: The convergence of the two inquiries in one subcommittee chair is the structural link between this board and The Vanishing.

missing-scientists-probe-2026.label: Eric Burlison
missing-scientists-probe-2026.why: Co-launched the probe; revealed the McCasland trigger
missing-scientists-probe-2026.note: Burlison's staff had been trying to reach McCasland about a separate congressional investigation before he vanished.
