uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.why: PURSUE named as an authorized receiving channel for waived-NDA disclosures
uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.note: Senior officials described former officials meeting with cleared AARO or PURSUE task force officials who may waive applicable NDAs during authorized discussions, with information then routed through existing declassification procedures.

uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.label: David Charles Grusch
uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.why: The waiver reproduces the channel that failed Grusch
uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.note: The directive unbinds witnesses only inside the executive channel controlled by the institution they would accuse, which is the structure that ended Grusch's career after his ICIG-channel disclosure.

uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.label: Luis D. Elizondo
uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.why: the paradigm case the waiver addresses
uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.note: Elizondo is the archetype of a former official constrained by prepublication review and secrecy obligations; the ODNI memorandum waives 'agreements, oaths, or commitments' for disclosure to government investigators, not to publishers.

uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.label: David Charles Grusch
uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.why: NDA waiver regime addresses the exact obstacle Grusch's witnesses faced
uap-nda-waiver-directive-2026.note: Grusch swore in 2023 that witnesses would come forward only behind closed doors and with assurances that breaking NDAs would not be prosecuted. The July 2026 directive waives UAP-related NDAs for disclosures to cleared AARO or PURSUE officials. Reasoning: the directive's mechanism maps directly onto the barrier Grusch described under oath, though no document ties the two.

nasic.label: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio
nasic.why: NASIC is the current tenant institution at Wright-Patterson
nasic.note: The National Air and Space Intelligence Center is a Wright-Patterson tenant and the direct institutional heir to ATIC/FTD's foreign materiel exploitation mission.

nasic.label: Air Force Research Laboratory
nasic.why: Co-located at Wright-Patterson with the successor to the Foreign Technology Division
nasic.note: NASIC is the lineal successor to ATIC and FTD, the organisations that ran SIGN, GRUDGE and BLUE BOOK and exploited foreign aerospace materiel. AFRL and NASIC share the installation.

nasic.label: "Jonathan Grey" (pseudonym)
nasic.why: Serving intelligence officer at NASIC, Wright-Patterson AFB
nasic.note: Kean identifies Grey as a currently serving NASIC officer with Top Secret clearance; the installation is the historical center of gravity for every legacy custody allegation.

compass-rose-legal-group.label: David Charles Grusch
compass-rose-legal-group.why: Firm that filed Grusch's statutory ICIG whistleblower complaint
compass-rose-legal-group.note: Grusch retained Compass Rose Legal Group (senior partner I. Charles McCullough III, the first Intelligence Community Inspector General) to file and pursue his statutory whistleblower and reprisal complaint with the sitting ICIG. The Debrief reported the firm formally concluded its representation in November 2023, and stressed that Grusch's public crash-retrieval claims were always outside the scope of that representation.

compass-rose-legal-group.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
compass-rose-legal-group.why: Senior partner was ODNI's Intelligence Community Inspector General
compass-rose-legal-group.note: Compass Rose senior partner I. Charles McCullough III was the Presidentially appointed, Senate-confirmed Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, reporting directly to DNI James Clapper and responsible for inquiries involving ODNI and the wider IC. That ICIG channel is the mechanism through which Grusch's complaint was routed.

judicial-watch.label: David Charles Grusch
judicial-watch.why: May 2026 On Watch interview restating the concealment allegation
judicial-watch.note: Interviewed by Chris Farrell for Judicial Watch's On Watch on 5 May 2026, restating that elements of the US government thwarted congressional oversight, withheld information from proper executive branch officials, and illegally concealed recovery and reverse-engineering programs. It is the immediate precursor to the June 2026 Capitol press conference.

project-sign.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
project-sign.why: AARO finds SIGN, GRUDGE and Blue Book sightings were ordinary objects
project-sign.note: The 2024 report concludes most sightings across all the legacy programs were ordinary objects and misidentification, and that no official review has ever confirmed extraterrestrial technology.

project-sign.label: Air Technical Intelligence Center
project-sign.why: SIGN hosted by AMC intelligence at Wright Field, ATIC's predecessor
project-sign.note: The first official UFO project was placed inside the foreign materiel exploitation organisation rather than a research or air defence body — the structural fact underlying this entire domain.

project-sign.label: Estimate of the Situation (1948)
project-sign.note: Project SIGN personnel wrote a Top Secret estimate concluding the objects were interplanetary. The Condon Report, written under Air Force contract, records that it was prepared.

project-sign.label: Twining Memorandum: AMC Opinion Concerning "Flying Discs"
project-sign.note: The Condon Report states Twining's 23 September 1947 letter directed establishment of a study of UFOs, which received priority designation in December 1947 and began as Project SIGN.

project-sign.label: Schulgen Collection Memorandum: Intelligence Requirements on Flying Saucer Type Aircraft
project-sign.why: Collection requirement fed the project that began weeks later
project-sign.note: The 30 October 1947 collection tasking and the 30 December 1947 direction of Project SIGN are two steps of a single sequence initiated by the Twining memo.

project-grudge.label: Project Blue Book
project-grudge.why: GRUDGE renamed Blue Book under Ruppelt in March 1952
project-grudge.note: Ruppelt was placed in charge of the reconstituted GRUDGE in late 1951 and the project was renamed Project Blue Book in March 1952.

project-grudge.label: Estimate of the Situation (1948)
project-grudge.why: Destruction of the Estimate preceded GRUDGE's dismissive posture by six months
project-grudge.note: SIGN became GRUDGE on 11 February 1949, months after the Estimate was destroyed, and GRUDGE's founding conclusions ran directly counter to it.

robertson-panel.label: 'CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-90' (Gerald K. Haines, Studies in Intelligence, 1997)
robertson-panel.why: CIA refused declassification and issued a sanitised version of the Robertson Panel report
robertson-panel.note: CIA 'prepared a sanitized version of the report which deleted any reference to CIA and avoided mention of any psychological warfare potential in the UFO controversy.'

robertson-panel.label: Central Intelligence Agency
robertson-panel.why: CIA convened and sponsored the panel, and concealed that sponsorship
robertson-panel.note: The panel was convened by the Office of Scientific Intelligence. The CIA's own history states that any mention of Agency sponsorship of the panel was forbidden.

robertson-panel.label: Frederick C. Durant III
robertson-panel.why: Durant was panel secretary and wrote the proceedings record
robertson-panel.note: Durant's memorandum of 16 February 1953 to the Assistant Director for Scientific Intelligence is the only substantive record of what the panel actually discussed.

robertson-panel.label: H. Marshall Chadwell
robertson-panel.why: Chadwell assembled the panel with Robertson
robertson-panel.note: The CIA's own official history states that in January 1953 Chadwell and H. P. Robertson put together the panel of nonmilitary scientists to study the UFO issue.

robertson-panel.label: Howard P. Robertson
robertson-panel.note: Robertson, a Caltech physicist and CIA consultant who had directed the DoD Weapons Systems Evaluation Group, chaired the 14-18 January 1953 sessions and signed the report.

robertson-panel.label: A Die-hard Issue: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-1990
robertson-panel.why: CIA's official history documents the panel's debunking and concealment
robertson-panel.note: Haines records the mass media and Disney recommendations and states plainly that CIA sponsorship of the panel was forbidden from being mentioned.

robertson-panel.label: Central Intelligence Agency
robertson-panel.why: CIA convened and staffed the January 1953 scientific advisory panel
robertson-panel.note: Convened by the Office of Scientific Intelligence under H. P. Robertson; the panel recommended debunking and the monitoring of civilian UFO groups.

robertson-panel.label: The Pentacle Memorandum
robertson-panel.why: Written five days before the panel met; per Vallee the panel was never briefed on its proposals
robertson-panel.note: Vallee's conclusion is that a separate group had already decided what the panel could and could not discuss - contractor-side predetermination of an official scientific review.

robertson-panel.label: Edward J. Ruppelt
robertson-panel.why: Ruppelt attended the panel as Blue Book director and later described it
robertson-panel.note: Ruppelt was present at the January 1953 sessions in his official capacity and published his account of the panel's function three years later.

robertson-panel.label: J. Allen Hynek
robertson-panel.why: Hynek presented to the panel but was not a member
robertson-panel.note: The Air Force's scientific consultant briefed the CIA-convened panel; the formal membership was Robertson, Alvarez, Berkner, Goudsmit and Page.

robertson-panel.label: 1953 Navy Photographic Interpretation Center analysis of the Great Falls and Tremonton films
robertson-panel.why: Contradicts the panel's 1953 disposition of the same films
robertson-panel.note: The Navy's own analysts assessed the Great Falls and Tremonton objects as intelligently controlled and not known technology in the same year the Robertson Panel recommended stripping the subject of special status.

robertson-panel.label: Air Force Regulation 200-2
robertson-panel.why: Panel recommendations became binding Air Force regulation
robertson-panel.note: AFR 200-2 was issued 26 August 1953 and revised 12 August 1954, restricting public release on unexplained cases to the bare fact of ATIC analysis — the debunking recommendation converted into internal law within months of the panel reporting.

robertson-panel.label: UAP Science Advisory Council
robertson-panel.why: third iteration of the external-scientific-panel pattern after Robertson (1953) and Condon (1966-68)
robertson-panel.note: Each prior panel supplied an authoritative dismissal on terms set by the sponsoring agency. Whether this one differs depends on its access to the Governance Board's classified holdings, which has not been publicly described.

twining-memo.label: George F. Schulgen
twining-memo.why: Addressed to Schulgen at Air Force intelligence requirements
twining-memo.note: Schulgen was the named addressee. Five weeks later he issued the worldwide collection memorandum, making the causal chain from assessment to collection tasking explicit in the documentary record.

twining-memo.label: Nathan F. Twining
twining-memo.note: Lt. Gen. Twining signed 'AMC Opinion Concerning Flying Discs' on 23 September 1947 as commander of Air Materiel Command. The document survives in scanned form and is quoted in the Condon Report.

twining-memo.label: Project SIGN
twining-memo.note: The Condon Report states Twining's 23 September 1947 letter directed establishment of a study of UFOs, which received priority designation in December 1947 and began as Project SIGN.

twining-memo.label: Howard M. McCoy
twining-memo.why: McCoy's shop produced the analysis Twining signed
twining-memo.note: The AMC intelligence organisation under McCoy did the staff work behind the 23 September 1947 assessment; McCoy signed related AMC correspondence to the Chief of Staff two months later.

schulgen-memo.label: George F. Schulgen
schulgen-memo.why: Schulgen signed the flying saucer collection requirement
schulgen-memo.note: As Chief of the Air Intelligence Requirements Division he signed 'Intelligence Requirements on Flying Saucer Type Aircraft' on 28 October 1947, distributed 30 October.

schulgen-memo.label: Project SIGN
schulgen-memo.why: Collection requirement fed the project that began weeks later
schulgen-memo.note: The 30 October 1947 collection tasking and the 30 December 1947 direction of Project SIGN are two steps of a single sequence initiated by the Twining memo.

estimate-of-the-situation.label: University of Colorado UFO Project (Condon Committee)
estimate-of-the-situation.why: The Condon Report is the primary documentary record of the Estimate's destruction
estimate-of-the-situation.note: Section V Chapter 2 records the estimate's preparation, Vandenberg's rejection and the destruction of copies — the Air Force paying to put its own suppression on the record.

estimate-of-the-situation.label: Project SIGN

estimate-of-the-situation.label: Project GRUDGE
estimate-of-the-situation.why: Destruction of the Estimate preceded GRUDGE's dismissive posture by six months
estimate-of-the-situation.note: SIGN became GRUDGE on 11 February 1949, months after the Estimate was destroyed, and GRUDGE's founding conclusions ran directly counter to it.

estimate-of-the-situation.label: Edward J. Ruppelt
estimate-of-the-situation.why: Ruppelt is the origin of public knowledge of the Estimate
estimate-of-the-situation.note: As a serving Blue Book director with access to the files, Ruppelt published the Estimate's existence and destruction in 1956; the Condon Report corroborated him twelve years later.

janap-146.label: Project Blue Book
janap-146.why: JANAP created a parallel reporting channel outside Blue Book
janap-146.note: JANAP 146(C) made UFO sightings a mandatory CIRVIS report under espionage-statute penalties while Blue Book handled the public-facing residue. Bolender confirmed the split in 1969.

janap-146.label: Bolender Memorandum
janap-146.why: Bolender names JANAP 146 as the channel Blue Book was not

janap-146.label: Project Blue Book

afr-200-2.label: Air Technical Intelligence Center
afr-200-2.why: ATIC was the terminal analytical authority under the regulation

afr-200-2.label: Project Blue Book
afr-200-2.why: AFR 200-2 governed what Blue Book could say publicly
afr-200-2.note: For unexplainable objects, 'only the fact that ATIC will analyze the data is worthy of release'. Every Air Force public statement that unknowns were unimportant was made under a regulation forbidding discussion of them.

afr-200-2.label: Nathan F. Twining
afr-200-2.why: The 1954 regulation was issued under Twining as Chief of Staff
afr-200-2.note: The officer who wrote in 1947 that the phenomenon was real was Air Force Chief of Staff when the regulation restricting public discussion of unexplained cases was promulgated.

afr-200-2.label: Robertson Panel
afr-200-2.why: Panel recommendations became binding Air Force regulation
afr-200-2.note: AFR 200-2 was issued 26 August 1953 and revised 12 August 1954, restricting public release on unexplained cases to the bare fact of ATIC analysis — the debunking recommendation converted into internal law within months of the panel reporting.

low-memo.label: University of Colorado UFO Project (Condon Committee)
low-memo.why: The memo states the intent to present differently to public and scientists
low-memo.note: 'The trick would be, I think, to describe the project so that, to the public, it would appear a totally objective study but, to the scientific community, would present the image of a group of nonbelievers.'

low-memo.label: Boulder, Colorado
low-memo.why: The Low memo shows the conclusion was framed before the study began
low-memo.note: Low's 9 August 1966 memorandum proposed a study 'conducted almost entirely by non-believers' with 'almost zero expectation of finding a saucer'. James E. McDonald found it in the project files in July 1967.

low-memo.label: Robert J. Low
low-memo.why: Low wrote the memo two months before the contract was signed
low-memo.note: Written 9 August 1966 to University of Colorado administrators, before the 6 October 1966 project formation — the design predates the data.

low-memo.label: James E. McDonald
low-memo.why: McDonald was the conduit that put the memo into public circulation
low-memo.note: McDonald received the memo from project staff and it reached John Fuller, who published it in Look in May 1968 as 'Flying Saucer Fiasco'.

gao-nsiad-95-187.label: RAAF Press Release, 8 July 1947
gao-nsiad-95-187.why: The message traffic that would document the release was destroyed
gao-nsiad-95-187.note: RAAF outgoing messages from October 1946 through December 1949 were destroyed with no recorded disposition authority, removing the base's own record of the 8 July 1947 announcement and its retraction.

gao-nsiad-95-187.label: Roswell Incident
gao-nsiad-95-187.why: GAO found the base's records for the event period destroyed
gao-nsiad-95-187.note: RAAF outgoing messages Oct 1946 - Dec 1949 and administrative records Mar 1945 - Dec 1949 were destroyed, and the disposition form does not record who destroyed them, when, or under what authority.

gao-nsiad-95-187.label: Steven H. Schiff
gao-nsiad-95-187.why: Schiff tasked GAO after DoD refused to answer him
gao-nsiad-95-187.note: A single member of Congress used the legislature's audit arm to go around an executive agency, producing the records-destruction finding no executive review has ever addressed.

gao-nsiad-95-187.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
gao-nsiad-95-187.why: AARO's legacy review does not address the documented records destruction
gao-nsiad-95-187.note: The report reaffirms the MOGUL conclusion without engaging GAO's 1995 finding that the relevant base records were destroyed with no disposition authority — the gap that makes the conclusion untestable.

gao-nsiad-95-187.label: Project MOGUL
gao-nsiad-95-187.why: The MOGUL attribution cannot be tested against destroyed records
gao-nsiad-95-187.note: GAO reported the base's message traffic for the relevant years was destroyed without disposition authority, so the Air Force's reconstruction rests on inference rather than on the contemporaneous record.

gao-nsiad-95-187.label: NARA Record Group 615 — UAP Records Collection
gao-nsiad-95-187.why: The first statutory records mechanism descends from the destruction problem
gao-nsiad-95-187.note: RG 615 was created under PL 118-31 sections 1841-1843 after decades in which the only auditable finding was GAO's: that the relevant legacy records had been destroyed with no recorded authority.

roswell-1947.label: 509th Bomb Group
roswell-1947.why: 509th intelligence office took possession of the Roswell debris
roswell-1947.note: The 8 July 1947 RAAF press release stated that 'the intelligence office of the 509th Bomb Group of the Eighth Air Force, Roswell Army Air Field, was fortunate enough to gain possession of a disc.' GAO later confirmed 'Army Air Forces personnel from the RAAF's 509th Bomb Group were credited with the recovery,' and located the July 1947 combined 509th/RAAF history report noting recovery of a 'flying disc' subsequently called a radar-tracking balloon.

roswell-1947.label: Jesse A. Marcel Sr.
roswell-1947.why: Marcel physically handled the recovered debris
roswell-1947.note: The 509th's staff intelligence officer collected the Foster ranch material with CIC Capt. Sheridan Cavitt and carried it to Fort Worth. His custody role is documented in the Air Force's own 1995 report.

roswell-1947.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
roswell-1947.why: AARO reaffirms MOGUL and finds no recovered extraterrestrial material
roswell-1947.note: The February 2024 report concludes the Roswell materials were consistent with a then-classified Project Mogul balloon and that there is no evidence the USG recovered aliens or extraterrestrial material.

roswell-1947.label: Project MOGUL
roswell-1947.why: Mogul is the Air Force's 1994 identification of the debris
roswell-1947.note: The 1994 USAF report attributed the debris to Project Mogul Flight No. 4, launched 4 June 1947 from Alamogordo, and acknowledged that the weather balloon account had been a cover story.

roswell-1947.label: Roger M. Ramey
roswell-1947.why: Ramey retracted the RAAF statement the same day at Fort Worth
roswell-1947.note: Brig. Gen. Roger M. Ramey, commanding Eighth Air Force, presented the debris as a weather balloon and radar target with weather officer Irving Newton. The Air Force conceded in 1994 that this was a cover story.

roswell-1947.label: Roswell, New Mexico and the Foster Ranch, Lincoln County
roswell-1947.why: The 1947 recovery was executed by Roswell Army Air Field
roswell-1947.note: Maj. Jesse Marcel of the 509th Bomb Group intelligence office and Capt. Sheridan Cavitt of the Counter Intelligence Corps were dispatched from RAAF to the Foster Ranch. Attested by the 1947 press record and the Air Force's own reports.

roswell-1947.label: Roswell, New Mexico and the Foster Ranch, Lincoln County
roswell-1947.why: The 509th Bomb Group at Roswell AAF was the only atomic-armed unit in the world
roswell-1947.note: The recovery, the announcement and the destroyed records all belong to a single installation with the most restrictive information discipline in the US military.

roswell-1947.label: Government Accountability Office
roswell-1947.why: Found Roswell AAF outgoing messages 1945-1949 destroyed without authorisation
roswell-1947.note: GAO reported that the outgoing message traffic for March 1945 to December 1949 had been destroyed and that no destruction certificate authorising it could be located.

roswell-1947.label: GAO/NSIAD-95-187 — Results of a Search for Records Concerning the 1947 Crash Near Roswell
roswell-1947.why: GAO found the base's records for the event period destroyed
roswell-1947.note: RAAF outgoing messages Oct 1946 - Dec 1949 and administrative records Mar 1945 - Dec 1949 were destroyed, and the disposition form does not record who destroyed them, when, or under what authority.

roswell-1947.label: COMETA - Comité d'Études Approfondies
roswell-1947.why: dedicated appendix on Roswell and disinformation
roswell-1947.note: COMETA's appendix 5 is titled 'The Roswell Affair - Disinformation'. A committee of retired French flag officers treating Roswell as a subject requiring an appendix in a defence study is itself part of what makes the document unusual.

roswell-1947.label: Kenneth Arnold
roswell-1947.why: Arnold's 24 June 1947 sighting opened the wave that Roswell fell inside
roswell-1947.note: The Cascades sighting on 24 June 1947 triggered the national wave; the Roswell recovery followed within two weeks and the Twining memo eleven weeks later.

roswell-1947.label: RAAF Press Release, 8 July 1947
roswell-1947.why: The press release is the event's only uncontested artifact
roswell-1947.note: Every subsequent official position — weather balloon, MOGUL, dummies — is a response to this single document issued by an atomic bomb group's own information office.

roswell-1947.label: Jesse A. Marcel Sr.
roswell-1947.why: Marcel was the 509th intelligence officer who recovered the debris
roswell-1947.note: Marcel and Cavitt were assigned by RAAF to retrieve the material from the Foster Ranch after Brazel reported it to Sheriff Wilcox on 6 July 1947.

roswell-1947.label: Walter Haut
roswell-1947.why: Haut issued the 8 July 1947 'flying disc' press release
roswell-1947.note: 1st Lt. Walter Haut, RAAF public information officer, issued the release stating the 509th's intelligence office had gained possession of a disc.

roswell-1947.label: Aztec, New Mexico claim, March 1948
roswell-1947.why: detail donor to later Roswell accounts
roswell-1947.note: After the story was revived in the 1970s, its specifics - small bodies, an intact hull, rapid military sanitisation of the site, storage at Wright-Patterson - migrated into allegedly first-hand Roswell testimony. A documented fraud became a supplier of narrative detail to the case the modern disclosure argument rests on, which is a contamination risk this board has to carry explicitly.

roswell-1947.label: Battelle Memorial Institute
roswell-1947.why: Alleged analysis of Roswell 'memory metal' via Wright-Patterson contracts
roswell-1947.note: The allegation rests on the coincidence of timing between the 1947 recovery, the 1948-49 Battelle NiTi work, and the absence of the reports from both archives. No document connects the two directly.

roswell-1947.label: Plains of San Agustin, New Mexico
roswell-1947.note: The Plains of San Agustin entered the Roswell corpus through Grady 'Barney' Barnett's reported account, transmitted second-hand via Vern and Jean Maltais to Stanton Friedman in October 1978 and published in Berlitz and Moore's 'The Roswell Incident' (1980). The claim is contested by Kevin Randle, who argues the site has no connection to Roswell, and no primary document supports it.

usaf-roswell-reports.label: Jesse A. Marcel Sr.
usaf-roswell-reports.why: The Air Force reports were produced to rebut Marcel's account
usaf-roswell-reports.note: Marcel's 1978 recantation restarted the case; the 1994-1997 Air Force volumes exist because of it and conclude against him, attributing the debris to Project MOGUL and reported bodies to test dummies.

usaf-roswell-reports.label: Steven H. Schiff
usaf-roswell-reports.why: Schiff's inquiry forced the Air Force to abandon the weather balloon story
usaf-roswell-reports.note: Both Roswell Reports state they were produced in response to Rep. Schiff's inquiry. The 1994-1995 volume conceded that the 1947 weather balloon explanation was false.

usaf-roswell-reports.label: Project MOGUL
usaf-roswell-reports.why: MOGUL is the load-bearing element of the official explanation
usaf-roswell-reports.note: The Air Force concluded the most likely source of the recovered wreckage was a Project MOGUL balloon train, replacing the weather balloon account it had maintained since 1947.

usaf-roswell-reports.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
usaf-roswell-reports.why: AARO's 2024 finding restates the 1994-1997 Air Force position
usaf-roswell-reports.note: Twenty-seven years later the successor office reaffirmed the MOGUL attribution without new primary records, because the primary records GAO identified as destroyed have not been recovered.

washington-flap-1952.label: H. Marshall Chadwell
washington-flap-1952.why: The flap put the CIA's science directorate onto the problem
washington-flap-1952.note: Within weeks of the July 1952 sightings Chadwell was writing to the DCI that reports totalled 250 in July alone and that the situation carried national security implications.

washington-flap-1952.label: A Die-hard Issue: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-1990
washington-flap-1952.why: CIA history confirms the 1952 flap drove Agency intervention
washington-flap-1952.note: Haines records the escalation from the summer 1952 sightings through Chadwell's memoranda to the January 1953 panel.

washington-flap-1952.label: Project Blue Book
washington-flap-1952.why: The flap occurred during Ruppelt's tenure and drove the record volume
washington-flap-1952.note: Blue Book case documentation for the 19 July 1952 Washington radar events survives; 1952 produced the largest single-year report volume of the program's history.

haines-cia-history.label: Project Blue Book
haines-cia-history.why: CIA states the Air Force made misleading and deceptive public statements
haines-cia-history.note: Haines writes that reconnaissance-programme secrecy 'led the Air Force to make misleading and deceptive statements to the public' — an agency of the US government confirming official deception on this subject.

haines-cia-history.label: Robertson Panel
haines-cia-history.why: CIA's official history documents the panel's debunking and concealment
haines-cia-history.note: Haines records the mass media and Disney recommendations and states plainly that CIA sponsorship of the panel was forbidden from being mentioned.

haines-cia-history.label: 1952 Washington DC Sightings
haines-cia-history.why: CIA history confirms the 1952 flap drove Agency intervention
haines-cia-history.note: Haines records the escalation from the summer 1952 sightings through Chadwell's memoranda to the January 1953 panel.

haines-cia-history.label: Central Intelligence Agency
haines-cia-history.why: CIA published its own institutional history of its UFO role in 1997
haines-cia-history.note: Gerald K. Haines, the Agency's historian, published an eighteen-page account in Studies in Intelligence acknowledging the OSI effort, the Robertson Panel and the later U-2/OXCART attribution.

hearing-1966-04-05.label: University of Colorado UFO Project (Condon Committee)
hearing-1966-04-05.why: Congressional pressure produced a contracted study, not oversight
hearing-1966-04-05.note: Six months after the hearing the Air Force let contract 44620-67-C-0035 to the University of Colorado — pressure in, study out, closure following.

hearing-1966-04-05.label: Gerald R. Ford
hearing-1966-04-05.why: Ford forced the first congressional hearing on the subject
hearing-1966-04-05.note: The House Minority Leader wrote to committee chairmen in late March 1966; the House Armed Services Committee held its one-day hearing on 5 April 1966, nineteen years into official investigation.

hearing-1966-04-05.label: J. Allen Hynek
hearing-1966-04-05.why: The swamp gas episode triggered the 1966 hearing
hearing-1966-04-05.note: Hynek's March 1966 Michigan press conference explanation was reported as a blanket dismissal, produced a public backlash, and led directly to Gerald Ford's demand for congressional hearings.

rg-615-uap-records.label: Project Blue Book
rg-615-uap-records.why: NARA holds the Blue Book series and is digitising legacy UFO records
rg-615-uap-records.note: Approximately 42 cubic feet of Blue Book material on 94 rolls of microfilm (T-1206) sits alongside the new RG 615 accessions; NARA states no Blue Book document discusses Roswell.

rg-615-uap-records.label: Bolender Memorandum
rg-615-uap-records.why: No records series has ever been identified for the JANAP channel
rg-615-uap-records.note: Blue Book's files went to NARA; whatever accumulated on the JANAP 146 side has never been named as a series, accessioned, or searched under any disclosure statute including the FY2024 NDAA.

rg-615-uap-records.label: GAO/NSIAD-95-187 — Results of a Search for Records Concerning the 1947 Crash Near Roswell
rg-615-uap-records.why: The first statutory records mechanism descends from the destruction problem
rg-615-uap-records.note: RG 615 was created under PL 118-31 sections 1841-1843 after decades in which the only auditable finding was GAO's: that the relevant legacy records had been destroyed with no recorded authority.

raaf-press-release-1947.label: GAO/NSIAD-95-187 — Results of a Search for Records Concerning the 1947 Crash Near Roswell
raaf-press-release-1947.why: The message traffic that would document the release was destroyed
raaf-press-release-1947.note: RAAF outgoing messages from October 1946 through December 1949 were destroyed with no recorded disposition authority, removing the base's own record of the 8 July 1947 announcement and its retraction.

raaf-press-release-1947.label: Roger M. Ramey
raaf-press-release-1947.why: Ramey retracted the disc announcement the same day
raaf-press-release-1947.note: The Eighth Air Force commanding general personally fronted a same-day correction identifying the debris as a weather balloon with radar reflector — the founding template for official UAP retraction.

raaf-press-release-1947.label: Walter Haut
raaf-press-release-1947.why: Haut issued the 8 July 1947 press release
raaf-press-release-1947.note: As RAAF public information officer Haut issued the announcement that the 509th Bomb Group had gained possession of a disc; the release is reproduced in the Air Force's own 1995 report.

raaf-press-release-1947.label: Roswell Incident
raaf-press-release-1947.why: The press release is the event's only uncontested artifact
raaf-press-release-1947.note: Every subsequent official position — weather balloon, MOGUL, dummies — is a response to this single document issued by an atomic bomb group's own information office.

project-moon-dust.label: Kean v. NASA, No. 1:03-cv-02509 (D.D.C.)
project-moon-dust.why: Project Moon Dust records were an express object of the FOIA request
project-moon-dust.note: Moon Dust - the programme for recovery of foreign space and aerospace debris - is named in the request as reproduced in the court's Background section.

project-moon-dust.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
project-moon-dust.why: AARO's 2024 historical review does not mention MOON DUST or BLUE FLY
project-moon-dust.note: A review commissioned to establish the historical record of USG involvement with UAP omits the named USG programmes whose charter was the recovery of unidentified fallen objects.

project-moon-dust.label: Operation BLUE FLY
project-moon-dust.why: BLUE FLY provided the quick-reaction airlift for MOON DUST recoveries
project-moon-dust.note: The two codewords appear together in Air Force intelligence correspondence; MOON DUST was the collection authority and BLUE FLY the transport and custody leg.

project-moon-dust.label: Project Blue Book
project-moon-dust.why: MOON DUST was the retrieval function alongside Blue Book's public sighting file
project-moon-dust.note: Blue Book was the acknowledged investigative programme; MOON DUST was a separate, quieter recovery and exploitation tasking that was never advertised to the public that Blue Book served.

operation-blue-fly.label: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio
operation-blue-fly.why: Recovered material routed to Air Force technical intelligence at Wright-Patterson
operation-blue-fly.note: Foreign Technology Division at Wright-Patterson was the designated technical exploitation centre; the Air Force felt it necessary in its January 1985 public fact sheet to deny that extraterrestrial equipment had ever been there.

operation-blue-fly.label: Project MOON DUST
operation-blue-fly.why: BLUE FLY provided the quick-reaction airlift for MOON DUST recoveries
operation-blue-fly.note: The two codewords appear together in Air Force intelligence correspondence; MOON DUST was the collection authority and BLUE FLY the transport and custody leg.

sac-overflights-1975.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
sac-overflights-1975.why: AARO's 2024 historical review does not address the 1975 nuclear-base overflights
sac-overflights-1975.note: A full-text review of Volume I finds no treatment of the Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom or Minot incursions despite the underlying records being publicly released by DoD's own FOIA office.

sac-overflights-1975.label: Malmstrom AFB and Minuteman Missile Fields, Montana
sac-overflights-1975.why: Malmstrom AFB and its Minuteman fields were among the installations overflown
sac-overflights-1975.note: DoD records released under FOIA case 97-F-1677 describe numerous unidentified craft over Malmstrom in November 1975.

sac-overflights-1975.label: John Greenewald Jr.
sac-overflights-1975.why: Malmstrom records released to The Black Vault under FOIA case 97-F-1677
sac-overflights-1975.note: The same September 1997 OASD release that produced the Halt memo produced the November 1975 Malmstrom overflight records.

sac-overflights-1975.label: Clear Intent: The Government Coverup of the UFO Experience (1984)
sac-overflights-1975.why: Fawcett and Greenwood reconstructed the 1975 wave from FOIA documents
sac-overflights-1975.note: CAUS filed on 26 December 1977; the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense identified twenty-four Joint Chiefs documents on 6 February 1978; Assistant Secretary Thomas Ross ordered the withheld fifteen released. The book reproduces and annotates them.

sac-overflights-1975.label: Malmstrom AFB missile shutdowns, March 1967
sac-overflights-1975.why: The 1975 wave returned to Malmstrom on documented record
sac-overflights-1975.note: The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's log and the NMCC memorandum of 8 November 1975 place radar-tracked objects over Malmstrom missile sites eight years after the Echo Flight shutdown, this time with F-106 scrambles logged.

sac-overflights-1975.label: Project Blue Book
sac-overflights-1975.why: Occurred six years after the Air Force closed Blue Book on a no-threat finding
sac-overflights-1975.note: The USAF fact sheet states Blue Book was terminated on 17 December 1969 on the conclusion that no UFO had ever indicated a threat to national security. The 1975 records document unidentified objects over nuclear weapons installations.

sac-overflights-1975.label: Computer UFO Network (CUFON)
sac-overflights-1975.why: 1975 NORAD and command-post message traffic circulated by CUFON
sac-overflights-1975.note: CUFON published the FOIA-released NORAD and SAC command-post records that transformed the 1975 incidents from anecdote into documents.

rendlesham-1980.label: Sheffield Hallam University
rendlesham-1980.why: Sheffield Hallam academic curated the MoD file release containing Rendlesham
rendlesham-1980.note: Dr David Clarke, associate professor at Sheffield Hallam University, first obtained MoD documents on the 1980 Rendlesham Forest incident in May 2001 under the Code of Practice for Access to Government Information, then served 2008-2013 as consultant and curator for the MoD/National Archives UFO files project that transferred and opened more than 60,000 pages, including the Rendlesham file at TNA reference DEFE 24/1948.

rendlesham-1980.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
rendlesham-1980.why: AARO's 2024 historical review does not mention Rendlesham
rendlesham-1980.note: A congressionally directed review of the historical record omits the best-documented physical-trace incident at a NATO nuclear-capable base, for which the Pentagon's own FOIA office has released the commander's memorandum.

rendlesham-1980.label: United Kingdom
rendlesham-1980.note: The December 1980 reports were made by USAF personnel stationed at RAF Woodbridge and RAF Bentwaters in Suffolk, England. That the reports were made at this location is documented in the MoD file; the nature of what was seen remains unresolved.

rendlesham-1980.label: Ministry of Defence Main Building, Whitehall, London
rendlesham-1980.why: MoD UFO desk held and released the Rendlesham file
rendlesham-1980.note: The MoD's UFO desk, run by the Directorate of Air Staff until its closure in 2009, held the Rendlesham Forest file; the complete file was released via The National Archives in August 2009 and includes Lt Col Charles Halt's account and the MoD's own investigation conclusions.

rendlesham-1980.label: Halt Memorandum, 'Unexplained Lights', 13 January 1981
rendlesham-1980.why: The memo is the primary official record of the incident
rendlesham-1980.note: The memo is the only contemporaneous US government document describing the events; everything else in the case is witness statement or later recollection.

rendlesham-1980.label: RAF Woodbridge / RAF Bentwaters, Suffolk, England
rendlesham-1980.why: Incident occurred at and around a USAF-operated nuclear-capable NATO base
rendlesham-1980.note: RAF Woodbridge and RAF Bentwaters were operated by the USAF's 81st Tactical Fighter Wing under NATO arrangements.

rendlesham-1980.label: Charles I. Halt
rendlesham-1980.why: Halt personally led the 28 December 1980 forest patrol
rendlesham-1980.note: Halt's own memo states 'Numerous individuals, including the undersigned, witnessed the activities in paragraphs 2 and 3.'

rendlesham-1980.label: James W. Penniston
rendlesham-1980.note: Penniston was the senior security police NCO who entered the forest; his notebook records 'craft of unknown origin' and he signed a USAF witness statement.

rendlesham-1980.label: John Burroughs
rendlesham-1980.note: Burroughs was with Penniston at the east gate; his account differs in detail from Penniston's, which the board treats as a marker of independence rather than contradiction.

halt-memo.label: Rendlesham Forest Incident, RAF Woodbridge/Bentwaters
halt-memo.why: The memo is the primary official record of the incident
halt-memo.note: The memo is the only contemporaneous US government document describing the events; everything else in the case is witness statement or later recollection.

halt-memo.label: John Greenewald Jr.
halt-memo.why: Released to The Black Vault under DoD FOIA case 97-F-1677
halt-memo.note: The Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense, Freedom of Information and Security Review Office released the memo in September 1997 under case 97-F-1677.

halt-memo.label: Charles I. Halt
halt-memo.why: Halt authored and signed the 'Unexplained Lights' memorandum
halt-memo.note: Halt was Deputy Base Commander of the 81st Combat Support Group and signed the memo on 13 Jan 81. The document is his; his authorship has never been disputed by the Air Force.

project-aquarius.label: Linda Moulton Howe
project-aquarius.why: Howe is the only named witness to the AQUARIUS paper's text
project-aquarius.note: No copy of the document has ever surfaced in any archive or FOIA release; Howe's notes are the sole record of its content.

project-aquarius.label: MJ-12 / Operation Majestic-12 Documents
project-aquarius.why: AQUARIUS and MJ-12 emerged from the same Albuquerque channel within 20 months
project-aquarius.note: The AQUARIUS paper was shown at Kirtland in April 1983; the MJ-12 film arrived postmarked Albuquerque in December 1984. Both channels ran through people in contact with AFOSI.

mj-12-documents.label: William L. Moore
mj-12-documents.why: Moore controlled the MJ-12 material's release with Shandera and Friedman
mj-12-documents.note: Moore and Shandera published 'The MJ-12 Documents: An Analytical Report' as Fair-Witness Project Publication 1500 in 1990, cited in CIA's own 1997 UFO history.

mj-12-documents.label: AARO Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with UAP, Volume I
mj-12-documents.why: AARO's 2024 review does not address MJ-12 or AQUARIUS
mj-12-documents.note: Two of the most persistent alleged programme names in the historical record are absent from the report tasked with resolving the historical record.

mj-12-documents.label: Jaime H. Shandera
mj-12-documents.why: Received the anonymous 35mm film on 11 December 1984
mj-12-documents.note: The film arrived at Shandera's Los Angeles home postmarked Albuquerque, New Mexico - the same city as the AFOSI operation running against Bennewitz.

mj-12-documents.label: Project AQUARIUS (alleged)
mj-12-documents.why: AQUARIUS and MJ-12 emerged from the same Albuquerque channel within 20 months
mj-12-documents.note: The AQUARIUS paper was shown at Kirtland in April 1983; the MJ-12 film arrived postmarked Albuquerque in December 1984. Both channels ran through people in contact with AFOSI.

caus.label: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. National Security Agency (Civil Action No. 80-1562)
caus.why: CAUS was the plaintiff in Civil Action No. 80-1562
caus.note: The organisation brought the case that produced judicial confirmation that NSA holds UFO-related records it will not release.

caus.label: Peter A. Gersten
caus.why: Gersten directed CAUS and brought its FOIA litigation
caus.note: Gersten's litigation against CIA, NSA and DoD is the origin of the document-first method in this field.

cufon.label: 1975 SAC Nuclear-Base Overflights (Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot)
cufon.why: 1975 NORAD and command-post message traffic circulated by CUFON
cufon.note: CUFON published the FOIA-released NORAD and SAC command-post records that transformed the 1975 incidents from anecdote into documents.

caus-v-nsa.label: National Security Agency
caus-v-nsa.why: NSA withheld its UFO holdings in full and won on an in camera affidavit
caus-v-nsa.note: NSA located responsive material, withheld it entirely, and supported the withholding with a classified affidavit by Eugene F. Yeates. The D.C. Circuit affirmed in 1981; certiorari was denied in 1982.

caus-v-nsa.label: Yeates Affidavit (NSA, 1980)
caus-v-nsa.why: The affidavit is the instrument by which withholding was sustained
caus-v-nsa.note: The United States has never asserted that the records do not exist. Its sworn position is that they cannot be disclosed.

caus-v-nsa.label: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy (CAUS)
caus-v-nsa.why: CAUS was the plaintiff in Civil Action No. 80-1562
caus-v-nsa.note: The organisation brought the case that produced judicial confirmation that NSA holds UFO-related records it will not release.

yeates-affidavit.label: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. National Security Agency (Civil Action No. 80-1562)
yeates-affidavit.why: The affidavit is the instrument by which withholding was sustained
yeates-affidavit.note: The United States has never asserted that the records do not exist. Its sworn position is that they cannot be disclosed.

yeates-affidavit.label: Eugene F. Yeates
yeates-affidavit.why: Yeates executed the affidavit as NSA Chief of Policy
yeates-affidavit.note: The affidavit was submitted for in camera review only; the plaintiffs never saw it and the judge ruled for NSA on its basis.

yeates-affidavit.label: John Greenewald Jr.
yeates-affidavit.why: 2013 Mandatory Declassification Review forced further release of the NSA UFO holdings
yeates-affidavit.note: NSA had released the COMINT records with most pages carrying only a few visible words, redacted in white-out; an MDR was required to obtain more.

sri-international.label: GRILL FLAME
sri-international.why: SRI methodology transferred into the Army/DIA GRILL FLAME programme
sri-international.note: GRILL FLAME formalised operational remote viewing at Fort Meade using the SRI protocols, with SRI continuing as the research contractor.

sri-international.label: Harold E. Puthoff
sri-international.why: Puthoff founded and led the SRI psychoenergetics programme
sri-international.note: CIA's Office of Technical Service funded the work from 1972; it was later sponsored by Army INSCOM and DIA under successive codenames.

sri-international.label: Russell Targ
sri-international.why: Targ was co-principal investigator at SRI 1972-1982
sri-international.note: Targ co-authored both the 1974 Nature paper and the November 1978 SRI remote-viewing protocol released in the STARGATE declassification.

sri-international.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995
sri-international.why: SRI held the science half of the remote viewing effort from 1972
sri-international.note: Puthoff and Targ began CIA-sponsored work at SRI's Artificial Intelligence Center in 1972 and continued with intelligence community funding until they left in the mid-1980s.

sri-international.label: Christopher C. 'Kit' Green
sri-international.why: Green was CIA's monitor for the SRI psychoenergetics work
sri-international.note: Green served in CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence, Life Sciences Division, and has stated he was the officer to whom anomalous-phenomena reporting was routed.

grill-flame.label: SRI International (Stanford Research Institute)
grill-flame.why: SRI methodology transferred into the Army/DIA GRILL FLAME programme
grill-flame.note: GRILL FLAME formalised operational remote viewing at Fort Meade using the SRI protocols, with SRI continuing as the research contractor.

grill-flame.label: CENTER LANE
grill-flame.why: CENTER LANE succeeded GRILL FLAME after the codename was compromised
grill-flame.note: Codeword churn on compromise is standard practice; the effort was continuous across the renaming.

center-lane.label: GRILL FLAME
center-lane.why: CENTER LANE succeeded GRILL FLAME after the codename was compromised
center-lane.note: Codeword churn on compromise is standard practice; the effort was continuous across the renaming.

sun-streak.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
sun-streak.note: DIA's prior experience running an unacknowledged programme in a ridiculed domain is the institutional precedent for its 2008 AAWSAP contract.

sun-streak.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995
sun-streak.note: CIA compiled and released roughly 12,000 pages of the programme record in 1995 after the American Institutes for Research evaluation.

rockefeller-initiative.label: GAO/NSIAD-95-187, Government Records: Results of a Search for Records Concerning the 1947 Crash Near Roswell, New Mexico
rockefeller-initiative.why: The initiative's live period coincides with the GAO records audit and its retention in the White House Roswell file
rockefeller-initiative.note: The Clinton White House Roswell file (2006-0476-F) contains the July 1995 GAO report; the unclassified records audit is what the White House ended up holding.

rockefeller-initiative.label: Laurance S. Rockefeller
rockefeller-initiative.why: Rockefeller financed and directed the 1993-1996 disclosure initiative
rockefeller-initiative.note: Rockefeller Family & Associates funded the effort, its briefing document and its distribution to officials and heads of state.

rockefeller-initiative.label: UFO Briefing Document: The Best Available Evidence (1995)
rockefeller-initiative.why: The briefing document was the initiative's principal instrument
rockefeller-initiative.note: The document was deliberately written as a government-style assessment rather than a popular book.

best-available-evidence.label: Marie 'Bootsie' Galbraith
best-available-evidence.note: Compiled with Stanton Friedman and Don Berliner under Rockefeller funding and distributed to legislators, officials and heads of state in 1995.

best-available-evidence.label: The Rockefeller UFO Disclosure Initiative
best-available-evidence.why: The briefing document was the initiative's principal instrument

gao-roswell-report-1995.label: Roswell, New Mexico and the Foster Ranch, Lincoln County
gao-roswell-report-1995.why: GAO found the relevant RAAF records destroyed with no recorded authority
gao-roswell-report-1995.note: RAAF administrative records March 1945-December 1949 and outgoing messages October 1946-December 1949 were destroyed; the disposition form records neither who destroyed them nor under what authority.

gao-roswell-report-1995.label: Steven H. Schiff
gao-roswell-report-1995.why: Schiff directed GAO to conduct the government-wide records search
gao-roswell-report-1995.note: GAO issued GAO/NSIAD-95-187 to Schiff on 28 July 1995 after DoD referred his 1993 inquiry to the National Archives instead of answering it.

gao-roswell-report-1995.label: The Rockefeller UFO Disclosure Initiative
gao-roswell-report-1995.why: The initiative's live period coincides with the GAO records audit and its retention in the White House Roswell file
gao-roswell-report-1995.note: The Clinton White House Roswell file (2006-0476-F) contains the July 1995 GAO report; the unclassified records audit is what the White House ended up holding.

cia-haines-1997.label: Central Intelligence Agency
cia-haines-1997.why: CIA's own published history concedes the Air Force made deceptive public statements
cia-haines-1997.note: 'This led the Air Force to make misleading and deceptive statements to the public in order to allay public fears and to protect an extraordinarily sensitive national security project.'

cia-haines-1997.label: Robertson Panel
cia-haines-1997.why: CIA refused declassification and issued a sanitised version of the Robertson Panel report
cia-haines-1997.note: CIA 'prepared a sanitized version of the report which deleted any reference to CIA and avoided mention of any psychological warfare potential in the UFO controversy.'

cia-haines-1997.label: Project Blue Book
cia-haines-1997.why: Blue Book investigators knowingly issued false explanations for U-2 sightings
cia-haines-1997.note: CIA records that Blue Book investigators aware of the secret U-2 flights attributed sightings to ice crystals and temperature inversions and 'were careful, however, not to reveal the true cause of the sighting to the public.'

cia-haines-1997.label: YANKEE BLUE (alleged AFOSI indoctrination program)
cia-haines-1997.why: A documented precedent for institutional falsification about UFOs by the US Air Force
cia-haines-1997.note: CIA's own history establishes that the Air Force knowingly issued false UFO explanations for at least a decade. That precedent is why the YANKEE BLUE allegation cannot be dismissed on plausibility grounds alone.

disclosure-project.label: John D. Podesta
disclosure-project.why: Podesta's 2002 declassification call followed the Disclosure Project's 2001 press conference
disclosure-project.note: Podesta appeared for the Coalition for Freedom of Information at the National Press Club on 22 October 2002, seventeen months after Greer's event in the same venue.

disclosure-project.label: Steven M. Greer
disclosure-project.why: Greer founded and led the Disclosure Project
disclosure-project.note: Greer founded CSETI in 1990 and the Disclosure Project in 1993, culminating in the 9 May 2001 National Press Club event.

disclosure-project.label: Thomas R. Wilson
disclosure-project.why: The Wilson notes place Wilson's 1997 inquiry immediately after exposure to Greer's Washington briefings
disclosure-project.note: The Disclosure Project briefed members of Congress and officials in Washington in April 1997; the notes record Wilson beginning his search for the programme in the same period.

l-raf-woodbridge.label: Rendlesham Forest Incident, RAF Woodbridge/Bentwaters
l-raf-woodbridge.why: Incident occurred at and around a USAF-operated nuclear-capable NATO base
l-raf-woodbridge.note: RAF Woodbridge and RAF Bentwaters were operated by the USAF's 81st Tactical Fighter Wing under NATO arrangements.

l-raf-woodbridge.label: John Burroughs
l-raf-woodbridge.why: Service medical records for the incident window could not be produced
l-raf-woodbridge.note: Burroughs reported that his USAF medical records for December 1980-January 1981 were unavailable when he sought them for a VA disability claim; the claim was granted in 2015 after congressional intervention.

l-malmstrom.label: 1975 SAC Nuclear-Base Overflights (Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot)
l-malmstrom.why: Malmstrom AFB and its Minuteman fields were among the installations overflown

doty-personnel-file.label: Richard C. Doty
doty-personnel-file.why: 321-page New Mexico State Police personnel file released 2021
doty-personnel-file.note: Obtained under NMSA 14-2-1 et seq. after federal channels produced nothing; state public-records law delivered what FOIA did not.

american-alchemy.label: Jesse Michels
american-alchemy.note: American Alchemy is Michels' series and the venue for every episode in this domain.

michels-gerb-structural-episode.label: Independent media as the disclosure substrate
michels-gerb-structural-episode.why: the most detailed structural reconstruction in circulation, published on a YouTube channel

michels-gerb-structural-episode.label: Jesse Michels
michels-gerb-structural-episode.why: Michels produced and hosted the structural episode

michels-gerb-structural-episode.label: Central Intelligence Agency
michels-gerb-structural-episode.why: Dedicated chapter 'The Office of Global Access' at 43:04
michels-gerb-structural-episode.note: The Office of Global Access, an element associated with CIA's Directorate of Science and Technology, is given a named chapter; Gerb separately links CIA OGA to NRO, MITRE and the Executive branch in his NRO investigation.

michels-gerb-structural-episode.label: United States Department of Energy
michels-gerb-structural-episode.note: The episode places the Department of Energy's Nuclear Emergency Support Team inside the crash-retrieval architecture, consistent with the AEC-custody thesis.

michels-gerb-structural-episode.label: The MITRE Corporation
michels-gerb-structural-episode.why: Dedicated chapter 'The Role of MITRE' at 51:28
michels-gerb-structural-episode.note: MITRE is given a named chapter inside the structural episode, seven months before Gerb published his full MITRE investigation - establishing that MITRE was already central to the model in January 2026.

michels-gerb-structural-episode.label: 'Manhattan Project 2.0' (alleged secrecy architecture)
michels-gerb-structural-episode.why: The episode's thesis is the Manhattan Project 2.0 architecture

d-structure.label: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)
d-structure.why: the provision that removes a contractor facility from the government's own industrial security oversight
d-structure.note: Defined in DoD Directive 5205.07 and DoD Manual 5205.07 Volume 1 as a provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense relieving the defence security agency of its National Industrial Security Program oversight responsibilities at a contractor facility. It is the structural seam at which a programme held at a company stops being visible to any government security official outside the programme.

d-structure.label: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)
d-structure.why: the office that holds the Department's SAP portfolio and is its single point of contact to Congress
d-structure.note: Established by DoD Directive 5205.07 (reissued 12 September 2024) 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense', with a Director who must be a general or flag officer or SES equivalent, and designated the primary DoD liaison with the Executive Branch and Congress on all DoD SAP issues. Any structural map of where a legacy programme could sit starts at this node.

d-structure.label: DoDI 5205.11 — Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD SAPs (12 Sep 2024)
d-structure.why: the issuance that documents the approval and oversight chain this domain is trying to map
d-structure.note: DoDI 5205.11 (effective 12 September 2024) sets out the prospective SAP approval sequence in days from establishment, the review bodies (SSWG, Senior Review Group, SAPOC) and the oversight roles. It is the only public document that walks the whole chain end to end, which makes it the domain's primary methodological source rather than merely one of its members.

d-structure.label: Intelligence Community special access program control office enterprise
d-structure.why: the parallel control-office enterprise on the intelligence-community side of the same architecture
d-structure.note: The IC maintains its own special access and controlled access program control architecture under DNI authority, separate from the DoD SAP enterprise administered by DoD SAPCO. AARO's Historical Record Report Volume I confirms its existence in the government's own UAP record. The two-sided structure matters because a programme can be lodged on either side, and the oversight statutes differ.

d-structure.label: Information Security Oversight Office
d-structure.why: the office charged with counting the classification system, and therefore the boundary of the public map
d-structure.note: ISOO is housed at the National Archives and is responsible to the President for policy and oversight of the government-wide security classification system and the National Industrial Security Program, under Executive Orders 13526 and 13556. Where ISOO's annual reporting stops is where this domain's open-source organisational mapping has to switch to inference.

d-structure.label: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence
d-structure.why: the OSD element with policy authority over intelligence, counterintelligence, security and sensitive activities
d-structure.note: OUSD(I), since 2020 OUSD(I&S), is where the sensitive-activities policy authority sits and where the whole Elizondo/AATIP dispute takes place. It is also the office under which the Military Intelligence Program is managed, which makes it the point where this domain's organisational and funding threads meet.

d-structure.label: Congressional oversight of special access programs
d-structure.why: the statutory oversight scheme, and the exception written into it
d-structure.note: Under 10 U.S.C. 119 the Secretary must report annually by 1 March to the four defense committees on every special access program, with a brief description, major milestones and costs - and under 119(e) may waive any of that on a case-by-case basis. The scheme and its exception are the same statute, which is why oversight belongs on the structural map rather than outside it.

d-structure.label: Waived SAP Notification Group
d-structure.why: the four-member channel that 10 U.S.C. 119(e) substitutes for committee reporting
d-structure.note: Sec. 119(e)(2) directs that where the Secretary exercises the waiver, the information and the justification go jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each of the defense committees - the Armed Services and Appropriations committees of both chambers. Attaching this node to the structural domain is what stops the two channels being conflated. [Corrected 14 Aug 2026: 10 U.S.C. 119(g) defines 'defense committees' as SIX bodies including both Appropriations Defense subcommittees, so notification runs to twelve seats, not eight. Section 119 uses its own definition, not 10 U.S.C. 101(a)(16).]

d-structure.label: 'Manhattan Project 2.0' (alleged secrecy architecture)
d-structure.why: the named model this domain is arguing about, and the reason to keep it graded Tier 3
d-structure.note: UAP Gerb's onion model of an indefinitely layered secrecy architecture, set out across two investigations published 1 May and 19 June 2026, is the most fully articulated structural hypothesis in circulation and is what the independent-media substrate has organised itself around.
