eg-and-g.label: Federal Contracting Mechanics
eg-and-g.why: contracting at a site whose existence was itself classified
eg-and-g.note: EG&G instrumented and fired US nuclear tests from the Manhattan Project onward and became the classified services contractor for the Nevada complex, including the Air Force operating location near Groom Lake - a facility whose existence required a Presidential Determination published at 60 FR 52823 to exempt it from disclosure. It is the historical template for how contracting works where the place of performance cannot be named.

eg-and-g.label: Alfred 'Al' O'Donnell
eg-and-g.why: O'Donnell was a senior EG&G manager and, per Knapp, first general manager of EG&G Nevada
eg-and-g.note: His documented career runs from nuclear test firing engineering through the company's Nevada operations, giving him access to the classified site infrastructure at the centre of the allegation.

eg-and-g.label: Groom Lake, Nevada
eg-and-g.why: EG&G provided the classified site services and personnel transport for the Groom Lake operating location
eg-and-g.note: The relationship is documented indirectly through the Groom Lake worker litigation and the annual presidential environmental exemptions rather than through any acknowledgment of the facility.

eg-and-g.label: Nevada Test Site / Nevada National Security Site
eg-and-g.why: EG&G was the classified services contractor for the Nevada complex in the testing era
eg-and-g.note: Its instrumentation and site services role is documented through DOE technical history and through the Groom Lake litigation rather than through any acknowledgment of the adjacent operating location.

eg-and-g.label: Richard D'Amato
eg-and-g.why: D'Amato's Senate inquiry reached EG&G and stopped there
eg-and-g.note: Knapp arranged, with EG&G co-founder Herbert Grier's blessing, a meeting between D'Amato and Al O'Donnell; O'Donnell said nothing. D'Amato reported to the Senator that the allegations did not merit further investigation.

eg-and-g.label: The Wilson-Davis Notes (16 October 2002)
eg-and-g.why: The meeting is reported to have taken place at an EG&G facility in Las Vegas
eg-and-g.note: EG&G held the Groom Lake support and personnel-transport contracts; the reported venue matters because it places the conversation inside the contractor perimeter it describes.

bechtel-nevada.label: Nevada Test Site / Nevada National Security Site
bechtel-nevada.why: Bechtel Nevada held the DOE management and operating contract for the Nevada Test Site 1996-2006
bechtel-nevada.note: DOE technical reports list Bechtel Nevada as research organisation of record through 2006, succeeded by National Security Technologies, LLC.

bechtel-nevada.label: 10 U.S.C. 119 — Special Access Programs: Congressional Oversight
bechtel-nevada.why: DOE contractor custody sits outside the DoD special access program reporting regime entirely
bechtel-nevada.note: Atomic Energy Act Restricted Data authorities are a separate statutory classification scheme; material held under them by a DOE management and operating contractor is not reachable by the Sec. 119 reporting obligations Congress relies on. No document places UAP material under DOE authority.

saic.label: Leidos Holdings, Inc.
saic.why: Leidos is the government services business spun out of SAIC in 2013
saic.note: The split moved the classified services portfolio, and whatever records attach to it, into a separate corporate entity.

saic.label: Off-World Technologies Division
saic.why: Alleged SAIC and Sandia connections to the division
saic.note: Gerb links the alleged division to SAIC and Sandia National Laboratories; the escorting weapons instructor is described as a private contractor employee.

saic.label: Central Intelligence Agency
saic.why: SAIC held the government's remote viewing research line after it left SRI
saic.note: A documented instance of a deniable government research program in an anomalous subject moving wholesale into corporate custody, terminated after an external assessment.

leidos.label: Science Applications International Corporation
leidos.why: Leidos is the government services business spun out of SAIC in 2013
leidos.note: The split moved the classified services portfolio, and whatever records attach to it, into a separate corporate entity.

leidos.label: FY2024 NDAA, Public Law 118-31 - Div. A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C (secs. 1841-1843), UAP Records Collection; Div. G (IAA FY2024) secs. 7341, 7343
leidos.why: The records collection reaches government-funded contractor-held records
leidos.note: Sec. 1841 defines the collection as record copies of all 'Government, Government-provided, or Government-funded records' relating to UAP, technologies of unknown origin and non-human intelligence - a formulation that reaches services primes holding classified records under contract. No accounting of contractor holdings has been made.

booz-allen.label: David Charles Grusch
booz-allen.why: The access architecture that denied Grusch his read-ons is largely contractor-built and contractor-maintained
booz-allen.note: Grusch was tasked to inventory the SAPs and CAPs relevant to the Task Force's congressional mandate and was refused. The billet lists, access rosters and classification guides that execute such refusals are administered in substantial part by security-support primes. No committee has requested those rosters.

booz-allen.label: 10 U.S.C. 119 — Special Access Programs: Congressional Oversight
booz-allen.why: Security-support primes administer the compartmentation the statute is supposed to make visible
booz-allen.note: Reasoning: Sec. 119 places the reporting duty on the Secretary of Defense, but the underlying program-protection and access records are held by contractors with no independent reporting obligation to Congress.

aerojet-rocketdyne.label: S. 2103 Sec. 1104 - SSCI contractor disclosure and immunity provision (stripped)
aerojet-rocketdyne.why: The provision named derived propulsion work as a defunding category
aerojet-rocketdyne.note: Sec. 1104(c) targets propulsion 'based on or derived from or inspired by inspection, analysis, or reverse engineering of recovered unidentified anomalous phenomena craft or materials,' and any aerospace craft using propulsion other than chemical, solar or electric ion thrust.

general-atomics.label: To The Stars Academy of Arts & Science Inc. (later To The Stars Inc.)
general-atomics.why: Securities disclosure is why the TTSA arrangement is visible and a privately held prime's would not be
general-atomics.note: TTSA's Reg A reporting obligations forced the CRADA into the public record. A privately held prime such as General Atomics has no equivalent obligation, which is the structural reason the documented case is a small company rather than a large one.

radiance-technologies.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
radiance-technologies.why: Radiance is a mid-tier technical prime in the space where compartmented analytical tasks are placed
radiance-technologies.note: Reasoning: roughly $2.6 billion in prime obligations since FY2008 across intelligence, sensors and advanced concepts. Radiance recurs in UAP-adjacent reporting as an employer of personnel who moved between government UAP work and industry, but no primary personnel record has been located and none is asserted.

project-bear.label: Battelle Memorial Institute
project-bear.why: Battelle's authorship of Special Report No. 14 was deliberately concealed behind an ATIC cover
project-bear.note: AARO states that Battelle 'released a report under the cover of ATIC to maintain its anonymity.' The first public analytical product of the government's UFO investigation was ghost-written by a private contractor at the contractor's request.

project-bear.label: Battelle Memorial Institute
project-bear.why: Battelle held the Project BEAR contract supplying the science behind Project GRUDGE and BLUE BOOK
project-bear.note: AARO's own history records the contract, the questionnaire and punch-card work, and the resulting Special Report No. 14.

iaa-fy2024-sec1104.label: Aerojet Rocketdyne
iaa-fy2024-sec1104.why: The provision named derived propulsion work as a defunding category
iaa-fy2024-sec1104.note: Sec. 1104(c) targets propulsion 'based on or derived from or inspired by inspection, analysis, or reverse engineering of recovered unidentified anomalous phenomena craft or materials,' and any aerospace craft using propulsion other than chemical, solar or electric ion thrust.

iaa-fy2024-sec1104.label: Lockheed Martin Corporation
iaa-fy2024-sec1104.why: SSCI would have compelled contractors to list all 'non-earth origin or exotic' material they hold, with immunity
iaa-fy2024-sec1104.note: S. 2103 Sec. 1104(d)-(e), reported unanimously on 22 June 2023, required notification to the DNI within 60 days and production within 180, and barred any criminal or civil action against a complying holder. The phrase 'non-earth origin' does not appear in the enacted law.

iaa-fy2024-sec1104.label: NDAA FY2024 Sec. 1687 - Limitation on Use of Funds for Certain Unreported Programs
iaa-fy2024-sec1104.why: Only the funding limitation and the IR&D restriction survived into law
iaa-fy2024-sec1104.note: Sec. 1687 and Sec. 7343 of Public Law 118-31 carry forward the funding cutoff and the IR&D clause from the Senate provision; the contractor disclosure, inventory and immunity subsections were removed.

aaro-metallic-specimen-analysis.label: Battelle Memorial Institute
aaro-metallic-specimen-analysis.why: Oak Ridge, operated by UT-Battelle, analysed the alleged 1947 crash specimen for AARO
aaro-metallic-specimen-analysis.note: AARO contracted ORNL in 2022; the laboratory assessed the specimen terrestrial in origin and incapable of functioning as a terahertz waveguide. Battelle thus appears at both ends of the file, in 1951 and in 2024.

aaro-metallic-specimen-analysis.label: CRADA between U.S. Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center and To The Stars Academy
aaro-metallic-specimen-analysis.why: The privately held specimen passed from the company through the Army to AARO and then to ORNL
aaro-metallic-specimen-analysis.note: AARO confirms the organisation 'negotiated an agreement in 2019 with the U.S. Army to analyze the samples' and that AARO subsequently acquired the sample with stakeholder permission. This is the only fully documented custody chain in the entire domain.

aaro-metallic-specimen-analysis.label: To The Stars Academy of Arts & Science Inc. (later To The Stars Inc.)
aaro-metallic-specimen-analysis.why: ORNL assessed the privately held 'crash' specimen as terrestrial
aaro-metallic-specimen-analysis.note: The finding does not resolve the custody question it arose from: AARO notes the specimen's 'undocumented chain of custody and conflicting personal accounts' leave its historical origin unclear.

groom-lake-presidential-determination.label: EG&G (Edgerton, Germeshausen and Grier)
groom-lake-presidential-determination.why: The state secrets defence shielded the contractor-operated facility from the workers' suit
groom-lake-presidential-determination.note: Rather than litigate the alleged open-air burning of classified waste, the government invoked state secrets and the President exempted the site; Kasza v. Browner, 133 F.3d 1159, sustained dismissal and certiorari was denied.

groom-lake-presidential-determination.label: Groom Lake, Nevada
groom-lake-presidential-determination.why: Annual presidential determinations exempt the Groom Lake operating location from environmental disclosure
groom-lake-presidential-determination.note: Published in the Federal Register every year since 1995, the determinations never name the facility or describe its contents - the cleanest documentary proof of a contractor-operated site legally exempted from statutory disclosure.

l-plant-42.label: Lockheed Martin Advanced Development Programs (Skunk Works)
l-plant-42.why: Skunk Works operates at the government-owned contractor-operated Palmdale facility
l-plant-42.note: Plant 42 is compartmented program by program inside a single fence line, which is the physical form of the concealment architecture at issue.

l-plant-42.label: Lockheed Martin Corporation
l-plant-42.why: The unnamed 'facility in California' in the sworn testimony is most plausibly in the Palmdale complex
l-plant-42.note: Reasoning: Knapp specified California and Lockheed; Lockheed's California SAP-accredited aeronautics footprint is concentrated at Palmdale. No witness has named a site and the board does not assert one.

l-pax-river.label: Lockheed Martin Corporation
l-pax-river.why: Lockheed Martin is named among the contractors supporting NAVAIR work at the site alleged to store an exotic vehicle
l-pax-river.note: Liberation Times reported in January 2026 that an exotic vehicle has been stored at Pax River for decades and that the supporting contractor ecosystem has included Lockheed Martin and MITRE.

l-pax-river.label: The MITRE Corporation
l-pax-river.why: MITRE is named among the FFRDC and contractor ecosystem supporting NAVAIR programs at Pax River
l-pax-river.note: The FFRDC form grants privileged long-term access to classified holdings while barring manufacturing and competition; no allegation of custody attaches to MITRE.

l-pax-river.label: Luis D. Elizondo
l-pax-river.why: Elizondo placed Pax River among the sites prepared for the blocked Lockheed-Bigelow transfer
l-pax-river.note: Reported from his written congressional testimony: a hangar at the base was allegedly designed to facilitate movement of material by air and by river.

l-nevada-test-site.label: Bechtel Nevada Corporation
l-nevada-test-site.why: Bechtel Nevada held the DOE management and operating contract for the Nevada Test Site 1996-2006
l-nevada-test-site.note: DOE technical reports list Bechtel Nevada as research organisation of record through 2006, succeeded by National Security Technologies, LLC.

l-nevada-test-site.label: United States Department of Energy
l-nevada-test-site.why: DOE operating authority over the Nevada National Security Site
l-nevada-test-site.note: The Nevada test complex is DOE/NNSA property operated by contract, with its own protective force and clearance regime, and is named repeatedly in retrieval testimony.

l-nevada-test-site.label: Northrop Grumman Corporation
l-nevada-test-site.why: A Northrop Grumman-led consortium took over Nevada Test Site management in 2006
l-nevada-test-site.note: National Security Technologies LLC succeeded Bechtel Nevada, inheriting the Remote Sensing Laboratory, the Special Technologies Laboratory and the classified support infrastructure adjacent to Groom Lake.

l-nevada-test-site.label: EG&G (Edgerton, Germeshausen and Grier)
l-nevada-test-site.why: EG&G was the classified services contractor for the Nevada complex in the testing era
l-nevada-test-site.note: Its instrumentation and site services role is documented through DOE technical history and through the Groom Lake litigation rather than through any acknowledgment of the adjacent operating location.

burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.label: Eric Burlison
burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.why: Author of the adopted FY2027 NDAA disclosure amendment
burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.note: The House adopted his Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act amendment on 23 July 2026, creating a subpoena-empowered review board and contractor disclosure obligations.

burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.label: National Archives UAP Records Collection (Record Group 615)
burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.why: Would impose statutory transfer timelines on the NARA collection
burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.note: The amendment would require agencies to identify, preserve and transfer covered UAP records under a statutory timeline, supplying the enforcement the FY2024 NDAA sections omitted.

burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.why: Statutory backstop for an executive release programme
burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.note: The amendment is framed as reinforcing PURSUE by creating statutory disclosure procedures rather than relying solely on executive-branch policy.

burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.label: House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets hearing, 9 September 2025 - 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection'
burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.why: The FOIA-reach finding is the antecedent of the 2026 contractor-disclosure amendment
burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.note: The Task Force found UAP spending flows to entities outside FOIA reach; the amendment adopted 23 July 2026 extends disclosure obligations to government contractors. Reasoning: direct correspondence between the finding and the remedy.

burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.label: FY2024 NDAA, Public Law 118-31 - Div. A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C (secs. 1841-1843), UAP Records Collection; Div. G (IAA FY2024) secs. 7341, 7343
burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.why: Restores the enforcement architecture stripped from the FY2024 sections
burlison-uapda-fy2027-ndaa-amendment.note: Sections 1841-1843 created a records collection without a review board, subpoena power or contractor reach; the 2026 amendment reintroduces all three.

fbi-vault-ufo.label: National Archives Record Group 615 - UAP Records Collection
fbi-vault-ufo.why: FBI transferred records to RG 615 while its standing Vault collection stayed frozen at 2013
fbi-vault-ufo.note: The FBI appears as an RG 615 contributor (catalog ID 580705010) and was the largest single contributor to PURSUE Release 03, while its public Vault UFO collection remained last-modified 25 July 2013.

fbi-vault-ufo.label: PURSUE Release 01
fbi-vault-ufo.why: Published FBI 62-HQ-83894, well beyond the Vault's 1947-1954 scope
fbi-vault-ufo.note: The Bureau's master flying disc file covering 1947 to 1968 was released as a single 101MB PDF through war.gov rather than through the FBI's own reading room.

fbi-vault-ufo.label: PURSUE Release 03
fbi-vault-ufo.why: 29 FBI files including a 2021-2025 orb corpus and an agents' own FD-1057
fbi-vault-ufo.note: The tranche established the FBI as an active modern UAP collector, a posture invisible in its own Vault collection last modified in 2013.

cia-readingroom-ufo.label: PURSUE Release 03
cia-readingroom-ufo.why: Released a less-redacted 1953 Robertson Panel record
cia-readingroom-ufo.note: A version of the Agency's own foundational UAP document less redacted than the one in its public reading room appeared seventy-three years later, by executive direction.

cia-readingroom-ufo.label: PURSUE Release 05
cia-readingroom-ufo.note: A CIA report of an alleged November 1963 recovery of a metal sphere with a deceased occupant, deemed unsubstantiated by the American Consulate, appears in Release 05 and not in the Agency's curated collection.

institute-advanced-studies-austin.label: DIRD: 'Clinical Medical Acute & Subacute Field Effects on Human Dermal & Neurological Tissues'
institute-advanced-studies-austin.why: Produced under the Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin imprint
institute-advanced-studies-austin.note: The document's cover page carries the IASA name above the headings 'Translational Sciences / Forensic Medicine - Engineering Mechanics', placing Puthoff's institute as the producing organisation for the government's medical study.

institute-advanced-studies-austin.label: EarthTech International / Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
institute-advanced-studies-austin.note: EarthTech's own About page states the corporate relationship; the two names are used interchangeably across the DIRD covers and the TTSA reporting.

aawsap-dird-series.label: DIA letter to Steven Aftergood listing 38 AATIP reference products (16 January 2019)
aawsap-dird-series.why: The 38-title list is the only official enumeration of the series
aawsap-dird-series.note: DIA released the list to Steven Aftergood of FAS on 16 January 2019 under FOIA; it had been provided to Congress in January 2018. Without this release the series would be known only from leaks.

aawsap-dird-series.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
aawsap-dird-series.why: The DIRDs are the documentary output of the AAWSAP contract
aawsap-dird-series.note: Each released DIRD states it is 'one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency, Defense Warning Office's Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program'.

aawsap-dird-series.label: Chain of custody
aawsap-dird-series.why: Exhaustive on paper flow, silent on object flow
aawsap-dird-series.note: The released AAWSAP corpus documents control numbers, fiscal years, contract status, statements of work and named programme managers - and contains no record of the receipt, transfer or storage of any physical sample. The asymmetry is the finding.

dird-traversable-wormholes.label: EarthTech International / Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
dird-traversable-wormholes.why: Contractor of record: EarthTech International Inc., 11855 Research Blvd, Austin TX
dird-traversable-wormholes.note: The author block on the released DIRD gives EarthTech's full street address, which makes the corporate performer identifiable and locatable rather than a generic 'contractor'.

dird-traversable-wormholes.label: Eric W. Davis
dird-traversable-wormholes.note: The cover of the released document names Eric W. Davis, Ph.D., of EarthTech International Inc. as author, with a DIA control number, a Defense Warning Office preparing office and an FY2009 production year.

dird-traversable-wormholes.label: James T. Lacatski
dird-traversable-wormholes.why: Lacatski named as AAWSA Program Manager on the document's administrative note
dird-traversable-wormholes.note: The administrative note directs comments to James T. Lacatski, D.Eng., AAWSA Program Manager, DIA, ATTN: CLAR/DWO-3, Bldg 6000, Washington DC 20340-5100 - naming the government official responsible for the series.

dird-green-clinical-medical.label: Harold E. Puthoff
dird-green-clinical-medical.why: Preface quotes a November 2007 proposal on 'Probable ET Generated' emissions addressed to Puthoff/Hathaway
dird-green-clinical-medical.note: This is the earliest dated documentary link between Puthoff and a US-sponsored effort to characterise fields associated with 'exotic propulsion' - nine months before the AAWSAP contract was awarded to BAASS.

dird-green-clinical-medical.label: Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
dird-green-clinical-medical.why: Produced under the Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin imprint
dird-green-clinical-medical.note: The document's cover page carries the IASA name above the headings 'Translational Sciences / Forensic Medicine - Engineering Mechanics', placing Puthoff's institute as the producing organisation for the government's medical study.

dird-green-clinical-medical.label: Christopher C. 'Kit' Green
dird-green-clinical-medical.why: Author of the AAWSAP human-injury reference document
dird-green-clinical-medical.note: Green, a physician-neuroscientist and former CIA life-sciences analyst, wrote the study of injuries attributed to proximity to anomalous craft; released publicly by Popular Mechanics on 14 February 2020.

dia-aatip-list-2019.label: AAWSAP Defense Intelligence Reference Document series
dia-aatip-list-2019.why: The 38-title list is the only official enumeration of the series
dia-aatip-list-2019.note: DIA released the list to Steven Aftergood of FAS on 16 January 2019 under FOIA; it had been provided to Congress in January 2018. Without this release the series would be known only from leaks.

dia-aatip-list-2019.label: Chain of custody
dia-aatip-list-2019.why: Converted an oral controversy into an enumerated procurement record
dia-aatip-list-2019.note: Whatever else AATIP/AAWSAP was, the FOIA release proves it bought 38 named studies on wormholes, warp drive, metamaterials, metallic glasses, negative mass propulsion and clinical injury pathology for roughly $22 million.

ttsa-army-crada-2019.label: ADAM Research Project (Acquisition and Data Analysis of Materials)
ttsa-army-crada-2019.why: ADAM materials became the subject of a five-year Army CRADA
ttsa-army-crada-2019.note: On 17 October 2019 TTSA entered a CRADA with the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command covering inertial mass reduction, metamaterials, quantum physics and beamed energy propulsion, with at least $750,000 in Army support and no public funding to the company.

ttsa-army-crada-2019.label: Chain of custody
ttsa-army-crada-2019.why: The chain goes dark inside a federal research agreement
ttsa-army-crada-2019.note: A CRADA is a records-generating instrument. Seven years after signature, no characterisation of the samples, no technical output and no Army statement of findings has been published. That silence is the darkest segment of the only documented private-to-federal materials transfer.

davis-sasc-briefing-2019.label: Eric W. Davis
davis-sasc-briefing-2019.why: Briefed SASC staff on 21 Oct 2019 and SSCI members on 23 Oct 2019
davis-sasc-briefing-2019.note: Davis told The New York Times on the record that he had given classified briefings on retrievals of unexplained objects to both committees within 48 hours.

davis-sasc-briefing-2019.label: Kirk McConnell
davis-sasc-briefing-2019.why: Delivered to the SASC professional staff cohort McConnell belonged to
davis-sasc-briefing-2019.note: McConnell was a Senate Armed Services professional staffer working UAP issues in this exact period. Whether he personally attended the 21 October 2019 briefing has never been confirmed by him or by the committee.

stanford-nolan-lab.label: Nolan, Vallee, Jiang & Lemke (2022), Progress in Aerospace Sciences 128:100788
stanford-nolan-lab.why: Analysis performed with MIBI, a Stanford-developed instrument
stanford-nolan-lab.note: Multiplexed ion beam imaging, developed by Angelo, Bendall and Nolan for tissue biology, resolved the sample at 200 nm laterally and 5 nm in depth - the technique's first application to alleged UAP material.

paper-nolan-vallee-2022.label: Nolan Laboratory, Stanford University School of Medicine
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.why: Analysis performed with MIBI, a Stanford-developed instrument
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.note: Multiplexed ion beam imaging, developed by Angelo, Bendall and Nolan for tissue biology, resolved the sample at 200 nm laterally and 5 nm in depth - the technique's first application to alleged UAP material.

paper-nolan-vallee-2022.label: Council Bluffs, Iowa molten metal fall, 17 December 1977
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.why: Subject of the analysis: the 17 December 1977 molten mass
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.note: Five independent witness groups, police photography, contemporaneous press coverage and a preserved sample - the only complete civil chain of custody in the published literature.

paper-nolan-vallee-2022.label: Garry Nolan
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.why: Senior author of the first peer-reviewed UAP materials analysis
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.note: Progress in Aerospace Sciences 128:100788, applying SIMS and MIBI at 200 nm lateral resolution to the Council Bluffs material.

paper-nolan-vallee-2022.label: Jacques F. Vallee
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.why: Co-author and source of the sample and its case file
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.note: Vallee supplied both the physical material and the 45-year documentary case record - newspaper reports, police photographs, fire-department accounts - that makes the analysis interpretable.

paper-nolan-vallee-2022.label: Larry G. Lemke
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.why: NASA Ames aerospace engineer supplying the exclusion arguments
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.note: Lemke's engineering judgement underpins the rejection of reentry-debris and aircraft-component hypotheses on thermal-history and materials-selection grounds.

paper-nolan-vallee-2022.label: Sizun Jiang
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.note: Jiang, then of the Nolan laboratory, ran the multiplexed ion beam imaging that produced the incomplete-mixing result.

paper-nolan-vallee-2022.label: The Sol Foundation
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.why: Sol Briefing No. 3 is the authoritative public exposition of the paper
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.note: The April 2026 briefing sets out the witness record, the 1978 initial identification, the SIMS/MIBI methodology and each hypothesis-elimination with its physical reason - work no journalism had done.

paper-nolan-vallee-2022.label: Materials and custody analysis
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.why: Establishes the standard the government's own holdings have never met
paper-nolan-vallee-2022.note: A published sample, a published method, a published elimination of alternatives, and a stated residual. No government-held UAP material has ever been subjected to anything comparable in public.

council-bluffs-1977.label: Nolan, Vallee, Jiang & Lemke (2022), Progress in Aerospace Sciences 128:100788
council-bluffs-1977.why: Subject of the analysis: the 17 December 1977 molten mass
council-bluffs-1977.note: Five independent witness groups, police photography, contemporaneous press coverage and a preserved sample - the only complete civil chain of custody in the published literature.

sol-briefing-3-2026.label: The Sol Foundation
sol-briefing-3-2026.why: publisher of Science and Policy Briefing No. 3
sol-briefing-3-2026.note: The briefing is issued in The Sol Foundation Science and Policy Briefings series (No. 3, April 2026, published online 30 April 2026) and carries the foundation's imprint and cofounders Garry Nolan and Peter Skafish on the colophon.

sol-briefing-3-2026.label: Garry Nolan
sol-briefing-3-2026.why: briefing analyses Nolan's Council Bluffs materials study
sol-briefing-3-2026.note: The briefing's subject is the SIMS and MIBI analysis led by Stanford professor Garry P. Nolan with Jacques Vallee, Sizun Jiang and Larry Lemke of the 1977 Council Bluffs, Iowa molten-metal sample, published in Progress in Aerospace Sciences 128 (2022).

sol-briefing-3-2026.label: Marik von Rennenkampff
sol-briefing-3-2026.why: author of Sol Science and Policy Briefing No. 3
sol-briefing-3-2026.note: Von Rennenkampff is the named author of 'First Peer-Reviewed Scientific Analysis of Possible UAP Materials Employs State-of-the-Art Technologies,' The Sol Foundation Science and Policy Briefings No. 3, April 2026.

galileo-project.label: Cambridge, Massachusetts (alias of l-cambridge)
galileo-project.why: first Galileo Observatory, Harvard College Observatory roof
galileo-project.note: The Galileo Project's first all-sky observatory is on the roof of the Harvard College Observatory in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It is the physical instrument site for the project's instrumented search, not merely an administrative address.

galileo-project.label: Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics
galileo-project.why: Host institution of the Galileo Project
galileo-project.note: The Galileo Project is listed as a research programme of the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian and is hosted on Harvard infrastructure; its first observatory was built on the roof of the Harvard College Observatory. Start date is the project's public launch in July 2021.

galileo-project.label: Richard Cloete
galileo-project.why: Lead author of the project's detection and tracking computing platform
galileo-project.note: Published in the Journal of Astronomical Instrumentation in 2023 - pipeline and classifier architecture published before the observations.

galileo-project.label: Wesley A. Watters
galileo-project.why: Research coordinator and co-editor of the JAI instrumentation special issue
galileo-project.note: The special issue is the artefact that established a peer-reviewed instrumentation literature in this field rather than a claims literature.

galileo-project.label: Sarah Little
galileo-project.why: Co-author on the 2025 geomagnetic variometer instrumentation paper
galileo-project.note: Published in Geoscientific Instrumentation, Methods and Data Systems in November 2025 - a Copernicus geophysics journal publishing hardware installed specifically to look for UAP signatures.

galileo-project.label: Cambridge, Massachusetts
galileo-project.why: The Galileo Project is based at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics
galileo-project.note: Avi Loeb founded the project in 2021 to build independent multi-modal observatories, addressing the structural problem that every high-quality UAP dataset is held by agencies that will not release it.

galileo-project.label: Abraham 'Avi' Loeb
galileo-project.note: Founded four weeks after the ODNI preliminary assessment on the premise that the way past a classified impasse is to build unclassified instruments and publish.

galileo-project.label: Galileo Project Pacific Ocean expedition to the CNEOS 2014-01-08 (IM1) site, June-July 2023
galileo-project.note: A magnetic sled dragged across the seabed off Papua New Guinea at a location determined from seismometer data; several hundred sub-millimetre spherules recovered.

galileo-project.label: ODNI Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (25 June 2021)
galileo-project.why: Founded in direct response to the June 2021 ODNI assessment
galileo-project.note: The project's founding rationale was the ODNI report's admission of an evidentiary vacuum, together with NASA administrator Bill Nelson's call for scientific analysis.

im1-pacific-expedition-2023.label: Amir Siraj
im1-pacific-expedition-2023.why: Siraj's interstellar-velocity and seismic localisation determined the search site
im1-pacific-expedition-2023.note: The Astrophysical Journal paper of November 2022 identified CNEOS 2014-01-08 as apparently interstellar; the Signals paper of September 2023 localised it seismically. Fernando et al. later attributed that signal to truck traffic.

im1-pacific-expedition-2023.label: The Galileo Project
im1-pacific-expedition-2023.note: A magnetic sled dragged across the seabed off Papua New Guinea at a location determined from seismometer data; several hundred sub-millimetre spherules recovered.

im1-pacific-expedition-2023.label: Materials and custody analysis
im1-pacific-expedition-2023.why: The control case: what a public physical-recovery attempt looks like, failures included
im1-pacific-expedition-2023.note: Claim, rebuttal and re-analysis all appeared in the peer-reviewed literature within eighteen months. That is the benchmark against which seventy years of unpublished government custody should be judged.

scu-uap-studies.label: Limina - The Journal of UAP Studies
scu-uap-studies.note: Grosvenor, Hancock and Porritt's 'UAP Indications Analysis 1945-1975 United States Atomic Warfare Complex' appeared in Limina in March 2025 with a DOI.

scu-uap-studies.label: Robert M. Powell
scu-uap-studies.why: Founding board member; author of the Stephenville and Aguadilla studies
scu-uap-studies.note: Powell established SCU's method: obtain the primary federal sensor record by FOIA, reconstruct it quantitatively, deposit it with a DOI.

scu-uap-studies.label: Sarah Little
scu-uap-studies.why: SCU board member and co-author of the 2023 characteristics study
scu-uap-studies.note: Little is one of the few researchers who publishes with both SCU and the Galileo Project, which is a measure of how small the actual civil analytical bench is.

scu-uap-studies.label: Materials and custody analysis
scu-uap-studies.why: Builds the documentary counterpart to the physical-sample record
scu-uap-studies.note: SCU's Hancock-Porritt-Grosvenor series correlating 1945-1975 UAP activity with the United States atomic warfare complex runs in parallel to the VASCO plate work on the same period.

scu-uap-studies.label: Kevin H. Knuth
scu-uap-studies.why: SCU's inaugural Distinguished Scholar Award, June 2025 - recognition, not an office
scu-uap-studies.note: Presented at SCU's Sixth Annual Conference, Von Braun Center, Huntsville, Alabama, 6-8 June 2025, by SCU Executive Board member Rich Hoffman, who said: 'Dr. Knuth's leadership in advancing empirical, interdisciplinary UAP research exemplifies the mission of SCU.' IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT: this pass found no evidence that Knuth holds an SCU board seat, officer post or executive role. The board's pre-existing SCU connection to this cluster runs through Robert Powell, an SCU founding board member and Knuth's co-author on the 2019 Entropy paper. The award is a recognition edge, and is labelled as one.

uapx.label: Matthew Szydagis
uapx.why: Co-founder; first author of the field-expedition results
uapx.note: A liquid-xenon dark-matter physicist applying direct-detection discipline - background rates, instrumental artefacts, false positives - to open-air field observation.

uapx.label: Szydagis, Knuth, Kugielsky & Levy (2025), Progress in Aerospace Sciences 156:101099
uapx.note: Progress in Aerospace Sciences 156:101099, June 2025 - a published field protocol against which any future government sensor release can be compared.

uapx.label: Kevin H. Knuth
uapx.why: Vice President of UAPx and co-author of the 2025 paper
uapx.note: Knuth links UAPx to the Galileo Project, where he is a research affiliate, and to SCU through the Entropy collaboration with Powell.

uapx.label: University at Albany (SUNY), Department of Physics
uapx.why: Academic base of UAPx's science leadership - NOT a host, sponsor or funder
uapx.note: The distinction matters and is drawn by the University itself. UAlbany's release separates 'UAlbany authors Matthew Szydagis, Kevin Knuth and Cecilia Levy' from 'Ben Kugielsky of UAPx, a non-profit scientific research organization'. UAPx is an independent 501(c)(3); the University is where its two lead scientists hold their chairs, not its institutional home. This is the opposite of the harvard-cfa / galileo-project relationship already on the board, where the CfA is the host institution. Funding for the 2021 California field work came from Caroline Cory of OMnium Media, to produce the documentary 'A Tear in the Sky' (2022) - not from UAlbany.

vasco-project.label: The Sol Foundation
vasco-project.why: Sol Briefing No. 1 (January 2026) is built on the pre-satellite-era plate evidence
vasco-project.note: 'Robust Evidence of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena in Pre-Satellite Era Night-Sky Images' translated the VASCO results into a policy artefact aimed at Congress.

vasco-project.label: Beatriz Villarroel
vasco-project.note: VASCO compares POSS-I plates exposed 1949-1957 against modern surveys; the pre-Sputnik exposure dates remove the satellite-glint confound entirely.

paper-villarroel-bruehl-2025.label: Stephen Bruehl
paper-villarroel-bruehl-2025.why: Lead author of the POSS-I / nuclear testing association
paper-villarroel-bruehl-2025.note: Scientific Reports, 20 October 2025 - a Nature-portfolio paper linking above-ground nuclear testing, contemporaneous UAP reports and anomalous optical transients.

paper-villarroel-bruehl-2025.label: Materials and custody analysis
paper-villarroel-bruehl-2025.why: Physical-archive evidence for the programme's origin period that no agency can classify
paper-villarroel-bruehl-2025.note: Glass plates in civil astronomical custody, exposed before Sputnik, are structurally immune to classification and to the archival destruction that affected the government's own 1940s-1950s records.

paper-knuth-powell-reali-2019.label: Kevin H. Knuth
paper-knuth-powell-reali-2019.why: Lead author of the Entropy kinematics paper
paper-knuth-powell-reali-2019.note: Entropy 21(10):939 estimated accelerations, velocities and required power from documented cases including the 2004 Nimitz encounter.

paper-knuth-powell-reali-2019.label: USS Nimitz Carrier Strike Group Encounters, 10-16 November 2004
paper-knuth-powell-reali-2019.why: Nimitz encounter analysed quantitatively in a peer-reviewed physics journal
paper-knuth-powell-reali-2019.note: A companion paper in the MaxEnt 2019 proceedings treated the Nimitz case specifically; this is the point at which the 2004 encounter entered the physics literature rather than the news cycle.

paper-knuth-powell-reali-2019.label: Robert M. Powell
paper-knuth-powell-reali-2019.why: Co-author; brought the SCU case reconstructions
paper-knuth-powell-reali-2019.note: Powell's FOIA-derived sensor reconstructions supplied the case inputs for the kinematic estimates.

paper-uapx-2025.label: Cecilia Levy
paper-uapx-2025.why: Co-author of the UAPx field-expedition results
paper-uapx-2025.note: Fourth-named author on Szydagis, Knuth, Kugielsky & Levy (2025). The board's existing node label for this paper already carries her surname; until now she had no node behind it.

paper-uapx-2025.label: UAPx
paper-uapx-2025.note: Progress in Aerospace Sciences 156:101099, June 2025 - a published field protocol against which any future government sensor release can be compared.

paper-uapx-2025.label: University at Albany (SUNY), Department of Physics
paper-uapx-2025.why: Three of four authors carry the UAlbany affiliation; the University publicised the result under its own name
paper-uapx-2025.note: The UAlbany News Center release of 4 June 2025 states: 'Utilizing a diverse set of devices to capture different types of data on many channels, UAlbany authors Matthew Szydagis, Kevin Knuth and Cecilia Levy, along with Ben Kugielsky of UAPx, a non-profit scientific research organization, collected observable-light and infrared images during a field expedition in 2021 to Laguna Beach, California.' The release also records the outcome honestly - 'the UAlbany research team succeeded in plausibly explaining all but one of the potential anomalies detected' - and quotes Szydagis on the single unresolved ambiguity. A state university issuing a press release claiming a UAP field-instrumentation result as institutional output is the substantive reason this node belongs on the board.

nasa-uapist.label: David N. Spergel
nasa-uapist.note: Commissioned 24 May 2022, one public meeting 31 May 2023, report delivered and team dissolved 14 September 2023.

nasa-uapist.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
nasa-uapist.why: Ran concurrently with, and separately from, AARO
nasa-uapist.note: Two federal UAP bodies operated in parallel through 2022-2023 with no public mechanism for the unclassified panel to see AARO's classified holdings.

nasa-uapist.label: Chain of custody
nasa-uapist.why: Concluded data was insufficient - having been given only the unclassified record
nasa-uapist.note: Sixteen serious scientists examining only unclassified material concluded that unclassified material is insufficient. The finding measures the panel's access, not the government's holdings.

harvard-cfa.label: Abraham 'Avi' Loeb
harvard-cfa.why: Loeb directs the Institute for Theory and Computation at the CfA
harvard-cfa.note: Avi Loeb, head of the Galileo Project, is Director of the Institute for Theory and Computation at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics and former chair of Harvard's Astronomy Department; his CfA position is the institutional base from which the Galileo Project operates.

harvard-cfa.label: The Galileo Project
harvard-cfa.why: Host institution of the Galileo Project
harvard-cfa.note: The Galileo Project is listed as a research programme of the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian and is hosted on Harvard infrastructure; its first observatory was built on the roof of the Harvard College Observatory. Start date is the project's public launch in July 2021.

university-at-albany.label: Cecilia Levy
university-at-albany.why: Employs Levy; Associate Professor of Physics and the third UAlbany author on the 2025 UAPx paper
university-at-albany.note: Levy is an LZ dark-matter physicist in the same department and co-developer, with Szydagis, of the Snowball Chamber supercooled-water detector. The University's own news office names her as one of three 'UAlbany authors' on the 2025 Progress in Aerospace Sciences field-expedition paper. Her faculty page does not itself list UAP among her research interests, which is worth recording rather than smoothing over: unlike Szydagis, her UAP involvement appears in the publication record and the university press office but not in her stated departmental research profile.

university-at-albany.label: Kevin H. Knuth
university-at-albany.why: Employs Knuth; Professor of Physics since 2023, on the faculty since 2005
university-at-albany.note: The UAlbany Department of Physics faculty page lists Knuth's appointments as Assistant Professor 2005-2009, Associate Professor 2009-2023, Professor 2023-present, immediately following four years as a GS-14 Research Scientist in the Intelligent Systems Division at NASA Ames (2001-2005). The same page records him as Editor-in-Chief of Entropy (MDPI) since 2012, which is the journal that published the 2019 Nimitz kinematics paper. This is the primary reason the institution is on the board: it is the salaried academic post from which the peer-reviewed UAP kinematics and field-instrumentation literature was produced.

university-at-albany.label: Matthew Szydagis
university-at-albany.why: Employs Szydagis; Associate Professor of Physics, with UAP listed as a departmental research interest
university-at-albany.note: The department's own faculty page for Szydagis lists his research interests as 'Experimental astroparticle physics, in particular direct detection of dark matter WIMPs (Weakly Interacting Massive Particles) and general detector development for rare event searches, neutron activation, and Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena'. That the phrase appears on a university department page, not a personal site, is the load-bearing fact: UAP is here a declared institutional research interest rather than a private hobby. Szydagis created the Noble Element Simulation Technique (NEST) in 2011 and works on LZ at the Sanford Underground Research Facility.

university-at-albany.label: Knuth et al. (2025), 'The New Science of Unidentified Aerospace-Undersea Phenomena (UAP)', Progress in Aerospace Sciences
university-at-albany.why: Knuth lead-authored the 34-author UAP review from his UAlbany post; Szydagis co-authored
university-at-albany.note: Published in the same Progress in Aerospace Sciences special edition as the UAPx field results. The UAlbany release states 'Knuth is lead author of the article, which was co-written by Szydagis and more than 30 other researchers from around the world'; SCU's June 2025 press release gives the count as thirty-four authors and the DOI as 10.1016/j.paerosci.2025.101097.

university-at-albany.why: Three of four authors carry the UAlbany affiliation; the University publicised the result under its own name
university-at-albany.note: The UAlbany News Center release of 4 June 2025 states: 'Utilizing a diverse set of devices to capture different types of data on many channels, UAlbany authors Matthew Szydagis, Kevin Knuth and Cecilia Levy, along with Ben Kugielsky of UAPx, a non-profit scientific research organization, collected observable-light and infrared images during a field expedition in 2021 to Laguna Beach, California.' The release also records the outcome honestly - 'the UAlbany research team succeeded in plausibly explaining all but one of the potential anomalies detected' - and quotes Szydagis on the single unresolved ambiguity. A state university issuing a press release claiming a UAP field-instrumentation result as institutional output is the substantive reason this node belongs on the board.

university-at-albany.label: UAPx
university-at-albany.why: Academic base of UAPx's science leadership - NOT a host, sponsor or funder
university-at-albany.note: The distinction matters and is drawn by the University itself. UAlbany's release separates 'UAlbany authors Matthew Szydagis, Kevin Knuth and Cecilia Levy' from 'Ben Kugielsky of UAPx, a non-profit scientific research organization'. UAPx is an independent 501(c)(3); the University is where its two lead scientists hold their chairs, not its institutional home. This is the opposite of the harvard-cfa / galileo-project relationship already on the board, where the CfA is the host institution. Funding for the 2021 California field work came from Caroline Cory of OMnium Media, to produce the documentary 'A Tear in the Sky' (2022) - not from UAlbany.

age-of-disclosure-2025.label: Eric W. Davis
age-of-disclosure-2025.note: Davis's participation puts the man who briefed two Senate committees on retrievals on camera alongside a sitting Secretary of State and a former Director of National Intelligence.

age-of-disclosure-2025.label: Harold E. Puthoff
age-of-disclosure-2025.note: The AAWSAP propulsion author sat for the same documentary as the AAWSAP wormhole author, the UAP Task Force chief scientist and the Stanford materials analyst.

d-custody.label: DIA letter to Steven Aftergood listing 38 AATIP reference products (16 January 2019)
d-custody.why: Converted an oral controversy into an enumerated procurement record
d-custody.note: Whatever else AATIP/AAWSAP was, the FOIA release proves it bought 38 named studies on wormholes, warp drive, metamaterials, metallic glasses, negative mass propulsion and clinical injury pathology for roughly $22 million.

d-custody.label: Retrieval & Recovery Operations
d-custody.note: The custody chain begins at the recovery site; every documented handoff is a scoring opportunity on the C axis.

d-custody.label: Eric W. Davis
d-custody.why: 'We couldn't make it ourselves' - a custody claim with no public chain
d-custody.note: Davis's on-record statement about analysed material has never been accompanied by any public documentation of where the material came from, who held it, or where it is now.

d-custody.label: Garry Nolan
d-custody.why: Approached by unnamed government and aerospace-corporation representatives about casualty biology
d-custody.note: Nolan told KQED he was approached about medical harm from 'supposed interactions with an anomalous craft'. Neither the government element nor the corporation has ever been named, which is where this chain goes dark at its first link.

d-custody.label: UAP Science Advisory Council
d-custody.why: No budget, no classified access - constitutionally unable to reach the material
d-custody.note: The Associated Press reported the council has no budget and no access to classified material, and the Sol Foundation confirmed all shared data is unclassified. An advisory body denied money and clearances cannot audit a special access programme.

d-custody.label: AAWSAP Defense Intelligence Reference Document series
d-custody.why: Exhaustive on paper flow, silent on object flow
d-custody.note: The released AAWSAP corpus documents control numbers, fiscal years, contract status, statements of work and named programme managers - and contains no record of the receipt, transfer or storage of any physical sample. The asymmetry is the finding.

d-custody.label: Harold E. Puthoff
d-custody.why: Private, non-FOIA-able laboratory sitting between a government programme and a public company
d-custody.note: EarthTech has published no analytical results on the samples it has held, and as a private corporation is outside FOIA. Every documented chain that reaches it stops there.

d-custody.label: To The Stars Academy - US Army CCDC Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (17 October 2019)
d-custody.why: The chain goes dark inside a federal research agreement
d-custody.note: A CRADA is a records-generating instrument. Seven years after signature, no characterisation of the samples, no technical output and no Army statement of findings has been published. That silence is the darkest segment of the only documented private-to-federal materials transfer.

d-custody.label: NASA Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Independent Study Team
d-custody.why: Concluded data was insufficient - having been given only the unclassified record
d-custody.note: Sixteen serious scientists examining only unclassified material concluded that unclassified material is insufficient. The finding measures the panel's access, not the government's holdings.

limina-journal.label: Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies (SCU)
limina-journal.note: Grosvenor, Hancock and Porritt's 'UAP Indications Analysis 1945-1975 United States Atomic Warfare Complex' appeared in Limina in March 2025 with a DOI.

l-austin.label: EarthTech International / Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
l-austin.why: 11855 Research Blvd - the address printed on a DIA reference document
l-austin.note: The single street address connecting the DIA Defense Warning Office to the AAWSAP propulsion and medical documents and thence to the To The Stars metamaterials work.

hr-8197.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
hr-8197.why: would abolish AARO outright and bar any successor entity
hr-8197.note: The terminal congressional judgement that a centralised UAP office inside the Department is a mechanism of concealment rather than a remedy for it.

hr-8197.label: Timothy Floyd Burchett
hr-8197.why: introduced the bill to abolish AARO, 6 April 2026
hr-8197.note: Four pages; abolishes the office, bars any successor, redistributes functions to the military departments, repeals the enabling statutes. Referred to HASC and HPSCI.

hr-8197.label: Anna Paulina Luna
hr-8197.why: recommended AARO's complete defunding to the DOGE subcommittee in March 2026, weeks before the bill
hr-8197.note: Luna's defunding recommendation and Burchett's abolition bill are the same judgement expressed through appropriations and authorisation respectively.

hr-5060.label: Timothy Floyd Burchett
hr-5060.why: sponsor of the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act
hr-5060.note: H.R. 5060 in the 119th Congress, reintroducing H.R. 10111 from the 118th.

hr-5060.label: House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets hearing, 9 September 2025 - 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection'
hr-5060.why: hearing findings underwrite the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act
hr-5060.note: The Task Force found witnesses face career damage and retaliation requiring congressional safeguards; the bill was on the agenda in the run-up to the hearing.

hr-5060.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
hr-5060.why: a separate statutory channel is needed because AARO's secure reporting mechanism is not a safe destination
hr-5060.note: Congress would not build a parallel protection regime if the aaro.mil mechanism functioned; AARO's own FY2025 figures show 255 of 262 contacts declared out of scope.

hearing-2024-11-19.label: Immaculate Constellation disclosure, October-November 2024
hearing-2024-11-19.why: Kosloski's statement for the record does not mention Immaculate Constellation
hearing-2024-11-19.note: The alleged programme had been entered into the congressional record weeks earlier and described in an ODNI unclassified press item of 22 October 2024; AARO's director addressed the Senate six days after the House hearing without naming it.

hearing-2024-11-19.label: Jon T. Kosloski
hearing-2024-11-19.why: first congressional testimony as AARO director
hearing-2024-11-19.note: Kosloski's statement for the record puts holdings at over 1,600 reports and delivers the standard no-verifiable-evidence formula.

kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.label: Sean M. Kirkpatrick
kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.why: authored the op-ed attacking the whistleblowers seven weeks after leaving office
kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.note: Published 19 January 2024, between his 1 December 2023 departure and the 8 March 2024 release of the report he had written.

kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.label: Luis D. Elizondo
kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.why: attributes the crash-retrieval narrative to AATIP and the Bigelow circle
kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.note: Kirkpatrick names AATIP and Robert Bigelow as the origin of what he calls circular reporting, an attack that lands on Elizondo without engaging his account as testimony.

kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.label: Robert T. Bigelow
kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.why: names Bigelow as the seeding influence behind the modern belief system
kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.note: The op-ed's causal account routes the entire disclosure record back through Bigelow's funding of the AAWSAP/AATIP orbit.

kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.label: YANKEE BLUE (alleged AFOSI indoctrination program)
kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.why: the 'circular reporting from a small group' thesis, seventeen months before the Air Force was identified as the seeding group
kirkpatrick-sciam-oped-2024.note: Kirkpatrick's mechanism was correct in form and wrong in agent: belief was seeded and repeated from a small source, but the documented source is a US Air Force indoctrination practice, not a civilian believer network. Whether AARO knew this when the op-ed ran is unresolved, given that AARO discovered Yankee Blue during his tenure.

peru-uap-office.label: Força Aérea Brasileira / Ministério da Aeronáutica
peru-uap-office.why: COMPARISON: Peru's own state news agency measured DIFAA's reopening against Brazil
peru-uap-office.note: COMPARISON EDGE — no institutional contact between the FAP and the FAB is claimed. Peru's state news agency Andina, reporting the reopening on 18 October 2013, closes: 'Con la reapertura de la DIFAA, el Perú se coloca a la paridad de países de la región como Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Brasil y Ecuador.' Brazil is named by a Peruvian government outlet as the regional benchmark. The same report establishes the office's identity that the peru-uap-office node lacked: the Departamento de Investigación de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos (DIFAA), sitting under the Dirección de Intereses Aéreos Espaciales (DINAE), whose head Coronel FAP Julio Vucetich Abanto announced the public reporting channel, the office having been closed for five years 'a causa de problemas administrativos'. The reopening was announced at an FAP-hosted 'Encuentro sobre Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos' addressing the Nazca Lines question.

peru-uap-office.label: CEFAA / SEFAA - Chilean anomalous aerial phenomena office, Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil
peru-uap-office.why: COMPARISON: a military-hosted office against a civil-aviation-hosted one, in the same region
peru-uap-office.note: COMPARISON EDGE — no joint work is claimed. Andina names Chile among the regional peers DIFAA's reopening brought Peru level with, and reports Peru's stated posture on cooperation as reserved: it considered itself able to analyse the phenomena independently and would appeal to exchange with neighbours only exceptionally, to compare data. Structurally the two are opposites: DIFAA sits inside the Fuerza Aérea del Perú under DINAE, while CEFAA/SEFAA sits inside Chile's civil aviation authority, the DGAC, and frames the subject as an aviation-safety matter. Tier 2 — the structural contrast is analytic, the Peruvian facts are Andina-sourced and the Chilean facts sit on the cefaa and dgac-chile nodes.

peru-uap-office.label: GEIPAN - Groupe d'Études et d'Informations sur les Phénomènes Aérospatiaux Non identifiés
peru-uap-office.why: COMPARISON: the military-host model against the space-agency-host model
peru-uap-office.note: COMPARISON EDGE — no contact is claimed and none was found. DIFAA is hosted by an air force; GEIPAN is hosted by a civil space agency and publishes its case database. The pairing exists on this board to keep the national-office row honest: 'a country has an office' is not one fact but at least three different institutional arrangements, and Peru is the least documented of them. This pass did not locate DIFAA's founding legal instrument, its current reporting line, its case output, or any evidence that it publishes findings.

arquivo-nacional-ufo.label: Brasilia, Federal District, Brazil
arquivo-nacional-ufo.why: The UFO fund is held in Brasília and its reference code says so
arquivo-nacional-ufo.note: The Arquivo Nacional's own notice identifies the holding as 'o Fundo Objeto Voador Não Identificado – OVNI (BR DFANBSB ARX)', produced by the Comando da Aeronáutica and held by the Arquivo Nacional, comprising 743 registros. DFANBSB is the archival code for the Arquivo Nacional's Brasília unit. RQS 193/2022 states the transfer route directly: 'A partir de 2007, a Aeronáutica, mas não o Exército e nem a Marinha, passou a enviar seus papeis resultantes de suas pesquisas para o Arquivo Nacional, em Brasília.' [CORRECTED 14 Aug 2026: RQS 193/2022 is a request for a COMMEMORATIVE SPECIAL SESSION under Art. 199 RISF, approved 16 Mar 2022, held 24 Jun 2022 - not a records-seeking or compelling instrument. Its durable value is the content of its justificacao, which names Operacao Prato, the 1986 night, SIOANI and the archive reference BR DFANBSB ARX. These edges assert what the document NAMES, which is verifiable in its text and unaffected by its procedural nature, so the tier is unchanged. Any claim that the instrument COMPELLED disclosure would be false.]

arquivo-nacional-ufo.label: National Archives Record Group 615 - UAP Records Collection
arquivo-nacional-ufo.why: COMPARISON: a voluntary military transfer into a civil archive versus a statutory collection ordered by Congress
arquivo-nacional-ufo.note: COMPARISON EDGE — no institutional contact between the Arquivo Nacional and NARA is claimed or evidenced. soyuzufotsentr.label: Vladimir Georgievich Azhazha
soyuzufotsentr.why: Azhazha headed SOYUZUFOTSENTR; named as its head in the UK Defence Intelligence Staff's own report
soyuzufotsentr.note: Project Condign Volume 3, Chapter 4 ('UAP Work in Other Countries'), para 1, verified against the released MoD OCR text: 'A "UFO" Commission was created under the USSR Union of Scientific and En[gi]neering Societies in 1989, tog[e]ther in 1990 with an Inte[r]-[I]ndustry Ufology Research Centre (SOYUZUFOSENTR) to co-ordinate records. This Centre had the rights of an Insit[u]te under the USSR Academy of Sciences, and was headed by V.G. AZAHAZHA (or AZHAZHA) an eminent researcher and former naval submariner.' Bracketed letters mark OCR damage in the released scan; the transliteration SOYUZUFOSENTR is Condign's own, and differs from the board's node label. Para 4 adds that under Azhazha 'The Institute have reportedly developed light fi[l]ters, instrumentation, IR and UV photography to pursu[e] the topic', and that claimed imagery of 'peculiar spheres, humanoid figures' has, 'if the imagery exists ... never been published'. This edge closes a gap that was already implicit in the board's own data: the vladimir-azhazha node has carried instId 'soyuzufotsentr' and affiliations ['soyuzufotsentr'] all along, with no edge written.

soyuzufotsentr.label: Project Condign Volume 3 - Potential for Exploitation of UAP-Associated Effects / UAP Work in Other Countries
soyuzufotsentr.why: Condign's Former Soviet Union chapter names, dates and assesses SOYUZUFOTSENTR
soyuzufotsentr.note: This is the reason the node exists at all. SOYUZUFOTSENTR reaches this board not through Russian ufology literature but through a UK SECRET UK EYES ONLY Defence Intelligence Staff assessment, which places the centre inside a paragraph opening 'It[s] clear that the Former Soviet Union has taken the study of UAPs seriously and th[a]t this may well be related to a programme of understanding and exploiting certain UAP-related natural phenomena, such as plasmas.' The same chapter runs on to Popovich's 1990 All Union Ufology Association at the Air Force Academy, General of Aviation Igor Maltsev's 1990 release of pilot reports, Vsevolod Troitsky of the Russian Academy of Sciences chairing a Commission for the Study of Anomalous Propagation and Phenomena, and Sokolov's account of Soviet aircraft incidents. Condign treats the public centre and the state effort as one national picture. Verified line by line against the released OCR.

soyuzufotsentr.label: SETKA-AN / SETKA-MO (later Galaktika, then Gorizont) - Soviet state anomalous phenomena programme
soyuzufotsentr.why: INFERENCE: the 1990 public centre stands up as the 1978-1990/91 state programme winds down, with Azhazha the common figure
soyuzufotsentr.note: READ THE LIMIT BEFORE USING THIS EDGE. No document located in this pass states any transfer of function, records, personnel or authority from SETKA-AN/SETKA-MO to SOYUZUFOTSENTR, and Project Condign - which describes both the Soviet state exploitation programme and SOYUZUFOTSENTR in the same chapter - does not name SETKA at all. What is documented is date adjacency and a shared principal: Condign dates SOYUZUFOTSENTR to 1990; the board dates the SETKA programmes 1978-1990/91; and the board already carries an edge vladimir-azhazha -> setka-program labelled 'ran the parallel public ufology centre after censorship lifted'. This edge makes that existing person-level assertion visible at institution level and nothing more. Reasoning, not evidence. If a later pass finds a document showing a formal succession, re-tier it; if a later pass finds the two were unconnected, delete it without loss.

nara-rg615.label: Arquivo Nacional (Brazil) - UFO/UAP collection
nara-rg615.why: COMPARISON: a voluntary military transfer into a civil archive versus a statutory collection ordered by Congress
nara-rg615.note: COMPARISON EDGE — no institutional contact between the Arquivo Nacional and NARA is claimed or evidenced. Brazil: from 2007 the Comando da Aeronáutica began sending its holdings to the Arquivo Nacional of its own motion, producing the Fundo Objeto Voador Não Identificado – OVNI (BR DFANBSB ARX), 743 registros, served online, with the service publicly disclaiming further competence. The United States: the UAP Records Collection in Record Group 615 exists only because sections 1841–1843 of Public Law 118-31 ordered it into being, with a statutory transfer deadline and with the independent review board stripped out in conference. Same archival endpoint, opposite mechanism — one service handed its record over, the other had to be legislated at. [CORRECTED 14 Aug 2026: RQS 193/2022 is a request for a COMMEMORATIVE SPECIAL SESSION under Art. 199 RISF, approved 16 Mar 2022, held 24 Jun 2022 - not a records-seeking or compelling instrument. Its durable value is the content of its justificacao, which names Operacao Prato, the 1986 night, SIOANI and the archive reference BR DFANBSB ARX. These edges assert what the document NAMES, which is verifiable in its text and unaffected by its procedural nature, so the tier is unchanged. Any claim that the instrument COMPELLED disclosure would be false.]
