l-nellis.label: Groom Lake, Nevada
l-nellis.why: Groom Lake was administratively carried as part of the Nellis complex
l-nellis.note: Until the 1995 presidential determination, the official position was that Groom Lake was simply another part of the Nellis Air Force Base complex.

l-tonopah.label: Groom Lake, Nevada
l-tonopah.why: Programmes matured from Groom Lake to operational basing at Tonopah
l-tonopah.note: HAVE IDEA moved to Tonopah in May 1973; the 4450th Tactical Group moved from Groom Lake to Tonopah beginning 17 May 1982 to operate the F-117A.

l-white-sands.label: Los Alamos, New Mexico
l-white-sands.why: Los Alamos and White Sands bracket the 1948-1951 green fireball reporting corridor
l-white-sands.note: The 16 February 1949 conference at Los Alamos and the Project Twinkle instrumented observation effort in southern New Mexico both arose from reporting across this corridor.

l-white-sands.label: Roswell, New Mexico and the Foster Ranch, Lincoln County
l-white-sands.why: Roswell sits inside the 1947 New Mexico nuclear and rocketry complex
l-white-sands.note: The Foster Ranch debris field, White Sands Proving Ground, the Alamogordo Mogul launch site, Los Alamos, Sandia and Kirtland all lie within a few hundred miles. Reasoning: geographic proximity is the reason a materiel recovery there fell inside multiple classified security envelopes at once.

l-edwards-afb.label: Groom Lake, Nevada
l-edwards-afb.why: Edwards defines the acknowledged-testing boundary that Groom Lake was built to escape
l-edwards-afb.note: Groom Lake exists because the U-2 could not be tested at Edwards. The pair therefore mark the boundary between the acknowledged and unacknowledged US flight test enterprise.

l-utah.label: Skinwalker Ranch, Uintah Basin, Utah
l-utah.why: The ranch sits inside the Uintah Basin reporting region
l-utah.note: The property is in Uintah County southeast of Ballard, bordering the Uintah and Ouray Indian Reservation, inside a region with a folk reporting record dating to the 1970s.

l-vandenberg.label: House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets hearing, 9 September 2025 - 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection'
l-vandenberg.why: The Vandenberg incidents entered the congressional record in September 2025
l-vandenberg.note: Nuccetelli named AARO and the FBI as custodians of the official Air Force records for specific dated incidents at a named installation - a checkable custody claim Congress has not pursued to production.

l-vandenberg.label: Jeffrey Nuccetelli
l-vandenberg.why: Nuccetelli served in security forces at Vandenberg 2003-2005
l-vandenberg.note: His sworn written testimony of 9 September 2025 describes the 14 October 2003 red square over two missile defense sites, a rectangular craft larger than a football field, a threatened witness, and a 2005 triangular craft.

l-boulder-co.label: Low Memorandum ("the trick would be...")
l-boulder-co.why: The Low memo shows the conclusion was framed before the study began
l-boulder-co.note: Low's 9 August 1966 memorandum proposed a study 'conducted almost entirely by non-believers' with 'almost zero expectation of finding a saucer'. James E. McDonald found it in the project files in July 1967.

l-boulder-co.label: University of Colorado UFO Project (Condon Committee)
l-boulder-co.why: The Condon Committee was hosted by the University of Colorado at Boulder
l-boulder-co.note: The Air Force contract was announced in October 1966 at $313,000, eventually exceeding $500,000, with Condon as director and Robert Low as coordinator.

l-detroit-arsenal.label: Dr. Joseph Cannon
l-detroit-arsenal.why: Cannon was the named government principal investigator at GVSC
l-detroit-arsenal.note: The Army located twenty-nine emails totalling a hundred pages of Cannon's TTSA correspondence and withheld all of them under FOIA exemptions (b)(4) and (b)(5).

l-detroit-arsenal.label: Detroit, Michigan
l-detroit-arsenal.why: Detroit Arsenal is in Warren, thirteen miles north of Detroit
l-detroit-arsenal.note: The installation sits in Warren, Michigan, within the Detroit metropolitan area that also holds Kit Green's post-agency academic base at Wayne State.

l-detroit-arsenal.label: Jeffery Langhout
l-detroit-arsenal.note: The signature block is the documentary anchor: an executed federal instrument, not a press release.

l-detroit-arsenal.label: CRADA between U.S. Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center and To The Stars Academy
l-detroit-arsenal.why: The CRADA was executed at Detroit Arsenal
l-detroit-arsenal.note: GVSC Director Jeffery Langhout signed the agreement on 10 October 2019; the Army released the text on 18 October 2019.

l-detroit.label: Detroit Arsenal, Warren, Michigan
l-detroit.why: Detroit Arsenal is in Warren, thirteen miles north of Detroit
l-detroit.note: The installation sits in Warren, Michigan, within the Detroit metropolitan area that also holds Kit Green's post-agency academic base at Wayne State.

l-dc.label: Congressional Oversight
l-dc.note: The July 2023 and September 2025 House Oversight UAP hearings, and the NARA records collection created by P.L. 118-31, are all seated in the District of Columbia.

l-dc.label: House Oversight hearing, 26 July 2023 - 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency'
l-dc.why: All three modern UAP hearings were held on Capitol Hill
l-dc.note: 2154 Rayburn on 26 July 2023 and 13 November 2024; HVC-210 on 9 September 2025.

l-nyc.label: New York Times, 'Glowing Auras and Black Money: The Pentagon's Mysterious U.F.O. Program'
l-nyc.why: The decisive act of the modern disclosure era was a New York editorial decision
l-nyc.note: The story added institutional standing rather than new physical evidence; every subsequent official step follows it in sequence. Reasoning: chronological review of post-2017 official actions.

l-la.label: The Black Vault
l-la.why: The Black Vault runs the private FOIA archive from Los Angeles
l-la.note: John Greenewald Jr.'s requests produced the GVSC/TTSA correspondence denial and much of the released AARO record.

l-la.label: Lockheed Martin Corporation
l-la.why: The most-repeated custody allegation names Lockheed and California
l-la.note: Knapp testified that Bigelow negotiated with a senior Lockheed executive for unusual material safeguarded in California; analysis found no unknown elements but a composition suggesting fabrication in zero gravity. The agreement was never completed.

l-las-vegas.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
l-las-vegas.why: BAASS ran the AAWSAP field effort from Las Vegas
l-las-vegas.note: Knapp testified that BAASS recruited about 50 cleared investigators, operated for 27 months and produced over 100 research papers and a 240,000-case data warehouse designed by Jacques Vallee.

l-las-vegas.label: George Knapp
l-las-vegas.why: Knapp broadcast the Lazar interviews from KLAS-TV Las Vegas in 1989
l-las-vegas.note: The May 1989 KLAS-TV interviews created the public reverse-engineering narrative attached to Area 51 and S-4.

l-las-vegas.label: Groom Lake, Nevada
l-las-vegas.why: The Groom and Tonopah workforce commutes from Las Vegas
l-las-vegas.note: The unmarked JANET fleet operates from a dedicated terminal at the Las Vegas airport. Reasoning: publicly observable daily operations; no primary personnel or contract record has been obtained.

l-sri.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995
l-sri.why: The research was conducted at Menlo Park, California
l-sri.note: SRI International, founded 1946 by Stanford trustees and separated from the university in 1970, hosted the work at Menlo Park.

l-stanford.label: The Sol Foundation
l-stanford.why: The Sol Foundation operates from the Stanford orbit
l-stanford.note: Garry Nolan of the Stanford School of Medicine co-founded the Sol Foundation with Peter Skafish; its symposia are the current academic venue for the subject.

l-huntsville.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF)
l-huntsville.why: The Task Force's chief scientist was employed by a Huntsville contractor
l-huntsville.note: Science magazine reported in June 2022 that Travis S. Taylor, a principal research scientist at Huntsville-based Radiance Technologies, was chief scientist of the UAP Task Force.

immaculate-constellation.label: Immaculate Constellation 12-page report entered into the Congressional Record
immaculate-constellation.why: The event is anchored by the document entered on 13 November 2024
immaculate-constellation.note: The twelve-page report is the physical artefact of the disclosure; it has never been located as a retrievable primary file at a stable public URL.

immaculate-constellation.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
immaculate-constellation.why: DoD spokesperson Sue Gough: no record of any SAP by that name
immaculate-constellation.note: 'The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION.' Recorded as a denial artefact: a categorical statement about records, issued by a press office, about a program alleged to be unacknowledged.

immaculate-constellation.label: SASC hearing: Activities of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office
immaculate-constellation.why: Kosloski's statement for the record does not mention Immaculate Constellation
immaculate-constellation.note: The alleged programme had been entered into the congressional record weeks earlier and described in an ODNI unclassified press item of 22 October 2024; AARO's director addressed the Senate six days after the House hearing without naming it.

immaculate-constellation.label: Independent media as the disclosure substrate
immaculate-constellation.why: the case that proves the substrate: leak, newsletter, congressional record, no newsroom
immaculate-constellation.note: An alleged unacknowledged special access program entered the public record in October 2024 through an independent journalist and the Congressional Record on 13 November 2024, via written testimony and the House Oversight hearing transcript. Whatever the underlying report is worth, the path it travelled is the clearest single demonstration of how disclosure is now produced and distributed.

immaculate-constellation.label: Micah Hanks
immaculate-constellation.why: Hanks published the first general-readership account, 17 October 2024
immaculate-constellation.note: The Debrief's 17 October 2024 piece framed the programme as an open question - 'UAP Bombshell or Disinformation?' - and predates the congressional submission by four weeks.

immaculate-constellation.label: Public
immaculate-constellation.why: Published the whistleblower brief naming the program
immaculate-constellation.note: Public, Michael Shellenberger's Substack news outlet, published the story alleging the DoD runs an 'active and highly secretive Unacknowledged Special Access Program' called Immaculate Constellation, based on a whistleblower brief supplied to the House Oversight Committee. NPR's contemporaneous hearing report links directly to the Public story.

immaculate-constellation.label: House Oversight joint hearing, 13 November 2024 - 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth'
immaculate-constellation.why: The disclosure event is constituted by the 13 November 2024 hearing
immaculate-constellation.note: The report was delivered, described under oath and entered into the record at this hearing.

immaculate-constellation.label: Nancy Ruth Mace
immaculate-constellation.why: Mace entered the twelve-page report into the Congressional Record
immaculate-constellation.note: Mace announced from the dais that committee staff had asked her to enter the document; it appears in the hearing's Index of Documents as 'Report, Pentagon, Immaculate Constellation; submitted by Rep. Mace.'

immaculate-constellation.label: Immaculate Constellation 12-page report entered into the Congressional Record
immaculate-constellation.why: The congressional-record instantiation of the alleged parent USAP
immaculate-constellation.note: Shellenberger described the program in the document as 'a central or parent USAP that consolidates observations of UAPs by both tasked and untasked collection platforms.'

immaculate-constellation.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
immaculate-constellation.why: AARO has never publicly addressed the alleged programme entered into the congressional record
immaculate-constellation.note: Neither the FY2024 nor the FY2025 annual report, nor any statement for the record, nor any of the five PURSUE tranches between 8 May and 7 August 2026, addresses a programme name that sits in the Congressional Record. Reasoning: review of the published AARO product set and release indexes.

immaculate-constellation.label: Luis D. Elizondo
immaculate-constellation.why: Elizondo declined to confirm or deny the programme by name or trigraph
immaculate-constellation.note: Asked by Mace whether he had been read in, Elizondo said he would not be authorised to confirm nor deny the existence of any special access program by name or trigraph - which is not a denial.

immaculate-constellation.label: Sean M. Kirkpatrick
immaculate-constellation.why: The former AARO director denied the programme exists
immaculate-constellation.note: Kirkpatrick, AARO's first director, has publicly denied the existence of Immaculate Constellation. He left AARO in December 2023, before the report surfaced.

immaculate-constellation.label: Susan Gough
immaculate-constellation.why: The Department's response is a records assertion, not a denial of existence
immaculate-constellation.note: Pentagon spokesperson Sue Gough has stated the Department has 'no record' of such a programme. The Department has not stated that the programme does not exist.

immaculate-constellation.label: Colorado Springs, Colorado
immaculate-constellation.why: The only provenance story ever attached to the report points at Schriever
immaculate-constellation.note: A self-identified whistleblower said in 2025 he located the material in a folder labelled '2018 Schriever Wargame'; Jason Colavito assessed the claimant had mistaken wargame documents for UFO revelations. Schriever Space Force Base is at Colorado Springs.

immaculate-constellation.label: Michael Shellenberger
immaculate-constellation.why: Brought the alleged USAP into the congressional record
immaculate-constellation.note: On 13 November 2024 Shellenberger testified to a House Oversight subcommittee and submitted a twelve-page report, sourced to an alleged insider, describing an unacknowledged special access program collecting UAP data outside acknowledged reporting channels.

immaculate-constellation.label: NewsNation
immaculate-constellation.why: Carried and explained the Immaculate Constellation report
immaculate-constellation.note: NewsNation ran explainer and news coverage of the alleged unacknowledged special access program named in the whistleblower brief that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress in autumn 2024.

immaculate-constellation.label: Fleet Forces Command 'URGENT SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE' Email (Jan 2015, recalled)
immaculate-constellation.why: Gallaudet's inference points at an unacknowledged SAP; Shellenberger named one
immaculate-constellation.note: Gallaudet concluded the recalled information 'must have been classified within a special access program managed by an intelligence agency'; at the same hearing Shellenberger described an alleged parent USAP consolidating UAP imagery collection.

immaculate-constellation.label: UAP Gerb - National Reconnaissance Office investigation
immaculate-constellation.why: Alleges NRO Sentient AI fed IMINT and SIGINT to Immaculate Constellation
immaculate-constellation.note: The most consequential single claim in the NRO investigation: that the NRO's Sentient program supplied tasked and untasked overhead collection to the USAP Immaculate Constellation, established 2017. This supplies a concrete collection pipeline for the programme Shellenberger entered into the congressional record in November 2024.

immaculate-constellation.label: New York Times, 'Glowing Auras and Black Money: The Pentagon's Mysterious U.F.O. Program'
immaculate-constellation.why: The alleged programme is said to have been created in response to this story
immaculate-constellation.note: Shellenberger's whistleblower alleges DoD created Immaculate Constellation in 2017 after the New York Times published on AATIP. The claim is attributed, not documented.

stargate-program.label: SRI International, Menlo Park, California
stargate-program.why: The research was conducted at Menlo Park, California
stargate-program.note: SRI International, founded 1946 by Stanford trustees and separated from the university in 1970, hosted the work at Menlo Park.

stargate-program.label: Defense Intelligence Agency
stargate-program.why: DIA held the programme from 1985 as SUN STREAK and STAR GATE
stargate-program.note: The effort moved to DIA's Scientific and Technical Intelligence Directorate as SUN STREAK in late 1985 and was consolidated as STAR GATE in 1991.

stargate-program.label: James R. Clapper Jr.
stargate-program.why: Clapper led the programme in the 1990s before becoming DNI
stargate-program.note: Clapper is recorded as a project leader in the 1990s; he later served as Director of National Intelligence.

stargate-program.label: Harold E. Puthoff
stargate-program.why: Ran the SRI International half of the government's psychoenergetics effort
stargate-program.note: The same principal investigator ran the SRI remote viewing science, produced Defense Intelligence Reference Documents under AAWSAP, and co-founded To The Stars Academy, which signed the CRADA with the Army in 2019. Reasoning: continuity of a single documented career, not of a single programme.

stargate-program.label: SUN STREAK
stargate-program.note: CIA compiled and released roughly 12,000 pages of the programme record in 1995 after the American Institutes for Research evaluation.

stargate-program.label: Harold E. Puthoff
stargate-program.why: Puthoff was principal investigator and project director
stargate-program.note: Puthoff co-founded the SRI programme with Targ and directed the research phase before leaving in the mid-1980s.

stargate-program.label: Russell Targ
stargate-program.why: Targ co-founded the SRI remote viewing research
stargate-program.note: Targ collaborated with Puthoff on the early SRI work and on the tests with Geller, Swann and Price.

stargate-program.label: SRI International (Stanford Research Institute)
stargate-program.why: SRI held the science half of the remote viewing effort from 1972
stargate-program.note: Puthoff and Targ began CIA-sponsored work at SRI's Artificial Intelligence Center in 1972 and continued with intelligence community funding until they left in the mid-1980s.

stargate-program.label: Christopher C. 'Kit' Green
stargate-program.why: Green ran the CIA analytic side of the anomalous-phenomena portfolio
stargate-program.note: Green's CIA Life Sciences work on anomalous phenomena is the analytic counterpart to the SRI research, and his later Wayne State position carried the biomedical line into NIDS/BAASS and the modern Stanford circle. Reasoning: continuity of documented affiliations, not of a single programme.

stargate-program.label: Groom Lake, Nevada
stargate-program.why: Both are demonstrations of decades-long concealment ending in bulk declassification
stargate-program.note: Groom Lake ran 58 years to specific acknowledgement via FOIA; STAR GATE ran 25 years to bulk CREST publication in 2017. Reasoning: structural comparison of two documented concealment lifecycles.

hearing-2026-06-30.label: Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets
hearing-2026-06-30.why: The Task Force's 2026 hearing addressed MKULTRA, not UAP
hearing-2026-06-30.note: Witnesses were Stephen Kinzer, Tom O'Neill and minority witness Dr. Elizabeth Ginexi. No UAP witness appeared.

hearing-2026-06-30.label: House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets hearing, 9 September 2025 - 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection'
hearing-2026-06-30.why: No UAP hearing was held in the eleven months between them
hearing-2026-06-30.note: The period covers the February 2026 release directive, five PURSUE tranches, the late FY2025 annual report, the NDA waiver and the Burlison amendment - all executive or floor action without contemporaneous testimony. Reasoning: House Oversight published hearing index.

stringfield-status-reports.label: Leonard H. Stringfield
stringfield-status-reports.why: Authored the seven-part Status Report series
stringfield-status-reports.note: Stringfield wrote and self-published or placed all seven Status Reports between July 1978 and February 1994. Title and copyright pages of the original printings attest authorship, dates and, for Report VI, the Cincinnati imprint.

stringfield-status-reports.label: Aztec, New Mexico claim, March 1948
stringfield-status-reports.why: Stringfield revived Aztec as a real retrieval in the late 1970s
stringfield-status-reports.note: After two decades in which ufologists treated Aztec as dead, Stringfield argued the incident was real and that the craft was one of many held by the US military; Status Report V lists Aztec alongside Roswell, Kingman, El Yunque and Brown County.

stringfield-status-reports.label: Del Rio / Mexican border claim, 1948 or 1950
stringfield-status-reports.why: Status Report chronology indexes Del Rio as Item B-7
stringfield-status-reports.note: The consolidated chronology in Status Report III lists Item B-7 of Status Report II as '1948 or 1950: Mexico, near Del Rio, Texas. Air Force officer observed crashed craft and one body.'

stringfield-status-reports.label: Kingman, Arizona claim, 1953
stringfield-status-reports.why: Status Report III printed the 1980 'Fritz Werner' Q&A on Kingman
stringfield-status-reports.note: Stringfield wrote to Raymond Fowler on 11 August 1980 for access to Fowler's pseudonymous source; the answers are dated 2 September 1980 and are printed verbatim in Status Report III.

stringfield-status-reports.label: Clear Intent: The Government Coverup of the UFO Experience (1984)
stringfield-status-reports.note: The two bodies of work are contemporaneous and methodologically opposite: 'Clear Intent' sources every claim to a released government document, the Status Reports to protected anonymous informants. Reasoning: the difference in grade this board assigns them is entirely a difference in sourcing, not in subject matter.

stringfield-status-reports.label: Majic Eyes Only: Earth's Encounters with Extraterrestrial Technology (2005)
stringfield-status-reports.why: The catalogue inherits Stringfield's case base
stringfield-status-reports.note: A substantial share of 'Majic Eyes Only' entries trace back through Stringfield's anonymised Status Report cases, so the catalogue inherits their provenance limits. Reasoning: an index cannot be graded above its sources.

roswell-report-1995.label: Capt. James McAndrew
roswell-report-1995.why: Wrote Attachment 32, the Project Mogul synopsis
roswell-report-1995.note: The DTIC abstract identifies Attachment 32 as McAndrew's synopsis describing Project Mogul as the explanation for the Roswell Incident.

roswell-report-1995.label: Col. Richard L. Weaver
roswell-report-1995.why: Authored the Air Force's report to the Secretary and GAO
roswell-report-1995.note: Written by Col. Weaver, Director of Security and Special Program Oversight, Office of the Secretary of the Air Force, with 1st Lt. James McAndrew.

roswell-report-1995.label: The Roswell Report: Case Closed (1997)
roswell-report-1995.why: The 1997 report completes what the 1994-1995 report left open
roswell-report-1995.note: The 1994 report addressed the debris and did not address the bodies claims; the 1997 report was produced to close that gap.

roswell-report-case-closed.label: W. Glenn Dennis
roswell-report-case-closed.why: The 1997 report dismantled the 'missing nurse' account by name
roswell-report-case-closed.note: Section 2.1 uses 427th AAFBU Squadron 'M' morning reports and National Personnel Records Center searches to show 'Naomi Maria Selff' never served, and identifies 1st Lt. Eileen M. Fanton as matching every other particular.

roswell-report-case-closed.label: James Ragsdale
roswell-report-case-closed.why: Ragsdale's own words were used to support the dummy explanation
roswell-report-case-closed.note: The report quotes Ragsdale saying of the objects, 'They were using dummies in those damned things', and prints his interview transcript at Appendix C p. 215.

roswell-report-case-closed.label: Plains of San Agustin claim, July 1947
roswell-report-case-closed.why: Air Force proposes San Agustin Pass confusion and dummy recoveries
roswell-report-case-closed.note: Section 1.4 argues that Maltais and Knight may have confused the Plains with San Agustin Pass or Peak, adjacent to White Sands and the Jornada Test Range, where numerous dummy flights terminated.

roswell-report-case-closed.label: Capt. James McAndrew
roswell-report-case-closed.why: Sole author of the 1997 bodies report
roswell-report-case-closed.note: Published by Headquarters USAF through the GPO; McAndrew, born 1963, is the named author on the catalogue record.

roswell-report-case-closed.label: The Roswell Report: Fact Versus Fiction in the New Mexico Desert (1995)
roswell-report-case-closed.why: The 1997 report completes what the 1994-1995 report left open
roswell-report-case-closed.note: The 1994 report addressed the debris and did not address the bodies claims; the 1997 report was produced to close that gap.

roswell-report-case-closed.label: Varginha incident, Minas Gerais, January 1996
roswell-report-case-closed.why: Two official inquiries that explained the recovery activity without producing the logs
roswell-report-case-closed.note: The Brazilian Army's 2010 inquiry explained the Varginha vehicle movements as routine maintenance and school transport; the USAF's 1997 report explained the New Mexico recovery teams as dummy-recovery operations. Both are plausible and neither published the underlying unit movement records. Reasoning: an explanation of activity is not the same artifact as the activity log. [Re-pointed from a collapsed duplicate, 14 Aug 2026.]

kean-v-nasa.label: Project MOON DUST
kean-v-nasa.why: Project Moon Dust records were an express object of the FOIA request
kean-v-nasa.note: Moon Dust - the programme for recovery of foreign space and aerospace debris - is named in the request as reproduced in the court's Background section.

kean-v-nasa.label: Cash v. United States, Civil Action No. H-84-348 (S.D. Tex.)
kean-v-nasa.why: The domain's only two federal dockets, twenty years apart
kean-v-nasa.note: Cash (1984-1986) sought damages and was dismissed on the pleadings and summary judgment; Kean (2003-2009) sought records and obtained a finding of inadequate search plus a supervised re-search. The record case succeeded where the injury case did not.

kean-v-nasa.label: Kecksburg incident, 9 December 1965
kean-v-nasa.why: The litigation was about the Kecksburg records specifically
kean-v-nasa.note: The underlying FOIA request of 31 January 2003 sought records on Kecksburg, the 9 December 1965 incident, the Fragology Files 1962-1967, Richard M. Schulherr, Project Moon Dust and Cosmos 96.

kean-v-nasa.label: Leslie Kean
kean-v-nasa.why: Plaintiff who forced a court-supervised NASA records search
kean-v-nasa.note: Kean filed the complaint on 9 December 2003, obtained a 27 March 2007 finding that NASA had not shown its searches adequate, settled in part on 16 October 2007 and litigated status reports until dismissal on 24 August 2009.

cash-v-united-states.label: Betty Cash
cash-v-united-states.why: The United States denied ownership of the object and the aircraft
cash-v-united-states.note: The government moved to dismiss and for summary judgment; the court dismissed under FRCP 12(b)(1), 12(b)(6) and 56. The Defense Department's internal investigation into whether the object was a US military device has never produced a released document.

cash-v-united-states.label: Betty Cash
cash-v-united-states.note: Betty Cash, Vickie Landrum and Colby Landrum v. United States of America, No. H-84-348, S.D. Tex., Houston Division, dismissed 21 August 1986 by Judge Ross N. Sterling.

cash-v-united-states.label: Kean v. NASA, No. 1:03-cv-02509 (D.D.C.)
cash-v-united-states.why: The domain's only two federal dockets, twenty years apart
cash-v-united-states.note: Cash (1984-1986) sought damages and was dismissed on the pleadings and summary judgment; Kean (2003-2009) sought records and obtained a finding of inadequate search plus a supervised re-search. The record case succeeded where the injury case did not.

kecksburg-1965.label: Kecksburg, Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania
kecksburg-1965.note: The claimed recovery occurred in woodland at Kecksburg, Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, on the evening of 9 December 1965.

kecksburg-1965.label: Kean v. NASA, No. 1:03-cv-02509 (D.D.C.)
kecksburg-1965.why: The litigation was about the Kecksburg records specifically
kecksburg-1965.note: The underlying FOIA request of 31 January 2003 sought records on Kecksburg, the 9 December 1965 incident, the Fragology Files 1962-1967, Richard M. Schulherr, Project Moon Dust and Cosmos 96.

kecksburg-1965.label: Shag Harbour incident, 4 October 1967
kecksburg-1965.why: Two documented official responses to undocumented objects, twenty-two months apart
kecksburg-1965.note: At Kecksburg the cordon is in the contemporaneous press and the object is in no record; at Shag Harbour the RCAF Air Desk telex, the Navy tasking and the Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic search are all in Department of National Defence files and the object is in none.

kecksburg-1965.label: Stan Gordon
kecksburg-1965.why: Principal field investigator of the Kecksburg witness pool
kecksburg-1965.note: Gordon collected local first-hand accounts over four decades, supplying the witnesses used by Unsolved Mysteries (1990) and the Sci Fi Channel documentary (2003).

shag-harbour-1967.label: Kecksburg incident, 9 December 1965
shag-harbour-1967.why: Two documented official responses to undocumented objects, twenty-two months apart
shag-harbour-1967.note: At Kecksburg the cordon is in the contemporaneous press and the object is in no record; at Shag Harbour the RCAF Air Desk telex, the Navy tasking and the Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic search are all in Department of National Defence files and the object is in none.

aztec-1948.label: Aztec, New Mexico
aztec-1948.note: Scully's account placed the landing in Hart Canyon, roughly twelve miles northeast of the city of Aztec, San Juan County, New Mexico. The location is the only fixed and checkable element of the story, and it is the one the town later built a symposium and a commemorative plaque around.

aztec-1948.label: Behind the Flying Saucers (Scully, 1950)
aztec-1948.why: The book is the sole origin of the Aztec claim
aztec-1948.note: No account of an Aztec crash predates Scully's 1949 Variety columns and the 1950 book; both derive from Silas Newton and Leo Gebauer, convicted of fraud in 1953.

aztec-1948.label: Roswell Incident
aztec-1948.why: detail donor to later Roswell accounts
aztec-1948.note: After the story was revived in the 1970s, its specifics - small bodies, an intact hull, rapid military sanitisation of the site, storage at Wright-Patterson - migrated into allegedly first-hand Roswell testimony. A documented fraud became a supplier of narrative detail to the case the modern disclosure argument rests on, which is a contamination risk this board has to carry explicitly.

aztec-1948.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
aztec-1948.why: Air Force denials of Hangar 18 bodies
aztec-1948.note: Robert Spencer Carr's 1974 public claim that bodies recovered near Aztec were held at 'Hangar 18' at Wright-Patterson AFB drew official Air Force denials. The FBI separately disowned the Guy Hottel memo, the one federal document ever cited as corroboration, in a published 2013 statement.

aztec-1948.label: UFO Crash/Retrieval Status Reports I-VII (Stringfield, 1978-1994)
aztec-1948.why: Stringfield revived Aztec as a real retrieval in the late 1970s
aztec-1948.note: After two decades in which ufologists treated Aztec as dead, Stringfield argued the incident was real and that the craft was one of many held by the US military; Status Report V lists Aztec alongside Roswell, Kingman, El Yunque and Brown County.

aztec-1948.label: Guy Hottel memorandum, 22 March 1950
aztec-1948.why: The Hottel memo predates and partly parallels the Aztec narrative
aztec-1948.note: Hottel's memo of 22 March 1950 describes three fifty-foot discs with three-foot occupants two months before Scully's book described one ninety-nine-foot disc with sixteen. The narratives are related but not identical, so the memo is better read as evidence that the recovery rumour was already in official circulation than as independent confirmation of Aztec.

plains-san-agustin-1947.label: The Roswell Report: Case Closed (1997)
plains-san-agustin-1947.why: Air Force proposes San Agustin Pass confusion and dummy recoveries
plains-san-agustin-1947.note: Section 1.4 argues that Maltais and Knight may have confused the Plains with San Agustin Pass or Peak, adjacent to White Sands and the Jornada Test Range, where numerous dummy flights terminated.

plains-san-agustin-1947.label: Gerald Anderson
plains-san-agustin-1947.why: Sole claimed first-hand witness to the San Agustin site
plains-san-agustin-1947.note: Anderson came forward in 1990; the Air Force's 1997 report identifies him as the one first-hand testimony among the three supporting the claim.

plains-san-agustin-1947.label: Grady L. 'Barney' Barnett
plains-san-agustin-1947.note: Every account of Barnett's experience is second-hand, relayed by Vern Maltais and Alice Knight after his death in 1969. Reasoning: no first-hand statement in any medium exists.

kingman-1953.label: UFO Crash/Retrieval Status Reports I-VII (Stringfield, 1978-1994)
kingman-1953.why: Status Report III printed the 1980 'Fritz Werner' Q&A on Kingman
kingman-1953.note: Stringfield wrote to Raymond Fowler on 11 August 1980 for access to Fowler's pseudonymous source; the answers are dated 2 September 1980 and are printed verbatim in Status Report III.

del-rio-1950.label: UFO Crash/Retrieval Status Reports I-VII (Stringfield, 1978-1994)
del-rio-1950.why: Status Report chronology indexes Del Rio as Item B-7
del-rio-1950.note: The consolidated chronology in Status Report III lists Item B-7 of Status Report II as '1948 or 1950: Mexico, near Del Rio, Texas. Air Force officer observed crashed craft and one body.'

malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.label: Robert L. Hastings
malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.why: Hastings holds and publishes the 17 March 1967 teletype
malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.note: The document is published in facsimile in the UFOs & Nukes archive under the Echo Flight heading, and is the tier-1 anchor for the occurrence of the shutdown.

malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.label: Minot AFB incursions, 1966
malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.why: Minot 1966 precedes the Malmstrom shutdowns by seven months
malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.note: Different wing, different state, same category of report. The sequence F. E. Warren 1965, Minot 1966, Malmstrom 1967 establishes recurrence rather than a single-site anomaly.

malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.label: Minot AFB B-52 incident, 24 October 1968
malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.why: Minot 1968 extends the pattern with instrumented detection
malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.note: Where Malmstrom 1967 is a documented shutdown with contested causation, Minot 1968 adds ground radar, airborne radar, weather radar, visual observation, a four-minute radio failure and physical security alarms at Minuteman silos.

malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.label: 1975 SAC Nuclear-Base Overflights (Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot)
malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.why: The 1975 wave returned to Malmstrom on documented record
malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.note: The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's log and the NMCC memorandum of 8 November 1975 place radar-tracked objects over Malmstrom missile sites eight years after the Echo Flight shutdown, this time with F-106 scrambles logged.

malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.label: Capt. Robert L. Salas
malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.why: Principal named witness to the March 1967 shutdown
malmstrom-echo-flight-1967.note: Salas first went on the record in 1996 with the Great Falls Tribune, describing a security police report of a glowing red object over the front gate immediately before his flight's missiles went off alert.

minot-1966.label: Robert L. Hastings
minot-1966.why: Publishes the 25 August 1966 Minot documents in facsimile
minot-1966.note: Three Air Force documents dated 25 August 1966 and Minot Daily News coverage of 6 December 1966 are reproduced in the archive.

minot-1966.label: Malmstrom AFB missile shutdowns, March 1967
minot-1966.why: Minot 1966 precedes the Malmstrom shutdowns by seven months
minot-1966.note: Different wing, different state, same category of report. The sequence F. E. Warren 1965, Minot 1966, Malmstrom 1967 establishes recurrence rather than a single-site anomaly.

minot-1968.label: Project Blue Book
minot-1968.why: Blue Book declined to field-investigate an instrumented nuclear-site case
minot-1968.note: The RADCAT directory records that Project Blue Book personnel did not send field investigators and the incident was written off despite interest from SAC generals including 15th Air Force's Maj. Gen. Nichols.

minot-1968.label: Malmstrom AFB missile shutdowns, March 1967
minot-1968.why: Minot 1968 extends the pattern with instrumented detection
minot-1968.note: Where Malmstrom 1967 is a documented shutdown with contested causation, Minot 1968 adds ground radar, airborne radar, weather radar, visual observation, a four-minute radio failure and physical security alarms at Minuteman silos.

npc-2010-ufos-nukes.label: Robert L. Hastings
npc-2010-ufos-nukes.why: Convened and hosted the National Press Club event
npc-2010-ufos-nukes.note: Hastings hosted the UFO-Nukes Connection press conference with seven USAF veterans; CNN streamed it live and quoted him from the podium.

npc-2010-ufos-nukes.label: Capt. Robert L. Salas
npc-2010-ufos-nukes.why: Spoke on the record and has a signed affidavit on file
npc-2010-ufos-nukes.note: Salas is among the named affiants in the UFOs & Nukes archive and spoke at the 2010 event.

majic-eyes-only.label: Ryan S. Wood
majic-eyes-only.note: Ryan S. Wood authored 'Majic Eyes Only' (2005), converting the narrative retrieval literature into an indexed catalogue with credibility weightings.

majic-eyes-only.label: UFO Crash/Retrieval Status Reports I-VII (Stringfield, 1978-1994)
majic-eyes-only.why: The catalogue inherits Stringfield's case base
majic-eyes-only.note: A substantial share of 'Majic Eyes Only' entries trace back through Stringfield's anonymised Status Report cases, so the catalogue inherits their provenance limits. Reasoning: an index cannot be graded above its sources.

ufos-national-security-state.label: Richard M. Dolan
ufos-national-security-state.note: Dolan wrote 'Chronology of a Cover-Up, 1941-1973' (2002) and 'The Cover-Up Exposed, 1973-1991' (2009).

behind-the-flying-saucers.label: Aztec, New Mexico claim, March 1948
behind-the-flying-saucers.why: The book is the sole origin of the Aztec claim
behind-the-flying-saucers.note: No account of an Aztec crash predates Scully's 1949 Variety columns and the 1950 book; both derive from Silas Newton and Leo Gebauer, convicted of fraud in 1953.

behind-the-flying-saucers.label: Frank Scully
behind-the-flying-saucers.note: Published by Henry Holt and Company, New York, 1950, out of two 1949 Variety columns.

the-roswell-incident-1980.label: William L. Moore
the-roswell-incident-1980.note: Charles Berlitz and William L. Moore, Grosset & Dunlap, 1980, ISBN 978-0448211992.

the-roswell-incident-1980.label: Maj. Jesse A. Marcel Sr.
the-roswell-incident-1980.why: Marcel's account is the spine of the 1980 book
the-roswell-incident-1980.note: Berlitz and Moore built 'The Roswell Incident' on Friedman's Marcel material together with the second-hand Barney Barnett account.

clear-intent-1984.label: 1975 SAC Nuclear-Base Overflights (Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot)
clear-intent-1984.why: Fawcett and Greenwood reconstructed the 1975 wave from FOIA documents
clear-intent-1984.note: CAUS filed on 26 December 1977; the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense identified twenty-four Joint Chiefs documents on 6 February 1978; Assistant Secretary Thomas Ross ordered the withheld fifteen released. The book reproduces and annotates them.

clear-intent-1984.label: Robert L. Hastings
clear-intent-1984.why: Hastings extended the Fawcett-Greenwood documentary method with named witnesses
clear-intent-1984.note: Hastings pairs the FOIA paper that 'Clear Intent' established with signed affidavits from named officers, which is the step the 1984 book could not take. Reasoning: comparison of the two evidence bases.

clear-intent-1984.label: UFO Crash/Retrieval Status Reports I-VII (Stringfield, 1978-1994)
clear-intent-1984.note: The two bodies of work are contemporaneous and methodologically opposite: 'Clear Intent' sources every claim to a released government document, the Status Reports to protected anonymous informants. Reasoning: the difference in grade this board assigns them is entirely a difference in sourcing, not in subject matter.

majestic-documents-archive.label: William L. Moore
majestic-documents-archive.why: The archive's core corpus entered the record through Moore's mailbox
majestic-documents-archive.note: The Eisenhower Briefing Document and Truman-Forrestal memorandum arrived as undeveloped 35mm film addressed to Moore and Shandera in December 1984; everything downstream in the corpus dates from that delivery.

majestic-documents-archive.label: Dr. Robert M. Wood
majestic-documents-archive.why: Co-principal of the document archive and its rating scheme
majestic-documents-archive.note: The site carries a 1999-2026 copyright in the name 'Majestic Documents Wood & Wood' and identifies Dr. Robert M. Wood and Ryan S. Wood as its principals.

majestic-documents-archive.label: Ryan S. Wood
majestic-documents-archive.note: Same copyright notice and About page attribution.

fund-for-ufo-research.label: Leonard H. Stringfield
fund-for-ufo-research.why: FUFOR funded Stringfield's later Status Reports
fund-for-ufo-research.note: Stringfield names the Fund for UFO Research first in the Status Report VII acknowledgements, thanking it for past funding.

fund-for-ufo-research.label: Gerald Anderson
fund-for-ufo-research.why: FUFOR co-authored the report against its own first-hand witness
fund-for-ufo-research.note: Fred Whiting for FUFOR with Mark Rodeghier for CUFOS. Cited at note 123 of the 1997 Air Force report.

cufos.label: Leonard H. Stringfield
cufos.why: CUFOS cooperated with and advised the Status Report series
cufos.note: Stringfield acknowledges CUFOS cooperation in Status Report VII and records consulting its scientific director on 6 November 1993 about the Roswell body count.

cufos.label: Gerald Anderson
cufos.why: CUFOS and FUFOR investigated and discredited their own witness
cufos.note: Mark Rodeghier of CUFOS and Fred Whiting of the Fund for UFO Research published 'The Plains of San Agustin Controversy' concluding against Anderson's reliability.

mufon.label: Leonard H. Stringfield
mufon.why: MUFON symposium platform and publisher for Reports I and II
mufon.note: Report I was delivered at the ninth annual MUFON Symposium in Dayton on 29 July 1978; Report II was published by MUFON in January 1980. Stringfield served as MUFON's director of public relations.

mufon.label: John F. Schuessler
mufon.why: MUFON International Director 2000-2006 and case investigator
mufon.note: Schuessler investigated Cash-Landrum for MUFON from 1981 and served as its International Director from 2000 to 2006.

mufon.label: William L. Moore
mufon.why: Made the AFOSI disinformation admission from the MUFON platform
mufon.note: Moore chose the 1989 MUFON symposium in Las Vegas to state that he had cooperated with Air Force Office of Special Investigations personnel and passed disinformation to Paul Bennewitz.

hottel-memo.label: Aztec, New Mexico claim, March 1948
hottel-memo.why: The Hottel memo predates and partly parallels the Aztec narrative
hottel-memo.note: Hottel's memo of 22 March 1950 describes three fifty-foot discs with three-foot occupants two months before Scully's book described one ninety-nine-foot disc with sixteen. The narratives are related but not identical, so the memo is better read as evidence that the recovery rumour was already in official circulation than as independent confirmation of Aztec.

l-kecksburg.label: Kecksburg incident, 9 December 1965
l-kecksburg.note: The claimed recovery occurred in woodland at Kecksburg, Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, on the evening of 9 December 1965.

l-kecksburg.label: Stan Gordon
l-kecksburg.why: Four decades of field investigation at the site
l-kecksburg.note: Gordon, a Greensburg-area researcher, assembled the local witness pool at Kecksburg that supplied the 1990 and 2003 broadcasts and the factual premise of the Kean litigation.

d-psyop.label: Counterintelligence
d-psyop.note: AFOSI is chartered for both counterintelligence and criminal investigation, and is the organisation named in the Bennewitz deception; the two domains share personnel.

d-psyop.label: The Cover-Up
d-psyop.why: Debunking recommended as a security measure
d-psyop.note: The Robertson Panel's January 1953 recommendation for a mass-media debunking programme is the documented point where concealment becomes an influence operation.

d-psyop.label: Disinformation & Fabricated Documents
d-psyop.why: Fabricated material as the delivery vehicle
d-psyop.note: The Bennewitz episode, in which AFOSI personnel supplied fabricated documents, is the documented case linking perception management to forged records; Doty's own personnel file is public.

d-disinformation.label: Majestic-12 Corpus
d-disinformation.note: The FBI's Majestic 12 file records the investigation into the corpus's authenticity, making MJ-12 the principal case study for the disinformation domain.

d-disinformation.label: Psychological Operations & Perception Management
d-disinformation.why: Fabricated material as the delivery vehicle
d-disinformation.note: The Bennewitz episode, in which AFOSI personnel supplied fabricated documents, is the documented case linking perception management to forged records; Doty's own personnel file is public.

d-records.label: The Cover-Up
d-records.note: GAO found Roswell AAF outgoing messages for 1946-1949 destroyed with no disposition authority and no destruction certificate - concealment executed through the records system.

d-records.label: Freedom of Information Practice
d-records.note: Before the FY2024 records provisions, FOIA was the only routine extraction mechanism; the NARA collection is an attempt to replace adversarial requesting with an affirmative duty.

d-records.label: Congressional Oversight
d-records.why: Records law as the oversight instrument that worked
d-records.note: Subtitle C of P.L. 118-31 is the only binding UAP transparency outcome Congress has produced, and it operates through records custody rather than through programme access.

d-records.label: Historiography
d-records.why: The corpus is what survives the records fight
d-records.note: Almost every primary document in this field arrived through FOIA or archival release; historiography here is downstream of records law.

d-foia.label: Signals & Sensor Intelligence
d-foia.note: NSA's statutory withholding, sustained in CAUS v. NSA on the classified Yeates affidavit, is the hardest documented barrier between sensor data and the public record.

d-foia.label: Litigation
d-foia.note: CAUS v. NSA is the canonical progression from FOIA request to appellate litigation, and the point at which the courts sustained withholding on a classified affidavit.

d-foia.label: Records & Archives
d-foia.note: Before the FY2024 records provisions, FOIA was the only routine extraction mechanism; the NARA collection is an attempt to replace adversarial requesting with an affirmative duty.

d-foia.label: Prime Contractor Custody
d-foia.why: Contractor records are outside the statute
d-foia.note: FOIA reaches agency records; material moved into contractor custody leaves the statute's reach without any change in classification. Reasoning stated in the d-foia dossier.

d-litigation.label: Freedom of Information Practice
d-litigation.note: CAUS v. NSA is the canonical progression from FOIA request to appellate litigation, and the point at which the courts sustained withholding on a classified affidavit.

d-litigation.label: Legal Doctrine & Liability
d-litigation.why: Courtroom outcomes set the witness's risk calculus
d-litigation.note: The dismissal in Cash v. United States and the withholding sustained in CAUS v. NSA together define the practical ceiling on judicial remedies in this field.

d-legislative.label: Congressional UAP Caucus
d-legislative.why: the member bloc that forces briefings and carries amendments outside committee jurisdiction
d-legislative.note: Launched by Rep. Tim Burchett on 22 August 2023 alongside a caucus letter to the Intelligence Community Inspector General, with documented members including Burchett, Luna, Burlison, Moskowitz and Ogles. Its confirmed operational achievement is the 12 January 2024 closed briefing; Ogles is a member without an Oversight seat, which is how the caucus extends reach beyond the committee.

d-legislative.label: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
d-legislative.why: the venue where the record is made under oath, and the only House committee with unilateral subpoena power in the chair's hands
d-legislative.note: Oversight held the 26 July 2023 hearing, the 13 November 2024 hearing and, through its declassification task force, the 9 September 2025 hearing. Sworn testimony taken in this committee is the mechanism by which allegations enter the legislative process at all, which is a different function from enacting text.

d-legislative.label: Senate Armed Services Committee
d-legislative.why: owns the only vehicle the disclosure text has ever ridden, and has never reported it
d-legislative.note: Every version of the Act - 2023, 2024 and the announced later attempts - has reached the floor as an amendment to a SASC bill rather than as a committee product, which means no committee report, no markup record and no members professionally invested in defending it in conference. A committee's non-action is a process fact and belongs in this domain.

d-legislative.label: United States House of Representatives
d-legislative.why: the chamber where the text was stripped in 2023 and where a successor passed in 2026
d-legislative.note: The House is where UAP oversight became public through the July 2023 Oversight hearing, where House leadership's role in the conference removal of the disclosure title became a contested question, and where the Burlison amendment was adopted on 22 July 2026. Both the defeat and the advance ran through the same chamber.

d-legislative.label: Enacted Statute
d-legislative.note: Division I of the Senate-passed H.R. 2670 contained a Review Board and eminent domain; P.L. 118-31 as enacted did not. The gap between these two documents is the domain boundary.

d-legislative.label: S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226 (Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act amendment)
d-legislative.why: the filing instrument - where the process starts and where its text is fixed
d-legislative.note: Submitted 13 July 2023 by Senator Schumer for himself and Senators Rounds, Rubio, Gillibrand, Young and Heinrich, ordered to lie on the table, text printed in the Congressional Record at pages S2953-S2959. The amendment, not the bill, is the object that carries the disclosure text, which is the process fact this domain exists to record.

d-legislative.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226; Division G of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA)
d-legislative.why: passed one chamber, stripped in conference - the domain's instructive defeat
d-legislative.note: The only text ever passed by a chamber of Congress legislating on the assumption that recovered non-human technology exists and is held in part by private entities. It rode to the Senate floor as an amendment, cleared the Senate as a division of S. 2226, and did not survive conference into P.L. 118-31 in that form. The mechanism of the defeat is the lesson, which is why it belongs to process rather than to statute.

d-legislative.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA
d-legislative.why: the successor framework, and the first time such a text has cleared the House floor
d-legislative.note: Adopted by the House on 22 July 2026 as an amendment to the FY2027 NDAA, after a similar proposal failed to advance in the previous defence-bill cycle. As of this pass it is an adopted House amendment, not law, which is precisely the status distinction this domain is for.

d-legislative.label: IAA FY2024 Sec. 1102 — contractor turn-in of 'non-earth origin or exotic' UAP material
d-legislative.why: a committee-reported provision that did not survive conference in the form reported
d-legislative.note: The Senate Select Committee on Intelligence's UAP provision in the reported IAA FY2024 would have compelled contractor turn-in of UAP material within 180 days. The enacted counterpart in Division G of P.L. 118-31 differed substantially from the text approved by Senate committees and by the full Senate. Its home is the process domain because what is interesting about it is the gap between what was reported and what was enacted.

d-legislation.label: Legislative Process (proposed and pending)
d-legislation.note: Division I of the Senate-passed H.R. 2670 contained a Review Board and eminent domain; P.L. 118-31 as enacted did not. The gap between these two documents is the domain boundary.

d-legislation.label: Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2023 (Div. F of PL 117-263) - secs. 6802-6803
d-legislation.why: Division F of P.L. 117-263 - the intelligence-side half of the same enactment
d-legislation.note: Sec. 6802 rewrote 50 U.S.C. 3373 to create AARO and inserted the 'unidentified anomalous phenomena' and 'transmedium' definitions; sec. 6803 attached a Comptroller General audit and briefing requirement to the Historical Record Report. Wiring it here fixes a degree-1 orphan and records that the statutory definitions the whole board uses were enacted in an intelligence authorization, not a defence one.

d-legislation.label: Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2024 (Div. G of PL 118-31) - secs. 7341, 7343
d-legislation.why: Division G of P.L. 118-31 - enacted intelligence-side UAP provisions
d-legislation.note: Division G carries Sec. 7341, modifying the AARO reporting requirement, and Sec. 7343, the funding limitation. The section list published by the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence confirms both as part of the enacted division. Its separate membership of the funding domain rests on 7343's substance, not on its status as law.

d-legislation.label: FY2022 NDAA Sec. 1683 (P.L. 117-81; 50 U.S.C. 3373)
d-legislation.why: the statutory root of the modern apparatus, codified at 50 U.S.C. 3373
d-legislation.note: Sec. 1683 of P.L. 117-81, signed 27 December 2021, directed establishment within 180 days of an office to carry out the duties of the UAP Task Force, with enumerated duties reaching beyond analysis into governance. Everything later in the enacted corpus amends or builds on what this section created.

d-legislation.label: Sec. 6802, James M. Inhofe NDAA for FY2023 (Pub. L. 117-263) - AARO establishment, Historical Record Report and annual reports
d-legislation.why: rewrote 50 U.S.C. 3373 to establish AARO and to mandate the Historical Record Report
d-legislation.note: Sec. 6802 of P.L. 117-263, enacted 23 December 2022, added subsection (j) requiring a Historical Record Report within 540 days and subsection (k) requiring joint DNI/SECDEF annual reports. This is the authority AARO itself cites for both report series, which makes it enacted law with directly observable output.

d-legislation.label: FY2024 NDAA, Public Law 118-31 - Div. A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C (secs. 1841-1843), UAP Records Collection; Div. G (IAA FY2024) secs. 7341, 7343
d-legislation.why: P.L. 118-31 Subtitle C, secs. 1841-1843 - the UAP Records Collection as enacted
d-legislation.note: What survived conference from the Senate-passed disclosure title was a records collection at NARA, a duty to transmit and a postponement regime, without the Review Board or the eminent domain provision. NARA's published guidance to federal agencies implementing the collection is the observable proof that this part is law and operating.

d-legislation.label: FY2025 NDAA, Public Law 118-159 - Div. G (IAA FY2025) secs. 6801-6802, GAO review of AARO
d-legislation.why: P.L. 118-159 Div. G, secs. 6801-6802 - GAO review of AARO and the sunset of the audit cadence
d-legislation.note: Approved 23 December 2024. Sec. 6801 directs a GAO review of AARO's implementation of 50 U.S.C. 3373; sec. 6802 sunsets the GAO audit requirements attached to the Historical Record Report. Wiring it here fixes a degree-1 orphan and records the first enacted step in winding oversight machinery back down rather than up.

d-legislation.label: FY2026 NDAA, Public Law 119-60 - secs. 1671-1673, NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept briefings and UAP classification-guide accounting
d-legislation.why: P.L. 119-60, Title XVI Subtitle E - the enacted corpus reduced to housekeeping
d-legislation.note: Approved 18 December 2025, with three UAP sections requiring that AARO briefings cover NORAD and NORTHCOM intercepts and accounting for UAP classification guides. Recording it in the enacted domain alongside the 2021-2023 provisions is what lets a reader see the trajectory of what Congress has actually been willing to enact.

d-legislation.label: 10 U.S.C. 119 — Special Access Programs: Congressional Oversight
d-legislation.why: codified permanent law - the only statute governing what Congress is told about special access programs
d-legislation.note: Added by sec. 1132(a)(1) of the NDAA for FY1988-89, P.L. 100-180, signed 4 December 1987, and amended five times since. It is positive law in title 10 rather than a standalone provision, which places it at the centre of the enacted corpus this domain isolates.

d-program.label: Anomalous Phenomena Adjacent to UAP
d-program.why: Anomalous phenomena inside a defence contract
d-program.note: The AAWSAP statement of work and its deliverables are the tier-1 basis for treating this material as a programme domain rather than folklore.

d-program.label: Exotic Technology & Physics
d-program.note: The AAWSAP statement of work and the thirty-eight DIRDs are the tier-1 evidence that a government agency paid for study of the physics a recovered craft would require.

d-program.label: Special Access Programs
d-program.note: The November 2009 OUSD(I) memorandum reviewing a special access programme request for AATIP is the documented moment where a FOIA-visible programme was considered for conversion.

d-exotic.label: Program Structure & Management
d-exotic.note: The AAWSAP statement of work and the thirty-eight DIRDs are the tier-1 evidence that a government agency paid for study of the physics a recovered craft would require.

d-exotic.label: Propulsion & Field Physics
d-exotic.why: Field physics is the propulsion answer
d-exotic.note: DIRD 15 and DIRD 19 are commissioned studies of metric engineering and antigravity - the exotic-physics domain applied to the flight problem.

d-exotic.label: Concepts for Extracting Energy From the Quantum Vacuum
d-exotic.note: Davis and Puthoff had published the same argument in the open literature the year before as Chapter 18, 'On Extracting Energy from the Quantum Vacuum', in 'Frontiers of Propulsion Science' (AIAA, 2009), the volume Davis co-edited with Marc G. Millis - who wrote the 'Cockpits' DIRD. The AAWSAP author network is largely a pre-existing publishing network.

d-prop.label: Military Aviators & Operators
d-prop.why: Reported kinematics set the physics requirement
d-prop.note: Aviator accounts with sensor corroboration generate the acceleration and power figures that any propulsion hypothesis must satisfy.

d-prop.label: Exotic Technology & Physics
d-prop.why: Field physics is the propulsion answer
d-prop.note: DIRD 15 and DIRD 19 are commissioned studies of metric engineering and antigravity - the exotic-physics domain applied to the flight problem.

d-aerospace.label: The Cover-Up
d-aerospace.why: Black aircraft generated real cover stories
d-aerospace.note: CIA's own historian states that U-2 and OXCART flights accounted for over half of late-1950s and 1960s reports and that false explanations were issued to protect them.

d-aerospace.label: Cockpits in the Era of Breakthrough Flight
d-aerospace.why: subject domain: crew-station design for breakthrough flight regimes
d-aerospace.note: The paper asks what a cockpit must look like once a vehicle has inertial control, a hover-to-superluminal speed range and no separation between near-ground, orbital and interstellar operating regimes, including the loss of the pilot's own inertia and visual motion cues. It is the only DIRD that reasons from observed flight behaviour back to onboard design constraints rather than to physics.

d-aerospace.label: Prime Contractor Custody
d-aerospace.why: Advanced projects shops are the industrial home
d-aerospace.note: The organisations with facility clearances, SAP infrastructure and IRAD accounts are the only plausible industrial venue for an exploitation programme.

d-contractor.label: The FFRDC Mechanism
d-contractor.why: The seam between government and industry
d-contractor.note: FAR 35.017 gives the FFRDC access to both government classified holdings and contractor proprietary data - the only entity type that can see both sides of the compartment.

d-contractor.label: Materials and custody analysis
d-contractor.note: Material alleged to be held by primes cannot be independently analysed, which is why the custody question and the materials question cannot be separated.

d-contractor.label: Aerospace Engineering & Advanced Projects
d-contractor.why: Advanced projects shops are the industrial home
d-contractor.note: The organisations with facility clearances, SAP infrastructure and IRAD accounts are the only plausible industrial venue for an exploitation programme.

d-contractor.label: Freedom of Information Practice
d-contractor.why: Contractor records are outside the statute
d-contractor.note: FOIA reaches agency records; material moved into contractor custody leaves the statute's reach without any change in classification. Reasoning stated in the d-foia dossier.

d-contracting.label: Funding Channels
d-contracting.note: The contract vehicle is the visible end of the money; the appropriation and transfer authorities are the invisible end.

d-contracting.label: DIA Contract HHM402-08-C-0072 (AAWSAP / BAASS)
d-contracting.why: the instrument itself - competed, awarded, numbered and released
d-contracting.note: Awarded 22 September 2008 off solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 through the DIA Virginia Contracting Activity. It is the domain's reference specimen: the object that shows what a contract for this subject looks like when the paper survives, against which every undocumented allegation of a contract can be compared.

d-contracting.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC
d-contracting.why: a company stood up to hold a single government contract
d-contracting.note: BAASS was registered as a legal entity distinct from Bigelow Aerospace, with its own DUNS and CAGE codes, in order to bid and hold DIA contract HHM402-08-C-0072. Standing up a corporate vehicle for the purpose of receiving one award is a contracting mechanic, and it is the one instance on this board that is fully documented in FOIA-released procurement paper.

d-contracting.label: EarthTech International / Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
d-contracting.why: the subcontract path - how work reached the government without a prime relationship
d-contracting.note: The reference documents that reached DIA were commissioned by the prime and written substantially by EarthTech and other subcontractors, then delivered as Defense Intelligence Reference Documents. The DIA transmittal list to SASC and the published list of funded studies establish the subcontract layer, which is the layer at which visibility normally stops.

d-contracting.label: EG&G (Edgerton, Germeshausen and Grier)
d-contracting.why: contracting at a site whose existence was itself classified
d-contracting.note: EG&G instrumented and fired US nuclear tests from the Manhattan Project onward and became the classified services contractor for the Nevada complex, including the Air Force operating location near Groom Lake - a facility whose existence required a Presidential Determination published at 60 FR 52823 to exempt it from disclosure. It is the historical template for how contracting works where the place of performance cannot be named.

d-contracting.label: Lockheed Martin Corporation
d-contracting.why: the prime where classified contract line items and sworn allegation meet
d-contracting.note: Lockheed Martin's prime contract obligations run to the hundreds of billions of dollars in USAspending records, a portion carried as classified line items visible in financial systems only as a number. It is also the only company named on the floor of a congressional hearing by a sworn witness in connection with the custody allegation, which makes it the test case for whether contracting records can be made to answer the question.

d-contracting.label: The MITRE Corporation
d-contracting.why: the largest operator of the one acquisition form built to be non-competitive by design
d-contracting.note: MITRE operates multiple FFRDCs. FAR 35.017 permits an agency to meet special long-term research needs through a sponsoring agreement with a single operator outside full and open competition, and obliges the FFRDC to disclose its activities to its sponsor and to no one else. That is a contracting mechanism, and MITRE is its largest single instance.

d-contracting.label: CRADA between U.S. Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center and To The Stars Academy
d-contracting.why: a non-FAR instrument binding the Army to a private claimant of recovered material
d-contracting.note: Signed 10 October 2019 by the Director of the Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center and announced 17 October 2019. A Cooperative Research and Development Agreement sits outside ordinary procurement, involves no exchange of appropriated funds to the partner, and protects the private party's proprietary data - which is exactly the class of vehicle this domain is about. The executed document is not public; sourcing is the partner's own contemporaneous FAQ.

d-contracting.label: The FFRDC Seam
d-contracting.why: the FFRDC seam is a species of contracting mechanics, not a separate subject
d-contracting.note: FAR 35.017 is a procurement regulation. The records status, disclosure direction and sole-source features that make the FFRDC form load-bearing on this board are all properties of the contracting instrument, which is why the seam domain should hang off contracting mechanics rather than float beside it.

d-contracting.label: Raytheon (RTX Corporation)
d-contracting.why: sensor-side prime - the contractor-generated data category nobody is asking for
d-contracting.note: Raytheon builds the AN/APG-79 and ATFLIR families through which the military detects and images the objects at issue, which makes it the corporate custodian of a withheld category of contractor-generated sensor data distinct from the custody allegation. Graded Tier 2: no source places Raytheon in any UAP-specific contract vehicle, and the edge rests on documented prime-contractor role plus hearing-record discussion of sensor data.

d-ffrdc-mechanism.label: Prime Contractor Custody
d-ffrdc-mechanism.why: The seam between government and industry
d-ffrdc-mechanism.note: FAR 35.017 gives the FFRDC access to both government classified holdings and contractor proprietary data - the only entity type that can see both sides of the compartment.

d-roswell.label: Fort Worth, Texas
d-roswell.why: Where the disc became a balloon
d-roswell.note: The Roswell debris was flown to Eighth Air Force headquarters at Fort Worth, where it was presented to the press as a weather balloon the same day.

d-roswell.label: Official Denial
d-roswell.why: Four official explanations for one event
d-roswell.note: Weather balloon in 1947, Project MOGUL in the mid-1990s, crash test dummies in 1997 - the sequence of explanations is itself the evidentiary object.

d-roswell.label: Retrieval & Recovery Operations
d-roswell.why: The founding case of the retrieval strand
d-roswell.note: Roswell is the origin of the crash-retrieval literature and the case against which every later retrieval claim is measured.

d-mj12.label: Disinformation & Fabricated Documents
d-mj12.note: The FBI's Majestic 12 file records the investigation into the corpus's authenticity, making MJ-12 the principal case study for the disinformation domain.

d-astro.label: Stockholm, Sweden
d-astro.note: Villarroel's Stockholm-based VASCO project produced the October 2025 Scientific Reports correlation between POSS-I transients, nuclear testing and UAP reports.

d-astro.label: Nuclear Weapons Complex Nexus
d-astro.why: Sky-survey transients correlate with nuclear testing
d-astro.note: Bruehl and Villarroel's Scientific Reports paper links POSS-I transients to nuclear testing and to UAP reports, connecting the astronomical and nuclear-nexus domains.

d-astro.label: Scientific Research
d-astro.note: The Galileo Project instrumentation papers and the VASCO archival work are the two productive observational programmes outside government.

d-medical.label: Huffman / Dayton, Texas
d-medical.why: The only injury case that reached federal court
d-medical.note: Cash v. United States arose from the December 1980 encounter on FM 1485 and was dismissed in August 1986.

d-medical.label: Biology & Non-Human Biologics
d-medical.why: Biologics claim and documented injury record
d-medical.note: The bio claim has no released material; the medical domain has DIRD 26 and the Cash-Landrum clinical record, which is the auditable end of the same question.

d-medical.label: Plasma Physics & Atmospheric Electricity
d-medical.note: Dermal burn and neurological presentations attributed to anomalous encounters are also produced by directed-energy and radiofrequency exposure, which the board records rather than resolves.

d-nuc.label: Astronomy & Astrophysics
d-nuc.why: Sky-survey transients correlate with nuclear testing
d-nuc.note: Bruehl and Villarroel's Scientific Reports paper links POSS-I transients to nuclear testing and to UAP reports, connecting the astronomical and nuclear-nexus domains.

d-nuc.label: Intelligence Tradecraft & Analysis
d-nuc.why: Indications analysis on the atomic complex
d-nuc.note: Hancock, Porritt and Grosvenor applied formal intelligence indications methodology to UAP reporting against the US atomic warfare complex.

d-nuc.label: Nuclear Security & Restricted Data
d-nuc.why: Phenomenon and the security regime around it
d-nuc.note: The sites where the correlation is strongest are governed by the Restricted Data regime rather than by DoD classification, which routes any resulting analysis outside the SAP framework.

d-plasma.label: Inertial Electrostatic Confinement Fusion
d-plasma.why: subject domain: compact non-tokamak fusion power
d-plasma.note: IEC is one of the few AAWSAP topics with a plausible conventional aerospace reading: a compact fusion device is what a small craft would need if it were producing the observed energy budget. The DIRD set contains four fusion-adjacent deliverables in total - Miley's IEC paper, Winterberg's advanced nuclear propulsion, Teofilo's aneutronic fusion propulsion for Lockheed Martin, and Culbreth's aneutronic fusion propulsion II.

d-plasma.label: Medical & Injury Effects
d-plasma.note: Dermal burn and neurological presentations attributed to anomalous encounters are also produced by directed-energy and radiofrequency exposure, which the board records rather than resolves.

d-signals.label: Freedom of Information Practice
d-signals.note: NSA's statutory withholding, sustained in CAUS v. NSA on the classified Yeates affidavit, is the hardest documented barrier between sensor data and the public record.

d-signals.label: Fort George G. Meade, Maryland
d-signals.why: NSA holdings and the FOIA wall
d-signals.note: The records at issue in CAUS v. NSA are held at Fort Meade, and AARO's current director came from the NSA research organisation based there.

d-signals.label: Military Aviators & Operators
d-signals.why: Sensor corroboration is what makes the accounts arguable
d-signals.note: Radar tracks and targeting-pod video convert a pilot's account into a multi-sensor event; DoD authenticated the imagery in April 2020 while declining to explain it.

d-signals.label: Detection and High Resolution Tracking of Vehicles at Hypersonic Velocities
d-signals.why: subject domain: sensing and tracking at hypersonic velocity
d-signals.note: The sensor-side counterpart to Leonhardt's cloaking DIRD: one asks how an object could be made undetectable, the other how an object moving at hypersonic velocity could nevertheless be tracked at high resolution. Together they bracket the observability problem that any UAP sensor programme has to solve.

d-signals.label: High-Frequency Gravitational Wave Communications
d-signals.why: subject domain: gravitational-wave communications and surveillance
d-signals.note: Baker's open-source 2010 counterpart claims theoretical aerospace, military and civilian applications in 'communications, surveillance, remote initiation of nuclear events and propulsion, including moving space objects and missiles in flight and frustrating anti-missile and anti-satellite systems.' The breadth of that claim is precisely what JASON's 'no foreign threat in HFGW is credible' was rejecting.

d-remote-viewing.label: Consciousness & Observer Effects
d-remote-viewing.note: Star Gate is the documented precedent that the US government funds anomalous-cognition research; the consciousness domain inherits its personnel and its framing.

d-remote-viewing.label: Anomalous Phenomena Adjacent to UAP
d-remote-viewing.note: Principal investigators from the SRI-era programmes reappear in the AAWSAP deliverables three decades later, carrying the research framing with them.

d-consciousness.label: Remote Viewing & Anomalous Cognition
d-consciousness.note: Star Gate is the documented precedent that the US government funds anomalous-cognition research; the consciousness domain inherits its personnel and its framing.

d-paranormal.label: Program Structure & Management
d-paranormal.why: Anomalous phenomena inside a defence contract
d-paranormal.note: The AAWSAP statement of work and its deliverables are the tier-1 basis for treating this material as a programme domain rather than folklore.

d-paranormal.label: Remote Viewing & Anomalous Cognition
d-paranormal.note: Principal investigators from the SRI-era programmes reappear in the AAWSAP deliverables three decades later, carrying the research framing with them.

d-international.label: Toulouse, France
d-international.note: GEIPAN has operated within CNES at Toulouse since 1977, publishing classifications and statistics openly.

d-international.label: Disclosure Movement
d-international.note: GEIPAN's published classification scheme and open case archive establish that an acknowledged state programme is possible, shifting the burden onto the concealment argument.

d-international.label: Varginha, Minas Gerais, Brazil
d-international.why: A foreign case now under US congressional inquiry
d-international.note: In July 2026 a US lawmaker formally requested FBI and CIA holdings on the 1996 Varginha incident.

l-san-agustin.label: Roswell Incident
l-san-agustin.note: The Plains of San Agustin entered the Roswell corpus through Grady 'Barney' Barnett's reported account, transmitted second-hand via Vern and Jean Maltais to Stanton Friedman in October 1978 and published in Berlitz and Moore's 'The Roswell Incident' (1980). The claim is contested by Kevin Randle, who argues the site has no connection to Roswell, and no primary document supports it.

l-aztec.label: Aztec, New Mexico claim, March 1948
l-aztec.note: Scully's account placed the landing in Hart Canyon, roughly twelve miles northeast of the city of Aztec, San Juan County, New Mexico. The location is the only fixed and checkable element of the story, and it is the one the town later built a symposium and a commemorative plaque around.

l-varginha.label: International & Allied Programs
l-varginha.why: A foreign case now under US congressional inquiry
l-varginha.note: In July 2026 a US lawmaker formally requested FBI and CIA holdings on the 1996 Varginha incident.

l-uk-mod-whitehall.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in the UK Air Defence Region (DIS Scientific & Technical Memorandum 55/2/00)
l-uk-mod-whitehall.why: Condign report held at MoD Main Building
l-uk-mod-whitehall.note: Project Condign was run by the Defence Intelligence Staff branch DI55 between 1997 and 2000; the resulting three-volume, 463-page report 'Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in the UK Air Defence Region' was held at the Ministry of Defence Main Building in Whitehall.

l-uk-mod-whitehall.label: Rendlesham Forest Incident, RAF Woodbridge/Bentwaters
l-uk-mod-whitehall.why: MoD UFO desk held and released the Rendlesham file
l-uk-mod-whitehall.note: The MoD's UFO desk, run by the Directorate of Air Staff until its closure in 2009, held the Rendlesham Forest file; the complete file was released via The National Archives in August 2009 and includes Lt Col Charles Halt's account and the MoD's own investigation conclusions.

l-huffman-tx.label: Medical & Injury Effects
l-huffman-tx.why: The only injury case that reached federal court
l-huffman-tx.note: Cash v. United States arose from the December 1980 encounter on FM 1485 and was dismissed in August 1986.

l-toulouse.label: International & Allied Programs
l-toulouse.note: GEIPAN has operated within CNES at Toulouse since 1977, publishing classifications and statistics openly.

l-brasilia.label: Arquivo Nacional (Brazil) - UFO/UAP collection
l-brasilia.why: The UFO fund is held in Brasília and its reference code says so
